## CSS migrations: media

*2020-10-29 to 2020-10-31 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/CSS.20migrations.3A.20media/with/1051754)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-10-29 23:29 UTC

For https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16654, the sweep is to replace our media CSS with using the bootstrap default breakpoints; the question is whether we like the naming that bootstrap uses for the sizes or want to use our own aliases.  (And I guess also if we like their set of size ranges, but I'm tempted to say it's a reasonable start).

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:12 UTC

Bootstrap 3.4.1 breakpoints and naming
```less

//== Media queries breakpoints
//
//## Define the breakpoints at which your layout will change, adapting to different screen sizes.

// Extra small screen / phone
//** Deprecated `@screen-xs` as of v3.0.1
@screen-xs:                  480px;
//** Deprecated `@screen-xs-min` as of v3.2.0
@screen-xs-min:              @screen-xs;
//** Deprecated `@screen-phone` as of v3.0.1
@screen-phone:               @screen-xs-min;

// Small screen / tablet
//** Deprecated `@screen-sm` as of v3.0.1
@screen-sm:                  768px;
@screen-sm-min:              @screen-sm;
//** Deprecated `@screen-tablet` as of v3.0.1
@screen-tablet:              @screen-sm-min;

// Medium screen / desktop
//** Deprecated `@screen-md` as of v3.0.1
@screen-md:                  992px;
@screen-md-min:              @screen-md;
//** Deprecated `@screen-desktop` as of v3.0.1
@screen-desktop:             @screen-md-min;

// Large screen / wide desktop
//** Deprecated `@screen-lg` as of v3.0.1
@screen-lg:                  1200px;
@screen-lg-min:              @screen-lg;
//** Deprecated `@screen-lg-desktop` as of v3.0.1
@screen-lg-desktop:          @screen-lg-min;

// So media queries don't overlap when required, provide a maximum
@screen-xs-max:              (@screen-sm-min - 1);
@screen-sm-max:              (@screen-md-min - 1);
@screen-md-max:              (@screen-lg-min - 1);

```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:12 UTC

I removed the screen part from our naming of the variables.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:13 UTC

Bootstrap 4.5 breakpoints:
```scss
$grid-breakpoints: (
  xs: 0,
  sm: 576px,
  md: 768px,
  lg: 992px,
  xl: 1200px
) !default;
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:14 UTC

We also have the option to use bootstrap 4.5 breakpoints if they make sense.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:14 UTC

@Steve Howell thoughts?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:15 UTC

Our breakpoints:

```js
// Media query breakpoints according to Bootstrap 3.4.1
const xs = 480
const sm = 768
const md = 992
const lg = 1200
const xl = 1400

module.exports = {
    plugins: {
        // Warning: despite appearances, order is significant
        "postcss-nested": {},
        "postcss-extend-rule": {},
        "postcss-simple-vars": {
            variables: {
                "xs-min": xs + "px",
                "sm-min": sm + "px",
                "md-min": md + "px",
                "lg-min": lg + "px",
                "xl-min": xl + "px",

                "xs-max": xs - 1 + "px",
                "sm-max": sm - 1 + "px",
                "md-max": md - 1 + "px",
                "lg-max": lg - 1 + "px",
                "xl-max": xl - 1 + "px",
            }
        },
        "postcss-calc": {},
        autoprefixer: {},
    },
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:24 UTC

In our codebase, we have ~50 different media query breakpoints. The pixel value for them was decided on the width where the media query change would have immediate impact or; the view breaks at a specific width, and we add media query there to fix the view.

The general strategy we can follow is moving the media query breakpoint to the nearest upper standard breakpoint. Like 970px can be moved to `md` = 992px.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-30 03:25 UTC

Then there are breakpoints like 772px, which make sense to belong in `sm` = 768px. I will live test them and make the change.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-10-31 02:40 UTC

I think using the values from Bootstrap 4.5 makes sense, given our plan is to upgrade all the way.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-10-31 03:31 UTC

Okay.


## Topic click didn't select

*2020-11-03 to 2020-11-09 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Topic.20click.20didn.27t.20select/with/1056021)*

**Nick Lindridge** · 2020-11-03 16:01 UTC

I just clicked within a topic in our all messages stream, posted and was told it went to the wrong stream. Turns out that clicking an attachment does not focus the topic whereas clicking text does. Would be useful for such a click to select the topic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-04 00:10 UTC

@Nick Lindridge interesting, thanks for the feedback.  I think clicking the attachment to view it in the lightbox moves focus to the lightbox; so I think what you're proposing is that we move focus back to that message when one closes the lightbox?  (Or move the selected message in the background while we open the lightbox?).

In any case, Zulip fades the background for messages that aren't where you're sending to -- so if the message you're looking at is faded, you're not sending to its topic.  That visual detail can help a lot in avoiding sending to the wrong place.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-04 00:10 UTC

I think that proposal might be net helpful.

**Nick Lindridge** · 2020-11-04 11:39 UTC

@Tim Abbott Thanks for the followup and yes, I'd propose that the message/topic should have become focussed having interacted.  For whatever reason, I find myself generally ignoring cues such as the fading and also other indicators for who a message is going to. I just can't train myself to make a conscious step to check, probably relying on what I intuitively expect to happen instead and unfortunately losing from time to time. My thought process is probably along the lines of "Oh that looks interesting, let's take a look, yep, need to say something about that, write a comment and send."

**Nick Lindridge** · 2020-11-04 13:20 UTC

@Tim Abbott Just sent another message to the strong stream, and remembered another design issue, which is when you click away from message in the all messages view they all become clearly visible. This is highly confusing as you can see a message come in, all bright and clear just like all the others, so you hit enter, type a reply and send. The problem is that if that isn't the selected topic, it'll go to the wrong place. Having either to click on the most recent message every time before sending something, visibly hunting for where a selected message is to see if it's in the same topic as the most recent message, or start replying and check that the topic is correct, is quite a problem. In the latter case, if you have started replying and realise that it's the wrong topic, it's quite awkward to unwind that, requiring cut/paste, or potentially deleting an unwanted draft. 

In short, by design, the place one would reasonably and intuitively expect a reply to go to often isn't the case when using the all messages view.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-09 00:22 UTC

@Nick Lindridge I believe the message will change color the moment you hit enter here?  

In any case, our path forward involves de-emphasizing the "All messages" view in favor of "Recent topics" (as the default view; both will be available in any case); you can play with it on this server.

**Nick Lindridge** · 2020-11-09 09:35 UTC

Thanks @Tim Abbott , must admit I'd not tried recent topics but that looks useful, though a split screen between all messages and recent topics might be even better. Personally I typically have several long term active topics/streams on the go that I need to monitor and possibly comment on, and 2 or 3 private chats with activity intermittently over the day. All messages is on the right lines in terms of usefulness because I can just glance at it to keep up to date, but the most recent message that came in not automatically being where a reply goes is where I tend to come unstuck. If that were an option it would be more efficient and reduce errors.

Some installations have Zulip content that they want to make web-public, and more importantly, searchable.  They can do that now by using zulip-archive to create a mostly static (kind of an overload word, but you get the idea) website that they can host on a completely different box than Zulip.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-11-05 20:13 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2020-11-05 20:15 UTC

One of our goals with web-public streams is to make it easier to create archive sites for Zulip apps where only **some** of the public streams should truly be considered "web public".  So part of the original web-public effort was somewhat orthogonal to the more current developments.  We simply want Zulip admins to have a way to flag that a stream's content isn't even quasi-private.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-11-05 20:30 UTC

So before we truly roll out web-public streams, we should all put on our lawyer hats for a little bit, since in one sense participating on a web-public stream is essentially like signing away any exclusive rights to your "content" on the chat.

## buggy markdown render for image

*2020-11-07 to 2020-12-19 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/buggy.20markdown.20render.20for.20image/with/1059143)*

**Shanu** · 2020-11-07 06:08 UTC

Without extra newline after image link, link of the text file is displayed just below image url. 

[index.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/4c/3aJtfzWfQ9ZwoikqiXKI8jFH/index.png) 
[pres.txt](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/5d/8DljeE4Bq5Ab5YnXpvfpXGT5/pres.txt) 


Is this the expected render?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-20 01:59 UTC

@Shanu That's the expected rendering, yes, because without the extra newline you're asking for the text file and image links to be in the same paragraph (with a line break within the paragraph), and we only insert the image previews between paragraphs.

**Shanu** · 2020-11-20 20:55 UTC

I see. This wasn't obvious at first glance. Maybe one should always preview messages before sending for most cases.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-12-19 02:55 UTC

I don't think that'd be worth the clutter for the majority of messages where it isn't an issue -- it's easy to enough to fix a mistake with message editing if need be.

(That detail about how paragraphs work is a standard aspect of Markdown, so not one we're likely to change).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-12-19 04:49 UTC

Our insertion of image previews between paragraphs certainly isn’t standard, and I expect we’ll stop doing that at least for `[…](…)` links when we enable the standard `![…](…)` syntax for images.

## escaping

*2020-11-30 to 2021-03-15 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/escaping/with/1071700)*

**Wesley Aptekar-Cassels** · 2020-11-30 01:59 UTC

is there a general consensus on where html escaping should happen? it seems like right now, it's a mix of i18next and handlebars, which seems not ideal — it's easy to double escape things, or to assume that something will be escaped in a place where it's not. (see [#16789](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16789) and [#16806](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16806)

in general, i18next seems like a sort of strange place to do escaping, since i don't think it's common to just slam strings right from i18next into the html — it seems like they usually go through handlebars first. but i haven't seen enough of the frontend code to say for sure that escaping should or shouldn't be done in a specific place, so i'm curious what people's thoughts are here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-30 06:22 UTC

Thanks for reporting!  Generally the only places we will want to have i18next escape is if we're inserting text into the DOM directly via Javascript, which we try to avoid

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-11-30 06:28 UTC

Almost all strings that have variables in them are in templates; @Wesley Aptekar-Cassels.  Ideally we'd have all escaping done via templates because that's a clean, simple policy.  But sometimes that isn't possible or convenient.

**Wesley Aptekar-Cassels** · 2020-11-30 06:55 UTC

is there a way to configure i18next to not escape by default? if so, i could put together a PR that switches i18next to not escape by default, and converts all the current call sites to explicitly escape in the few cases where we currently need it, to make it harder to accidentally escape in i18next. this has the downside of being more unexpected for people used to the current behaviour, but seems like it would be better in the long term, imo.

doesn't seem like this would be too tricky, there aren't a ton of callsites to i18next where we use templating right now:

**Steve Howell** · 2020-11-30 14:47 UTC

Going back to your larger proposal, your strategy seems promising. **Wesley Aptekar-Cassels** · 2020-12-17 05:17 UTC

i got busy with some life stuff, but do plan to get back to at least looking over the 2 PRs i made and checking to make sure that they're safe in all codepaths. not sure exactly when i'll get to that.

on the more general topic, i don't think we have consensus on whether we should disable escaping in i18next. personally, i think it's the right move, but i understand that it's nuanced and i'm somewhat of a drive-by contributor, so i definitely understand if people who work on the frontend more think that's not the right move.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-12-19 02:36 UTC

I'd be potentially OK with disabling escaping in `i18next` if we have a `semgrep` like policy tool to prevent passing `i18next` content directly into `.html()` type functions, but otherwise it's too risky for inexperienced developers creating XSS issues.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-12-19 02:38 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-29 18:30 UTC

FYI this issue was re-reported two days ago as https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/16969.  My opinion here is that we should err on the side of double-escaping, which means we just keep the current default for `i18next` of `escapeValue: true`.  The double-escaping bugs are slightly embarrassing, but they should be mostly harmless, and I think we can just fix them as we notice them, using the same strategy as @Wesley Aptekar-Cassels used in https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16789

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-15 05:26 UTC

## Font Size Values

*2020-12-11 to 2020-12-11 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Font.20Size.20Values/with/1079244)*

**Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20)** · 2020-12-11 19:52 UTC

I have been working on [#15967](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/15967) and am trying to change font-size values for improving readability. I found values of font for the 'code blocks' as
```
code {
        /* Copied from rendered_markdown.css */
        font-size: 0.857em;
```
How was this 3 place precise value chosen? Is it based on pixel sizes?

**Greg Price** · 2020-12-11 20:52 UTC

@Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20) A very handy tool I like for answering questions like this one is `git log -S`. See our short guide here:
https://github.com/zulip/zulip-mobile/blob/master/docs/howto/git.md#reading-history

In this instance, looking at `git log --stat -p -S 0.857`, this turns out to date to a very early commit:
```diff
commit b558d062ba0b942134e4aaefd817ccd29f9872fb
Author: Reid Barton <rwbarton@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Feb 14 22:01:54 2013 -0500

    Scale code and pre contents with font size
    
…
--- a/zephyr/static/styles/zephyr.css
+++ b/zephyr/static/styles/zephyr.css
@@ -57,9 +57,19 @@ li, .table th, .table td {
 /* Inline and block code */
 
 code {
+    /* 12/14 em, so bootstrap's default 12 px,
+       when body is the default 14 px */
+    font-size: 0.857em;

**Greg Price** · 2020-12-11 20:52 UTC

So based on that comment, it was indeed based on a ratio of sizes in `px`.

**Greg Price** · 2020-12-11 20:55 UTC

(The `--stat` isn't really needed here, but I basically always include it because for diffs that are longer than a screenful it often comes in very handy. I [have an alias](https://gist.github.com/gnprice/5f71b63464a76bd7e0480f207b1bbff3) so `git lsp` means `git log --stat -p`.)

**Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20)** · 2020-12-11 20:56 UTC

Thanks for the help Greg. I'll keep this tool in mind when stuck at similar points.

## node tests failure

*2021-01-02 to 2021-01-04 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/node.20tests.20failure/with/1091232)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-01-02 05:26 UTC

Don't know why, but node tests are suddenly failing on all PRs. Opened #16997 to fix it. git bisect isn't fruitful either.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-01-02 16:23 UTC

The tests were failing because the timestamp was from previous year Jan 2 and we skip YYYY in date syntax if the timestamp is in the same year.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-03 16:36 UTC

@Aman Agrawal So was this one of those failures that only happens around midnight on New Year's Eve?  Does your fix that I merged address it going forward, or is there a cleaner fix?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-01-04 01:08 UTC

The test failure we fixed will not repeat, but we could do the mistake of writing such tests again. One way to fix them all would be to always mock today's date when writing such tests. I don't know how we will enforce this.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-04 16:06 UTC

I actually prefer to write tests in terms of the current date, not mocking them, although I would say I'm about 80/20 on that.  Test flakes can be good if they expose actual brittleness in the real code.  Of course, most of the time the flakes are in the test code itself, which is just annoying.  But you can write robust tests in terms of the current date usually, without having to mock.

And I don't think there's any great enforcement strategy here.

## Zulip doesn't do numeric lists?

*2021-01-03 to 2021-01-04 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Zulip.20doesn.27t.20do.20numeric.20lists.3F/with/1091774)*

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-03 17:27 UTC

One thing our members are used to from Slack is the ease of creating nicely and automatically-formatted numeric lists.  Zulip doesn't do this although the help claims it does:  https://zulip.com/help/format-your-message-using-markdown#lists

Is there some reason this doesn't work?

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-03 18:43 UTC

In fact it doesn't seem to work in this community either.  Has markdown been deprecated or something?

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-03 19:54 UTC

So numeric lists DO work, but they have to literally be typed the way they display in the help:
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/26/UmShOYHnE9BrmhUPd67CAi7n/image.png)

This is utterly unintuitive.  Everyone is used to being able to enter regular numbers like

1. item one
2. item two
3. etc.

And have the list automatically maintained as you edit.  I hope you guys can improve upon this or at least support the standard that is in place basically everywhere.

**Jonathan Rudenberg** · 2021-01-03 20:12 UTC

The "regular number" list that you posted rendered fine. You can confirm this by right clicking on your message and inspecting the element, noting that it has the proper HTML markup for a list (`<ol>`). Markdown lets you use any numbers within certain constraints. For example, view the source of my message (from the "..." menu when hovering over it) and note that it has numbers that are not monotonic or in order, but renders properly (as long as the first item is numbered `1.`):

1. item one
5. item two
4. item three

Automatically adding in the numbers after pressing enter while typing a list is a thing that has been [recently discussed](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/2-general/topic/Typeahead.20for.20Numbered.20list).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-01-03 22:09 UTC

Yeah, as of #12921 we’re following the [CommonMark standard](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.29/#lists) for numbered lists: “The start number of an ordered list is determined by the list number of its initial list item. The numbers of subsequent list items are disregarded.” So it doesn’t matter whether you type them as 1., 1., 1. or 1., 2., 3.

We intend to follow CommonMark in general, but for historical reasons there are a couple of known differences, which we treat as bugs to be fixed.

Your message seems to work as expected. If you think there’s a bug, please explain how the actual behavior differs from expected.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-04 02:17 UTC

TL;DR see Slack.

The expected behavior is that as I type, as soon as I type a number followed by a period followed by a space, the list begins and indents slightly so I can visually tell I'm in a list.  Then whenever I hit enter, I am automatically met with the next number.  I can see the list happen as I go, I don't need to type the numbers myself.

**Rein Zustand** · 2021-01-04 02:24 UTC

That Slack's WYSIWYG text editing feature is actually controversial. A lot of people complained: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=21589647.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-04 18:56 UTC

Yeah I'm sure they did, just like lots of our members are complaining about not having it.  I think it comes down to developers vs. non.  Devs love their text editors, and are used to things like markdown.  Non-devs most certainly are NOT and they hate not having a WYSIWYG, Rich-Text, etc.  We're getting a lot of feedback in our community and while much of it can just be attributed to "change shock", some of it is also very reasoned, such as markdown being the only way to do simple things like lists.  Our users are never going to get the syntax right, they'll not put spaces after the periods, or they'll double space, or they'll use 1 space in a bullet indent instead of 2, etc.  It's going to cause a lot of frustration so I would strongly vote for the option of at least a Slack-level WYSIWYG (which was extremely basic anyway...)

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-04 20:07 UTC

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> TL;DR see Slack. The expected behavior is that as I type, as soon as I type a number followed by a period followed by a space, the list begins and indents slightly so I can visually tell I'm in a list. Then whenever I hit enter, I am automatically met with the next number. I can see the list happen …

We had a related discussion recently here (as @Jonathan Rudenberg mentioned above):
https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/2-general/topic/Typeahead.20for.20Numbered.20list/near/1088091

That corresponds to a somewhat stripped-down version of this feature, which might look like:
> The expected behavior is that as I type, as soon as I type a number followed by a period followed by a space, […] whenever I hit enter, I am automatically met with the next number.  I can see the list happen as I go, I don't need to type the numbers myself.

I'd be in favor of that feature. GitHub recently added one that works much like that, and I've been appreciating it.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-04 20:13 UTC

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> So numeric lists DO work, but they have to literally be typed the way they display in the help: [image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/26/UmShOYHnE9BrmhUPd67CAi7n/image.png) This is utterly unintuitive. Everyone is used to being able to enter regular numbers like 1. item one 2. item two 3. etc.

As you learned later in the thread, you can indeed perfectly well do that in Zulip. In fact I think of that as the normal way to enter a list, and the 1., 1., 1. thing as a technical detail of the syntax.

I think it'd probably be best for the example in the help to look like
```
1. item one
2. item two
3. etc.
```
rather than emphasizing the 1., 1., 1. option, so it doesn't cause this confusion.

## Naming group DMs?

*2021-01-11 to 2021-01-14 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Naming.20group.20DMs.3F/with/1096144)*

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-11 03:48 UTC

I have a situation where I have multiple groups, each of which consist of at least a few of the same specific people.  That means I end up with multiple group DMs that look either the same or very similar.

For instance DM #1 consists of person A, B, C, and D.  DM #2 consists of person A, B, and D.  DM #3 consists of person B, C, and D.  Would be really useful to be able to somehow organize/name these groups DMs so I could easily keep track of which one contains which people.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-11 15:58 UTC

@Jonathan van Clute We have tended not to invest too much development effort to improving the Group PM experience.  Generally we encourage folks to just create small private streams for small group conversations.

To be clear, there are times when group PMs are effective, especially for kinda quick ad hoc conversations, so I appreciate the feedback.

I believe we have a search feature that makes it easy to find all conversations in which somebody has participated...

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-11 15:59 UTC

If you type `group-pm-with:` into the search bar it will autocomplete.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-12 03:31 UTC

Yeah and we do use private streams for specific groups of people ("staff", "moderators"), but group PMs solve a different need, which is the less structured quick "heads ups" or whatever to a variable subset of people, that often happen in an organization.  Search really doesn't help because like I said, the same people are in multiple streams, with maybe one participant difference.  Oh well, will just have to make do.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-01-12 07:23 UTC

Would user groups accomplish that? I'm not familiar with whether the webapp supports them as pm recipients, I'm guessing maybe not?

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-01-12 13:25 UTC

I'm not sure, I haven't really explored User Groups as I'm not entirely clear where they fit in the scheme of Zulip.  Now I'm wondering though so, thanks!

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-12 21:54 UTC

I don't think user groups are for this. The thing they enable is @-mentions of a group -- like `@mobile` or `@desktop`.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-12 22:03 UTC

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> Yeah and we do use private streams for specific groups of people ("staff", "moderators"), but group PMs solve a different need, which is the less structured quick "heads ups" or whatever to a variable subset of people, that often happen in an organization.

Here's an experiment that might be helpful to try:
* Take one of the group PM threads that you'd be interested in naming.
* Make a private stream, with the same name you'd want to use for that thread, and add the same people to it.
* Use that private stream the way you would use the named group-PM thread.

Then it'd be informative to try to identify specifically what it is that makes you feel you'd rather the conversation be in "PMs" rather than a "private stream". There are some UI differences between that private stream and a possible named group-PM thread... but fundamentally they're much alike -- they're both ways to have a conversation with a named set of people -- so I think it hasn't been obvious what the difference is that makes a difference.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-12 22:07 UTC

In particular, one thing about naming a group is that it feels (to me, at least how I'm imagining the UI or from my experience with apps like FB Messenger) like it makes it not ephemeral -- it got a name because it's expected to last for more than a handful of messages or a single conversation.

So at that point it seems like it really might as well be a private stream. That's our main feature for enabling conversations ongoing over time for a given set of people.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-12 22:10 UTC

Naming a group also detaches its identity from the exact set of people involved. If the group is identified by a name -- perhaps a name referring to a team, or a project -- then it will very often make sense to add or remove people from it over time.

That too is a core feature of a private stream, and not such a good fit with what a group-PM conversation is.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-12 22:13 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> Then it'd be informative to try to identify specifically what it is that makes you feel you'd rather the conversation be in "PMs" rather than a "private stream". There are some UI differences between that private stream and a possible named group-PM thread... but fundamentally they're much alike -- …

(And to be clear: I don't mean to say that I think there really isn't a difference! I can think of a couple of possibilities, and you may also have one I haven't thought of. But if we can identify what the difference is that drives this request... one possible solution is we might be able to add an option on private streams that takes care of it.)

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-01-14 01:55 UTC

@Greg Price said:
> I don't think user groups are for this. The thing they enable is @-mentions of a group -- like `@mobile` or `@desktop`.
They may not be intended for this (if that's what you meant by 'for'), but after mentioning it as just a thought earlier, I just checked and currently putting a user-group name in a PM (in the webapp) expands it to the list of members. I do agree that private streams have more long term use - they're easier to review later, users who take over roles can see the history, etc.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-14 02:15 UTC

(replying to Neil Pilgrim)
> They may not be intended for this (if that's what you meant by 'for'), but after mentioning it as just a thought earlier, I just checked and currently putting a user-group name in a PM (in the webapp) expands it to the list of members.

> I feel strongly that as an admin, I need better control over who is in what stream. I should at a minimum be able to see who is subscribed to any given stream, and what streams are subscribed to by any given member.

It sounds like one improvement that would go a long way here would be to have a version of the "Stream Membership" area that's expanded out to a whole settings page of its own, just showing the members of one given stream.

**Greg Price** · 2021-01-28 09:43 UTC

And then related to that, the whole settings UI probably should not have the maximum height that it has:

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> Also related to this, I can't even see a full list of the members of a stream anywhere, I have to scroll and scroll and scroll. I was thinking I could have the list of members in stream A up in the desktop app, and the list of members of stream B up in the web app, and just compare them that way... …

On my desktop (with a large monitor), the settings UI won't go taller than about half the total height available to it.

A maximum *width* can have a lot of value, especially for anything with paragraphs of text, in order to keep it possible to read the text in a natural way. But when there's potentially a lot of content to show, as there is on many of our settings pages, it's hard for me to see a good justification for putting an absolute limit on the height -- vs letting it grow taller and taller to make use of as much vertical space as the user cares to give it on their display.

*2021-01-20 to 2021-01-20 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/media.20breakpoint.20naming.20issue.20.2316680/with/1102886)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-01-20 15:30 UTC

There is a slight naming issue that Tim has raised here https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16680#discussion_r516381443 

[Screenshot-2021-01-20-at-9.00.21-PM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/da/d2lCDrRvD398k5Lk__Y_RGmz/Screenshot-2021-01-20-at-9.00.21-PM.png) 

Thoughts on this ? @Anders Kaseorg @Steve Howell

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-20 15:34 UTC

I don't know enough about CSS conventions to have a strong opinion here, but Tim's comment seems right to me.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-20 15:35 UTC

I enjoy Douglas Crockford's take on hyphens in CSS:

https://frontendmasters.com/courses/good-parts-javascript-web/retrieving-nodes/

[00:03:06] So I need to rant for a moment. So the CSS and the DOM were both designed about the same time. And each project was aware of the other. The guy who designed CSS was aware that some day programming languages were going to manipulate style sheets, not that was a certainty.

[00:03:27] And yet he chose to use the minus sign as a hyphen, knowing that most of our programming languages want to do subtraction with it and that this creates a syntactic difficulty for all of you. He did that, anyway. Meanwhile, at Netscape they're working on the DOM and they see what just happened to CSS and they go.

[00:03:49] Okay, what are we gonna do about that? What they could have said was, well, that's annoying but we'll just say you take the brackets and you put the string in, that's that, so. You have to type for extra characters but it was completely compatible. Or they could have said, well minus signs are a problem, so we'll just change them to under bars.

[00:04:11] So minimal change, search and replace config, no. They went with the least compatible way of writing these names.

 And it matters, cuz you need to be aware of which space am I in right now? Am I in CSS space, or am I in DOM space? And it's really easy to get confused about where you are and if you pick the wrong form, it's total failure.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-01-20 15:40 UTC

I enjoyed reading it. Let's do `media_breakpoints.xl_max` then.

## Several improvement suggestions...

*2021-02-02 to 2021-02-02 · 70 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Several.20improvement.20suggestions.2E.2E.2E/with/1112302)*

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-02 19:04 UTC

These came out of a community open Q&A we held today.  I don't know if any are already being considered or in progress, but...

1. It would be useful to be able to do boolean searches.  "combine and drawdown" for instance.  Right now putting in multiple words will result in all instances of either of the words (plus their stems which is another issue).
2.  There seems to be no way to do an absolutely literal search.  I can't put a search in quotes in order to get the exact phrase ONLY.  Zulip keeps trying to "help" by including stems and other stuff which is absolutely not helpful.  We need a separate way to do literal searches.
3.  Could there be a community-specific dictionary so that words can be added that are in common usage there?  We are a niche financial group and so we have a LOT of terms that are specific to us, and that our members would potentially want to search for.  It would be really nice to be able to add them to a dictionary somewhere so that Zulip would understand them and be better able to search for them. Hmm, I'm now recalling that I think this server chat.zulip.org may be using the PGroonga backend.

Zulip supports two different backends for full-text search: the one built into the PostgreSQL database engine, and PGroonga which is an extension. By default we use the built-in one.

**Greg Price** · 2021-02-02 21:43 UTC

From a quick look at the docs, it appears that the underlying backend supports AND and OR just fine:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-intro.html

And on the other hand PGroonga also supports OR as well as AND, though our interface to it doesn't currently give you a way to use the OR:
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/5603

So if that's the story, then it seems like a bug in our search code but should be a very fixable one.

**Greg Price** · 2021-02-02 21:59 UTC

Hmm.

The search already includes messages in private streams, when they're messages you actually received (i.e., they were sent while you were already subscribed.) The "expand" thing just adds the earlier history for public streams.

It used to be that you couldn't see earlier history in private streams. Now we have two kinds of private streams: those where you can't see earlier history of messages you didn't directly receive, and those where once you're added you can. I suspect that that search feature just didn't get updated to handle the new flavor of private stream.

## Message edit form doesn't close after losing connection.

*2021-02-03 to 2021-02-03 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Message.20edit.20form.20doesn.27t.20close.20after.20losing.20connection.2E/with/1112599)*

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-02-03 10:25 UTC

When I try to close the message edit form after losing internet connectivity, the edit form doesn't close. Instead the window just scrolls up.

I filed an issue for this. https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/17190

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-02-03 10:32 UTC

This happens because messages sent after the connection is lost have a floating-point zid. Clicking the close button causes jQuery to get an element with an id having a dot, for e.g. "#message-edit-send-status-159.04", which raises an error
"Error: Failed to execute 'querySelector' on 'Document': '#message-edit-send-status-159.04' is not a valid selector."

The dot should be escaped using double slashes. Currently, this doesn't happen because we use this to parse the zid in `static/js/rows.js`:
```javascript
return Number.parseFloat(zid);
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-03 23:09 UTC

I’m not sure how to follow your reproduction steps, since for messages that haven’t yet been acknowledged by the server, we don’t let you open the edit form in the first place. However, the unescaped selector is certainly a bug, and I’ve tried to fix that comprehensively in #17200.

## selector code

*2021-02-04 to 2021-02-04 · 54 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/selector.20code/with/1113342)*

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 19:58 UTC

I am wondering if it's worth investing in finding or writing a small library to build CSS selectors.

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/17200#issuecomment-773565192

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:01 UTC

Because we use templates to build DOM, it's very common for us to have to find rows via something like `.user_settings[user_id='555']` when we do things like live updates, and it would be nice if that code weren't so brittle to things like CSS escaping issues.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:01 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/aa650a4c88e1b577549f19683bf833d47a745292 solves the problem on a line-by-line basis.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:03 UTC

It's unfortunate that we have about five different ways of finding elements in our DOM, but there are some fairly common patterns.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:10 UTC

On a related note, it would nice to audit our code to make changes of this nature:
* before: `data-id="description-555"`
* after: `data-field="description" data-stream-id="555"`

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-04 20:22 UTC

I’m not sure whether that would be an improvement. The browser can query `#description-555` using a fast hash map (assuming you meant `id` rather than `data-id`), but would need to do a linear scan to query `[data-stream-id='555']`, unless it’s way more clever than I expect at automatically generating the needed indexes.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:29 UTC

Code like the following is scary: 

~~~ js
const setting_checkbox = $(`#${CSS.escape(setting)}_${CSS.escape(sub.stream_id)}`);
~~~

which I believe maps to this line in our templates:

~~~
<label class="subscription-control-label" for="{{setting_name}}_{{stream_id}}">{{label}}</label>

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-04 20:35 UTC

`<label for=…>` can’t reference anything other than an `id` anyway.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:36 UTC

If nothing else, we should probably be consistent about dashes vs. hyphen when we build up ids.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:50 UTC

For performance, https://www.sitepoint.com/optimizing-css-id-selectors-and-other-myths/ suggests it's not worth fretting too much over selectors.  Of course, while linear scans might be fine, there's the concern of quadratic slowdowns.  For example, when we do compose-fade on the buddy list, theoretically we are invoking the caller of this code N times:

~~~ js
 23     get_li_from_key(opts) {
 24         const user_id = opts.key;
 25         const container = $(this.container_sel);
 26         return container.find(`${this.item_sel}[data-user-id='${CSS.escape(user_id)}']`);
 27     }
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-04 20:52 UTC

The buddy list isn't the best case study, since we do lazy rendering that would probably prevent quadratic behavior from being noticed.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-04 20:53 UTC

Attribute selectors are conspicuously missing from the benchmarks on that page.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-04 20:54 UTC

And I think we have a lot more DOM elements flying around than most other programmers would consider reasonable.

## stream_data's slug_to_name

*2021-02-08 to 2021-02-10 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/stream_data.27s.20slug_to_name/with/1115316)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2021-02-08 23:34 UTC

How should clients interpret a stream slug in a URL that looks like '999something'?

Following zulip/zulip@2574efde3, it appears that the web app will treat it as a new-style slug: it'll be taken to refer to a stream with ID 999, if that stream exists. (If it doesn't, it'll be taken as an old-style slug, as referring to a stream with name '999something'.)

````spoiler [exports.slug_to_name in stream_data.js](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/js/stream_data.js#L302-L348)
```js
exports.slug_to_name = function (slug) {
    /*
    Modern stream slugs look like this, where 42
    is a stream id:
        42
        42-stream-name
    We have legacy slugs that are just the name
    of the stream:
        stream-name
    And it's plausible that old stream slugs will have
    be based on stream names that collide with modern
    slugs:
        4-horseman
        411
        2016-election
    If there is any ambiguity about whether a stream slug
    is old or modern, we prefer modern, as long as the integer
    prefix matches a real stream id.  Eventually we will
    stop supporting the legacy slugs, which only matter now
    because people have linked to Zulip threads in things like
    GitHub conversations.  We migrated to modern slugs in
    early 2018.
    */
    const m = /^(\d+)(-.*)?/.exec(slug);
    if (m) {
        const stream_id = Number.parseInt(m[1], 10);
        const sub = subs_by_stream_id.get(stream_id);
        if (sub) {
            return sub.name;
        }
        // if nothing was found above, we try to match on the stream
        // name in the somewhat unlikely event they had a historical
        // link to a stream like 4-horsemen
    }

    /*
    We are dealing with a pre-2018 slug that doesn't have the
    stream id as a prefix.
    */
    return slug;
```
````

I ask about this example in particular because it's not a well-formed slug in the new style, at least as I read the code comment in `slug_to_name` describing the new style (i.e., the new style will either be an integer by itself, or an integer *followed by a dash* followed by a stream name). And I noticed while reviewing a PR for #M4185 that we have a test for a slug that looks like this in the mobile project.

CC @Greg Price

**Chris Bobbe** · 2021-02-08 23:44 UTC

Also CC @Steve Howell (showell), as the author of zulip/zulip@2574efde3.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2021-02-08 23:48 UTC

(As a test, you can see that the web app currently follows https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6something to this stream, since this stream has ID 6.)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-10 13:20 UTC

I think my commit was buggy:

~~~
# this was intended to fail:
> slug = "6something"
'6something'
> m = /^([\d]+)(-.*)?/.exec(slug)
[
  '6',
  '6',
  undefined,
  index: 0,
  input: '6something',
  groups: undefined
]

# normal behavior
> slug = "6-fred"
'6-fred'
> m = /^([\d]+)(-.*)?/.exec(slug)
[
  '6-fred',
  '6',
  '-fred',
  index: 0,
  input: '6-fred',
  groups: undefined
]

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-10 13:25 UTC

I described the policy in the comments as follows:

~~~
    If there is any ambiguity about whether a stream slug
    is old or modern, we prefer modern, as long as the integer
    prefix matches a real stream id

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-10 13:27 UTC

So, technically, there is no ambiguity that "999something" is a **non-modern** slug.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-10 13:35 UTC

@Chris Bobbe See https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/17264

@Jonathan van Clute so, the way Zulip currently hints for this situation is that whatever messages you're looking at will be faded when you're writing a message that goes to a different recipient than the messages you're looking at.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-13 00:24 UTC

After several experiments, we went with this design, because it means the thing you're actually look at looks wrong (as opposed to there being an extra place you need to check), and experimentally that reduced that sort of error (which we call a "mix") more than other options we looked at.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-13 19:14 UTC

Gotcha.  In this case I can see now exactly what confused me.  I was having a PM with a specific person, and that person was also the one who posted in another public topic that I went and read.  So I replied as if I was still in the PM because I saw their name as who I was talking to and everyone else had scrolled off screen.  This is where some kind of color differential would be nice... there would've been no way to mistake that I was talking to the right person, but in the wrong place.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-14 16:19 UTC

@Tim Abbott OK it almost just happened again, and I caught why this time:

First, I was in the "Private Messages" view, which shows me all PMs but highlights whatever one has scrolled past the top or bottom of the screen (there is some very odd logic to this function, that I don't really understand and that doesn't work well, IMO).

Next, I was scrolling down reading the PMs.  I read them all, and wanted to reply to the last one.  Here is where the failure happens...

I hadn't *quite* scrolled far enough for Zulip to decide that the bottom PM was the selected PM.  So when I hit reply, it started to reply to the next-to-last PM (the selected one) instead.  I tend to operate so fast that I almost missed it.  Fortunately the PM I wanted to reply to was with a single person, and the PM is started replying to was a group PM with 3 people, so it jumped out as not looking right.

This has happened to me numerous times, I now realize.  I've always caught it in time thankfully, but this is a poor design IMO.  I'm fairly certain it has bit other members of our community as well because I've seen numerous posts that got deleted, and when I check the delete history it's very clear that the post was meant for somewhere else, either another thread or a PM.  The same thing can very easily happen from the All Messages view, which since it's the default view on launching the Zulip app, I can tell has been an issue.

## Admins should be able to...

*2021-02-18 to 2021-04-05 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Admins.20should.20be.20able.20to.2E.2E.2E/with/1120027)*

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-18 00:31 UTC

As an admin, I feel we should always be able to move posts between streams no matter what.  Currently we can only move posts from public streams, to public streams.  As we keep ALL our streams private, this makes it a huge pain when someone posts something in the wrong stream.  I have to make both streams public, move the topic, then make them private again.  Far less than ideal.  We're admins, we should be able to always move topics.

Additionally it would be nice if admins ad the actual ability to edit posts always instead of only during the lockout period defined for members.  We like to keep it set at 24 hours to edit a post, just so nobody can "rewrite history" long after the fact.  But we often need to edit posts (calendar posts of upcoming weekly events, for example) but we can't, so we have to change the edit lockout period, make the changes, then change it back.  Again we're admins, we should always be able to edit our posts.

Lastly, it would be great if Admins could edit user posts.  Yes this means there is the potential for abuse, but we're admins on a self-hosted Zulip, we could edit the data directly if we *really* wanted to anyway.  I often spot typos or badly worded English (numerous non-native English speakers in our community) and would like to help correct their posts when I see such things, but I can't.  I don't want to ask them to make corrections either publicly or privately as I don't want them to feel "policed" as that's not the intent.  I just want to make their post easier to interpret when it's obvious what they meant to say but just chose the wrong word, forgot a word, etc.

Also not admin related but... there is no "brain" emoji and I wish there was.

:pray:

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-18 00:36 UTC

🧠 is in Unicode, and don’t forget you can add custom emoji.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-18 00:40 UTC

Yeah we just haven't gotten around to trying to add custom emojis yet.  No idea about unicode anything... don't know how you did that but I'll look into it.

**Cyphase** · 2021-02-18 07:30 UTC

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> Additionally it would be nice if admins ad the actual ability to edit posts always instead of only during the lockout period defined for members. ... we have to change the edit lockout period, make the changes, then change it back.

I've used this workaround multiple times as well.

> Lastly, it would be great if Admins could edit user posts. Yes this means there is the potential for abuse, but we're admins on a self-hosted Zulip, we could edit the data directly if we *really* wanted to anyway.

Keep in mind that the set of Zulip admins is not necessarily (at all) a subset of the set of server admins, i.e. people who could edit the database. It would be incorrect to assume that a realm administrator should have as much power as a server admin. That even applies to the "Owner" role.

```
export function do_settings_change(request_method, url, data, status_element, opts) {
    const spinner = $(status_element).expectOne();
    spinner.fadeTo(0, 1);
    loading.make_indicator(spinner, {text: strings.saving});
    let success_msg;
    let success_continuation;
    let error_continuation;
    let remove_after = 1000;
    const appear_after = 500;

    if (opts !== undefined) {
        success_msg = opts.success_msg;
        success_continuation = opts.success_continuation;
        error_continuation = opts.error_continuation;
        if (opts.sticky) {
            remove_after = null;
        }
    }
    if (success_msg === undefined) {
        success_msg = strings.success;
    }

    request_method({
        url,
        data,
        success(reponse_data) {
            setTimeout(() => {
                ui_report.success(success_msg, spinner, remove_after);
                display_checkmark(spinner);
            }, appear_after);
            if (success_continuation !== undefined) {
                if (opts !== undefined && opts.success_continuation_arg) {
                    success_continuation(opts.success_continuation_arg);
                } else {
                    success_continuation(reponse_data);
                }
            }
        },
        error(xhr) {
            if (opts !== undefined && opts.error_msg_element) {
                loading.destroy_indicator(spinner);
                ui_report.error(strings.failure, xhr, opts.error_msg_element);
            } else {
                ui_report.error(strings.failure, xhr, spinner);
            }
            if (error_continuation !== undefined) {
                error_continuation(xhr);
            }
        },
    });
}
```

**Sanchit Gupta (pilgrim2308)** · 2021-02-22 15:48 UTC

If a user has muted a particular stream, the unread count for that stream is still visible and that may seem a bit disorienting. I thought we could add a feature where the user can disable the unread count display, which would be visible only when the user clicks that stream.

The main concern here was probably around how to handle mentions. 
I think we can show the user has been mentioned the way @Tim Abbott  suggested (using a `!` or similar) but that should serve only to inform the user that they have been mentioned, and they can hence check it out from the `mentions` tab. **Sanchit Gupta (pilgrim2308)** · 2021-02-23 17:35 UTC

> I think we can show the user has been mentioned the way @Tim Abbott suggested (using a `!` or similar) but that should serve only to inform the user that they have been mentioned, and they can hence check it out from the `mentions` tab. If the user clicks on the muted stream then it should remov …

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-23 21:07 UTC

Ohh. Can I ask why that is? :sweat_smile:

**Steve Howell** · 2021-02-24 10:34 UTC

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-25 00:13 UTC

For comparison, zulip-terminal currently shows an `M` instead of the count. I see the appeal of observing how busy a stream is, but ultimately if it's muted then the count is something I'm not interested in. **Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-01 23:48 UTC

We've heard this feature request like 5 times from different people in the Rust community -- I think because they have a way of using Zulip that involves muting like 90% of streams.  And I think it's structurally pretty reasonable -- if you're mentioned on a muted stream, you may not see the mention.  

I'm personally just finishing ending a 4-month period where I had 20-50 unread mentions at all times because I get a lot of unnecessary mentions, but it'd have been useful to see what streams/topics had mentions when thinking about where to prioritize my reading.

## Admin can't subscribe myself??

*2021-02-24 to 2021-03-15 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Admin.20can.27t.20subscribe.20myself.3F.3F/with/1123041)*

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-24 01:20 UTC

I just accidentally clicked in the wrong place, and just like that I was unsubscribed from one of our streams.  Since all our streams are private, I now am unable to re-subscribe myself!

This seems like total madness to me.  I'm an admin.  How on earth do I not have full, unfettered privileges?  How am I supposed to get re-subscribed?  Am I stuck waiting until I can get ahold of one of my two fellow admins to have them re-add me?  This seems like a huge oversight in the way permissions are handled.  I hope there's some other workaround, it was incredibly easy to do this by accident... no confirmation first, nothing.  One click and that's it, I'm locked out.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-24 01:33 UTC

Oh and to add to this, I originally created this stream in the first place.  It really makes no sense that I could be unable to add myself back again.

**Sahil Batra** · 2021-02-24 04:43 UTC

Yes for private streams, only an existing member of the stream can resubscribe you.

And there is an open PR for adding confirmation modal for unsubscribing from private streams. I hope this will be merged soon.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-02-26 02:27 UTC

That's good to know it's in the pipeline.  Still however, it seems like an admin should always be able to do whatever with any stream.  There should be no such thing as a stream that is private to a true admin.  Maybe there needs to be multiple levels of admin.  Like "Sysop" who is effectively "God" on the server, and "Admin" who has the current admin rights.  Was very weird to, as an Admin, be unable to re-invite myself to a stream I created.

**Pat Roam** · 2021-03-04 04:58 UTC

God aka Dba. I’m still pretty new to this community but probably wouldn’t hurt to dig around in the database for a solution.. after you back it up.

**Greg Price** · 2021-03-04 08:58 UTC

(replying to Jonathan van Clute)
> That's good to know it's in the pipeline. Still however, it seems like an admin should always be able to do whatever with any stream. There should be no such thing as a stream that is private to a true admin. Maybe there needs to be multiple levels of admin. Like "Sysop" who is effectively "God" on …

For a lot of communities, it's important for privacy that if I'm talking to you in a private stream, it really is private, and not open for any of the admins to just barge into at any time and see what we've been saying. Private means that the content can only be shared if someone who already has access to the content decides to share it. Here's what we say [in our docs](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/security-model.html#users-and-bots):
> Owners and administrators have the ability to deactivate and reactivate other human and bot users, delete streams, add/remove administrator privileges, as well as change configuration for the organization.
>
> Being an organization administrator does not generally provide the ability to read other users’ private messages or messages sent to private streams to which the administrator is not subscribed. There are two exceptions: [one that applies only to corporate customers in Zulip Cloud; and one that involves the admin subverting a bot, if there's already a bot in the stream.]

**Greg Price** · 2021-03-04 08:59 UTC

In particular, in a lot of open communities -- like for open-source projects -- it would not feel right for a person who's serving as an admin to have the ability to go read messages that weren't public and weren't shared with them. The admins in those communities are more like a host, facilitating a place to meet and talk, and not like a boss or "god". So for that reason, I think it's important that the default for a Zulip community is that private means private, and admins can't breach it.

**Greg Price** · 2021-03-04 09:12 UTC

It probably would make sense to have a product feature where for a given organization, the owners have super-admin powers to bypass privacy protections and do things like add themselves to a private stream. In a corporate environment, people generally expect that nothing is actually private if the corporate IT team (or HR or legal or upper management, working through corporate IT) is determined to see it. And as mentioned above, it's already the case for corporate customers on Zulip Cloud that they can ultimately get their hands on the data by requesting an export.

And of course outside Zulip Cloud, the org owners/admins are typically the same people who run the server and can do arbitrary things with the database directly.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-05 17:24 UTC

We actually have a field called `Realm.org_type` that has the two values of "COMMUNITY" and "CORPORATE".  I am not sure how often we actually take advantage of these in our codebase, but I remember the original intentions behind them.  I would propose for these types of issues, if we get to a place where corporate admins have different forces than community admins, then we should possibly take note of the flag.

**Jonathan van Clute** · 2021-03-14 05:22 UTC

This seems like it shouldn't even be possible, since I created it originally and am an admin as well.  Maybe there should at least be a confirmation of some sort of unsubscribing from a stream.  It was just a slip of the mouse which did it and once it was done, that was that.  Fortunately I was able to ask one of my partners, also an admin, to re-add me.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-15 05:30 UTC

We're definitely planning to add a confirmation dialog to make it hard to accidentally leave (like we do for other actions without an undo button).

## webpack development bug

*2021-03-05 to 2021-03-11 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/webpack.20development.20bug/with/1127386)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-05 00:40 UTC

I started seeing this when saving files today:
```
RuntimeError: abort(Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '/home/tabbott/zulip/static/styles/.#zulip.css'). Build with -s ASSERTIONS=1 for more info.
    at process.abort (/srv/zulip-npm-cache/d9a07716531e5201d07fd174980ef7b3af306cd8/node_modules/@vusion/webfonts-generator/node_modules/ttf2woff2/jssrc/ttf2woff2.js:1:10832)
    at process.emit (events.js:315:20)
    at process.EventEmitter.emit (domain.js:467:12)
    at process.emit (/srv/zulip-npm-cache/d9a07716531e5201d07fd174980ef7b3af306cd8/node_modules/source-map-support/source-map-support.js:495:21)
    at processPromiseRejections (internal/process/promises.js:245:33)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:32)
```

My guess is this is some sort of webpack-dev-server issue with emacs backup files. (Though I thought I'd configured those to be saved in a separate tree, so I'm a bit confused why this affects me).  New today, though maybe I'd have missed it if it had appeared earlier this week.

@Anders Kaseorg FYI since we just upgraded a lot of dependencies.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-05 05:04 UTC

`.#zulip.css` is a [file lock](http://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/File-Locks.html), not a backup. It’s implemented as an intentionally broken symlink, which confuses tools written by the kinds of whippersnappers who eschew using LISP machines as editors in favor of using *entire web browsers* as editors. I’ve seen issues like that before, but never so fatal, and it’s weird that it’s happening inside webfonts-generator… One workaround would be to customize `create-lockfiles` to `nil`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-05 06:31 UTC

Opened https://github.com/nfroidure/ttf2woff2/pull/64 to make it less fatal again. The underlying problem is https://github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-server/issues/2821, which upstream indicates can only be fixed by upgrading to webpack 5. My previous work toward that (#16653) was blocked on waiting for django-webpack-loader to come back from the dead, but that may not be happening, so it might need a different strategy.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-05 06:51 UTC

Hrm, yeah, that looks stuck in a fairly persistent way.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-11 21:32 UTC

I found a workaround: #17575

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-11 23:51 UTC

Yay, thanks!

## cyclical dependencies

*2021-03-16 to 2023-03-14 · 161 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/cyclical.20dependencies/with/1133670)*

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-16 17:52 UTC

Continuing the conversation from https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/92-learning/topic/Node.20tests.20for.20clear.20search.20buttons/near/1132203 I wonder how we want to set up singletons on the frontend such as BuddyList?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-16 17:52 UTC

For testing purposes we want access to the class, so we can re-instantiate the class in each test to avoid state leaking between tests.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-16 17:53 UTC

But the webapp clearly wants a singleton for certain things.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-16 17:55 UTC

We have some classes like `Filter` that **aren't** singletons, and they are fairly pleasant to test.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-16 18:02 UTC

Our singletons basically come in two flavors:
* we have module-level singletons like `people.js` and `stream_data.js` and `unread.js`
* we have things like `BuddyList` and `RecentPrivateMessages` that are true syntactic classes that are singletons

I think most of our remaining pseudoclasses are non-singletons.

I’ll preface this by proposing that, although BuddyList is an existing class, we may want to hold off on building lots of new singleton classes until we have TypeScript, since it might make it harder to understand our control flow. The basic questions one asks a lot to understand unfamiliar code are “given a function definition, where are its call sites?” and “given a call site, where is the function defined?”. TypeScript is great for that, but singleton classes add some extra indirection over modules, especially if those singleton classes start being constructed from other singleton classes and so on.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-03-18 14:45 UTC

Python and JS both have the pattern where a module-based singleton can be turned into a proper class that you instantiate as a singleton, and both languages share the annoying property that you have to re-indent all the code for the diff.  Not the end of the world, just annoying.  And then JS throws in the annoying use of `this`, but the pitfalls of `this` don't really apply to data-based modules, so that's not the end of the world either.  I personally don't have a huge problem with module-based singletons, but I can certainly understand the viewpoint that classes are more tidy.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-18 20:36 UTC

Speaking of delegation, here’s a possible pattern for dealing with circularity in classes if there are cases where that’s what we really need:

```ts
// outer.ts
import {Foo} from "./foo";
import {Bar} from "./bar";
export class Outer {
  foo = new Foo(this);
  bar = new Bar(this);
}
```

```ts
// foo.ts
import type {Outer} from "./outer";
export class Foo {
  outer: Outer;
  constructor(outer: Outer) {
    this.outer = outer;
  }
  foo(): void {
    console.log("foo");
  }
  use_bar(): void {
    this.outer.bar.bar();
  }
}
```

```ts
// bar.ts
import type {Outer} from "./outer";
export class Bar {
  outer: Outer;
  constructor(outer: Outer) {
    this.outer = outer;
  }
  bar(): void {
    console.log("bar");
  }
  use_foo(): void {
    this.outer.foo.foo();
  }
}
```

(`import type` is a TypeScript feature that does not cause an `import` at runtime.)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-18 20:44 UTC

(It comes with the usual caveats about circularity, namely that `outer.bar` isn’t initialized yet in the `Foo` constructor, and that circularity makes it hard for humans to find a starting point for understanding an unfamiliar system.)

**Akshat** · 2021-03-18 15:58 UTC

Right now, we can use the `copy and close` button when message editing time has passed. But that button doesn't appear when we can edit the messages sent.

**Akshat** · 2021-03-18 16:02 UTC

Adding the `copy and close` button to the message **edit** area (or `textarea`) can help in general and also to those organisations who have set `Allow message editing` to `Any time`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-18 22:41 UTC

@Akshat (akshatdalton) I'm not sure I understand the question?

**Akshat** · 2021-03-18 23:00 UTC

Right now, when you click on `view source`, you can copy the message content by clicking on `copy and close` button.
But `view source` button doesn't appear unless editing time has passed for the message.
When we edit a message, there is no `copy and close` button to copy the message content.
So, in that case, user has to select the message content and do `Ctrl + C` & `Ctrl + V` to copy & paste the message content.
This thing continues to be there for them who have set their org settings: `Allow message editing` to `Any time`. I.e., for them view source option never appears and hence `copy and close` button would never be there.
So in such a case, we should add the `copy and close` button.

## Markdown dynamic elements

*2021-03-29 to 2022-02-22 · 44 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Markdown.20dynamic.20elements/with/1146602)*

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-29 12:38 UTC

@Tim Abbott 
I went through this [issue #16029](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16029) more deeply, and tried calling `update_elements` in `rendered_markdown.js` after they are appended in drafts_table (because `update_elements` expects `JQuery<HTMLElement>`) and was successfully able to do that but for dynamic elements it does not updates them, so probably this nullifies the benefit of what we are trying to achieves by calling rendered_markdown.js.
(Like I tested by changing few user names after I had their mentions in drafts, but changing the name breaks the mention and it is renders as normal text.)
I think that is the reason you suggested to update them before they are inserted to dom. But I had some doubts regarding this that as we are currently applying markdown every time drafts overlay is shown so how to ensure that a mention is correct(after its name is changed), or a particular stream was mentioned once it's name is changed etc. (similar thoughts in edit history).

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-29 12:51 UTC

I had thought of another way and wanted to discuss about it. Currently drafts are stored as raw text and markdown is applied every time drafts are rendered, which is the reason for above problem. If we store frontend rendered content of the drafts with them while storing/updating them, and then call `rendered_markdown` before showing drafts overlay.  This way dynamic elements could be rendered  more efficiently.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-29 16:46 UTC

I don't think we want to plan to have the markdown processor run 100x when opening the browser (i.e. render all of them on startup) as that could consume nontrivial time if you have more than 100 of them.  I suppose we could store the rendering in local storage, but I think that's probably complexity we don't want in the system.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-29 20:49 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I suppose we could store the rendering in local storage, but I think that's probably complexity we don't want in the system.
Actually `update_elements` in `rendered_markdown.js` expects `JQuery<HTMLElement>`, for updating elements so I thought storing rendered content would save us from re-renderring  the content every time drafts are opened(which we do currently do). We will need to pass the content through markdown.js (only during edits and when it is created) and we can directly append that rendered content to draft table when overlay is opened. Would that be a good qualifier for including rendered content while storing drafts. Please correct me if I am thinking about this too locally. Will it increase complexity in handling edit history, as I was first solving drafts part and didn't go to edit history side much now.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-29 20:52 UTC

(Renamed from #**mobile>LaTeX long equations gets cut off**.) This isn’t related to #**mobile**, right?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-29 21:39 UTC

Correct, this belongs in #**frontend**.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-30 20:12 UTC

Looks like I am blocked on this :smile: .
Can I please get some suggestions to continue on it, also can this topic be moved to #**frontend** if possible.
To summarize previous discussion, we wanted to our drafts content to pass through `rendered_markdown.js` to render dynamic elements with consistency, for which I see there are two possible ways:
1.  currently we store raw content(with `content` as key) in drafts and before before showing drafts overlay we pass it through`markdown.js` and append in the draft table and then show the overlay. So, with this method we can pass it through `rendered_markdown.js` after appending to draft table or just before showing overlay. But it has disadvantages like it does not give any benefit of using `rendered_markdown.js` for dynamic elements like mentions, stream mentions because in this method we are passing content through the markdown every time before showing the overlay so if name changes later on then  on passing through markdown it will not be considered as a valid mention  so passing it through `rendered_markdown.js` will not update the name. 
2. Another way is to store rendered markdown content once when draft is saved initially and then before showing the drafts overlay pass it through `rendered_markdown.js` this overcomes the problem faced in point 1 about breaking of most of the dynamic elements.

I would also try to implement any other suggestions I get for this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-31 00:10 UTC

I don't think I understand the downside with that first approach, which seems simplest.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-31 12:57 UTC

Hmm, I'll try to explain it a bit, like before showing the drafts overlay all the drafts are passed through the frontend markdown processor(`markdown.js`) after which they are appended in the draft_table(thus dom) and overlay is shown. This happens every time one tries to open the drafts overlay. So suppose a draft contains a mention(dynamic element) `@aaron` so every time on going through `markdown.js` this gets converted to 
`<span class="user-mention" data-user-id="6">@aaron</span>` to get rendered as a mention.

Now in this issue we want to pass our draft content through `rendered_markdown.js` so that we can support dynamic elements if they change later on(for example: if `aaron` changes name from `aaron(changed)`) then in drafts overlay his updated name should be shown in mention. But in first approach what we are doing is that we are passing our raw content through markdown processor(`markdown.js`) every time one opens drafts overlay so if name changes later on then `@aaron` will be treated as an invalid mention and will not get converted to:
`<span class="user-mention" data-user-id="6">@aaron</span>` or `<span class="user-mention" data-user-id="6">@aaron(changed)</span>` 
so passing through `renderred_markdown.js` will not give any benefits because what `renderred_markdown.js` does to update things like this is that it uses id in `data-user-id` attribute to fetch the user and thus updates `<span class="user-mention" data-user-id="6">@aaron</span>` with
`<span class="user-mention" data-user-id="6">@CHANGED USER NAME</span>`. But as frontend markdown processor sends `@aaron(changed)` after the name is changed `rendered_markdown.js` is not able to update it and its benefits are nullified. Similarly for other type of elements.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-03-31 13:10 UTC

So this can be fixed if we initialize ClipboardJS  for code blocks in following manner:
* Include a codeblock_container parameter in `rendered_markdown.update_elements`.
* and then initialize it  like:
```javascript
let clipboard = codeblock_container
            ? new ClipboardJS(copy_button[0], {
                  text(copy_element) {
                      return $(copy_element).siblings("code").text();
                  },
                  container: document.querySelector(codeblock_container),
              })
            : new ClipboardJS(copy_button[0], {
                  text(copy_element) {
                      return $(copy_element).siblings("code").text();
                  },
              });
```

it appears that root cause for the issue when using bootstrap is:
> The root cause is that the Bootstrap modal backdrop keeps the fakeElem from getting focused normally.

**Reason in our case:**
It is similar in our case too, ClipboardJS [creates fake textarea](https://github.com/zenorocha/clipboard.js/blob/734d36b6ffe3346304904a44f12e4f3f69330101/src/clipboard-action.js#L35) and focuses it but bootstrap modal backdrop does not allows any fake element to get focussed so ClipboardJS fails to copy.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-04-20 15:06 UTC

overlays.js has code for handling opening and closing of both overlays and modals, I guess you wanted me to answer "How using overlays here is a workaround".
Overlays are our custom components which do not use any extra backdrop component like bootstrap modals to stop interaction from background elements. They just have width and height of 100% which keeps the focus in them, means there is nothing special js code in our overlays apart from opening and closing(and some occasional content specific click handlers). In other words are just handled by using appropriate background color and z-index so they are like any other element whose display can be toggled while modal first creates a backdrop element which prevents any events/interactions from background element and then opens modal over that backdrop.
I think it is possible to achieve role of backdrop in overlays because of focus property like any other html element.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-04-20 19:10 UTC

May be in short, modal backdrop was responsible for it, as it removed focus from the created element(by clipboardJS)  in order to keep focus in the modal. As overlays use CSS for creating backdrop effect, clipboardJS works well with overlays.

We have a new module that contains these three functions that help folks deal with scrolling containers:

~~~
  1 import $ from "jquery";
  2 import SimpleBar from "simplebar/dist/simplebar";
  3
  4 export function get_content_element(element_selector) {
  5     const element = element_selector.expectOne()[0];
  6     const sb = SimpleBar.instances.get(element);
  7     if (sb) {
  8         return $(sb.getContentElement());
  9     }
 10     return element_selector;
 11 }
 12
 13 export function get_scroll_element(element_selector) {
 14     const element = element_selector.expectOne()[0];
 15     const sb = SimpleBar.instances.get(element);
 16     if (sb) {
 17         return $(sb.getScrollElement());
 18     } else if ("simplebar" in element.dataset) {
 19         // The SimpleBar mutation observer hasn’t processed this element yet.
 20         // Create the SimpleBar early in case we need to add event listeners.
 21         return $(new SimpleBar(element).getScrollElement());
 22     }
 23     return element_selector;
 24 }
 25
 26 export function reset_scrollbar(element_selector) {
 27     const element = element_selector.expectOne()[0];
 28     const sb = SimpleBar.instances.get(element);
 29     if (sb) {
 30         sb.getScrollElement().scrollTop = 0;
 31     } else {
 32         element.scrollTop = 0;
 33     }
 34 }
