## fetching message history

*2022-04-01 to 2024-06-25 · 147 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/fetching.20message.20history/with/1358272)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 20:55 UTC

So I'd like to start a discussion one of one more messy pieces of legacy code, namely the way that we fetch the data that populates Recent Topics and the `all_messages` view in the web application (and a few other things).

To start with the backstory, the early design of Zulip's message fetching system that we still used at the end of 2014 worked as follows:
* We'd fetch your `pointer` message, which was basically the cursor for the last message you'd read in the "All messages" view, and 200 messages before and after. Another 1000 before would be fetched once that returned.
* A loop would fetch messages forward from that point until it got to the latest messages.
* Once it had done so, we had all your unread messages cached locally in the browser, and thus could do things like display unread counts.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:00 UTC

The current implementation is substantially refined from that:
* A `pointer` no longer exists; we use the `anchor="first_unread"` parameter when fetching blocks of messages from the server (E.g. to display a topic where we don't already have enough of the topic's full message history in the local message cache).
* We fetch unread message data in /api/register-queue, and thus that information is immediately available on page load, independent of what fully messages we have in our local cache.
* However, we still do essentially the same loop described above, where we fetch all the message history between the user's oldest non-muted unread message and the latest messages (which is potentially 10Ks of messages!) into the local cache in a loop.
* We do an additional bonus query for just the latest messages, which is important to have "Recent topics" work at all as a homepage.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:06 UTC

This algorithm creates multiple problems:
* We do a very large number of `GET /messages` queries, potentially totally 100K or more messages, for users in busy organizations who have years-old unread messages. This effect is the primary thing contributing to the potential thundering herd issues when restarting a production Zulip server. (We have mostly addressed that class of problem through other techniques, but it'd be nice to just do less work).  The positive side of fetching so much history into your local cache is that whatever topics you're likely to click on are already in cache, leading to very fast loading times. Ideally whatever solution we select here will try to preserve that fast loading time experience.
* Any data sets that are based on this "cached message history" data structure exhibit odd behavior while this backfill operation is running, largely because of the oldest-first ordering of this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:11 UTC

Going deeper into the data set problem, some places where we use data from "all messages in local cache" are quite subtle, e.g. typeahead sorting of other users, but there's a couple that are pretty visible:
* The loop through which we fetch messages into the browser's local cache starts with the oldest messages. As a result, if you scroll far enough down in "Recent topics" to get past the 400 most recent messages in unmuted topics (which of course could be easily visible above the fold or not depending on how many distinct topics are included in those 400 messages) while this loop is running, you'll see that (say) your 23rd most recent topic is continuously changing as each block of 1000 messages is fetched from the server, and there's a weird time gap between the 23rd topic (which will be dated roughly 400 messages ago in time) and the 24th topic (which will be dated wherever we're at in this backfill loop, potentially 2 months ago and decreasing with each batch of 1000 messages fetched from the server).
* You'll see the same thing if you click into a stream with little recent history, because the list of recent topics within a stream that we display when you click into it and have not yet clicked "more topics" is also based on this "All messages" data set, and thus potentially if only the first two topics have recent messages, you'll see the other 3 in that block shifting between various groups of "what 3 topics were most recent at time X" for a time X that iterates towards now with each batch of messages.
* Because "Recent topics" does not yet have its own functionality to fetch additional message history when you get to the bottom of it, one cannot clearly explain to users what topics are there (it may be the last 2 days or the last 6 months depending on the seemingly irrelevant variable of whether you're clearing your unread messages).

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:12 UTC

This is a little bit of a tangly problem, and so I'd like to talk about a few potential directions for how we can move forward here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:14 UTC

There's two high-level directions here: Improving how we backfill message history into the client cache, and arranging to not need to do so.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:18 UTC

For improving how we do the backfill (while still ending up with the same data), I think that the simplest thing we can do is changing the order of the backfill to fetch the newest messages first, and continue the backfill until we've included the oldest unmuted unread message (which we can determine from the independent `unread_msgs` data set that we have in the client). This would eliminate both of the "during loading time" user experience artifacts that I mentioned above, in that one would instead just have additional older data appearing over time, which is a much more reasonable experience than "Newest topics, followed by some of the oldest, and we're filling in the topics in between oldest-first".

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:21 UTC

That change would have some hard-to-model effect on the performance of clicking on topics during the first few minutes after loading a page for users whose oldest unread is 100K messages ago, but I think nothing that would be worth blocking such a change on. (Basically, viewing a topic that's new would be more likely to be in cache  than a topic that's temporally around your oldest unmuted unread message, which is probably an improvement).

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:24 UTC

So I think sequencing-wise, that change has relatively few dependencies. That change is likely more tricky than in might seem, because it's very possible that we implicitly assume in the "All messages" view rendering logic that we'll always have the oldest unread message in that view in cache. Likely what this means concretely is making "All messages" no longer a special view in terms of how it's implemented. But it's possible that doing #16697 first would let us avoid such a refactor.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:31 UTC

If we want to go further and actually stop doing this expensive loop to fetch message history, we'll need to look at the following:
* Do an audit of all the frontend data structures that use the "All messages` data to make sure the below is appropriately exhaustive. The core question we'll be asking in this audit is "If we replaced the rule that fill our local message cache all the way back to the user's oldest unread message with a more rational rule, like the most recent N unmuted messages, would this feature's behavior regress?". 
* Make some changes directed towards the goal of making removing this cache not materially affect the performance of switching views in Zulip.  Perhaps the most significant thing that we can do is caching the `message_list_data` objects from individual narrows, so that visiting a view you've been to before in the current session is fast. This is #15131, which also has independent benefit of just making things faster in cases where our current implementation (E.g. you're repeating switching back and forth between two conversations that both contain history older than your oldest unread message). 
* For the places where we display some version of all topics by recency and currently avoid independently querying the server for full data (E.g. we fetch all historical topics in a stream via /api/get-stream-topics when you click "more topics", but not when you just view a stream, because it's a fairly expensive query), we'll want to determine whether we need to start using /api/get-stream-topics for those features (possibly with the addition of new server-side optimizations or caches for the data).

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-01 21:35 UTC

Not having done that audit, my suspicion is that "Recent topics" and the pre-"more topics" display of topics in the left sidebar are likely to be the primary two features affected here. Various other feature use this data -- e.g. the mention typeahead uses your local cache to look at who has posted in the topic/stream/organization recently as an input to its sort order, and that will of course be a bit better if we have 100K messages of history than if we have 2K (plus 100 in the current topic itself) ... but probably it'd be a pretty subtle effect and clearly unable to justify caching the 100K messages of history.

@Tim Abbott is this roughly what you have in mind?

```js

export function initialize(finished_initial_fetch) {
    // get the initial message list
    function load_more(data) {
        // See server_events.js for this callback.
        // Start processing server events.
        finished_initial_fetch();

        if (data.found_oldest) {
            return;
        }

        if (all_messages_data.num_items() >= MAX_INITIAL_BACKFILL_SIZE) {
            start_backfilling_messages();
            return;
        }

        // If we fall through here, we need to keep fetching more data, and
        // we'll call back to the function we're in.
        //
        // But we do it with a bit of delay, to reduce risk that we
        // hit rate limits with these backfills.
        const oldest_id = data.messages.at(0).id;
        setTimeout(() => {
            load_messages({
                anchor: oldest_id,
                num_before: consts.catch_up_batch_size,
                num_after: 0,
                msg_list_data: all_messages_data,
                cont: load_more,
            });
        }, consts.catch_up_backfill_delay);
    }

    load_messages({
        anchor: "newest",
        num_before: consts.initial_backfill_fetch_size,
        num_after: 0,
        msg_list_data: all_messages_data,
        cont: load_more,
    });
}

```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-04-25 20:18 UTC

To talk a bit more about how the system works now, it's certainly a more normal algorithm but could certainly be tuned:
- We do an initial fetch of 400 messages.
- After that, we loop, fetching 1k messages at a time, until a maximum of 4k messages. I assume that means you end up with 4400, but haven't double-checked... This detail seems a bit odd.
- For me, that set of messages is about 9 days of chat.zulip.org traffic, based on just looking at the bottom of "recent conversations". We could consider doing an adaptive algorithm that stopped at 2k messages if that was at least 1 month of your history, but it might not make much difference in practice.

This preloaded/cached message history is used for a several things:
- It's the data set for "Recent conversations" and for displaying non-unread topics in the left sidebar for streams where one has not fetched the full topic history for that stream (via clicking more topics, or several other hooks, like trying to autocomplete a topic within a stream). It would probably be a good idea to look at that algorithm -- it might be that we can easily tell when we don't have enough topics in our recent history but more probably exist, and ask the server.
- Data on who's sent messages recently -- used in sorting matches for `@`-mention typeahead for matches that are more likely to be relevant.
- Optimizing the experience of visiting views; we can locally load (without waiting for the network) any views/conversations where all the messages that would appear onscreen are present in our cache.

- We increase the base numbers for how much to fetch along the lines of some hybrid of https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/fetching.20message.20history/near/1787968 and https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/fetching.20message.20history/near/1787997.
- We make the "load more" button in "Recent conversations" not do a single fetch, but instead do fetching in a loop until it's hit some much higher tier of how much data we have -- maybe stopping at your oldest unread message (aka the previous definition) or 50k messages fetched, whichever is more data -- to give a way for folks who want it to access the preexisting level of data without like 100 clicks.

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-25 04:30 UTC

FWIW I think it is likely that the change discussed in this thread has effectively caused a regression in that issue #30530, in that it's caused significantly more users to experience it than before.

That's because if you take a simple model of a channel's lifecycle where it comes into use; it's used regularly for a while; and then it stops being used, then
* the old way of fetching history, starting from some point in the past and then filling in toward the present, will always get its final answer for "is this channel inactive" from the very first fetch;
* but the new way, starting from the present and working back through time until some point in the past, will start out by considering a lot of channels inactive that it later decides are active, as it reaches the time when they fell out of use.

Real-world usage is more complicated than that, but I think it has enough resemblance to that model that the model probably points in the right direction for this effect.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 16:59 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:14 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> FWIW I think it is likely that the change discussed in this thread has effectively caused a regression in that issue [#30530](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/30530), in that it's caused significantly more users to experience it than before.

I don't think this analysis is correct; I think we just permuted which streams/users are affected. The previous model would fetch 1000 messages at a time starting from an arbitrary point that is 0-30 months ago, depending on when your oldest unread unmuted message is.

While streams that were active for a long time but then fell into disuse are more likely to show up in a slice of messages from 7 months ago, new streams since then are more likely to show up in a slice starting from now. And in both cases, a stream that was active for 3 weeks about 4 months ago is going to show up after dozens of fetches.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:17 UTC

But from the standpoint of what to do, the symptom is bad and we should figure out how to purge it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:18 UTC

Oh, actually there is a detail that probably explains how this might be significant worse following our changes.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:19 UTC

The previous algorithm was the following:
- Load the last 1k messages (to make the Recent view not totally broken).
- In parallel, load in a loop starting from "oldest unmuted unread" until we get to the current.

And that algorithm meant that we'd have early samples of both the old end and the new end of the range we're going to process.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:20 UTC

So previously, both currently active channels, and channels that were highly active around that random first unread point would be immediately accurate, but a channel only active in the middle would not.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:22 UTC

So we could probably do a hacky workaround of fetching messages around some point in history, if we didn't find it feasible to invest in a proper fix in a timely fashion, to avoid a regression on this detail.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:25 UTC

I think there's probably a better hack available, though:
- We could have the left sidebar not attempt to demote streams for inactivity until its finished its initial fetching process (after 1 minute), such that the failure mode is that inactive streams appear in the left sidebar in their alphabetical position for the first minute before disappearing into the bottom.

This would avoid the annoying loading experience, at the cost of having the setting be ineffective at simplifying your sidebar during the first 30 seconds of loading the app.

## CSS pain

*2022-04-04 to 2022-04-05 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/CSS.20pain/with/1359696)*

**Steve Howell** · 2022-04-04 18:37 UTC

Some of our core team folks were on a call today, and I think we have a plan that can possibly reduce the pain from our current CSS implementation.  I believe the first steps are these:

* have our portico system use its own copy of bootstrap CSS, so that we can make forward progress on the main app without risk of breaking the portico pages
* remove any low-hanging-fruit uses of bootstrap JS
* try to remove the use of bootstrap CSS from the main app, particularly any CSS that affects all elements
* where possible, remove bootstrap CSS in general, even if it involves somewhat janky workarounds like subsuming a few key rules into the Zulip CSS
* once the dust settles, do a serious investigation into Tailwind

Folks who were on the call should feel free to clarify, but that was my basic takeaway.  Even if I am off on a few details, I am very excited about this plan.

## mark-as-read-turned-off banner

*2022-04-04 to 2022-04-04 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/mark-as-read-turned-off.20banner/with/1360042)*

**Evy** · 2022-04-04 22:58 UTC

Hi! Update on making the x button work for this banner (#21595). I made it so that the x hides the banner, but then some logic makes it show up again! :upside_down: 

The two places we show the banner are:

(1) as you scroll past messages

```
// Scroll handler that marks messages as read when you scroll past them.
    $(document).on("message_selected.zulip", (event) => {
        if (event.id === -1) {
            return;
        }

        if (event.mark_read && event.previously_selected_id !== -1) {
            // Mark messages between old pointer and new pointer as read
            let messages;
            if (event.id < event.previously_selected_id) {
                messages = event.msg_list.message_range(event.id, event.previously_selected_id);
            } else {
                messages = event.msg_list.message_range(event.previously_selected_id, event.id);
            }
            if (event.msg_list.can_mark_messages_read()) {
                unread_ops.notify_server_messages_read(messages, {from: "pointer"});
            } else if (
                unread.get_unread_messages(messages).length !== 0 &&
                // The below checks might seem redundant, but it's
                // possible this logic, which runs after a delay, lost
                // a race with switching to another view, like Recent
                // Topics, and we don't want to displ[ay this banner
                // in such a view.
                //
                // This can likely be fixed more cleanly with another approach.
                narrow_state.filter() !== undefined &&
                message_lists.current === event.msg_list
            ) {
                unread_ui.notify_messages_remain_unread();
            }
        }
    });
```

(2) on scroll to bottom

```
export function process_scrolled_to_bottom() {
    if (message_lists.current.can_mark_messages_read()) {
        mark_current_list_as_read();
        return;
    }

    // For message lists that don't support marking messages as read
    // automatically, we display a banner offering to let you mark
    // them as read manually, only if there are unreads present.
    if (message_lists.current.has_unread_messages()) {
        unread_ui.notify_messages_remain_unread();
    }
}
```

I can think of two ways forwards:

* Store some state that the user has hid the banner, and keep that state until they leave the current narrow. Use that state to prevent the banner from being shown.
* Change the location of the logic that shows the banner, such that it only shows on the initial load of the narrow.

Neither options seem trivial. I'm not familiar enough with the code around here to know if one of these paths will be more fruitful than the other, so I wanted to ask if anyone has advice on how to move foward. Thanks :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-04 23:50 UTC

I think the current behavior that the notice appears in situations when you might have marked something as read seems potentially correct, so I don't think we want to change that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-04 23:51 UTC

But it would be relatively straightforward to add a variable for `user_hid_mark_as_read` or some better name that gets cleared by a call from `narrow.activate/deactivate`.

## EM vs PX

*2022-04-06 to 2022-04-11 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/EM.20vs.20PX/with/1360989)*

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-04-06 04:53 UTC

Hey guys @Anders Kaseorg expressed some good thoughts in [his draft about css](https://paper.dropbox.com/doc/CSS-considerations-for-redesign--BfGGjRO9K5Jpafpvt8hiAOyXAg-4zHfwj8aaTnYK2d8ZUW3W). One of the ideas is to use em instead of px usage.
Could you help me to understand the benefit of that?

Do we want to support cascading em across the whole Zulip app?

Yes sometimes is convenient to calculate anything from your font size of the current element you are in... but I don't see how it is the case for Zulip, when in the redesign we have precise pixel sizes for things and it's hard to tell to which font-size do they correspond.

For example the message font-size would be 15px and line-height is 19px. Why should somebody define line-height in em? To automatically scale that if the font-size changes? Well, we don't want automatic scale in this case and nobody can change the line-height value easily in the Zulip codebase.

Are we preparing a feature where a user can increase the font-size in settings and have everything automatically adapted? Keep in mind that browser zoom works fine.

The only case I could think of is supporting browser feature to increase font-size for a user. In this case we have to define body em size as % from whatever browser has (usually 16px). Right now Zulip defines body font-size as 14px.

I personally don't think we should run with em everywhere. Defining size in px is no more trouble than em. Browser zoom works fine. If we want a feature where people change their font-size we would need to think about what exactly would change and how and be precise about it.

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-04-06 04:56 UTC

the alternative could be to define body-size as 10px. In this case em (when font-size isn't defined) would be easily calculable. But as soon as some parent div redefines the font-size... there might be a problem

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-04-06 04:59 UTC

yes `rem` is away to avoid cascading problems... but in this case we should recommend use `rems` and I should spec the design accordingly. So the decision here is timely important

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-04-06 05:03 UTC

Right, we want to support a configurable font size. Many users aren’t used to using browser zoom for this and/or think of it as a hack. Also, it will be important when we finish thumbnailing support to have control over the px sizes of images.

`rem` would also work.

If you want to write a scalable value that’s 19px when the font size is 15px, you can always write `calc(19rem / 15)`. No need to do math that the computer can do for you; our CSS minifier will compile this to a plain number. ([line-height should be unitless](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/line-height#prefer_unitless_numbers_for_line-height_values) though: `calc(19 / 15)`.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-06 21:40 UTC

I'm not sure whether our first version would have this range of values, but Discord has sliders for font size, and I think that's something we'd want as well:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/2b/CN6_To-QkRprKRwrBwPfFTnF/image.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-06 21:41 UTC

(I know there are some users who prefer very large fonts due to poor eyesight, and it'd be better to not require them to rely on browser zoom for that)

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-04-10 14:25 UTC

Let me think about that feature. It is not a small one. If we agree that we increasing the base font size of the body and the default line height on the body should we mention that in every UI redesign task or we will go another pass on all the styles once we finish the current size redesign?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-11 17:45 UTC

I think it probably makes sense to do as an independent pass.

## update emoji #19371

*2022-04-26 to 2023-04-05 · 245 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/update.20emoji.20.2319371/with/1373452)*

**Alya Abbott** · 2022-04-26 00:33 UTC

Hey folks! I'd love for us to start making progress towards **Add emoji from Unicode 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13** #19371, which is a 6.0 release goal. 

My understanding is that there are two essentially separate things we need to do in this space.

1. Handle emoji missing from Google Classic
2. Figure out a plan for emoji naming (and then make it happen)

Since it's all a bit tangly, I've summarized my understanding in a [Paper doc](https://paper.dropbox.com/doc/Emoji-migration-plan--BgWBi1CCQV3yhNE9gO2caPlJAQ-D7oKMu1dRAXaTquf3cTNH) (annotated by @Tim Abbott with some helpful feedback and references).

I'm happy to transcribe next steps to new or existing issues once we have an initial plan.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 16:55 UTC

If a custom emoji has been added with the same name as a unicode emoji, then API requests to just add that emoji by name will always prefer the custom emoji.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 16:55 UTC

However, it is still possible to access the unicode emoji on messages that already have emoji reactions with that emoji (basically, you can still upvote/downvote the original unicode emoji).

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 16:56 UTC

That arrangement is important to achieve an important design goal for the emoji system: That we can adjust the name mappings for unicode emoji freely, without breaking existing messages or emoji reactions.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 16:58 UTC

In other words, emoji reactions record the (emoji name, codepoint) pair that the user selected when adding the reaction, not whatever new default name we might now have for that codepoint or whatever new codepoint we might now have for that name.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 17:01 UTC

@Evy Kassirer but this means that it is not a valid configuration at present to give the same name to multiple unicode codepoints, which is a problem for directly using some data sets, like CLDR, that provide a primary name plus several "search keywords", rather than Zulip's model of a primary name plus several aliases (which are alternative allowed names you can use for that codepoint, when you have a specific one of several associated meanings in mind).

**Evy** · 2022-04-26 17:54 UTC

So to double check I have this right:

* Every "default" (unicode) emoji has name(s) that we have mapped to it.
* No two unicode emoji can share a name.
* Custom emoji *can* share names with unicode emoji, and the custom emoji will always show up first when that name is typed in.

New backfilled unicode emoji can share names with any existing custom emoji that share those new names, and custom emoji will continue to be prioritized.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-04-26 19:41 UTC

While most systems treat an emoji as a character, Zulip currently has a unique model where an emoji is treated as a (character, alias) pair. The alias is communicated along with the character in messages and reactions, and exposed as a hidden tooltip to readers whose devices happen to support mouse hovering. The CLDR proposal in #18121 would change that model; search keywords are used in the emoji lookup UI but are not communicated with the emoji. I argue in #18121 that our unique alias model is not worth its maintenance cost; see my comments there.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 20:17 UTC

As we've seen with the previous discussion of the unicode emoji `folded_hands` that, as I understand it, is widely used on the Internet both to express `:pray:` and `:thank_you:`, it's sufficiently annoying if you meant to say "thank you" to have "pray" be the label of your text that we've created the :thank_you: custom emoji as a workaround. I'm fairly confident that there are many other practical issues of this form where a single unicode codepoint is used for __very__ different meanings in different communities.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 20:18 UTC

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-04-26 20:32 UTC

That’s how emoji work in other systems, and that’s how human language has evolved around those systems.

**Evy** · 2022-05-11 00:30 UTC

Usually we only have one of these stylesheets present at a time. When the emoji style is switched in settings, this code is run to switch out the stylesheets:

```
export async function select(name) {
    const new_emojiset = emojisets.get(name);
    if (new_emojiset === current_emojiset) {
        return;
    }
    await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const sheet = new Image();
        sheet.addEventListener("load", resolve);
        sheet.addEventListener("error", reject);
        sheet.src = new_emojiset.sheet;
    });
    if (current_emojiset) {
         current_emojiset.css.unuse();
     }
    new_emojiset.css.use();
    current_emojiset = new_emojiset;
}
```

**Greg Price** · 2022-05-11 01:40 UTC

I think the right solution is to drop support for the Google Classic emojiset.

It's been unmaintained for five years. Users that are still on it are going to be seeing a lot of emoji drawn in a different style no matter what we do (once we finally start supporting all those years' worth of new emoji.) It'd be better to give a coherent experience with that new emojiset.

That would also save us from having to do engineering work to blend together two sets of emoji glyphs.

**Greg Price** · 2022-05-11 01:53 UTC

I know there are a few people who definitely prefer the Google  Classic glyphs. We'll probably hear some complaints whenever we do finally desupport it. I expect @Tim Abbott, and perhaps some other users, would choose to have a mixed set of glyphs with a lot of Google Classic over having a set with none of them.

But there will also be people annoyed by seeing a weird mixture where some of the emoji of faces show up as blob-people, while others show up in a very different style with circular faces. Most people who see that will have never made a choice for it, or a choice for Google Classic at all -- while we've changed the default for new users, I believe we've never migrated existing users. Surely the vast majority have never looked at that setting - they leave it to us to give them a reasonable emoji experience.

We might not hear active complaints about that weird mixture. But it will be part of the "Zulip is ugly and not well designed" feeling that we hear a lot.

**Evy** · 2022-05-11 15:51 UTC

Though here's a rough and somewhat hacky plan to still support it:

* Migrate users that never chose Google Classic to Twitter. Show them a modal.
* Show a modal to all users who chose Google Classic, to let them know they're entering mildly-janky-land.
* In the settings menu, make some note on the Google Classic option that mentions this emoji set is no longer supported and is mixed with another emoji set.
* Load two spritesheets for Google Classic (but not both CSS sheets) -- we might already load both?
* Update the Google Classic CSS to override the spritesheet for emojis past a certain point, i.e. the emoji-specific styling would be to use the Twitter background and positions.

It's a little janky to override CSS for another spritesheet like that, and to load both, but the experience of Google Classic will be overall a bit jank so I think it's okay to have less good support for people who really want to keep this option.

**Evy** · 2022-05-11 15:52 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-16 20:26 UTC

So, reminding myself of the CSS setup, I think the infrastructure would be pretty easy if we wanted to do the fallback thing. Specifically, we already have this in the blobs emoji generated CSS:

```
// Normal emoji
.emoji-00a9 {
    background-position: 0.000% 0.000%;
}

// Octopus emoji existing hardcoding is a correct way to use an image for a given codepoint.
.emoji-1f419
{
    background-image: url(../emoji/images-google-64/1f419.png) !important;
    background-position: 0% 0% !important;
    background-size: contain !important;
}
```

And `static/generated/emoji/images-google-64/` has individual emoji files for all the emoji (we already need this for sending emoji in email notifications, I think).

Well, I'm imagining a plan along the lines of:
* Do the few hours of work to make the Google modern backfill work to unblock adding new emoji for other emoji sets.
* Do some minimal documentation that this as a downside of the Google classic emojiset, e.g. an informational popup in the settings UI.
* Change everyone to the Google modern emoji set (perhaps with some communication or marking Google classic as deprecated).
* See how many people switch back.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-06-10 22:58 UTC

> removes aliases that were also canonical names

That may not be enough. The current architecture doesn’t support aliases that duplicate other aliases even if they don’t duplicate canonical names.

**Evy** · 2022-06-10 23:03 UTC

There's an issue that came up, though. There are four emoji we're getting from CLDR whose canonical name *is already used* by a custom zulip name.

* `:kiss:` is currently :kiss: ("kissing face") and we want to add 💏. We could come up for our name for this such as "couple_kiss"
* `:cricket:` is currently :cricket: ("cricket game")  and we want to add 🦗 which is literally a cricket, so I'd prefer to remove our old `cricket`, though I'm not sure how people feel about this considering that there might be existing emoji reactions for it.
* `:receipt:`is currently :receipt: ("curled paper") and we want to add 🧾 which is literally a receipt. Same question here as for cricket.
* `:beetle:` is currently :beetle: ("lady beetle" or "lady bug") and we want to add 🪲 which I would also prefer for beetle than what we currently have.

There are some comments about why these were chosen as custom Zulip names a while ago, such as:

```
    # Unicode/gemoji have lady_beetle; hopefully with ladybug we get both the
    # people that prefer lady_beetle (with beetle) and ladybug. There is also
    # ladybird, but seems a bit much for this to complete for bird.
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-06-10 23:10 UTC

I still maintain that our effort would be better spent demolishing this broken legacy architecture. We’re wasting our talent and energy on resolving inane dilemmas like this.

**Evy** · 2022-06-10 23:11 UTC

I haven't looked much into the current architecture, but it seems like it would be nice to allow duplicate aliases.

Ohhh I see, it's because we allow things like `:alias:` in messages. I'd love for that to auto-complete to the canonical name instead.

**Evy** · 2022-06-10 23:12 UTC

So far I don't think I'm doing much work that wouldn't be involved in the demolition anyways. If we get to a point where we need to migrate old emojis over to new names, then we may as well migrate to CLDR names overall, but if we're not there yet then I'd rather do something simpler first.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-06-10 23:13 UTC

#18121 is not about “migrating to CLDR names”. The whole point is that *emoji are characters, not names*.

**Evy** · 2022-06-10 23:16 UTC

At my current experience level both as an Zulip engineer and engineer overall, I find it a bit overwhelming to think about a migration (or "architecture redesign") of that size without taking several hours to think about it and understand what it involves. I do see how a lot of apps use emoji as characters and not names, and think that would be helpful to us, but that's a pretty big change and it would be great to support more emoji if we can before embarking on that project.

I'm down to make changes to our approach if people want, but I'm not the person to convince -- the more tenured engineers are. Which is to say I welcome these comments but I probably will not be responding to them particularly helpfully.

Something that would be helpful to me Anders is if you wrote a Paper doc that outlined what you want, why, and also how to do it -- the engineering steps involved (including various migrations) with enough detail that someone could do an estimate of how long they think the project might take for them. If it's less work than I've been guessing it is, that would also inspire me to work on that instead. I would be open to working on it a bit with you and helping create the structure/questions I'd want answered.

**Greg Price** · 2022-06-11 00:50 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> I still maintain that our effort would be better spent demolishing this broken legacy architecture. We’re wasting our talent and energy on resolving inane dilemmas like this.

I'm sympathetic to this, but if we were to block adding all the recent-years emoji on doing so, I'd be concerned that it's a much bigger project. Not only in engineering questions to answer, but in product questions -- in getting everyone involved in the discussion comfortable with the new way that things would work.

I'm hopeful that we can instead move forward with a somewhat different approach: wherever we run into an "inane dilemma" related to our current emoji-with-names model, resolve it in a way that avoids putting a lot of effort into (again) choosing names for individual emoji. Even if that means that for some of the new emoji, we get only like 50-70% of the value of adding them, that's still more than 0%, plus we get 100% of the value of adding the many other emoji that don't pose such naming dilemmas.

**Greg Price** · 2022-06-13 23:15 UTC

Emoji reactions have an emoji name recorded in the database, in addition to the emoji code which (together with the `reaction_type`) uniquely and stably identifies the actual emoji, in the sense of a character. So when someone looks back at an old message with an old reaction and hovers on the reaction, they'll see the name that was originally attached to it.

This fits with the existing Zulip model of an emoji, which is that it's a pair of a name and a character, not simply a character. (A model we've never really consistently implemented, as Anders has pointed out, but it's what was imagined when the system was designed.)

**Greg Price** · 2022-06-13 23:18 UTC

And as for emoji inside old messages: this means that re-rendering those old messages would no longer produce the same result as it did then. But we regularly make changes that have that effect -- as do users when they add or delete custom emoji -- and so we basically never do attempt to go back and re-render old messages. The rendered HTML, on the other hand, specifies the emoji ID and type (… at least I hope it specifies both of those, hmm), so again uniquely and stably identifies the actual emoji character.

**Greg Price** · 2022-06-13 23:26 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> The rendered HTML, on the other hand, specifies the emoji ID and type (… at least I hope it specifies both of those, hmm),

Well, it's hardly explicit about it, but good enough.

Empirically, a Unicode emoji comes out as a `span.emoji`, with the emoji code encoded in a further class. A realm emoji (aka custom emoji) or Zulip extra emoji (i.e. :zulip:) both come out as an `img.emoji`; for a realm emoji, the `src` has a particular shape which includes the emoji code, and for a Zulip extra emoji, the `src` has a fixed value of a different shape.

In all cases, the way the emoji actually displays in the client should be determined entirely by the type and code, and in particular that's true when one just takes the rendered HTML and shows it in a browser.

> so again uniquely and stably identifies the actual emoji character.

I.e., it accomplishes this.

## duplicate message

*2022-04-26 to 2024-01-04 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/duplicate.20message/with/1374032)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:38 UTC

So I had a duplicate message appear in a view, like so, just now:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/5d/AIcxb1lIIwQLTTXu-EO2WVGx/image.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:38 UTC

I guess that's not a screenshot of the message, but it's showing that we have two messages in the same view with the same ID.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:39 UTC

What I did was send the message and then which it was sending, us `Ctrl+.` to narrow to that view.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:40 UTC

So the bug is very likely a race between:
* The API request to the server to fetch the messages matching the target view.
* The `server_events` response indicating that the message had been successfully sent and should be added to that view.

It may be important for reproduction that I did not have any recent messages in that view (i.e. likely none cached by my browser), but I'm not sure.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:41 UTC

I suspect it's possible to reason out what sequence must have happened -- I think in particular, it's likely that we got the `GET /messages` API response just before the `GET /events` response gave us that message?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:42 UTC

It's probably possible to artificially simulate that sequence in a development environment or possibly even a node test; if we can do that, I suspect it won't be that hard to find out where we're failing to deduplicate.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:48 UTC

Opened #21921 to track this; I don't think I have time to dig into the code path yet, but I'd probably start by reading the code to find the specific code that's expected to deduplicate these in both of the two possible sequences.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-04-26 23:49 UTC

I guess this is one such block of code, which prevents adding newly arrived messages before the `GET /messages` call has returned:
```
export function add_new_messages(messages, msg_list) {                                                   
    if (!msg_list.data.fetch_status.has_found_newest()) {                                                
        // We don't render newly received messages for the message list,                                 
        // if we haven't found the latest messages to be displayed in the                                
        // narrow. Otherwise the new message would be rendered just after                                
        // the previously fetched messages when that's inaccurate.                                       
        msg_list.data.fetch_status.update_expected_max_message_id(messages);                             
        return undefined;                                                                                
    }                                                                                                    
    return add_messages(messages, msg_list, {messages_are_new: true});                                   
}                                                                                                        
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-04 18:57 UTC

## is_user_in_group implementation

*2022-05-02 to 2022-05-04 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/is_user_in_group.20implementation/with/1376823)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2022-05-02 12:12 UTC

I am working on adding `is_user_in_group` function in `user_groups.ts` to check whether a user is part of a user group or not. Checking direct members would not be enough and we would need to check whether the user is part of one of the subgroups of the user group or not and if not then we have to check whether user is part of subgroups of subgroups and so on.

So, this would be implemented using recursion. I am not sure how efficient would it be to check all the subgroups (if needed) each time when there are large number of user groups.

One other way would be to add a field like `all_members`, which will be a list of ids direct members of all subgroups and their subgroups and so on, while initializing the user group data.

Any other ideas or feedback?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-02 23:15 UTC

I would expect it to be quite efficient to just check if the user is a direct member of the group, and then do the same check for each subgroup that hasn't been visited yet.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-02 23:17 UTC

Which I think one can do readily in a single function with a list of subgroups to check and a set of already checked subgroups.

**Sahil Batra** · 2022-05-03 07:31 UTC

The direct members is simple. Checking for subgroups is complex. Not only we need to check in subgroups of the asked user group, but in subgroups of those subgroups as well and then this will continue.

An example taking users in our development server, we want to check whether Iago is member of "@role:everyone" user group. Iago is not direct member of the group and it has one subgroup, "@role:members", and Iago is not a direct member of that subgroup as well. Then we need to check in subgroups of "@role:members" group as well, and then "@role:fullmembers" group and so on.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-03 19:27 UTC

@Sahil Batra I'm imagining pseudocode like this:
```
def is_user_in_group(user_id, target_group_id):
    groups_to_check = [target_group_id];
    groups_checked = set()

    for group_id in groups_to_check:
        if group_id in groups_checked:
             continue;
        if is_user_directly_in_group(user_id, group_id):
             return true;
        for subgroup_id in get_subgroup_ids(group_id):
             groups_to_check.append(subgroup_id);
        groups_checked.add(group_id);
    return false;
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-03 19:29 UTC

Though it might be cleaner to instead split as two functions: First one that returns all recursive subgroups of a group (which seems like something that we'll end up using for display purposes later), and then this would just iterate through that list calling `is_user_directly_in_group`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-03 19:30 UTC

That refactor would also avoid the somewhat smelly aspect of the above pseudocode that it is adding things to the list it is iterating through.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-05-03 19:31 UTC

But hopefully that gives you the idea of an efficient algorithm for this problem. The key thing is the `grouped_checked` set prevents the potential combinatorial explosion issues one could have if someone was trying to make a bad algorithm run in exponential time.

**Sahil Batra** · 2022-05-04 02:36 UTC

Thanks, got it.

We currently add the user by default in the user group while creating, but user can remove themselves later on, so I think we can keep the "Remove" button enabled and add the user to the list by default as we do now.

Since we add the user creating the group by default while processing the create user group request on backend, and if we do not disable remove button for user creating the group so we could have a weird user experience as user creating the group might try creating a group with no subscriber  but would see himself subscribed after the group is created. This was the reason I kept remove button for user creating the group disabled. Although this is minor and I can change it in case we decide that.

Regarding
> The "User group created" banner shown after creating a user group should probably have left and right margins. Hmm; @Alya Abbott thoughts on whether we want to require that groups have at least one member, like we do for streams? 

On the one hand, I can imagine situations where it'd be annoying to not be able to make a group with no members (since then we'd have to prevent deactivating the last user who's in the group until the group is removed, etc., and maybe you've got an "Interns" group that is sometimes empty), and in fact our UI discussions have included a "nobody" virtual system group that would be empty (I think it may not actually exist in the database). 

On the other hand, I don't have a clear story for why this should be different. (And there's kinda a similar problem statement that we ideally don't want to have to consider cases where someone sets "The users who can administer X" to be the empty set).

> It seems like we deliberately copy the whole of messages and not just parts of messages, in cases where the selection overlaps multiple messages. I think this is counterintuitive - thoughts on stopping doing this?
The intended use case is when you're trying to grab a large block of messages, it's not uncommon for it to be somewhat inaccurate (in that you maybe your selection didn't quite cover a couple edge characters within messages that you'd intended).

I think it'd be very reasonable to change "multiple" in this definition to a definition like "at least 3 messages"; I think just about every case I've seen someone unhappy with this design has been when they're trying to copy a fairly small chunk of text, not the "I'm trying to copy an entire screenful of messages" case that this feature was designed for. @Alya Abbott thoughts on that detail?

Not easily. For the ones associated with compose, these imports at the top of `compose_validate.js` are relatively complete. The filenames are bad, so `all_everyone` is wildcard mentons, and `invite_users` is the warning about mentioning someone who isn't subscribed to the stream:
```
import render_compose_all_everyone from "../templates/compose_all_everyone.hbs";                         
import render_compose_announce from "../templates/compose_announce.hbs";                                 
import render_compose_invite_users from "../templates/compose_invite_users.hbs";                         
import render_compose_not_subscribed from "../templates/compose_not_subscribed.hbs";                     
import render_compose_private_stream_alert from "../templates/compose_private_stream_alert.hbs";         
import render_compose_resolved_topic from "../templates/compose_resolved_topic.hbs";                     
```

(There's also a generic "compose_error" used for error messages, and the `send_status` component, which is technically different but shows the indicator that a file is being uploaded)

@Vlad Korobov FYI.

* We remove the ability to do anything with where a poll is sent from the modal -- the modal just sets the content of your compose box with the the `/poll` syntax corresponding to what you made in the wizard.

**Sayam Samal** · 2022-07-04 14:01 UTC

Having gone through the references by @Tim Abbott , here's my findings and progress till now,

* We target particular elements that require a tooltip with the `delegate` function and supply custom configs, if required, to override the default config.
* There are multiple ways to render a tooltip,
  * `data-tippy-content` --> simple text tooltip
  * `data-tooltip-template-id` --> HTML tooltip
  * function returning string or a DOM elem
  Out of these we may want to use the `data-tooltip-template-id` since we aim for a custom tooltip style.
* I went ahead and created a WIP handlebar partial for the hotkey tooltips
`tooltip-keyboard-hint.hbs`
```html+handlebars
    <template id="{{tooltip_id}}">
        <div class="hotkey">
            <span class="hotkey-title">{{tooltip_text}}</span>
            <span class="hotkey-hint">{{hotkey_hint}}</span>
        </div>
    </template>
```
`some_other_file.hbs`
```html+handlebars
    <div class="hotkey-tooltip" data-tooltip-template-id="emoji_reaction">
        <i class="fa fa-smile-o"></i>
    </div>

    {{> tooltip-keyboard-hint
        tooltip_text="Custom"
        hotkey_hint="Shift"
        tooltip_id="emoji_reaction"
    }}
```
I realised soon that this wasn't an effective approach, making it difficult to pass multiple key combinations and excess code in general.

**Sayam Samal** · 2022-07-04 14:15 UTC

* After this, I decided to check the `tippyjs.js` more in depth to check for a more programmatic way to address the issue. And sure enough there were snippets of code that performed similar operations to the one I required. The `onShow()`method of tippyjs.js allows dynamic insertion of content depending on the instance triggered.
* So tinkering around I came up this approach,
`tippyjs.js`
```js
    delegate("body", {
        target: ".hotkey-tooltip",
        placement: "top",
        hideOnClick: "false", // for debugging
        trigger: "click", // for debugging
        appendTo: () => document.body,
        onShow(instance) {
            const tooltip_text = $(instance.reference).attr("data-title")
            const hotkey_hints = JSON.parse($(instance.reference).attr("data-hints"))
            console.log(hotkey_hints)
            instance.setContent(parse_html(render_hotkey_tooltip({tooltip_text, hotkey_hints})));
        },
        onHidden(instance) {
            instance.destroy();
        },
    });
```
`tooltip-keyboard-hint.hbs`
```html+handlebars
<div class="hotkey">
    <span class="hotkey-title">{{tooltip_text}}</span>
    {{#each hotkey_hints}}
        <span class="hotkey-hint">{{this}}</span>
    {{/each}}
</div>
```
`message_controls.hbs`
```html
    <div class="hotkey-tooltip" data-title="smile" data-hints='["ctrl", "shift", "a"]'>
        <i class="fa fa-smile-o"></i>
    </div>
```

**Sayam Samal** · 2022-08-18 19:03 UTC

@Tim Abbott @Yash RE can you please look at the implementation for the hotkey tooltips? I have submitted a WIP PR at https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/22746.

I'll go forward and give a summary of the whole thing.

As mentioned above, I have opted for the split method to pass the required hotkey hints into the elements through the `data-hints` attribute.

Since many tooltips have different methods applied to them before being displayed, this makes the content of the tooltips very dynamic in nature. Hence I couldn't target all the tooltips under a same delegate method. Instead, I tried to approach this with a function call, which appends the hotkeys to the tooltip only if the data-hints attribute is present, and then passes it on to the .setContent() method for the usual render.

```js
function render_with_hotkeys(content, data_hints) {
    if(data_hints == undefined)
        return content;
    let hotkey_hints = split(data_hints, ', ')

    return(parse_html(render_hotkey_tooltip({content, hotkey_hints})));
}
```
```js
instance.setContent(render_with_hotkeys(content, data_hints));
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2022-07-11 07:14 UTC

We track `message_lists.home`, `message_lists.current` and `message_list.narrowed`. I checked the places where `message_lists.narrowed` is used, and they could easily be replaced to use `message_lists.home` and `message_lists.current`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-07-11 19:00 UTC

Hmm. I agree that `message_lists.current` is kinda a funny structure that can equal either `message_list.narrowed` or `message_lists.home`, and that the `.narrowed` item as a unique thing is not super consistent with the #15131 direction.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-07-11 19:01 UTC

I guess we have this class of conditional in a bunch of places: `message_lists.current === message_list.narrowed`

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-07-11 19:02 UTC

I think probably I'd start with replacing that kind of conditional with something that better says what we mean -- e.g. adding a `message.lists.current.is_narrowed()` boolean that can be checked to see whether the current user is looking at a narrowed list or not.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2022-07-12 04:36 UTC

I am replacing code like this:
```js
    message_lists.home.view.rerender_messages([message]);
    if (message_lists.current === message_list.narrowed) {
        message_list.narrowed.view.rerender_messages([message]);
    }
```

with
```js
    message_lists.home.view.rerender_messages([message]);
    if (message_lists.current_different_than_home()) {
        message_list.current.view.rerender_messages([message]);
    }
```

```js
export function current_different_than_home() {
    return message_list.current !== undefined && message_list.current !== home
}
```

and make sure `current` is always narrowed. So, we don't need to check if `current` is narrowed or not.

## directory reorganization

*2022-07-20 to 2023-02-24 · 55 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/directory.20reorganization/with/1407791)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-07-20 21:43 UTC

We’ve wanted to clean up our `static` directory structure for [a while](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/code.20sharing/near/792791). I drafted #22535 to see what that would look like.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-07-20 21:43 UTC

Currently, it does

- `static/assets` → `web/assets`
- `static/generated/emoji-styles` → `web/generated/emoji-styles`
- `static/generated/pygments_data.json` → `web/generated/pygments_data.json`
- `static/generated/timezones.json` → `web/generated/timezones.json`
- `static/html` → `web/html`
- `static/images` → `web/images` (only the ones that are bundled by webpack)
- `static/js` `web/js`
- `static/shared` → `web/shared`
- `static/styles` → `web/styles`
- `static/templates` → `web/templates`
- `static/third` → `web/third`
- `tools/webpack.assets.json` → `web/webpack.assets.json`
- `tools/webpack.dev-assets.json` → `web/webpack.dev-assets.json`

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-07-20 21:44 UTC

That leaves just the following in `static` for now:

- `static/audio/notification_sounds` (could possibly move to `web` if bundled with webpack in the future)
- `static/generated/bots` (doesn’t need to be in `static`, but not really frontendy either)
- `static/generated/emoji` (some of these need to stay here to preserve references from old email notifications)
- `static/images` (images referenced from backend templates will stay here forever; others might move to `web` as we bundle more with webpack)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-07-20 21:44 UTC

I plan to also move the Node and Puppeteer tests into `web` in a separate step.

Here are some open questions to discuss.

- Is `web` the right name? Other proposals were
  - `webapp` (which would guarantee we never see the end of #18489),
  - `frontend`.
- Do we want to take this opportunity to make further organizational improvements?
  - Merge `web/assets` and `web/images`, now that the former is not unique in its exclusion from release tarballs and web serving?
  - Rename `web/js` to `web/src`, which is more common and more inclusive of TypeScript?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-02-22 22:10 UTC

> It looks like it needs a minor rebase and also I'd like explicit confirmation that you've tested it in production before I merge it.

Did the minor rebase. Yes, it’s running in production on andersk.zulipdev.org.

> (I know we merged a big change from @Alex Vandiver to how static assets are managed).

Yep, I had already been on top of that.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-02-22 22:26 UTC

> Oh so one thing I don't understand is the nature of the things that are still in `static/` after this transition; specifically `static/audio` and how to explain the difference in terms of where to place images between `static/images` and `web/images`.

Things go in `static/` if and only if they need to be referenced from a `/static/` URL. That includes anything referenced from Python or Jinja templates (since Webpack has no interaction with those), and anything that needs to have a fixed URL for other reasons, such as the emoji URLs we’re stuck with because they’re baked into stored message content. You [asserted](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/24286#discussion_r1103358317) that the URLs to the notification sounds are part of the API, so those stay in `static/` for now too (I don’t think anything actually relies on those being part of the API, but we can have that discussion separately).

Anything referenced in the Webpack way—JavaScript `import`, CSS relative `url()` references, the one file `5xx.html` processed by `html-loader`, Handlebars attributes matching the `inlineRequires` regex Alex added in #24286—are bundled by Webpack and replaced with Webpack-hashed URLs, so those files should live in `web/` unless there’s some other reason to put them in `static/`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-02 22:38 UTC

One of the things that's annoying about this sort of feature is the test matrix for it -- ideally, we want to change an impactful set of UI locations, but ideally with a minimum of layout changes. **Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-02 22:39 UTC

I think that's usually a better UI anyway, because what we don't want is folks to be thinking "Wow, Zulip is terrible, it doesn't even have private messages". **Alya Abbott** · 2022-08-04 11:07 UTC

Thanks for the poking around / thinking through this @Adam S ! 

I filed #22659 as a meta-issue to track the work on improving this feature. One thing to note is that I don't think we should hide "view private messages" options not just for the reason @Tim Abbott gave above, but also because this setting can be changed. *2022-08-04 to 2022-08-04 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/no-jquery.2Fno-parse-html-literal/with/1414814)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-08-04 01:22 UTC

The zjquery mock doesn’t do HTML parsing at all, and we avoid parsing HTML with real jQuery too for security reasons.

Since the `<p>hi</p>` doesn’t matter for your test, just use something like `<message-stub>` instead.

## Message edit UI still open after message is moved

*2022-08-09 to 2022-08-26 · 18 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Message.20edit.20UI.20still.20open.20after.20message.20is.20moved/with/1417350)*

**Jai soni** · 2022-08-09 10:07 UTC

I've started working on this [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/21724).
The steps I followed in debugging the reason behind why the edit UI still remains open after the message is moved if we navigate to some other topic/stream while the process -> 

I took a look at the events triggered in network tab if the message is moved successfully --> this led me to `message_events.update_messages(update_message_events)` function being triggered inside `server_events.js` file , which eventually run these lines from `message_events.js` to close the edit UI after the message is successfully moved ->

```js
        const $row = message_lists.current.get_row(event.message_id);
        if ($row.length > 0) {
            message_edit.end_message_row_edit($row);
        }
```

**Jai soni** · 2022-08-09 10:10 UTC

Now the reason behind why the edit UI remains open is -> we do get the `event.message_id` right always, but when we navigate to some other topic -- `message_lists.current.get_row(event.message_id)` returns us a blank object and thus the `$row` comes as {} and which is why we do not enter inside and run->

```js
message_edit.end_message_row_edit($row);
```

**Jai soni** · 2022-08-09 10:11 UTC

Now the reason behind `message_lists.current.get_row(event.message_id)` returning us a blank object is pretty clear ->

we're inside a topic in which this message hasn't moved yet, so finding the `message_id` in the list is obviously going to return us a blank object.

@Aman Agrawal (amanagr)  would like to know your views on this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:41 UTC

I posted a tactical comment on it, but that's I think pretty clearly an improvement.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:42 UTC

That said, I think we may want to guard this behavior behind some sort of check for who initiated the edit that we're processing. If I'm editing the content of a message, and someone moves the topic that I'm working in, I'm pretty sure I **don't** want the message edit UI to close, losing the text I've typed.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:45 UTC

I'm not sure what the best logic is. In an ideal world, we (1) send a `local_id` like we do for sending messages that the server will deliver back to us, that we can use to close just the edit operation that we ourselves requested, and (2) do something to highlight for the user that the stream/topic just changed if they're currently editing something... I'm not sure what that highlighting should be.

The `local_id` complexity is only going to help in situations where you, for some unlikely reason, are personally doing multiple edit operations at the same time; I'm not sure whether it's worth the complexity to handle that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:46 UTC

But it's very plausible that someone else moves a topic while you're trying to edit a message's content, and somewhat plausible that you move a topic while trying to edit a message's content in that topic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:48 UTC

I think an algorithm that is not correct but will work 99% of the time and not have particularly bad failure modes is:
* Close the edit window when processing an `update_message` event from the server if and only if both (1) the edit action was done by you and (2) the edit action was done with the message in question as its anchor.

This would mean that edits by others never close the edit window, and if you've got multiple edit windows open in a topic, only the one that you actually clicked "Save" in will close ... unless you're editing the same message in two different browsers, in which case both will incorrectly close (which is probably most easily fixed with the `local_id` technique mentioned above, but I think it's unlikely enough to be not worth the effort at this time).

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-09 17:49 UTC

@Jai soni I think you can go ahead and implement that algorithm in a new second commit in your PR; we'll likely want to merge something quite similar to it.

## channel retry on success

*2022-08-19 to 2022-08-19 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/channel.20retry.20on.20success/with/1421578)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-08-19 02:39 UTC

Commit 7f174213ede4396acfa86ab0b75d6254dc6dc7e2 added a retry loop to the…*success* handler? Where it’s been ever since. When would we ever retry on *success*?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-08-19 03:19 UTC

#22753

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-19 18:59 UTC

Since it's an interesting story, I figure I'll mention: Some unknown bug resulted in Zulip API endpoints returning 200 status responses with empty data after not having actually reached the server, generally when the server was being restarted, and this code was a workaround to avoid that resulting in the Zulip app being confused (as it'd otherwise show feedback to the user that the request had succeeded). 

Based on browser exception stack traces (we logged something whenever this happened), this failure mode happened frequently between that code being introduced in early 2014 until late 2019, when it suddenly went from a daily occurence to no longer happening. I still don't understand the nature of the original bug, and suspect it was likely in some third-party dependency, but given that it's stopped happening, we can likely safely remove the hack.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-19 19:03 UTC

I really hate this kind of workaround that is clearly incorrectly but important to block a bug we could not directly reproduce and that had significant user-facing impact, so am glad we get to delete it.

## Visual editor

*2022-08-21 to 2022-08-24 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Visual.20editor/with/1422600)*

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-08-21 16:01 UTC

I heard there is a desire to make visual editor and I understand that it is a challenging task. 
What do you think about using [ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net/)? It is open source with a permissive license and has great features and a proper flexibility to create [markdown/visual editor switch](https://prosemirror.net/examples/markdown/)
 and there is a way to define [custom nodes](https://prosemirror.net/examples/dino/) in the editor

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-22 23:43 UTC

I think we definitely want to use a library like it; I can't say I'll have an opinion on that sort of thing without someone trying to prototype one (I know there's several in this space; for example I've met the https://github.com/quilljs/quill guy). Some specific considerations I'd look at early in evaluating one:
* We have various Markdown extensions (some more standards-like than others).
* We care about messages up to 10K characters (which can be a perf issue for some libraries).
* We're probably fairly picky about the interaction design feeling nice.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-08-22 23:48 UTC

It’s not going to be possible to integrate a visual editor with any kind of reliability until we fix the protocol to transmit formatted messages using a syntax tree instead of Markdown. (Previous discussion: #**frontend>live preview within the compose box**.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-23 00:00 UTC

I wouldn't say impossible, but certainly agree that it's required to integrate something that doesn't have tons of quirky/buggy situations where the visual editor's preview is inaccurate. It is likely possible to play whack-a-mole and have the bugs be fringe enough that some users might be excited about such a visual editor feature anyway... but I'm not excited about that strategy, because it basically involves doing a bunch of wasted work.

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-08-24 03:27 UTC

I worked with Quill deeply, doin an editor for https://timestripe.com/. It is abandoned kind of product since the team is focused on https://slab.com/.
The library isn't bad, but I feel like performance and quality of prose mirror is higher.

**Vlad Korobov** · 2022-08-24 03:29 UTC

Prose Mirror and Code Mirror got recently great updates. Interaction design feeling nice is always a custom work. Bot ProseMirror and Quill are using operation transform approach.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2022-08-24 03:30 UTC

The problem we’re worried about isn’t the quality of the editor itself; the problem is the mismatch between the editor’s idea of Markdown and Zulip’s idea of Markdown, given that Zulip’s idea of Markdown is gkriroiesdipewirjkersfd jk regex!!! ekrwjferisdxftjsrifkirj,jidasldasdl;.

We have a very similar function, `clear_compose_box` in `compose.js`. `clear_box` gets called when exiting compose without successfully sending a message; `clear_compose_box` when the compose box is being cleared because a message of sent.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:18 UTC

I was looking at this because of #22775. 

I think what we want to do is a little prep PR that unifies those two functions; if they need different behavior, we should just have a flag passed for whether it's after a successful send. Here's a diff I generated showing what changes would need to be made for the two to be identical:


**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:19 UTC

I have not made an effort to figure out what is correct here... but it seems likely that most of those things should happen in both situations.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:23 UTC

I think each change we make as part of trying to unify them will require some care. For example, `clear_invites()` and `clear_preview_area` are already called at the start of the function for trying to send a message:
```
export function finish() {                                                                                                             
    clear_preview_area();                                                                                                              
    clear_invites();                                                                                                                   
    clear_private_stream_alert();                                                                                                      
```

So it's likely not correct to just add it to `clear_compose_box`, which is largely called once the message __finishes__ sending, not when it starts. Which are usually approximately the same time, when we can locally echo, but there's a network delay if `!locally_echoed`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:24 UTC

There's also `hide_box`, which is called alongside `clear_box` only when closing the compose box, not when resetting its state while leaving it open.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:25 UTC

I posted a comment on #22775 inspired by that observation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:26 UTC

Back to your original question: I think some of those alerts/warnings, like `compose_validate.set_user_acknowledged_all_everyone_flag(undefined)`, seem like things that clearly need to be their own call.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:27 UTC

I suspect the reason we don't clear all of the warnings in the close function has to do with the fact that we hide that element when opening or changing the recipient in the compose box:

```
function show_compose_box(msg_type, opts) {                                                                                            
    if (msg_type === "stream") {                                                                                                       
        $("#private-message").hide();                                                                                                  
        $("#stream-message").show();                                                                                                   
        $("#stream_toggle").addClass("active");                                                                                        
        $("#private_message_toggle").removeClass("active");                                                                            
    } else {                                                                                                                           
        $("#private-message").show();                                                                                                  
        $("#stream-message").hide();                                                                                                   
        $("#stream_toggle").removeClass("active");                                                                                     
        $("#private_message_toggle").addClass("active");                                                                               
    }                                                                                                                                  
    $("#compose-send-status").removeClass(common.status_classes).hide();                                                               
    $("#compose").css({visibility: "visible"});                                                                                        
    // When changing this, edit the 42px in _maybe_autoscroll                                                                          
    $(".new_message_textarea").css("min-height", "3em");                                                                               
                                                                                                                                       
    set_focus(msg_type, opts);                                                                                                         
}                                                                                                                                      
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-08-24 00:29 UTC

So the `clear_box` code path may, at present, always be followed by `show_compose_box` clearing the `compose-send-status` element, at least.

**Evy** · 2022-08-30 18:01 UTC

`clear_box`

* hides warning/error banners (this is most of it)
* clear_preview_area and clear_textarea
* removes the draft_id data from the html element
* autosizes the textbox

called from:

* `compose.start`, when the recipient is changed and the box needs to be cleared
* `compose_actions.cancel`, when the composebox is closed

**Evy** · 2022-08-30 18:01 UTC

(need to leave for a bit, will come back to this later)

**Evy** · 2022-08-30 19:12 UTC

`clear_compose_box`

* returns the composebox to normal size if it was previously full-screen
* clears the textarea (using its element `id`, where `clear_box` does not) and puts focus on it (which `clear_box` also does not)
* clears only two specific warning banners (overflow text, topic resolved), and any error banner in `compose-send-status`
* removes the draft_id data from the html element
* autosizes the textbox
* hides the compose spinner

called from

* clicking compose-new-message-button
* `send_message_success` if `locally_echoed` is false
* at the end of `send_message` if `locally_echoed` is true
* messages sent through `zcommand` calls it from `compose.finish()`
* in the success function of `schedule_message`

* essentially hides all of the preview-related elements and shows the textarea
* notably: brings focus to the textarea

called from:

* `enter_with_preview_open` which closes preview view if a message is sent while in preview -- this one probably needs no focus because a message was just sent
* `compose.finish` at the very start
