## no-use-before-define

*2023-03-22 to 2023-03-26 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/no-use-before-define/with/1530797)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-22 19:08 UTC

We currently [configure](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/a691f0c5273a4b6e23870cb10ebce7636fe057ed) the ESLint [`no-use-before-define` rule](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/no-use-before-define) to skip complaints about `function` ordering in JavaScript, but not in TypeScript. If we turn them back on for JavaScript, it flags 232 violations in 72 files. This is a style issue and not a correctness issue because `function`s are [hoisted](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Hoisting), but it is nicer to read the code in a consistent order.

Should we

1. Leave the ESLint configuration as-is, and have people reorder functions as they migrate JavaScript to TypeScript?
2. Do a reordering pass on the JavaScript, separately from the TypeScript migration? This can probably be automated.
3. Skip these complaints in TypeScript too?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-22 23:13 UTC

I wonder how many circular ordering things we'll run into if we try to sort these.

**Greg Price** · 2023-03-24 18:32 UTC

I don't have a stake in the choice you make for web, but FWIW my feeling in the React Native codebase, where we've had this rule enabled, has been that its effect is pretty mixed between pushing code to be better vs. pushing it to be worse.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-24 20:47 UTC

Yeah, that's my worry with this. So maybe the right answer is to skip these complaints in TypeScript.

Having the TypeScript migrations for individual files be as simple as possible is valuable, and bundling another basically unrelated task into it is probably just going to make that harder to complete.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-03-26 02:50 UTC

Mixing reordering tasks with the ts migration makes the commits harder to read. I would prefer to hold off on this for now. We can always change our minds after the TypeScript migration is finished.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-26 17:14 UTC

Yeah, done in #24865.

**Lalit** · 2023-03-31 18:36 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I think the calculation for whether the user has changed and default settings is going to be hard statically, since it's a function of the organization type, so the messy thing we'd need to do is probably have the code path for changing a user default setting store a "this has been changed" value or …

My idea was to write a function in `RealmUserDefault` model and then using it while computing `page_params` on initial page load:
```py

class RealmUserDefault(UserBaseSettings):
    """This table stores realm-level default values for user preferences
    like notification settings, used when creating a new user account.
    """

    realm = models.OneToOneField(Realm, on_delete=CASCADE)

    def user_defaults_changed(self) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the realm's user defaults are different from the defaults defined in model fields."""

        for field in self.property_types.keys():
            if getattr(self, field) != self._meta.get_field(field).get_default():
                return True

        return False
```

## Correctness of is_editing_stream

*2023-03-24 to 2023-04-11 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Correctness.20of.20is_editing_stream/with/1532586)*

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2023-03-24 12:54 UTC

`hash_util.is_editing_stream` checks whether a stream with given `stream_id` is being edited or not. For that it uses url on the browser window. However consider the case where after opening a stream settings on the right pane a user clicks on either of `subscribed`/`All streams` tab. In that case the stream edit settings are open for that stream in the right pane but `hash_util.is_editing_stream` returns false for the given stream id.

This check is mainly used in live update functions for streams, and it only affect the live update during add/remove subscription events.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2023-03-24 12:56 UTC

We have a similar check for `#groups` as well. I was thinking if we could have a more solid way of checking if a stream/group was being edited then we could update it for both #streams and #groups overlay.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-24 20:54 UTC

@Purushottam Tiwari I think it's possible the bug is in part that probably clicking that toggle should still leave you on a URL with that stream ID. But in any case, checking that via the hash is kinda hacky, and we'd probably be better off with the `stream_edit` module itself maintaining a state variable for what stream id being edited (`null/undefined` if nothing is); we'll just need to be careful to ensure that gets mutated correctly when leaving the view.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2023-04-01 19:18 UTC

Yes I think maintaining a variable for active stream would not be that hard, as I have used that approach for `#groups` overlay ([commit](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/24766/commits/31e6f77b21f315daaf66bb84ba50f29fa7099750)) to have a reliable way to decide if a group is being edited.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2023-04-01 19:34 UTC

But I think the concept of active stream is not so clear, or at least it is very tightly binded with the stream-row selected in the left panel in the `streams` overlay. Currently if a stream settings are open and the user searches in the left search bar then if the stream selected (active stream) is not part of the streams matching search query then that also closes that stream settings from right pane. This I think is not correct because as per the URL that stream is still being edited (and searching for a stream in no way indicates that user wanted to close the stream edit that he/she was on).

In my opinion the behavior should be:
* The stream edit for a stream to remain open even when the stream is not present on the left panel (due to some search query or may be due to switches between all-streams and subscribed).
* Across the updates in the  list of visible streams in the left pane we check if the active stream (on whose settings are open on the right pane) is visible we add active class to that stream-row.
* `get_active_data()` on `stream_settings_ui.js` should return the value of the maintained variable for active stream id.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2023-04-01 19:39 UTC

Also I have kept this behavior for for `#groups` on #24766, so wanted to ask if this sounds correct?

**Alya Abbott** · 2023-04-10 21:18 UTC

Keeping the currently selected stream/group in the right-side panel even if the current filter doesn't include it sounds good to me.

**Alya Abbott** · 2023-04-10 21:19 UTC

(I can't comment on the technical parts of the proposal.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-11 00:16 UTC

@Purushottam Tiwari I think moving to a model like what you implemented in the groups overlay makes sense to me; @Sahil Batra may have some additional thoughts, but I thought the groups PR made things more readable.

## color notation

*2023-03-25 to 2023-03-25 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/color.20notation/with/1533316)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-25 00:34 UTC

In #24780 we’ve switched our CSS colors from legacy to [modern](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/) notation: `hsl(16, 60%, 45%)` → `hsl(16deg 60% 45%)`, `hsla(147, 57%, 25%, 0.4)` → `hsl(147deg 57% 25% / 40%)`. Stylelint will flag uses of the legacy syntax, and automatically fix them with `--fix`.

If you have open PRs with many frontend changes, it may be hard to rebase them across this reformatting in the normal way, but it’s easy with these commands:

```shell
git pull --rebase https://github.com/andersk/zulip.git color-prep

FILTER_BRANCH_SQUELCH_WARNING=1 \
    git filter-branch --force \
    --tree-filter '../../node_modules/.bin/stylelint --fix web/styles \
        && sed -i "s,/ 100%),),g" web/styles/*.css web/styles/*/*.css \
        && ../../node_modules/.bin/prettier --cache -w web/styles' \
    --commit-filter 'git_commit_non_empty_tree "$@"' \
    "FETCH_HEAD^..HEAD"
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-25 00:48 UTC

@Aman (amanagr) @Evy as folks who likely will want to do this rebase on a bunch of PRs.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-03-26 03:44 UTC

For type definitions, there are two syntaxes that are *mostly* interchangeable.
`interface` can also be extended by declaring it repeatedly, i.e. it is open.

We do
```typescript
interface Foo {}

or
```typescript
type Foo = {}

To my understanding, it is similar to why we use `const` as opposed to `let` unless necessary.
`interface` is less restricted than `type`, so potentially more error-prone when its usage is spread out in the codebase.

**Lalit** · 2023-03-26 10:52 UTC

I think the main difference between interfaces and type aliases is that we can use "union(|)" in our type aliases for example: `type id = string | number` other than that I don't know if they differ that much?

**Vlad Korobov** · 2023-03-26 21:32 UTC

you can extend interface to add more things

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-27 01:27 UTC

The world seems divided on this.

- [TypeScript documentation](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/everyday-types.html#differences-between-type-aliases-and-interfaces): “If you would like a heuristic, use **`interface`** until you need to use features from `type`.”
- [`@typescript-eslint/strict` default](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/consistent-type-definitions): **`interface`**
- [XO default](https://github.com/xojs/eslint-config-xo-typescript/releases/tag/v0.52.0): **`type`**
- [Total TypeScript](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zM9UPcIyyhQ): “**`type`**s instead of `interface`s to declare most things”
- [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37233735/interfaces-vs-types-in-typescript/65948871#65948871): about as inconclusive as you’d expect

It used to be that you couldn’t declare a `class` that `implements` a `type`, but that’s [fixed](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/pull/13604) in TypeScript 2.2. It also used to be that `interface` was faster because a `type` alias was expanded to its contents too eagerly, but that’s [fixed](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-4-2/#smarter-type-alias-preservation) in TypeScript 4.2. Now the only real difference seems to be `interface` merging, which we probably never want to do (at least with our own types).

Therefore, I’m leaning weakly toward `type`, like Zixuan.

## ✔ tippy tooltip with tables

*2023-03-29 to 2023-03-31 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20tippy.20tooltip.20with.20tables/with/1536297)*

**Ishaan Singh** · 2023-03-29 11:57 UTC

Hi,
Not sure if this has been pointed out earlier, but tippy-tooltips are cut in UI when applied to an element in a table with only 1 row.
I suspect this has something to do with the `zIndex` setting, but need to explore further.

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c7/wU1tMeS5oxv1D5yJVxtjW1PS/image.png)

Seen when playing around with [GH-24666](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/24666).
[Link to specific thread](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/24666#pullrequestreview-1358949738)

**Hardik Dharmani** · 2023-03-29 15:15 UTC

(replying to Ishaan Singh)
> Hi, Not sure if this has been pointed out earlier, but tippy-tooltips are cut in UI when applied to an element in a table with only 1 row. I suspect this has something to do with the `zIndex` setting, but need to explore further. [image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c7/wU1tMeS5oxv1D5yJVxtjW1PS/image.png) See …

Generally, Tippy tooltips have a very high z-index, typically 9999. Therefore, I don't think the problem is related to the z-index. It is more likely that the Tippy tooltip is being appended to the parent element and not to the body. In this case, the parent element is a table, and the Tippy tooltip may be getting clipped by the boundaries of the parent element.

**Ishaan Singh** · 2023-03-30 20:54 UTC

Aaha, I will play around with the `appendTo` prop and report. Thanks!

**Ishaan Singh** · 2023-03-31 06:01 UTC

(replying to Ishaan Singh)
> Aaha, I will play around with the `appendTo` prop and report. Thanks!

Discovered this in tippyjs.js  
And yep, `appendTo` was the real problem as it is set to `parent` by default.
```js
delegate("body", {
    target: ".button-class",
    appendTo: () => document.querySelector(".desired-parent-class"),
});
```

**Notification Bot** · 2023-03-31 06:01 UTC

@Ishaan Singh has marked this topic as resolved.

## popovers migration to tippy

*2023-03-31 to 2023-09-25 · 25 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/popovers.20migration.20to.20tippy/with/1538280)*

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-03-31 10:44 UTC

Hello everyone! While it may be late, I believe it would be beneficial to create a dedicated thread for migration discussions. This would allow us to thoroughly discuss all aspects related to the popovers migration to `tippy` and the framework we are currently working on in `popover_menus`.

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-03-31 10:47 UTC

To begin with, I would like to gather your thoughts on the `get_starred_messages_popover` and `get_topic_menu_popover` kind of functions in `popover_menus`. Do you believe it is necessary to have these interfaces for users of the `popover_menus` API? Alternatively, should we allow them to use `popover_instances` and make their own decisions regarding how to handle the popovers? I am interested in hearing your opinions on this matter. 

I would like to suggest including @Aman (amanagr), @Palash Baderia , @Tim Abbott  in this discussion, as you guys have relevant background knowledge on the topic being discussed.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-03-31 12:25 UTC

Would it be better to add something like `popover_menus.hide_popover("starred_message")` and let that function handle it instead of returning the whole `popover_instances`.

**Palash Baderia** · 2023-03-31 12:30 UTC

The current implementation uses `popover_menus.get_topic_menu_popover()?.hide()` to hide the popover. This makes more logical sense, but I am not sure what dangers there could be in using this for every popover.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-31 18:00 UTC

I would expect that basically the only code outside the popover's own implementation that should need to access any state of the popover is (1) things like the keyboard UI logic, which we've already mostly made part of the `popover_menus` library itself and (2) code to hide popovers (often when processing some live-update that might obsolete the popover's state).

So an API like `popover_menus.hide_popover("starred_messages")` seems OK. I don't think it's ideal in that passing the identify of the popover as a string doesn't make it easy for the type-checker to verify whether we have a typo (e.g. typing `starred_message` instead might fail only at runtime). But that's a manageable issue.

## starred_messages.js import cycle

*2023-04-04 to 2023-04-08 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/starred_messages.2Ejs.20import.20cycle/with/1541235)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-04 19:09 UTC

I happened to be reading `starred_messages.js` today, and it's definitely a simple import cycle:
```
import * as message_store from "./message_store";    
import {page_params} from "./page_params";           
import * as popover_menus from "./popover_menus";    
import * as top_left_corner from "./top_left_corner";
import {user_settings} from "./user_settings";       
```

Basically, the module does two things -- it maintains a data structure keeping track of the client's understanding of starred messages, and it also triggers rerendering UI across the app when those change (which is why it imports the last 3 things, which very likely recursively import it). I'm not sure what the cleanest way to cut this is, but one option would be to just split into a `starred_messages_data.js` module that just does the data work that other modules need to import, and a `starred_message_ui.js` module that does the rerendering part, and gets imported by other modules.

**Satyam Bansal** · 2023-04-05 06:08 UTC

Yeah, it worked, moving the function `rerender_ui` to `starred_message_ui` and then calling that function after every call of any data function that is present in`starred_messages_data` fixes the circular dependency b/w `starred_messages.js` and `popover_menus.js`.

**Lalit** · 2023-04-08 15:29 UTC

(replying to Satyam Bansal)
> Yeah, it worked, moving the function `rerender_ui` to `starred_message_ui` and then calling that function after every call of any data function that is present in`starred_messages_data` fixes the circular dependency b/w `starred_messages.js` and `popover_menus.js`.

But according to my understanding a data module should never import an UI module, right?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-08 23:59 UTC

Generally that's correct, though the starred messages module may be badly named; it doesn't have much UI in it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-04-06 20:58 UTC

There’s no `istanbul ignore throw`. In this case the way to ignore it would be to `istanbul ignore if` before the branch. [Documentation](https://github.com/gotwarlost/istanbul/blob/master/ignoring-code-for-coverage.md#the-interface).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-04-06 21:05 UTC

Some relevant libraries: [minimalistic-assert](https://www.npmjs.com/package/minimalistic-assert), [@sindresorhus/is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sindresorhus/is), [tiny-invariant](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tiny-invariant), [ts-invariant](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ts-invariant), [nullthrows](https://www.npmjs.com/package/nullthrows), [typed-assert](https://www.npmjs.com/package/typed-assert).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-04-06 21:06 UTC

The function we need is [very small](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-3-7.html#assertion-functions).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-07 03:22 UTC

I'm happy to defer to you on which assert function we grab.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-04-07 04:37 UTC

They all have their own quirks. minimalistic-assert needs a separate types package, @sindresorhus/is has too many functions and doesn’t look tree shakable, tiny-invariant and ts-invariant take a message but don’t print it in production mode, nullthrows is for a slightly different problem, typed-assert needs three layers of wrapper functions to get to the point.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-04-07 04:38 UTC

Probably minimalistic-assert is the best option, and we happen to already have it in the tree, likely for the same reason that it’s the most popular. nullthrows is maybe also worth pulling in if we have that problem.

That's the wrong fix. A few general points:
* Thanks for bringing this up -- generally we should avoid contorting code because of a linter -- we control the linters, and it's worth discussing and figuring out a way to make them support a happy codebase.
* Generally we should not rename things when importing them.

The right fix is to just change this block in `custom_check.py` to have `include_only` of `web/tests` -- the linter warning is intended only for the node tests, and so we should scope it as such.

```
        {                                                        
            "pattern": r"assert\(",                              
            "description": "Use 'assert.ok' instead of 'assert'. 
 be confused with 'assert.equal'.",                              
            "good_lines": ["assert.ok(...)"],                    
            "bad_lines": ["assert(...)"],                        
        },                                                       
```

This is happening because the `reference` of the tooltip is being removed from DOM before the tooltip is displayed, causing tippy to lose track of it altogether. Also, the `reference` is removed from DOM without any user action which seems like more probable cause of the bug.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-04-07 02:47 UTC

We need to use the `hide_tooltip_if_reference_removed` method for the tooltip here.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-04-07 02:47 UTC

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-04-07 02:54 UTC

I think this is a correct moment to audit all the tooltips which use `appendTo: () => document.body` and can be removed from DOM without any user action or the reference can be removed before the tooltip is displayed. Then, use `MutationObserver` to remove it from the DOM.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-04-07 02:56 UTC

Another potential solution is to directly look for stray tooltips on every DOM change, but that seems like an expensive fix.

**Palash Baderia** · 2023-04-07 11:08 UTC

Thanks for pointing out the source. However, I figured out that we can simply add a simple if condition inside `onShow` to check if the reference element is present in the DOM or not and prevent the other tooltip from appearing. Do you still suggest using `hide_tooltip_if_reference_removed` method to implement `mutationObserver`? To my knowledge, it keeps on checking for the DOM changes to that respective reference. However, in this case, we just need to check once if the reference is present or not just before the tooltip appears.

```js
 delegate("body", {
        target: ".view_user_card_tooltip",
        content: $t({
            defaultMessage: "View user card (u)",
        }),
        delay: LONG_HOVER_DELAY,
        onShow(instance) {
            if (!document.body.contains(instance.reference)) {
                return false;
            }
        },
        appendTo: () => document.body,
    });
```

**Lalit** · 2023-04-17 08:06 UTC

@Junyao Chen  I think we can shorten up `narrow_hooks` little bit, I had something like this in my mind:
```typescript
export const register_hook = (scope: string, hook: Hook): void => {
    const hook_name = hook.name;
    narrow_hooks.set(`${scope}.${hook_name}`, hook);
};

export const call_hook = (name: string, ...args: unknown[]): unknown => {
    const hook = narrow_hooks.get(name);

    if (hook === undefined) {
        blueslip.error(`Unknown narrow hook: ${name}`);
        return undefined;
    }

    return hook(...args);
};

```

* The `popovers.js` module has a lot of import cycles built into it. * The `compose` and `compose_actions` modules don't have clear definitions/interfaces and thus are hopelessly tangled with each other. `compose_state` and `compose_recipient` are also entangled due to the work on the new compose box switcher, but I suspect that is not going to be super hard to solve, and https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/25785 will likely make this easier.
* The `narrow.js` module has a bunch of hooks that it runs on both narrowing and unnarrowing that should become a hooks system. I think probably we might want to do some of the work described in #23812 of making those hooks the same set of functions for narrowing and unnarrowing (possibly with different parameters), and then register them as on-view-change hooks of some sort. 
* The `settings_org` module has two different classes of things in it -- the common code for save/discard widgets, and the specific code for the "organization settings" and "organization permissions" panels. It will need some refactoring; probably the most useful first thing to do is rework how it keeps track of what dropdown_list_widget objects correspond to what objects. I don't think any action on this makes sense right now other than keeping this in mind when @Aman (amanagr) works on porting these to the replacement `dropdown_widget` module.

But I expect it'll usually be pretty quick for a maintainer to resolve.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 19:14 UTC

I can't entirely shake the feeling that perhaps it's a failure of the tooling that import cycles are a constraint that is worth spending time on; I still don't love the way the `on_narrow_to_recipient` style callback-passing thing we've had to do in like a dozen places works from a readability standpoint. 

But ultimately 85% of the actual time spent here was moving code breaking apart modules in ways that improve our abstraction boundaries, and I feel like basically all of that effort was fixing misplaced code, the aggregate impact of which is material in making the codebase harder to read. So I don't think it is important whether some fancier tooling could have made import cycles not a thing to avoid.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-10-10 19:17 UTC

Well fundamentally, the tooling failure is that we’re writing in a dynamic imperative language where the only way to define anything is by mutating a variable, and that mutation happens at some point in time that needs to be after those points for its dependencies.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-10-10 19:26 UTC

If you imagine fancier tooling that’s able to interleave your definitions along finer-than-module boundaries to break cycles, that would destroy the ordering semantics that JS developers rely on.

*2023-04-07 to 2023-04-28 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/tooltip.20opens.20on.20click/with/1543068)*

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-04-07 14:30 UTC

While working on the `message_control_button`s, I discovered that tooltips were sometimes opening on click (see the attached GIF). I believe this is caused by the default trigger value in Tippy, which is set to "mouseover focus". Therefore, when we click, the element gets focused and the tooltip appears. The crux of the issue is that previously, you could start composing a message using the `c` keyboard shortcut (planning to start a new topic, but in a different stream from what you're looking at). That opens the compose box with the topic input focused. From there:
* From the topic input, pressing `Shift` + `Tab` moves focus to the stream input
* You start typing `fr`, and hit `Enter` or `Tab` to select `frontend` as the stream via the typeahead

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-18 16:56 UTC

* Hit Shift+Tab to move focus to the stream dropdown_list_widget. Nothing tells you that this worked -- but we could fix this with a proper focus outline on the element.
* Then you have to hit `Enter` to open the stream picker. If you starting typing the stream name, the `fr` get processed as keyboard shortcuts; and depending what those letters are, you might randomly get navigated.
* Then you type `fr`, and can hit `Enter` to select `frontend`. (`Tab` does the same thing as `Down`, namely moving you to the first item).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-18 01:35 UTC

@Aman (amanagr) cool, I understand the reproducer, but I don't understand how the change in the PR is the right fix. I have a few notes:
* One observation is that we probably should just replace `message_live_update.rerender_messages_view_by_message_ids` with something that just changed the display for whether messages as shown as read, like we do for marking messages as read, which uses this function:

```
    show_message_as_read(message, options) {                                                                   
        const $row = this.get_row(message.id);                                                                 
        if (options.from === "pointer" || options.from === "server") {                                         
            $row.find(".unread_marker").addClass("fast_fade");                                                 
        } else {                                                                                               
            $row.find(".unread_marker").addClass("slow_fade");                                                 
        }                                                                                                      
        $row.removeClass("unread");                                                                            
    }                                                                                                          
```

I think changing that would save a bunch of wasted resources being spent rerendering messages, and allow us to do animations if we want to, while fixing this bug as a side effect.

* The second bug is I think that rather than calling `this.list.select_id(message_container.msg.id);`, we should be using this function, which passes the "this is a silent rerender" parameters to `this.select_id`.

```
    reselect_selected_id() {                                                                                   
        const selected_id = this.data.selected_id();                                                           
                                                                                                               
        if (selected_id !== -1) {                                                                              
            this.select_id(this.data.selected_id(), {from_rendering: true, mark_read: false});                 
        }                                                                                                      
    }                                                                                                          
```

* Probably there's a missing check for the message list being the current one somewhere; I think it's possible the place you've put it is the right one, but we might need a comment that "Reselecting the currently selected message is a noop in a message list that is not currently displayed", which I think will become true once we've done the above.

## home_msg_list architecture

*2023-04-21 to 2023-04-21 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/home_msg_list.20architecture/with/1552963)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:31 UTC

So in #25120 (making "All messages" display unmuted topics), we're bumping into with an architectural complication with how `home_msg_list` is designed that I'd like to talk through.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:34 UTC

In general, narrows are defined using `Filters` aka the set of search operators for the narrow, which are used by the web app to decide things like "If a new message comes in, should it be appended to this message". So, at present, `home_msg_list` is defined using the `in:home` `Filter` that is defined as "messages that mention me or are not in a muted stream". A version of the change that we need to make for unmuted topics is to change that `in:home` definition to be "messages that mention me or are in an unmuted topic or are not in a muted stream".

Doing that change itself is straightforward.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:34 UTC

What gets complicated is how to live-update the state when a topic is changed from being muted to unmuted.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:37 UTC

First, to explain how we handle muted topics and muted users, it's actually a different mechanism; in every message list that aren't supposed to show muted topics, we maintain an `_all_items` that is all messages matching the message list's `Filter`, and a second `_items` that is computed from `_all_items` by removing messages that are affected by those forms of muting. This is a nice architecture because in the event that topic/user muting status changes, we can live-update the message feed locally by just recalculating `_items` from `_all_items`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:38 UTC

That approach doesn't work for `home_msg_list`, because if you unmute a previously muted stream, whatever messages are in that previously muted stream aren't present in `_all_items` either, since they didn't match the `Filter`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:43 UTC

So instead we do a different thing, which is that we have a lengthy custom function in `stream_muting.js` that recalculates `_all_items `from `message_lists.all`, a parallel `MessageListData` structure that contains a contiguous block of all recent messages (and is used for Recent Conversations; etc. see #**frontend>fetching message history** for some background). I think it's in practice about as expensive as the code path for adjusting muted topics; so the main problem with this different workflow is that it's a near-duplicate complex piece of logic.

Previously, that function would only be called when toggling whether a stream is muted, a rare operation. But with "unmute topics", now we will likely need to do this operation every time someone unmute a topic. It's a bit annoying to check just because the API doesn't tell you what to do, and #25120 makes the mistake of actually doing both rerenders for `home_msg_list`, which can be readily fixed but reflects the fact that this is an unfortunate way for things to be set up.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:44 UTC

I guess given that the `home_msg_list` rerender is about equally expensive as `update_muting_and_rerender` (the nicer code path for changing topic muting), probably for integrating #25120, just calling the version that supports stream muting is probably the right plan.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:46 UTC

But I guess I'm left wondering whether the right longer-term fix would be to make the `in:home` Filter actually do nothing at the "filtering messages for addition to _all_items", do the "muted streams" filtering inside the `_all_items => _items` function (presumably it'd be a flag on the `MessageList` data structure whether to do this), and use that to basically merge `message_lists.home` and `message_lists.all`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:52 UTC

Sigh, I've mixed up names a decent amount above due to finger memory; the things are actually called:
* `message_lists.home` (used to be `home_msg_list`, and that's still in my finger memory)
* `all_messages_data` (used to be `all_msg_list` and `message_lists.all`).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:54 UTC

Anyway I think that's probably a good idea and would let us delete a lot of complexity -- `message_fetch.js` is way harder to read because of all the exceptions related to the tangling of `message_lists.home` and `all_messages_data`. 

We'd be replacing that complexity with quirks like `Filter.predicate` for `in:home` now matching every message; but I don't think that would even impact how anything is displayed at all, because we'll be dropping the extra messages in the `_all_items` => `_items` calculation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 19:54 UTC

So I don't think I even see a significant downside to doing so.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 20:03 UTC

I think I can probably eliminate the semi-duplicate stream muting code path with a simple `if` statement at least, without changing the `Filter` logic; I think I'll do that to try to integrate a version of #25120.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-21 20:24 UTC

OK, updated #25120 with that change, which works great and is quite satisfying.

## moving message when anchor is not available with client

*2023-04-24 to 2023-04-24 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/moving.20message.20when.20anchor.20is.20not.20available.20with.20client/with/1553818)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-04-24 11:35 UTC

While working on #21817, I noticed a bug where the message list is not updated correctly when moving message in case when anchor message is not available locally with the client.

This happens when user tries to move all messages in the topic without having permission to do so due to time limit. In such case, if user is allowed to move some of the messages, the server sents the new message ID to be used as the anchor when making the request from the confirmation modal. And this new message ID may not be available with the client locally.

The events handling code returns and does nothing if the message is not available locally with the client as per the [code here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/src/message_events.js#L181).

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-04-24 14:36 UTC

I am trying to find a solution to fix this probably by re-narrowing to the topic. But not sure, will update after I reach to a conclusion.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-24 19:40 UTC

@Sahil Batra good find! I think the bug is actually just that the check at the top of that function is only correct for content edits.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-24 19:43 UTC

I think probably just removing that line, and instead having it be guarding a block for whether to do anything for the `content_edited` part of the code path would be the right refactor to fix this, and maybe some later ones that might need a check for whether there's any messages to rerender?

I think the main reason that `get_item` exists is to deal with live updates.  Let's say that you are using ListWidget to manage users, and then I change my name from "Steve" to "Stephen".  If `ListWidget` has its own copy of users, then I will continue to be called "Steve".  If it does a bit more lazy rendering with `get_item` (and the whole point of the widget is to be kind of lazy), then you will get "Stephen".

## narrow via message header click handler

*2023-05-03 to 2023-05-09 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/narrow.20via.20message.20header.20click.20handler/with/1560779)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-03 12:04 UTC

So, for context, this is related to work I'm doing on **Topic link in search results should always go to "near:" narrow**, #21216.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-03 12:04 UTC

Looking at how we update the view when clicking on either the stream, topic or direct message recipients in the message header, we use `get_row_id_for_narrowing` in `/web/src/click_handlers.js` to pick the message ID for the `target_id` we pass to the narrow `activate`.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-03 12:04 UTC

```js
    function get_row_id_for_narrowing(narrow_link_elem) {
        const $group = rows.get_closest_group(narrow_link_elem);
        const msg_id = rows.id_for_recipient_row($group);

        const nearest = message_lists.current.get(msg_id);
        const selected = message_lists.current.selected_message();
        if (util.same_recipient(nearest, selected)) {
            return selected.id;
        }
        return nearest.id;
    }
```

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-03 12:04 UTC

In the last part of that function, we compare the nearest message (the one closest to the message header) with the selected message for the same recipient. This makes a lot of sense for views that collapse recipients as often the user is clicking on the message header for the selected message (e.g. a stream view or all direct messages view).

But for search-like views (e.g. is starred or keyword search with stream and topic), this can be confusing since every message in the view has a message header to click on, and it's pretty easy to click on the message header for a message that's not selected by the blue box, but could easily be in the same conversation due to the search criteria.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-03 12:05 UTC

I'm thinking that adding a check for `message_lists.current.view.collapse_messages` with `util.same_recipient(nearest, selected)` would help avoid this occasionally confusing situation.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-05-03 20:57 UTC

I see what happened. Terser has optimized

```js
            const stream_id = this.bucketer.reverse_lookup.get(message_id);
            const stream_bucketer = this.bucketer.get_bucket(stream_id);
            const topic = stream_bucketer.reverse_lookup.get(message_id);
```

to

```js
   const o=this.bucketer.reverse_lookup.get(e),t=this.bucketer.get_bucket(o).reverse_lookup.get(e);
// 1------------------------------------------1332--------------------------23--------------------3
```

where the second line has been inlined into the third, and the source map reflects this. The browser reports an error for the expression `this.bucketer.get_bucket(o).reverse_lookup`, and the starting location of this expression is source-mapped to the second line.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-05-04 19:54 UTC

Hi Everyone -- I'm picking up #25403, which raises the need to localize times in the scheduling modal (e.g., "Tomorrow at 9:00 AM").

At least at present, there are two things to note:

1) The days as listed in the modal are relative ("Today", "Tomorrow"), with the exception of "Monday" (which is being added in #25427, but which will be a hard-coded value, I think)
2) The actual date is, in this part of the interface, irrelevant. What needs localization is just the time string.

If I'm reading the `get_localized_date_or_time_for_format()` defined in `timerender.ts` correctly, it looks like it expects an actual Date object. So I'm wondering how to just fudge the date part (e.g., `1970-01-01` in order to get the correct time part--so essentially `new Date('1970-01-01T09:00:00')` when I just need to localize the hour.

I'm also wondering if there's already a better solution for this, or if I'm overthinking or misthinking here :) Thank you!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-05-04 20:14 UTC

There is an actual date of “Tomorrow at 9:00 AM”, even if it’s not being displayed. Use the actual date in the computation, rather than trying to do something with a fake date that will fail in corner cases like daylight saving time transitions.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-05-04 20:17 UTC

that’s a really good point about DST, Anders. Thank you

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-05-05 15:52 UTC

(replying to Steve Howell)
> I **think** for the latter part of your description, the idea is that the code assumes this invariant: **If historical is false, we must have done a complete fetch of the entire topic history.**

I don't think so. The below code for `stream_topic_history.add_or_update` is called for each message fetched from the server and on recieving a message event from `message_helper.process_new_message`. So, we set `historical` as `false` after receivng first message of the topic.
```js
add_or_update({topic_name, message_id = 0}) {
        message_id = Number.parseInt(message_id, 10);
        this.update_stream_max_message_id(message_id);

        const existing = this.topics.get(topic_name);

        if (!existing) {
            this.topics.set(topic_name, {
                message_id,
                pretty_name: topic_name,
                historical: false,
                count: 1,
            });
            return;
        }

        if (!existing.historical) {
            existing.count += 1;
        }

        if (message_id > existing.message_id) {
            existing.message_id = message_id;
            existing.pretty_name = topic_name;
        }
}
```

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-01-24 06:55 UTC

> We have this corner case of "If the latest message in a topic is deleted / moved, we now may not know what's the new latest". I think in most cases -- we in fact do know because we have that topic in all_messages_data and has_found_newest and we can look it up there.
The `all_messages_data` dataset  contains 1200 messages after the initial fetch. And then the messages are added in two cases - if a new message is received after the initial fetch and if the user scrolls up in the `All messages` view. We do not add the messages to `all_messages_data` dataset in many cases like if we narrow to a old topic whose messages were not in the latest 1200 messages. 

And there is a bug when moving or deleting messages, due to this behavior of `all_messages_data` and it being used to get messages in topic in `get_messages_in_topic`. I am sharing the code below, the problem here is that if I move/delete only the latest message from a old topic by narrowing to that topic, the `all_messages_data` might not have its data and thus `message_util.get_messages_in_topic` returns an empty list and the `message_id` is set to 0. 

```js
export function remove_messages(opts: {
    stream_id: number;
    topic_name: string;
    num_messages: number;
    max_removed_msg_id: number;
}): void {
    const stream_id = opts.stream_id;
    const topic_name = opts.topic_name;
    const num_messages = opts.num_messages;
    const max_removed_msg_id = opts.max_removed_msg_id;
    const history = stream_dict.get(stream_id);

    // This is the special case of "removing" a message from
    // a topic, which happens when we edit topics.

    if (!history) {
        return;
    }

    // This is the normal case of an incoming message.
    history.maybe_remove(topic_name, num_messages);

    const existing_topic = history.topics.get(topic_name);
    if (!existing_topic) {
        return;
    }

    // Update max_message_id in topic
    if (existing_topic.message_id <= max_removed_msg_id) {
        const msgs_in_topic = message_util.get_messages_in_topic(stream_id, topic_name);
        let max_message_id = 0;
        for (const msg of msgs_in_topic) {
            if (msg.id > max_message_id) {
                max_message_id = msg.id;
            }
        }
        existing_topic.message_id = max_message_id;
    }

    // Update max_message_id in stream
    if (history.max_message_id <= max_removed_msg_id) {
        history.max_message_id = message_util.get_max_message_id_in_stream(stream_id);
    }
}
```

```javascript

    tomorrow_four_pm: {
        text: $t(
            {defaultMessage: "Tomorrow at {time}"},

```javascript

then the modal renders 24-hour times as expected. So that means my issue here is down to the values for the text strings for the modal being rendered before the user-settings value for `twenty_four_hour_time` is available.

@Karl Stolley I think the bug is caused by a thing I posted about -- which is that you're doing this check at module load time, which is before `page_params` is populated.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-05 17:46 UTC

In general we never want to run any real code at module import time, which this kinda qualifies as -- code we want to run once during app startup should always be in an `initialize` method so that our initialization order is explicit.

All right. I think this actually comes down to a bug I introduced yesterday, in  #25449. The issue is that `flatpickr` get set with a minimum date five minutes in the future, starting from when someone clicks the 'Custom time' option in the popover.

The function I wrote yesterday, `is_send_later_timestamp_missing_or_expired()`, determines expiration based on whether there are less than five minutes between the current time and the timestamp. The idea there was to not offer to reschedule a previously scheduled message within the popover. 

So you can see the issue: any time Flatpickr returns its minimum time, set on the Flatpickr `minDate` option, the logic I wrote will always consider that minimum date expired for the purpose of rendering the success banner in the compose box.

## is_common_narrow rewrite

*2023-05-12 to 2023-09-01 · 38 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/is_common_narrow.20rewrite/with/1568064)*

**Syed Rafat** · 2023-05-12 16:21 UTC

`is_common_narrow` is a method of Filter in `web/src/filter.js`  The comment down below describes what it does.

as [TODO mentions](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/fe54df0b01569f2442bfe09800d8398d25ae36af/web/src/filter.js#LL564C1-L564C1), piggy backing on `can_mark_messages_read` is causing some bugs to appear when extra filters are added to can_mark_messages_read in this pr #25351 as reviewed by @Lauryn Menard  . So we need to **rewrite is_common_narrow** and I need suggestion on what should be done.  

```javascript
    // This is used to control the behaviour for "exiting search",
    // given the ability to flip between displaying the search bar and the narrow description in UI
    // here we define a narrow as a "common narrow" on the basis of
    // https://paper.dropbox.com/doc/Navbar-behavior-table--AvnMKN4ogj3k2YF5jTbOiVv_AQ-cNOGtu7kSdtnKBizKXJge
    // common narrows show a narrow description and allow the user to
    // close search bar UI and show the narrow description UI.
    //
    // TODO: We likely will want to rewrite this to not piggy-back on
    // can_mark_messages_read, since that might gain some more complex behavior
    // with near: narrows.
    is_common_narrow() {

        // can_mark_messages_read tests the following filters:
        // stream, stream + topic,
        // is: dm, dm,
        // is: mentioned, is: resolved

        // that leaves us with checking:
        // is: starred
        // (which can_mark_messages_read_does not check as starred messages are always read)

        if (this.can_mark_messages_read()) {
            return true;
        }

        const term_types = this.sorted_term_types();


        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["is-starred"])) {
            return true;
        }
        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["streams-public"])) {
            return true;
        }
        return false;
```

**Syed Rafat** · 2023-05-12 16:27 UTC

I propose a solution: 

* We add `initial_filters_for_mark_messages` method which has only the filters that work with `is_common_narrow` and 

* we then extend the `initial_filters_for_mark_messages` in the `calc_can_mark_messages_read`

**Syed Rafat** · 2023-05-12 16:29 UTC

```javascript
initial_filters_for_mark_messages_read() {
        const term_types = this.sorted_term_types();

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["stream", "topic"])) {
            return true;
        }

    }

    calc_can_mark_messages_read() {

        if (this.initial_filters_for_mark_messages_read()) {
            return true
        }

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["not-is-dm"])) {
            return true;
        }

        return false;
    }
```

**Syed Rafat** · 2023-05-12 16:32 UTC

```javascript
is_common_narrow() {
        if (this.initial_filters_for_mark_messages_read) {
            return true
        }
```

        }

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["stream"])) {
            return true;
        }

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["is-dm"])) {
            return true;
        }

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, ["is-resolved"])) {
            return true;
        }

        if (_.isEqual(term_types, [])) {
            // All view
            return true;
        }

        if (term_types.length === 1 && ["in-home", "in-all"].includes(term_types[0])) {
            return true;
        }
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-06-22 13:10 UTC

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-22 21:00 UTC

An `assert` function does not return true or false. It raises an exception if the provided condition fails. That allows the following code to rely on the condition having succeeded, without additional checks and branches.

> This logic used to be in extract_people_from_message(), but

Is this still the case now?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-06-29 22:41 UTC

It also seems that its use case drifted away from handling deactivated users, to users being missing in the absence of the events system. According to this [comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/8e63c0e42c8b948b64b00bfbf7e711b1c41814d8/web/src/people.js#L1274-L1286):
```javascript
export function report_late_add(user_id, email) {
    // If the events system is not running, then it is expected that
    // we will fetch messages from the server that were sent by users
    // who don't exist in our users data set. This can happen because
    // we're in the middle of a reload (and thus stopped our event
    // queue polling) or because we are a spectator and never had an
    // event queue in the first place.
    if (reload_state.is_in_progress() || page_params.is_spectator) {
        blueslip.log("Added user late", {user_id, email});
    } else {
        blueslip.warn("Added user late", {user_id, email});
    }
}
```

Ideally we'd have access to the height and width of the images and represent those as `height` and `width` attributes on the image tag (that might be a limitation of the markdown processor too, though). Combined with some clever CSS, that ought to be enough to placehold space for images.

The markdown doesn't know the image size.  It could also change after we do the Markdown -> HTML conversion, and we write the HTML into the database, so we can't really do this on the markup side.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-05-19 13:38 UTC

(replying to Vlad Korobov)
> Can you recommend a screen reader or multiple that I should try? Which one is your favorite?

If you're on MacOS, try experimenting with [the VoiceOver rotor](https://support.apple.com/guide/voiceover/with-the-voiceover-rotor-mchlp2719/mac). The rotor is a very good bridge technology for sighted users to approach what it's like to use a screen reader--and it will help catch a good number of accessibility problems.

And although it has some flaws, the [Firefox Accessibility Inspector](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/accessibility_inspector/) is a good companion tool when it comes to teasing out accessibility issues at the code level. It's not an accessible technology itself, the way the VoiceOver rotor is, but it provides some additional insight as to how HTML in particular is made available (or not) to assistive technologies--including things like [ARIA roles](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles) and [accessible names](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/).

## date rendering performance

*2023-05-22 to 2023-05-22 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/date.20rendering.20performance/with/1573907)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-05-22 04:28 UTC

We are spending 10 to 15% of initial load time on rendering date and most of the time is consumed by this function:
```js
// Given an Date object 'time', return a DOM node that initially
// displays the human-formatted date, and is updated automatically as
// necessary (e.g. changing "Today" to "Yesterday" to "Jul 1").

// (What's actually spliced into the message template is the contents
// of this DOM node as HTML, so effectively a copy of the node. That's
// okay since to update the time later we look up the node by its id.)
export function render_date(time: Date, today: Date): JQuery {
    const className = `timerender${next_timerender_id}`;
    next_timerender_id += 1;
    const rendered_time = render_now(time, today);
    let $node = $("<span>").attr("class", className);
    $node = render_date_span($node, rendered_time);
    maybe_add_update_list_entry({
        needs_update: rendered_time.needs_update,
        className,
        time,
    });
    return $node;
}
```

We should look into optimizing it. Just opening a thread so that I can track it and start discussion on it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-05-30 01:07 UTC

(For context, I discovered this vulnerability on Wednesday, and kept it private until we were ready to make a security release, per our usual policy.)

The challenge with Zulip is not that we’re lacking in ways to escape things safely. The challenge is to *avoid* introducing patterns that might be *misused* by new contributors, who are often copying and pasting the existing code and tweaking it just enough to get it working for their example input, and might not be thinking about or even aware of the security vulnerabilities they might be introducing for other inputs.

This is especially difficult in the presence of Handlebars, which generates raw HTML strings without specially wrapping them in any way, and jQuery, which accepts raw HTML strings that are not specially wrapped in any way. This patch is not a perfect solution. However, reducing the number of distinct patterns makes it somewhat more likely that deviations will stick out.

And, again, just like for jQuery, my opinions on this were pretty well-formed by experiences even prior to 2013, and I just had to do everything I could do to be a good soldier. **Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 02:03 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 03:01 UTC

I honestly think that templates are more insidious than jQuery.  jQuery is just a wrapper library.  Templates, on the other hand, totally defeat any kind of mindset where you want to have composable components.  And templates reinforce the ancient paradigm that every website is a document, instead of actually being an application, and that's why templates don't do anything to defeat cross-site-scripting attacks.  The natural way to avoid cross-site-scripting attacks is to get **away** from the document mindset.

*2023-05-26 to 2023-06-01 · 204 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/resize.20undo.20redo.20condense/with/1578081)*

**Evy** · 2023-05-26 22:57 UTC

This is what it looks like on CZO right now when resizing a window with collapsed messages. It looks like we have some code that recalculates if a message should be collapsed every time the window changes size, and uncollapses and recollapses the message in that process. 

I think it would b better to do nothing than do what we're doing right now. Maybe we can do some invisible rendering and measuring, but it feels a lot nicer to only recalculate this when a message is rendered and maybe when resizing hits a breakpoint. Thoughts?

[Kapture-2023-05-26-at-15.54.59.gif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f5/o3MC_kKXjK_T8mx1BdcdodFa/Kapture-2023-05-26-at-15.54.59.gif)

The `condense_and_collapse` loop looks like a textbook case of [layout thrashing](https://web.dev/avoid-large-complex-layouts-and-layout-thrashing/#avoid-layout-thrashing) when the height cache is cleared (which the `resize` handler does).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-05-27 03:37 UTC

No we should fix them not to thrash.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-05-27 05:55 UTC

The fix for any layout thrashing problem is to reorder the read-write-read-write-read-write DOM operation pattern to do all the reads first, and then all the writes. (To anyone working on the frontend, if this doesn’t make sense to you, you should take the time to understand the article I linked above, because this is a non-obvious but very important performance detail.)

* (next resize)
* height is big, so we condense it

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 22:45 UTC

(replying to Evy)
> Steve, can you share why you want to turn off the caches?

They're just an extra moving part that makes problems like this really difficult to debug, and it's just another failure point.  As @Anders Kaseorg alluded to earlier (and I will let him put it in his own words if I am mis-paraphrasing), the only reason that these caches exist is because earlier developers mis-diagnosed performance issues.  The functions that are being cached here are probably super fast.  The only reason not to call them is to avoid layout thrashing.  And we want to be smart about avoiding layout thrashing, which in this particular case is just a matter of splitting up a loop.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:03 UTC

Figuring out the height of the screen should be **incredibly** cheap, and we have to invalidate that cache during `resize`, so it's not like we get tremendous benefit from it.

And then caching the size of messages leads to problems like we may forget to invalidate the cache after you edit a message.

In general people resort to caching way too much.  Usually you can avoid caches by identifying simpler performance solutions that don't have nearly as many negative tradeoffs.  Lift stuff out of a loop.  Batch up your reads before doing writes.  Tune a query.  Etc. etc. etc.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:11 UTC

Going back to layout thrashing, I would point out that the techniques in the article that Anders pointed us to for web development apply equally well on the backend.  It's not perfectly analogous, but it's also true on the backend that you generally want to do a lot of the read-related steps before any writes.  It just ends up being cleaner for reasons that are kind of subtle, but which I believe to be very true.  And it also narrows the window when you are actually doing things like possibly holding locks on the database.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:12 UTC

And both Python and JS/TS have evolved in a way that the mechanics of doing this are a lot easier.  You can build up little intermediate objects in a type-safe natural kind of way while you are doing all the read processing, and then you just finally pass them to a function to do the write steps.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:23 UTC

To put the advice in a general way: **Try your best not to interleave reads and writes.**

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:33 UTC

Re-linking the article for convenience: https://web.dev/avoid-large-complex-layouts-and-layout-thrashing/#avoid-layout-thrashing

**Steve Howell** · 2023-05-30 23:39 UTC

BTW we should also replace `$.fn.height` with DOM APIs.  There are probably several places in the resize/viewport code where it would just be more clear to use DOM APIs.  We already talk directly to the DOM API for certain things.

## inconsistent mark as read

*2023-05-30 to 2023-07-24 · 71 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/inconsistent.20mark.20as.20read/with/1580820)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

Okay, so debugging the behavior I can reproduce that may be the issue reported in #**issues>messages not getting marked as read**.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

What I can see / reproduce in the dev environment when:
- There are unread messages in a topic or direct message conversation
- The bottom of the topic's message feed will not be in view (due to the window size and/or the number of unreads)
- The network is not throttled
- You navigate to the topic view by either using the `N` shortcut or clicking through the topics in the left sidebar

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

In this case:
- The message fetch in `narrow.activate` returns before the timer for `message_scroll.scroll_finished` is called
- Which means the second document scroll happens and resets the timer while the value for `update_selection_on_next_scroll` is still `false`
- So, when the timer eventually calls `message_scroll.scroll_finished`, `message_viewport.keep_pointer_in_view` is not called and the selected message is not marked as read

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

But, if you throttle the network:
- The message fetch may return after the original timer has called `message_scroll.scroll_finished` and reset  `update_selection_on_next_scroll` to true
- Which means the second document scroll event sets a new timer
- And the `message_viewport.keep_pointer_in_view` is called this time and the selected message is marked as read.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

So I think, based on whether a document on scroll event resets the timer for `message_scroll.scroll_finished` or sets a new timer after the previous one has happened, will likely change our mark on read behavior.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

I don't know if the behavior we want is for the selected message to be marked as read, which only happens now when the network is bad or the message fetch from the server takes a while. Or if we want the selected message to remain unread until the user triggers a document scroll via the mouse/keyboard/etc.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 12:57 UTC

I cannot reproduce messages not being marked as read when the bottom of the message feed is visible, which did seem to be the original reports from the issue noted above. The `process_visible` call happens before the `message_scroll.scroll_finish` sets the timer for `message_scroll.scroll_finished`.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-05-30 13:10 UTC

I'll also note here that this code from `ui_init.js` is where the `update_selection_on_next_scroll` is getting set to `false` in cases where the last condition is true:

```javascript
    $(document).on("message_selected.zulip", (event) => {
        if (message_lists.current !== event.msg_list) {
            return;
        }
        if (event.id === -1) {
            // If the message list is empty, don't do anything
            return;
        }
        const $row = event.msg_list.get_row(event.id);
        $(".selected_message").removeClass("selected_message");
        $row.addClass("selected_message");

        if (event.then_scroll) {
            if ($row.length === 0) {
                const $row_from_dom = message_lists.current.get_row(event.id);
                const messages = event.msg_list.all_messages();
                blueslip.debug("message_selected missing selected row", {
                    previously_selected_id: event.previously_selected_id,
                    selected_id: event.id,
                    selected_idx: event.msg_list.selected_idx(),
                    selected_idx_exact: messages.indexOf(event.msg_list.get(event.id)),
                    render_start: event.msg_list.view._render_win_start,
                    render_end: event.msg_list.view._render_win_end,
                    selected_id_from_idx: messages[event.msg_list.selected_idx()].id,
                    msg_list_sorted: _.isEqual(
                        messages.map((message) => message.id),
                        message_lists.current
                            .all_messages()
                            .map((message) => message.id)
                            .sort(),
                    ),
                    found_in_dom: $row_from_dom.length,
                });
            }
            if (event.target_scroll_offset !== undefined) {
                message_lists.current.view.set_message_offset(event.target_scroll_offset);
            } else {
                // Scroll to place the message within the current view;
                // but if this is the initial placement of the pointer,

                message_viewport.recenter_view($row, {
                    from_scroll: event.from_scroll,
                    force_center: event.previously_selected_id === -1,
                });
            }
        }
    });
```

## tooltips for top left sidebar, #25500

*2023-06-01 to 2024-02-12 · 25 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/tooltips.20for.20top.20left.20sidebar.2C.20.2325500/with/1582412)*

**Aidan Maney** · 2023-06-01 02:01 UTC

(replying to Alya Abbott)
> > For All messages, Starred messages, and Drafts, it would probably be very useful to have title tips for those. They all look like unread counters, but the only true unread counter is for "All messages", whereas the counters for "Starred messages" and "Drafts" are just the number of messages. What …

Hi all, 

I assigned myself to the issue spawned by this comment (https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/25500) a little while ago and I've been trying out a couple different approaches but none of them behave in an acceptable manner. 

The functionality I desire is that the tooltip for the counters functions as a separate element from its parent, a left sidebar button, i.e. different trigger regions. Due to how each left sidebar counter is inscribed in its respective left sidebar button, it is possible to trigger both with one quick movement into the left sidebar counter region. The way the tooltips function as far I understand is that the triggering function is ran on the event (in these cases mouseenter) and followed up upon after a delay to check that the condition is still satisfied so destroying the overlapped tooltip is not option without having  different delays or positioning for each. If it was possible to destroy the left sidebar tooltip before the left sidebar counter tooltip begins to show, this could be mitigated (a la https://github.com/atomiks/tippyjs/issues/259) but I have found no way capture this through Tippy JS (the lifecycle hooks are limited to `onMount( )`, `onTrigger( )`, `onShow/n( )` etc.). 

The "singleton" Tippy addon looks promising because it provides delay and a common tooltip across a few elements but this addon is incompatible with the delegation addon used to generate the tooltips based on classes (as is currently done). 

I have considered using  jQuery to find and replace the contents of the parent (left sidebar button) tooltip programmatically so there is no issue of duplicate/transitioning tooltips but this would mean not using the current handlebars templating approach (with translation) and that the left sidebar counter tooltip would only be a psuedo-tooltip (e.g. using a combination of `onTrigger( )` and disabling the child tooltip before it can even show). 

Another option would be do reinvent the wheel and use eventlisteners/delays to reconstruct the desired tippy functionality and fire it but this is obviously undesirable.  

Finally, entering the left sidebar counter could be treated as exiting its inscribing element (the left sidebar button) but this would mean transiting medially from the left to right side of the left sidebar button would destroy the tooltip in the process. 

Ideally moving to the inner element (the left sidebar counter) would display the tooltip and only that tooltip after 1.5 seconds (the initial delay for `EXTRA_LONG_HOVER_DELAY` defined in `web/src/tippyjs.js`) within the bounds of this element. Moving out to the remainder of the parent element's region should hide the counter tooltip and function as if the parent was newly entered (i.e. after 1.5 seconds the tooltip would appear) and with the left sidebar tooltip active, moving back into the left sidebar counter would cleanly replace/appear to replace the existing tooltip with the new description (e.g. "Number of unread messages"). 

**My question boils down to:** is this functionality even possible without going too far outside Tippy JS and if it is not, what intermediate functionality (if any) would be acceptable (e.g. showing both tooltips but having the left sidebar counter tooltip on the bottom). 

I apologize for the lengthy message and If this in the wrong place — but I would really appreciate some guidance.

## quote-and-reply fence length

*2023-06-08 to 2023-06-08 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/quote-and-reply.20fence.20length/with/1588269)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-06-08 01:40 UTC

Here's the code (in `web/shared/src/fenced_code.ts`) for getting the right "fence" length to use in quote-and-reply:

```js
const fence_length_re = /^ {0,3}(`{3,})/gm;
export function get_unused_fence(content: string): string {
    // we only return ``` fences, not ~~~.
    let length = 3;
    let match;
    fence_length_re.lastIndex = 0;
    while ((match = fence_length_re.exec(content)) !== null) {
        length = Math.max(length, match[1].length + 1);
    }
    return "`".repeat(length);
}
```

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-06-08 01:46 UTC

So for example, if the Markdown of the message to be quoted looks like this:

&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;
code
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;

then it'll give a "quote" fence with four backticks:

&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;quote
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;
code
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;

instead of three:


&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;quote
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;
code
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;
&#x60;&#x60;&#x60;

and so on; if there's a code block with four backticks it'll use five, etc.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-06-08 01:48 UTC

I'm wondering about this part in the regex:

```
^ {0,3}
```

Why is that there? Can a multiline code block be fenced off by lines that start with one to three spaces?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-08 01:50 UTC

Yes, [in CommonMark](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.30/#fenced-code-blocks). We don’t comply with that detail currently, but any CommonMark non-compliance is a bug to be fixed at some point.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-06-08 01:51 UTC

Thank you!

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-14 14:57 UTC

I've opened #26265 -- the [previous commit](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26163/commits/342d717c8a6fda182dc629c4985d7dbe94e4c6d4) that I mentioned above no longer works because of [this commit from #25997](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/25997/commits/d7c7d022ac2d927ff658495753e0d6c0a721e718) that ensured there was no interaction gap between the avatar image and username (a regression I'd introduced otherwise).

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-14 14:59 UTC

I know it's way past time to move on from this feature, but I think #26265 is interesting because of how it demonstrates what can be achieved by carefully controlling `line-height` values. In this case, the line-height value for `.message-avatar`, which participates in the message grid, is set to match the height of the avatar image. By setting `align-self: baseline` on `.message-avatar` in a me-message context, the other grid elements (sender/message, controls, time) snap into centered alignment with the avatar, which elsewhere is ignored because of `align-self: start`, which prevents `.message-avatar` from participating in the baseline group.

To keep the actual avatar image displaying as expected with its rounded corners, etc., `.inline_profile_picture` gets *its* line-height set to 1, so as not to inherit the value from `.message-avatar`--which would have the effect of clipping the top of the image due to the top and bottom margins set on `.inline_profile_picture`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-07-15 16:55 UTC

The issue is that we're not parsing emoji with ZWJ (zero width joiner, i.e. multiple emoji joined together to make a new emoji like `🤷‍♀️` which turns into 🤷‍♀️)

```
  unicodeemoji: RegExp('^(\ud83c[\udd00-\udfff]|\ud83d[\udc00-\ude4f]|' +
                       '\ud83d[\ude80-\udeff]|\ud83e[\udd00-\uddff]|' +
                       '[\u2000-\u206F]|[\u2300-\u27BF]|[\u2B00-\u2BFF]|' +
                       '[\u3000-\u303F]|[\u3200-\u32FF])'),
```

There’s also a corresponding Python regex `zerver.lib.markdown.UNICODE_EMOJI_RE`.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 19:57 UTC

Are they different...?

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 19:58 UTC

Oh wow I appreciate that the python one has a comment explaining the regex. Wonderful

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 19:59 UTC

Python regexes operate on Unicode characters, while JavaScript regexes operate on UTF-16 code units.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 20:04 UTC

Or at least that was true in 2014. Nowadays JavaScript has Unicode regexes with the `u` flag that operate on Unicode characters.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:05 UTC

So we could change the JavaScript one to match the Python one now?

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:07 UTC

*puts learning cap on and googles some things* Okay so Unicode is the general word to describe this set of characters encoded in this way, and UTF-16 is a way of storing them that is max 16 bits.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:12 UTC

Naively, I'm wondering if I can just say "any number of [current emoji regex] separated by `U+200D`"?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 20:18 UTC

No, for example, #️⃣ = U+0023 U+FE0F U+20E3.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:19 UTC

#️⃣

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:19 UTC

That one is already recognized by the regex though.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 20:20 UTC

No it isn’t. You’re seeing your OS’s native Unicode rendering of the Unicode emoji, not an image that Zulip has substituted.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:21 UTC

Oh I see! And we want it to show :hash: instead.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:22 UTC

That seems like a separate issue than the ZWJ one, or at least in that it looks less broken now.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:22 UTC

(replying to Evy)
> Naively, I'm wondering if I can just say "any number of [current emoji regex] separated by `U+200D`"?

I'm first thinking about fixing the issue in the linked PR

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 20:22 UTC

It only looks less broken because we don’t recognize *any part of it* as an emoji sequence.

**Evy** · 2023-06-27 20:23 UTC

If adding the ZWJ character fixes more visible issues, I'd be happy about that.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-27 20:25 UTC

We should use the [actual specification](https://unicode.org/reports/tr51/#Emoji_Sequences), not some ad-hoc regex with some cases we threw in with no particular justification.

**Evy** · 2023-06-28 01:25 UTC

Are you imagining building a regex from the spec definition? Or a different direction

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-06-28 01:53 UTC

That’s one approach. It’d be easier with `re2` which directly supports the Unicode character classes referenced by the spec.

**Evy** · 2023-06-28 02:06 UTC

This is all great information, thanks :)

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-06-28 14:26 UTC

If the rerendering of the message doesn't trigger a scroll event, then the "sticky_header" class may not get added back to the message header, which can cause the selected message to then scroll under the message header when the next message (from them or another user) is received.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-06-28 14:26 UTC

[Screenshot-from-2023-06-27-21-14-48.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/86/6c24sRWCkQa_n5DKdJu90V4i/Screenshot-from-2023-06-27-21-14-48.png)

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-06-28 14:27 UTC

There are more screenshots / screencasts of the issue / fix on the pull request.
