## Changing definition of inactive stream

*2023-07-13 to 2023-11-07 · 32 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Changing.20definition.20of.20inactive.20stream/with/1609070)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-07-13 15:22 UTC

So, @Karl Stolley  and I were discussion how to fix #23501 (Shift left sidebar correctly when following a link to an inactive stream). 

Karl was confused by his experience of clicking on `inactive` stream that it went from `inactive` to `active` by clicking on it. This is also the main cause of #23501 since the stream jumps from the position our UI expects it to be by going from `inactive` group to `active` group in the left sidebar.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-07-13 15:23 UTC

So, we were thinking a direction to explore for this bug is to keep the stream inactive which was inactive. I am not sure how or if it is even possible to have a boundary between these two types of stream other  than we having messages fetched locally or not.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-13 15:43 UTC

I'm guessing there has to be some kind of boundary in order to group and alphabetize by Active/Inactive status.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-13 15:44 UTC

But it does seem to me to be a miscue to suggest via the interface that an inactive stream can be made active just by opening it. That can be jarring also for someone who just wants to nose through the topics on multiple inactive streams to see when last the streams actually were active.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-13 15:46 UTC

And I do notice that an inactive stream remains sorted as being active even after clicking away to a genuinely active stream. Only a reload returns inactive streams to their usual place.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-07-13 15:50 UTC

I agree with Karl here.  It's always been my viewpoint that pushing inactive streams to the bottom is a misfeature.  One compromise that never occurred to me up until now is that we could simply gray out inactive streams but keep them in alphabetical order with the rest of the other streams.  Users who see this can probably figure out that the stream is inactive, and then they can either a) unsubscribe or b) possibly resurrect it.

I think it's mildly insidious that nascent streams that just require a bit of bootstrapping to stay active get pushed to the bottom. #**music** is an example of this.  It's the not most wildly popular stream, but I think people would engage with it more if it didn't get pushed down everybody's left sidebar after a little bit of dormancy.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-07-13 21:58 UTC

Yeah, we should change the definition. 

The backstory for this is related to #**frontend>fetching message history**. The way that we define "inactive" is just whether we have at least one messages from that stream on our local cache, and the bug is that we look at "Have the web app ever seen a message in that stream", whereas the similar thing we might want to be looking at is "does `all_messages_data`, aka the data set for "Recent conversations" and similar things, have a copy of a message in that stream?", so that it's not a function of what you've clicked on in this browser session.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-07-14 02:37 UTC

Nice, that sounds reasonable to me.

**Alya Abbott** · 2023-10-03 15:58 UTC

I filed **Change definition of inactive streams** #27009 to keep track of this.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-10-03 16:06 UTC

Sorry, it has been on my tracker for too long.

**Chisom** · 2023-10-18 00:32 UTC

Hi @Alya Abbott  I'm working on this  issue #27009. Please how do I know which streams  are inactive for me to test how clicking on it makes it active

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 01:19 UTC

@Chisom you can grep for `demote_inactive_streams` to find how that code works today. I expect you'll find it tricky to reproduce the bug in a development environment without using `populate_db -n10000` (see `localhost:9991/devtools`), creating a new stream, deleting the automated message added to that stream and then moving the very oldest messages to that newly stream.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 01:19 UTC

(The new stream resulting from that process should definitely be inactive)

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-10-18 02:17 UTC

`---extra-streams=100` would help too.

**Soniya Karamchandani** · 2023-10-18 05:28 UTC

(deleted)

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 15:53 UTC

> whereas the similar thing we might want to be looking at is "does `all_messages_data`, aka the data set for "Recent conversations" and similar things, have a copy of a message in that stream?", so that it's not a function of what you've clicked on in this browser session. 

I investigated this. I think using `all_messages_data` won't solve the issue completely because when a user views a message of an inactive stream by scrolling back in "All messages", the stream moves to the active streams section.

The correct fix, I think, would be to maintain a separate data structure to store the "inactive streams IDs" on web client load; and update it based on if new message loaded has id greater than the max message id in that stream i.e. the stream actually has new message instead of past message fetched?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 16:07 UTC

I don't understand your point. Can you describe it more in terms of how a stream starts out as (active / inactive) and when does it become active / inactive?

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 16:24 UTC

Sure,

`stream_list.initialize()` calls ` build_stream_list()` which has:
```
// The main logic to build the list is in stream_list_sort.js, and
// we get five lists of streams (pinned/normal/muted_pinned/muted_normal/dormant).
const stream_groups = stream_list_sort.sort_groups(streams, get_search_term()); 
```

In `stream_list_sort.sort_groups()`, we iterate over the streams and any stream that is neither pinned nor `has_recent_activity` is pushed into `dormant_streams`(inactive).

```js
export function has_recent_activity(sub) {
  if (!filter_out_inactives || sub.pin_to_top) {
     return true;
   }
  return stream_topic_history.stream_has_topics(sub.stream_id) || sub.newly_subscribed;
}
```

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 16:30 UTC

On another hand

`message_fetch.process_result()` has `messages.map((message) => message_helper.process_new_message(message))`

that leads to ` stream_topic_history.add_message()`

So, whenever we an old message is fetched it get added to the relevant ` stream_topic_history` and hence `stream_topic_history.stream_has_topics()` in `has_recent_activity` returns true when a user clicks on an inactive stream and the messages come in view.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 16:34 UTC

I meant more plainly without code :sweat_smile:

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 16:41 UTC

Okay :)

If a stream is neither pinned nor has recent activity, then it is termed as inactive. 

To check if a stream has recent activity, we take help of data structures in `stream_topic_history`. When a user clicks on an inactive stream, the messages fetched are also updated to data structures in `stream_topic_history`. So, it gives the info that the stream has recent activity; so the stream moves to active section on click.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 16:43 UTC

Isn't this what we do right now?

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 16:46 UTC

Yes, so I'm suggesting that we should instead maintain a separate data structure for the check in `has_recent_activity`. It should update only when the new message loaded has id greater than the max message_id in that stream. So if old messages are loading it won;t update and therefore the stream remains in inactive section.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 16:48 UTC

The [first para in this message](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/Changing.20definition.20of.20inactive.20stream/near/1676134) was related to why using `all_messages_data` won't work (as Tim earlier suggested)

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 16:52 UTC

I am not how that would work given we will need to get that `max message id` in the stream first, which itself would be marking it as `acive`.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 16:54 UTC

I agree that Tim's approach won't fix the issue of scrolling to the correct stream but it would set the right expectation for the user that just clicking on an inactive stream won't mark it as active.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 17:00 UTC

` PerStreamHistory ` has `max_message_id `. So whenever we fetch a message we can compare if it is greater than `max_message_id `; if yes the stream_id will be removed from the `inactive_streams` data structure.

`max_message_id` is "Most recent message ID for the stream."

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 17:05 UTC

> but it would set the right expectation for the user that just clicking on an inactive stream won't mark it as active 

Hm that's correct. But we might face other cases in the future where just viewing the message leads to marking the stream as active.
But yeah, Tim's approach fixes the "marked as active on click bug"

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-11-05 17:05 UTC

> `PerStreamHistory`  has `max_message_id` 

We have set it at one point from 0 to say X which would mark it as active.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-11-05 17:14 UTC

Okay, I think I'll code it (tomorrow maybe) for better discussion. Should be a couple hours of work. I might be missing something.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-07 01:03 UTC

I think fundamentally, the `all_messages_data` approach would be coherent than what we have (since effectively the definition would become "A stream is active if it has messages in 'recent conversations'".). I don't think that definition is a great one; I was thinking we should connect to `all_messages_data` mainly because it'd be relatively simple to implement and fix the very high weirdness of "Does the stream have messages that are cached locally, including from any mechanism one might have searched for messages in the stream or having clicked into it".

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-07 01:04 UTC

I don't really know what a great definition would be, and don't have the attention to try to figure out a great proposal -- but it likely would require a lot of work including new server support to do reasonably.

## messages marked as read in open tabs when page reloaded

*2023-07-17 to 2023-07-24 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/messages.20marked.20as.20read.20in.20open.20tabs.20when.20page.20reloaded/with/1611162)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:57 UTC

While looking into why messages are marked as read in pinned tabs that are set to narrowed views, I think that I've determined the logic behind commit 8f1c3a0fa1e81e5790460e39ab261c8016cea0d2 was incorrect.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:57 UTC

When we reload an open tab in a narrowed message view (that can mark messages read), then this will now mark the first unread message as read because we haven't yet set a selected message ID in the message list ...

[CODE LINK](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/ad10c77919eee5e7f40740185c70a601e59805ed/web/src/message_list.js#L126-L133):
```javascript
        if (this.narrowed && !this.visibly_empty() && this.selected_id() === -1) {
            // The message list was previously empty, but now isn't
            // due to adding these messages, and we need to select a
            // message. Regardless of whether the messages are new or
            // old, we want to select a message as though we just
            // entered this view.
            this.select_id(this.first_unread_message_id(), {then_scroll: true, use_closest: true});
```

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:58 UTC

We set the selected message ID that was recorded as the `narrow_pointer` in `update_selection` call in the `opts.cont()` eventually. But first the fetched messages are processed in the narrowed message list when we call `message_util.add_old_messages` in `message_fetch.process_result`.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:58 UTC

The changes I've got in #26023 seem to fix the issue in that if `select_id` gets called in an unfocused tab / window, then the mark as read event doesn't happen. But it seems like we'd want to address the issue here as it's where that `select_id` call is happening.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:58 UTC

Steps to reproduce:
- Have two users logged into the development environment.
- Have them in the same conversation view that can mark messages as read.
- Have one person send some messages, at least two.
- Stop and start the dev server.
- Note that the user with the unread messages will have the first unread message marked as read, but the selected message / blue box won't move.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-17 19:58 UTC

Noting that a user recently reported the above happening in an existing GitHub issue: https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/10886#issuecomment-1632004214. I haven't yet seen a new issue created for this particular case though, but if someone does, then it would be good to link it here.

**Nimish Medatwal** · 2023-07-19 20:47 UTC

(replying to Lauryn Menard)
> When we reload an open tab in a narrowed message view (that can mark messages read), then this will now mark the first unread message as read because we haven't yet set a selected message ID in the message list ... [CODE LINK](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/ad10c77919eee5e7f40740185c70a601e5980 …

I was going through [#10886](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/10886) and then saw you mention this same issue [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26023/files#r1252068282) in your code review, so I made a new [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/26299) and am working on it!

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-20 13:41 UTC

Thanks for opening that issue!

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-20 13:42 UTC

These `message_list.select_id` calls are a bit complicated, so I think it would be best to discuss here the direction for how best to fix this.

**Nimish Medatwal** · 2023-07-21 15:07 UTC

(replying to Lauryn Menard)
> When we reload an open tab in a narrowed message view (that can mark messages read), then this will now mark the first unread message as read because we haven't yet set a selected message ID in the message list ... [CODE LINK](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/ad10c77919eee5e7f40740185c70a601e5980 …

As I understand it, this code scrolls the user to the first unread message. Also I noticed by removing this code the issue was fixed this is because the default behavior of the select_id() function is to mark the selected message as read (mark_read: true). 
```javascript
    select_id(id, opts) {
        opts = {
            then_scroll: false,
            target_scroll_offset: undefined,
            use_closest: false,
            empty_ok: false,
            mark_read: true,
            force_rerender: false,
            ...opts,
            id,
            msg_list: this,
            previously_selected_id: this.data.selected_id(),
        };
``` 
So to override this default behavior and prevent the message from being marked as read when calling select_id(),  I explicitly set mark_read to false in the options object like this. 
```javascript
if (this.narrowed && !this.visibly_empty() && this.selected_id() === -1) {
            // The message list was previously empty, but now isn't
            // due to adding these messages, and we need to select a
            // message. Regardless of whether the messages are new or
            // old, we want to select a message as though we just
            // entered this view.
            this.select_id(this.first_unread_message_id(), {then_scroll: true, use_closest: true, mark_read: false});
        }
```
I thought this would solve this issue, but it didn't. Am I missing anything here?

**Nimish Medatwal** · 2023-07-21 21:04 UTC

So did some debugging and finally found out that this select_id()  function was getting called with the same message id ( of first unread message) three times so I explicitly set mark_read to false (specifically in message_fetch.js, message_list.js and narrow.js) for this specific message id and now the problem is solved !

**Nimish Medatwal** · 2023-07-21 23:14 UTC

@Lauryn Menard  I solved this issue and opened the [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26323) so you can start the reviewing process.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-24 11:26 UTC

Thanks for working on this! I left some review comments on #26323, but in general I think we still need to figure out here how to address the issue.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-24 11:26 UTC

In general, we do want the first unread message marked as read (if possible) when a view loads and a message is selected. This is currently inconsistent; see #**frontend>inconsistent mark as read**.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-24 11:26 UTC

In this case, if there was a message selected before the reload happened, then we want to reselect that message and not the first unread. But that information isn't available when we're adding messages from the first message fetch during the reload process.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-07-24 11:26 UTC

And that's what I think would be the direction to go for fixing this so that we don't change the behavior for the other situations where we're adding messages after successfully fetching them from the server.


## tabbing to hover controls?

*2023-07-18 to 2023-10-03 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/tabbing.20to.20hover.20controls.3F/with/1611741)*

The only open issue I've found for this is the vague and ancient #6235, but I'm curious to know what the ideal expected behavior is here?

To my mind, using arrow keys or j/k to move through message lists should bring Tab context along with it. That would go a long way toward better keyboard accessibility. True, there are keyboard shortcuts for the hover-control icons, but users of pointerless assistive technology presumably can't reach, say, a link in a message without tabbing for miles through the entire interface...

I don't think making the controls be visible should be difficult from a technical perspective, since you can basically apply CSS to `.selected_message .message_controls`.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-09 13:37 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> * I didn't quite understand the implications of the changes to the dead column -- are there potential downsides we should be considering?

So previously, the timestamp column was sized generously enough that there was almost always leftover space around the timestamp itself. That meant under most cases that there was always space between the star icon and the timestamp. But in other cases, such as 24-hour time or certain Asian-language timestamps, the timestamp occupied the entire column, and butted up against the star.

What the "dead" column does is wrest some of the space previously allotted to the timestamp column, which is itself reduced to accommodate whatever size the timestamp itself is. But the "dead" column ensures that there will always be a small amount of space between the star icon and the timestamp, regardless of the timestamp's size.

Put another way, the overall size allotted remains the same; we're just now more explicitly reserving some of that space to keep the hover icons and timestamp separate. And by using a "dead" column, we make that part of the grid, rather than getting into the business of putting margin or padding on grid items--which would also have the side-effect of making the grid's column declarations less than the source of truth for how different tracks are sized.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-22 19:45 UTC

(replying to Karl Stolley)
> Yeah. I don't find any evidence that Source Sans 3 has tabular figures, and setting `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;` on the timestamps' selector has no effect on them.

Oooooh do I have an interesting update here. Source Sans 3 absolutely *does* have tabular figures; in fact, as the typeface's designer [Paul D. Hunt points out](https://github.com/adobe-fonts/source-sans/issues/236#issuecomment-983224391), Source Sans 3 **defaults** to lining, tabular numbers. Ironically, that's why I couldn't find any evidence of the typefaces support for them.

So why aren't we rendering them on timestamps? Because we [switched them off](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/styles/zulip.css#L1155), in a way that apparently neutered my experiment with setting `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;`:

```css
.messagebox-content .message_time {
  display: block;
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 400;
  text-align: right;
  opacity: .8;
  color: var(--color-text-default);
  font-feature-settings: "pnum" on,"lnum" on;
  letter-spacing: .02em;
}
```

Setting `"pnum" on` is the culprit, as that sets proportional, aka non-lining figures there. Because lining numerals (`"lnum"`, verus old-style numbers, where like part of the 3 or 7 sit below the baseline) are the default, that's unnecessary to even declare. 

I suspect this was done, however, because the tabular figures put a "foot" on the 1, which does make timestamps with 1s in them feel a little heavier. The foot itself is probably a device to keep it from looking like the footless 1 is sitting way out in space.

So, here's what we've currently got: the footless but proportional/non-tabular numerals:

[proportional-numerals.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/48/tdX-ELx3xKmV0S4z_kLS8KQW/proportional-numerals.png)

And here's what we'd get if we use the tabular default. That default is used even here in the message area, as well as on things like unread counts--which is what makes unread counts line up so well in the left sidebar:

[tabular-numerals.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/53/sPcY1vKHWkIITVxvcVYrQKTl/tabular-numerals.png)

I'll put up a PR for this in a moment.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-08 18:04 UTC

Yeah I would expect this project to involve changing the use of `window.location` in the handful of places where do that to instead use the history API. It is the kind of thing that isn't fundamentally hard but will require very careful QA -- the existing implementation has been carefully implemented to handle a bunch of things. Just to lay out the handful of different flows that all need to work and should be the core testing process for whatever one is doing:
* Functions like `narrow.by_*` or the settings internals can trigger a change in the hash/view (and needs to update the hash without causing that to attempt renarrowing again)
* Clicking a link to `#narrow/...` URLs, such as links to other messages, currently just change the URL and then have that call `hashchanged` which then triggers changing the view -- and that needs to not attempt to change the hash again (or save an duplicate history entry or whatever).
* Reloading the page while in a particular view needs to have you start up again in that same view.
* The back/forward buttons need to navigate you through past views cleanly.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-08 18:05 UTC

I'm not sure whether we need to put that in browser local storage or do something else. We could also consider the possibility of changing our URL format to have the currently selected message ID be part of the URL, and have adjustments to that part of the URL just update the existing history entry rather than changing it -- if we found that using the browser history API to store this stuff had constraints that are problematic.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-08 20:56 UTC

Before navigating from view A to view B, we actually want to store the blue box location with A on the stack, not with B. That involves using `replaceState`, not `pushState`. This could happen immediately before navigation, but it’s cleaner to do it right after moving the blue box, because then there’s no need to track down and intercept all the different ways we could navigate away from A (some of which are outside our control anyway).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-09 18:51 UTC

> we usually don't want a "bounce" on a previous view to prevent the first save in a new view.

Neither `debounce` nor `throttle` has that behavior. Every call to `debounced_f = _.debounce(f)` or `throttled_f = _.throttle(f)` will eventually be followed by a call to `f`. The difference is that `debounced_f` delays the `f` call until there have been no `debounced_f` calls for a while, while `throttled_f` delays the `f` call until it has made no `f` calls for a while.

## Going to source/edit view on collapsed message

*2023-08-09 to 2023-08-10 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Going.20to.20source.2Fedit.20view.20on.20collapsed.20message/with/1622348)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-09 20:56 UTC

In working this afternoon to improve how the SHOW MORE button is handled when a message is collapsed, I discovered a kind of odd state where you can still enter the message-edit/source view--leaving the SHOW MORE button visible:

[Screenshot-2023-08-09-at-3.54.49-PM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/3f/DyKSrFk7WKb6436nVomOgEF7/Screenshot-2023-08-09-at-3.54.49-PM.png)

Clicking the SHOW MORE button doesn't change the source view--instead, it makes the SHOW MORE button seem to disappear.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-09 21:02 UTC

At first glance, it seems best to simply hide the SHOW MORE button while in edit/source mode, and show the button once more once returned to the regular message view. But if that view is still collapsed, that's a kind of a weird state to return to after editing a message, even if a collapsed message is a weird state to enter edit/source mode from in the first place.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-09 21:03 UTC

So another option would be to say "Okay, you want to edit? View source? Let's uncollapse this message first." And then users are returned to the uncollapsed message view.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-09 21:05 UTC

A third option, I suppose, would be to suppress any actions as well as the hover controls when a message is collapsed. But you can still, for example, react to a collapsed message (but existing reactions are still shown on collapsed messages).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-09 23:08 UTC

I think having the hover controls available when a message is collapsed is probably useful? Hard to say, I guess a related case that we've thought about more recently is likely to be the "Mute user" display of messages sent by such a user or in group DM threads with such a user, so may be worth studying that in case it provides inspiration.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-10 20:55 UTC

Agree. That's definitely the least-surprising behavior. I also opted in #26472 simply to hide the SHOW MORE button when in an edit/source view, rather than monkey with the collapsed state. It seems safe to assume a user knows what they're doing if they collapse and then go into edit mode. Changing state is more likely to be an irritation than a help.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-10 21:41 UTC

Yeah that sounds right.

**Steve Howell** · 2023-08-10 18:31 UTC

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-10 18:39 UTC

Sharing CSS across separate components is one of those things that sounded like a good idea in 2013, but works very badly in practice as you need to maintain the code over time. What you think is going to happen is that all your components will remain nicely in sync automatically. What actually happens is that inevitably someone will want to change how one of the components looks, and either they accidentally affect other components without realizing it, or they start weaving a tangle of increasingly complicated selectors that override each other. CSS is just not designed to be the right abstraction for this kind of sharing. Either share at the component level or don’t share at all.

When we talked about the left sidebar changes made here: #26468, @Karl Stolley and I noticed that the unread count isn't aligned well horizontally. The reason is the line in the CSS: `letter-spacing: .6px;` Should we remove the letter spacing for the unread counts to achieve better alignment, or are there specific reasons why we are using the `letter-spacing` property?

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-08-14 20:38 UTC

[before.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ac/6DJrEKz7F9R6OE0y5llPX_1Z/image.png)
[after.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8c/5-UBsxeOaZioS6xK6k8yXEpn/image.png)

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-08-14 21:01 UTC

We could also improve the vertical alignment by removing `line-height`.

[before.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ca/286CEYlfGlNpomGIQ7SX8ycB/image.png)
[after.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8b/Pl-DcNzZmRvIPFZ5H47RVhLy/image.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-14 21:32 UTC

These are no-brainer fixes to me (but then, I was in on them :upside_down:). One major thing I learned about this is that the `letter-spacing` value is not just for interstitial spaces between letters, but also the space after the last letter. Which is why it's basically a fool's errand to try and center text that has had it's letter-spacing messed with.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-14 21:35 UTC

More philosophically and typographically speaking, I think it's poor form to make minor adjustments like this to letter spacing. Either you trust the typographer who designed the typeface and their judgement about letters, or you look to see if there are stylistic alternates that offer [tabular figures](https://www.fonts.com/content/learning/fontology/level-3/numbers/proportional-vs-tabular-figures)--which is kind of like monospace, but just for numerals, so that they always align in a column. But I don't think that's even the intention with the extra spacing here.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-14 21:39 UTC

As far as line-heights go, that's something that needs some serious work app-wide. We've got a lot of magical numbers floating around, not least of which is the unitless `1.214` line-height in the message area, which given the 14px font-size there, works out to `16.996px`. While we should definitely strive for a relative-unit expression of line heights (and font size, and other font- and line-height-dependent values), to get things in order and more consistent, we should at least have a pixel value--a sane, non floating-point value--to use across the app.

**Topic Bridge Bot** · 2023-08-14 21:41 UTC

@Daniil Fadeev mentioned this topic in **[#issues > long names of `global_filters` break the layout](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/9-issues/topic/long.20names.20of.20.60global_filters.60.20break.20the.20layout/near/1624901)**.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-08-14 21:44 UTC

A lot of the classic articles about line-height and vertical rhythm have pretty creaky CSS, but [this article](https://designmodo.com/vertical-rhythm/) is fairly up-to-date, and offers some pretty good depictions of what's at stake when you're setting a baseline grid with line-height. Obviously we're lucky to have @Vlad Korobov as our designer, so we don't necessarily need to go completely down a purely mathematical road with this, but just having some concrete values that we can then draw from for spacing throughout the UI would be a huge help.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-14 21:48 UTC

That `letter-spacing` CSS is traced to a 2014 era design change (56f1c023ab2bf170ce7b0cf9ebea68ca7295fc7a). I doubt it'll be possible to figure out the intent behind it; but in any case, I think we should bias towards what we think makes sense now given that AFAIK that detail hasn't been considered in forever.

export function get_stream_name_from_id(stream_id) {

## data-reference-hidden

*2023-08-31 to 2023-09-01 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/data-reference-hidden/with/1633859)*

**Daniil Fadeev** · 2023-08-31 15:09 UTC

We have this CSS:
```css
/* If the reference of the tooltip is went offscreen while scrolling,
       the tooltip will be visible until the scrolling stops. Popper adds
       `data-reference-hidden` attribute to those tooltips whole reference is
       hidden. Since tooltips have `absolute` position, they can occupy scroll
       space offscreen and cause document to have the wrong scroll height.
       Setting `display: none` makes sure it doesn't occupy any offscreen space.

       NOTE: This data attribtute has changed each time in the past 3 releases and
       if we upgrade tippy from v6, we should check if this attribute is still valid.

       See https://github.com/atomiks/tippyjs/issues/555 for some discussion on this.
    */
    [data-reference-hidden] {
        display: none;
    }
```

@Aman (amanagr), can I switch from `display: none` to `visibility: hidden`? In my situation, it messes up the positioning calculations. I also read that using `display: none` isn't recommended here - https://popper.js.org/docs/v2/modifiers/hide/.

## Wildcard mentions in direct messages

*2023-09-15 to 2023-09-15 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Wildcard.20mentions.20in.20direct.20messages/with/1641123)*

**Hardik Dharmani** · 2023-09-15 13:03 UTC

`@all` and `@everyone` mentions in direct messages are not counted as mentions until the page is reloaded, while `@user` and `@group` mentions work fine and are counted as mentions. In streams, all mentions work completely well.

[Mentions in direct message](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/91/b1BkNO6v_S5aOr-9unvUeF8S/2023-09-15-17-01-54.mkv) vs [Mentions in streams](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/d8/fb-RyG0X7CeLiPAcSb9VCmuM/2023-09-15-17-59-15.mkv)

```spoiler Easy steps to reproduce this Issue
1) Set `Automatically mark messages as read` to `Never`.
2) Mark a direct message containing `@all` or `@everyone` as unread, it will not update the unread mention counter in the left sidebar, reload the page it will update the mention unread counter to 1.
[Reproducer: wildcard-mention-issue-in-direct-message.gif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/b/P4kUf5FDWqn8GG98I-NEzXiD/Reproducer-wildcard-mention-issue-in-direct-message.gif)
```

The reason for this bug is that the `unread_mentions_counter`, which stores the mention count, is updated in the `update_message_for_mention()` function in `unread.js` if `is_unmuted_mention` is true, which is calculated like this:

```
const is_unmuted_mention =
        message.type === "stream" &&
        message.mentioned &&
        !user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic);
```

Should this code be updated to remove the `message.type === "stream" &&`? 


````spoiler update_message_for_mention() function
    export function update_message_for_mention(message, content_edited = false) {
    // Returns true if this is a stream message whose content was
    // changed, and thus the caller might need to trigger a rerender
    // of UI elements displaying whether the message's topic contains
    // an unread mention of the user.
    if (!message.unread) {
        unread_mentions_counter.delete(message.id);
        remove_message_from_unread_mention_topics(message.id);
        return false;
    }

    const is_unmuted_mention =
        message.type === "stream" &&
        message.mentioned &&
        !user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic);

    if (is_unmuted_mention || message.mentioned_me_directly) {
        unread_mentions_counter.add(message.id);
        add_message_to_unread_mention_topics(message.id);
    } else {
        unread_mentions_counter.delete(message.id);
        remove_message_from_unread_mention_topics(message.id);
    }

    if (content_edited && message.type === "stream") {
        return true;
    }
    return false;
    }
````

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-15 17:54 UTC

@Hardik Dharmani I think the answer is likely yes -- though of course you can't just remove that without making the `!user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic);` check invalid -- it just needs to a `message.mentioned && (DM case ||   stream case)` sort of thing.

**Hardik Dharmani** · 2023-09-15 19:04 UTC

So, the stream case is that we don't count `@all` and `@everyone` mentions if they are in muted topics, but for DMs, we don't have such a case so it becomes `message.mentioned && (message.type ==="private"  ||  !user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic); )`, 
but `!user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic);` returns true in case of direct message so we can directly write:
```
const is_unmuted_mention =
        message.mentioned &&
        !user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic);
```

Thoughts??

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-15 20:33 UTC

@Hardik Dharmani no, I prefer actually spelling it out -- we don't want to write code that passing two `undefined`s to that function. 

When we move the relevant files to TypeScript your version will be an error.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-15 20:34 UTC

More generally, I'd argue that is the sort of "simplification" (not showing the two cases explicitly) that makes the code shorter but harder to read, and you basically never want to do that sort of thing in a production codebase.

## Left sidebar rows as grids

*2023-09-21 to 2023-09-28 · 43 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Left.20sidebar.20rows.20as.20grids/with/1645011)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:13 UTC

I've put up a WIP PR at #26807, which expresses topic rows as CSS grid. What follows here is a duplicate of the content I posted with the PR today that merits discussion (there are more things in the PR itself):

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:13 UTC

#26807 is the first of a few closely-related planned PRs to introduce grid-based layout to all the different rows in the left sidebar. I'm beginning with topics because they're the innermost rows, and getting them right will make it easier to move up the tree to stream rows, DM rows, and ultimately the heading rows (which will increase in number in [the redesigned left-sidebar](https://zulip-sidebar.vladkorobov.repl.co/) and [collapsing views PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26035)).

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:14 UTC

The goal of this rewrite is to make it so that adding, removing, and repositioning icons, markers, and other elements do not disturb other parts of the existing layout--while also making sure that those placed elements behave predictably.

To that end, the grid defined on topic rows initially is meant to ultimately apply to all the other rows in the left sidebar--just with different dimensions.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:19 UTC

Breaking things down, all rows in the left sidebar--both existing and proposed, in @Vlad Korobov's redesign--can be expressed as some variation of this (you'll almost certainly need to scroll right to see the whole thing):
```txt
| Left   | Anchor element    | Text content (heading, | Markers and controls | Anchor element         | Right  |
| offset | (chevron control, | stream/topic name,     | (@s, bells, unreads) | (vdots, heading icons) | offset |
| space  | stream icon,      | conversation partners) |                      |                        | space  |
|        | checkmark)        |                        |                      |                        |        |
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:19 UTC

Some rows, of course, do not have offset space; and that's fine, as the actual `grid-template-column` for that particular left-sidebar row can just specify `0` as the offset space; likewise for any other column element that doesn't exist in a given row.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:20 UTC

But when things like offset space is needed, it can be declared at the grid level--instead of as margin or padding on an inner element or the grid container itself.

And that use of grid to manipulate negative space comes with some important benefits:

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:20 UTC

1. Things like offset space or empty interstitial columns get occupied by other elements in the row
2. Adding new elements to occupy that space means just adjusting the grid definition, *rather than* playing around with padding or (worse) margin that would be otherwise set to occupy the negative space--or keep elements out of it
3. Positioning rows within the left sidebar is a matter of positioning solid blocks: there's no margin hanging around to bleed through and make life messy and unpredictable when tweaking the design, especially as those elements sit in the column of the overall left-hand sidebar (which [may be getting wider as part of the redesign](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/101-design/topic/UI.20redesign.3A.20left.20sidebar/near/1643891), too)
4. Elements like zero-unreads can either be safely removed from the DOM, or given `display: none` (the zero-unreads are currently obscured from view with `visibility: hidden`, as are the resolved checkmarks on topics); that means no mystery clickable elements, or keeping a hidden element around for the sake of preventing the layout from collapsing

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:21 UTC

Other, positive space in the grid can be used as expected. The WIP grid here also uses `max-content` as the width for the grouped markers and controls area. That area itself can probably best be presented as a flexbox, but its overall relationship to other elements in the row is all handled by grid.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:21 UTC

**Here endeth the PR text in slightly modified form.**

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:22 UTC

A few additional thoughts to add here:

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:24 UTC

**1. Why not stick with or extend flexbox?** The trick with flexbox is that it's great for specifying how *content* should behave. That's why things like `flex-grow` and `flex-shrink` are set on the child flex items of a flexbox--not the flexbox itself. The thing with the left sidebar is that--as you can tell by looking at the columns formed by icons, unreads, and so on--we don't *really* want to give the content a say about how it's laid out in the left sidebar. Instead, we want to reserve a certain number of pixels for, say, the vdots icon, and then fully expect it to occupy exactly that space. No more, no less.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:25 UTC

**2. So no flexbox at all???** No! There's still an important role for flexbox to play. There's a new structure I've introduced in #26807 that holds all the various markers (things like @s, bells, unreads) to a single grid item. But the actual markers themselves are presented in a flexbox. That's essential, because we don't know whether an unread will be `1`, `8888`, or not appear at all. Flexbox is great at that.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:29 UTC

**3. What about vertical alignment?** That can be handled just as well in grid as in flexbox. Where we're likely to run into trouble, especially as [the redesign of the left sidebar](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/101-design/topic/UI.20redesign.3A.20left.20sidebar/near/1638042) proceeds, is that past loosey-goosey stabs at line height (e.g., mysterious `line-height: 1.1;` declarations) are going to need to be made more explicit and more precise. That's how we'll, for example, ensure proper top-of-row alignment of anchor elements like icons and vdots and things with the very first line of a multi-line topic, or a multi-line list of conversation partners in group DMs. (Or, if the thought is to make the icons align with, say, the second line of a 3-line conversation, the same explicit line-height deal applies.)

**Vlad Korobov** · 2023-09-21 21:50 UTC

I see you are a fan of grids.  It might be a way to technically manage everything. 
I don't understand why flexbox with placeholders isn't a right thing here.
Any column of declared grid might be wider or narrower and manage grid columns in addition to just a size of elements seems as extra work.
I guess with grid you feel like you can control balance between different width's better

> we don't really want to give the content a say about how it's laid out in the left sidebar

You right about vdots, but I don't see anything else which would behave like that. 

Anyway if you feel like you wan to get things working with a grid, lets try.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:54 UTC

Thanks Vlad! A bunch of things behave like that: the chevrons for expanding and collapsing headers, the stream icons, presence/DM group icons (though those might have to be flexed with usernames, depending), the resolved checkbox, as well as the negative space itself on either side of a row. With grid, we can reserve space anywhere we like *without having to put something there*. That's one of the key differences between grid and flexbox.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 21:59 UTC

And with grid, we get to have our cake and eat it too, care of things like `max-content`, which can accommodate, say, zero or more indicators like @s and bells adjacent the topic name. And the topic name itself can grow to swallow up unused grid space by defining it with fractional units (e.g., `minmax(0, 1fr)`)

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 22:02 UTC

Put another way, to get something like a multi-line text wrap in flexbox means very precisely controlling the size of everything else in the flexbox, while the text wrap is kind of just expanding in reaction to that. That's in pretty high contrast to grid, where you can tell the wrapping text's spot in the grid how to behave. 

And if we want to do something like only show 3 lines of text when more are present, we can bring a `grid-template-row` definition to the party and constrain the number of lines that way, instead of diving down into the text element itself and using like `max-height` or something that shares only a passing relationship with the other elements on the row.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-21 22:20 UTC

The text wrap we want is a pretty detail so if grid makes that easier, that seems like a good reason to be excited about using grid here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-21 22:23 UTC

So we can consider going with incremental merges here or going more "do a full rewrite that's nice, and then test it until we fix all the regressions"; I don't have a strong idea a priori for what will be better.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-21 22:48 UTC

**Vlad Korobov** · 2023-09-22 13:07 UTC

> very precisely controlling the size of everything else in the flexbox

Yeh, you right it was useful for me to see easy when things misbehave... But if was during the design phase and it might be better to manage all that with a bit more reliable and fault tolerant layout system.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-22 13:44 UTC

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-22 16:33 UTC

Okay so here's another reason that, as much as I love flexbox for certain applications, it can be crazy brittle: text nodes and whitespace become flex items. 

Here's an @ marker and unread count sitting in the new grid, with those two items flexing within the grid:

[](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/9c/QUiXO41DZy6yTz8BX9ZxLksT/mention-grid-flex-after.png)

Look good!

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-22 16:34 UTC

But then, here's the same icon + unread combination--this one with the bell:

[](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f5/Meef4p8qkfuHoVX5OriSLILc/bell-grid-flex-after.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-09-22 16:42 UTC

What's happening here is that the left-sidebar row template is actually using space on `main` right now to keep the bell separate from the unread count. But in a proper flex setting, that whitespace *becomes a flex item*.

So we remove the space:

```diff
--- i/web/templates/topic_list_item.hbs
+++ w/web/templates/topic_list_item.hbs
@@ -12,8 +12,7 @@
                     @
                 </span>
             {{else if is_followed}}
-                <i class="zulip-icon zulip-icon-follow" aria-hidden="true"> </i>
-                &nbsp;
+                <i class="zulip-icon zulip-icon-follow" aria-hidden="true"></i>
             {{/if}}
             <span class="unread_count {{#if is_zero}}zero_count{{/if}}">
                 {{unread}}
```

And then we end up with proper flexing of just the items we intend (the bell and the unread):

[](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/11/a_s7hxJDGfyzn7L1qGMiFp38/bell-ws-fix-grid-flex-after.png)

## Eliminating popovers.js

*2023-09-25 to 2023-09-27 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Eliminating.20popovers.2Ejs/with/1646405)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:23 UTC

In #26613 (#**frontend>popovers migration to tippy**, #**frontend>bootstrap** for context), I added a bunch of commits that move the parts of the old `popovers.js` that aren't horribly entangled import cycles into the modern tippy-based `popover_menus.js` module.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:24 UTC

The entirety of the remaining module is this:

```
export function any_active() {                                                                          
    // True if any popover (that this module manages) is currently shown.                               
    // Expanded sidebars on mobile view count as popovers as well.                                      
    return (                                                                                            
        popover_menus.any_active() ||                                                                   
        stream_popover.is_open() ||                                                                     
        user_group_popover.is_open() ||                                                                 
        user_card_popover.user_sidebar.is_open() ||                                                     
        user_card_popover.message_user_card.is_open() ||                                                
        user_card_popover.user_card.is_open() ||                                                        
        emoji_picker.is_open() ||                                                                       
        playground_links_popover.is_open() ||                                                           
        $("[class^='column-'].expanded").length                                                         
    );                                                                                                  
}                                                                                                       
                                                                                                        
// This function will hide all true popovers (the streamlist and                                        
// userlist sidebars use the popover infrastructure, but doesn't work                                   
// like a popover structurally).                                                                        
export function hide_all_except_sidebars(opts) {                                                        
    $(".has_popover").removeClass("has_popover has_actions_popover has_emoji_popover");                 
    if (!opts || !opts.not_hide_tippy_instances) {                                                      
        // hideAll hides all tippy instances (tooltips and popovers).                                   
        hideAll();                                                                                      
    }                                                                                                   
    emoji_picker.hide_emoji_popover();                                                                  
    stream_popover.hide_stream_popover();                                                               
    user_group_popover.hide();                                                                          
    user_card_popover.hide_all_user_card_popovers();                                                    
    playground_links_popover.hide();                                                                    
}                                                                                                       
                                                                                                        
// This function will hide all the popovers, including the mobile web                                   
// or narrow window sidebars.                                                                           
export function hide_all(not_hide_tippy_instances) {                                                    
    right_sidebar_ui.hide_userlist_sidebar();                                                           
    stream_popover.hide_streamlist_sidebar();                                                           
    hide_all_except_sidebars({                                                                          
        not_hide_tippy_instances,                                                                       
    });                                                                                                 
}                                                                                                       
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:25 UTC

Which is fundamentally written as a giant import cycle -- each popover module calls some version of the `hide_all` methods, but also needs to have its own `hide` method called from that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:28 UTC

The main `popover_menus.js` library module has bit of a system that seems intended for this problem:
```
const popover_instances = {                                                                             
    compose_control_buttons: null,                                                                      
    starred_messages: null,                                                                             
    drafts: null,                                                                                       
    all_messages: null,                                                                                 
    message_actions: null,                                                                              
    stream_settings: null,                                                                              
    compose_mobile_button: null,                                                                        
    compose_enter_sends: null,                                                                          
    topics_menu: null,                                                                                  
    send_later: null,                                                                                   
    change_visibility_policy: null,                                                                     
};                                                                                                      
```

But only the dozen popovers directly defined in that module use it. And really I'd prefer to put each of those in their own module(s);`register_popover_menu` is an exported method but those small popovers were migrated before we set up that API.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:29 UTC

The most basic thing we could do is export `popover_instances`, have the independent modules like `stream_popover.js` mutate that rather than having a locally managed `stream_popover_instance` variable.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:31 UTC

It could be a good idea to do a bit fancier registration process, like the `PopoverMenu` class we have in `user_card_popover.js` for the 4 popovers defined in that module:

```
class PopoverMenu {                                                                                     
    constructor() {                                                                                     
        this.instance = null;                                                                           
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    is_open() {                                                                                         
        return Boolean(this.instance);                                                                  
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    hide() {                                                                                            
        if (this.is_open()) {                                                                           
            this.instance.destroy();                                                                    
            this.instance = undefined;                                                                  
        }                                                                                               
    }                                                                                                   
```

But I don't have a great sense of what the best API for that would be.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:33 UTC

I think if we fix this and then after getting that API working nicely, we split the individual-popovers part of `popover_menus.js` into individual per-popover modules, it'll be a huge huge step in #**frontend>simple import cycles** -- ~18/68 of our edges to cut to eliminate import cycles involve `popovers.js` or `popover_menus.js`, and I think the majority of those issues would be resolved by doing this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-25 05:35 UTC

So proposals for a good API here would be much appreciated!

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-03-27 12:07 UTC

The right section can also be handled similarly, but we would get a clear idea once the refractoring is done for the left panel. I will just explain what I am thinking about how we should structure the code.

We want to avoid calling `activate_section_or_default` twice - it is first called from `launch` when the overlay is opened and then it is called when the code to select one of the "Personal" or "Organization" toggle is called. We need `activate_section_or_default` call while toggling between "Personal" and "Organization" settings, so we cannot remove that, but we can instead remove the call in `launch` function.

To preserve the section name which we want to open when opening the overlay, we would  save it in a variable defined in `settings_panel_menu` just like we define `$curr_li`. So, we would set it like `settings_panel_menu.org_settings.curr_section = section` in `launch`. And then the `current_tab` can return the `curr_section` instead of using `$curr_li` which will be passed to `activate_section_or_default` called in `show`.

Note that you can first refactor the code to handle opening the correct section based on the option selected in left panel as a prep commit before the code to have three tabs in right section for "Users" which will use a similar approach.

There’s no reason to wait for `Map` support. This works fine.

```nodejsrepl
> Handlebars = require("handlebars")

> template({my_map_entries: my_map.entries()})
'key 2, value true\n' +
  'key 1, value true\n' +
  'key b, value true\n' +
  'key 00, value true\n' +
  'key a, value true\n' +
  'key 3, value true\n'
```

## private => direct renaming

*2023-10-05 to 2023-10-05 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/private.20.3D.3E.20direct.20renaming/with/1656603)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-05 23:43 UTC

This is definitely a bit of an advanced refactoring project just to do it carefully to make it reviewable and avoid breaking things, but it would be nice to do a bit more of `s/private_/direct_` for code involving direct messages. We will want to be careful to rename concrete collections of things with a good commit structure that's easy to verify; and not make any API changes in a PR that's mostly internal renames.

Here's a couple collections of things that seem like they're small enough to work through renaming elements that match them:

```
$ git grep private_message_recipient | wc
    142     519   13252
$ git grep private_messages  | wc
    167     578   13973
$ git grep update_private_messages  | wc
     24      71    1585  # good chunk that's small enough for a commit.
```

I think we're mostly not doing big projects that are likely to greatly merge conflict with this sort of rename, so figured I'd mention it in case someone is in the mood for this sort of thing as a break from more urgent projects.

*2023-10-10 to 2023-10-12 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/renaming.20modal-.2A.20classes/with/1659209)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-10-10 12:04 UTC

There are a couple of class names of the form `modal-*` which we can rename.
- `modal-footer` class is used for the footer in stream and user group creation form, which is not a modal. @Tim Abbott suggested `settings-sticky-footer`[here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/27124#issuecomment-1753457338).
- `modal-body` class is used in the keyboard shortcuts and "About Zulip" UI. The code used for both of them is the overlays code and not modals. @Tim Abbott suggested `overlay-scroll-container` class name but the "About zulip" UI is not scrollable, so maybe we can just add the required CSS using a more specific selector for "About Zulip" UI.
- `modal-bg` class is also used for overlays. This class is only used to set background color of the overlay, so we can either set the CSS to more specific selectors or just use a common class like `overlay-container`.

I am going to open a PR to split modals and overlays right now, in case that's relevant.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 17:06 UTC

`overlay-container` seems good for replacing `modal-bg`, a lot of the individual elements have names like `user-groups-container` or `overlay-messages-container` that align with that as a base class name.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 17:06 UTC

I think this is mostly orthogonal to #27140 because the classes are all things we weirdly added `modal-*` classes to that were not in fact actually overlays :)

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-10-12 07:02 UTC

One issue with replacing `modal-bg` class with `overlay-container` class is that we also use `overlay-content` class and for some cases the `modal-bg` class is used in same element with `overlay-content` class and for some `modal-bg` class is used for a child element of `overlay-content` element.

So, using `overlay-container` for a child element of `overlay-content` might be weird. We can probably do a audit of the code to check if there are some cases to fix in these class names.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-12 16:40 UTC

I think that's OK -- we can clean that up separately. I'm not sure whether renaming it to `overlay-body` or just getting rid of that interstitial `div` makes more sense, but I don't think we need to block on figuring out how we want to restructure that detail.

If we plan to show only one banner when outside narrow, there's a technical trade off to discuss.

The "narrow to stream > topic" banner is displayed during echo whereas the "automatic new visibility policy" banner is displayed after we receive 200 response.

If we plan to display only the "automatic new visibility policy" banner, we need to stop displaying the other banners during echo step and move the logic to display them only after server response.

```HTML
<ul>
   <ul>
    <li></li>
    <li></li>

The [only valid child of `<ul>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-ul-element) is `<li>`. Neither `<div>` nor `<hr>` are valid HTML there.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-10-16 18:03 UTC

So, would you guys agree for me to use this structure here:
```html
<div>
<ul>
<li></li>
<li></li>
</ul>
<hr />
<ul>
<li></li>
<li></li>
</ul>
</div>
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:13 UTC

(replying to Aman (amanagr))
> I just mean that I wouldn't expect ul > li> ul > li structure to be used to just to create a simple list with dividers.

You might not expected it, but the `<li>` that wraps the inner `<ul>` makes a great element for adding a border. And @Anders Kaseorg is absolutely right that we make lists more navigable to assistive technologies by using nested lists properly, rather than a `<div>` solution.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:14 UTC

The rethought gear menu provides a good opportunity to set the structural tone for other places in the app with nested lists. It would be a great example to point other contributors to.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:16 UTC

I also don't see what an `<hr>` element would contribute here. A humble border on, say, a containing list item, offers the ability to change the design more handily, including whether even to include a border--whereas an `<hr>` is always going to have to be addressed or designed around, or removed.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-10-16 18:26 UTC

I could say the same for design constraints for using a `ul > li > ul > li`structure stated above. You will alway have work around that structure. On the other hand using something simple like:
```
<div>
<a></a>
<a></a>
<div class/role="divider"></div>
<a></a>
<a></a>
</div>
```
offers much more freedom. We can use the appropriate `role` attributes to guide screen readers.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:45 UTC

Freedom, but at the expense of semantics. When a screenreader hits a list, for example, it tells the user exactly how many items are in there (I'm unaware of a role attribute that can duplicate that). In a navigation context, it's very helpful for a) a user to know how many items are there, and b) if they're grouped in some way. A stack of anchor tags between divs is about as low-quality an assistive experience as could be offered :-/

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:47 UTC

Also, [this section of WAI-ARIA linked to from the ARIA in HTML spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#implicit_semantics) makes it explicit that:

> if an element with the functionality already exists, such as a checkbox or radio button, use the native semantics of the host language. WAI-ARIA markup is only intended to be used to enhance the native semantics (e.g., indicating that the element is required with aria-required), or to change the semantics to a different purpose from the standard functionality of the element.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 18:48 UTC

The key there is "use the native semantics"--lists are a part of HTML for that reason. Yes, they can be tricky to get right, but at least for my part, we owe that much to users of assistive technologies.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2023-10-16 19:11 UTC

Thanks Karl for sticking with me. I understand it now this way that, for standard lists like the one we want to implement, it is infinitely more prefereable to be semantically correct but if we wanted some very non-standard desinged dropdown it would be okay to give up a bit of semantics and use `role` attributes.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-16 19:16 UTC

Right. The whole point of the [ARIA in HTML spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#rules-wd) (which was in draft status FOREVER but finally saw recommendation status just days ago, on 4 October 2023) is to see `role` attributes and the like as enhancements to native HTML semantics, not a replacement for them. It's far more preferable to write, say `<button>Subscribe</button>` than, say, `<div class="button" role="button">Subscribe</div>`, for a simple example

## typing notifications efficiency

*2023-10-18 to 2023-12-10 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/typing.20notifications.20efficiency/with/1664905)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 18:43 UTC

So we need to do some optimization of how much traffic typing notifications generate in order to make it reasonable to have typing notifications for stream messages. One thing we can do is tune the constants for how quickly we repeat typing notifications ... but I think it's probably the case that changes in the web app's logic for determining whether the user is typing might be at least as significant an area for optimization. @Prakhar Pratyush FYI.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 18:44 UTC

The main logic in `typing.js` for deciding whether a user is typing is the following:
``` js
export function initialize() {                                                                          
    const worker = {                                                                                    
        get_current_time,                                                                               
        notify_server_start,                                                                            
        notify_server_stop,                                                                             
    };                                                                                                  
                                                                                                        
    $(document).on("input", "#compose-textarea", () => {                                                
        // If our previous state was no typing notification, send a                                     
        // start-typing notice immediately.                                                             
        const new_recipient = is_valid_conversation() ? get_recipient() : null;                         
        typing_status.update(                                                                           
            worker,                                                                                     
            new_recipient,                                                                              
            typing_started_wait_period,                                                                 
            typing_stopped_wait_period,                                                                 
        );                                                                                              
    });                                                                                                 
                                                                                                        
    // We send a stop-typing notification immediately when compose is                                   
    // closed/cancelled                                                                                 
    $(document).on("compose_canceled.zulip compose_finished.zulip", () => {                             
        typing_status.update(worker, null, typing_started_wait_period, typing_stopped_wait_period);     
    });                                                                                                 
}                                                                                                       
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 18:46 UTC

There are probably some opportunities for optimization here:
* Only initiate a typing notification if there's at least N characters in the compose box, and/or compose has been open for some period of time.
* Some sort of temporal debouncing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 18:58 UTC

Oh, I guess actually most correctly, we should expect every message to result in at least 2 typing notifications -- one from starting to write a message, and one from finishing the message.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 19:03 UTC

There are a few constants that control how often we send typing notifications, and how often we re-send them if one continues typing (or pauses typing).
```
# How long before a client should assume that another client sending                                    
# typing notifications has gone away and expire the active typing                                       
# indicator.                                                                                            
TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 15000                                                       
                                                                                                        
# How long after a user has stopped interacting with the compose UI                                     
# that a client should send a stop notification to the server.                                          
TYPING_STOPPED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 5000                                                          
                                                                                                        
# How often a client should send start notifications to the server to                                   
# indicate that the user is still interacting with the compose UI.                                      
TYPING_STARTED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 10000                                                         
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 19:07 UTC

I did a bit of log spelunking. chat.zulip.org is generating:
* About 7.4 `/typing` API requests to send/cancel typing indicators per message sent.
* About 6.25 `typing` notification events delivered to clients per `message` event sent. 

Tripling those 3 constants leads to the following:
* About 4.7 `/typing` API requests to send/cancel typing indicators per message sent. (Much lower!)
* About 5.6 `typing` notification events delivered to clients per `message` event sent. (About the same!)

The different between the definitions for those ratios it that the "API requests" metric weights every message equally. Whereas the "notification events" weights stream messages in our streams that everyone is subscribed to at hundreds of times the weight of a DM, since every connected client gets an event when you send a stream message (or send a typing notification about a potential such stream message), while only recipients get that for a DM.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 19:09 UTC

(The tests are of course at different times and thus with different traffic so not at all directly comparable.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 19:29 UTC

So I think the first thing we should do is tune these parameters more rationally. I think the following might be a reasonable proposal for the long term:
* `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 45000`. The user impact of this is that "If a user's computer loses network or they close a browser window or otherwise we lose contact after the system had sent a typing notification, when do other clients stop displaying this user as typing". The current 15 seconds is great but I feel like probably this situation is rare enough that 30-45 seconds would be basically OK too.
* `TYPING_STARTED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 30000`. This should have no user impact as long as it is safely well below the previous value, such that even with some networking delay/failures, clients will definitely get the "I'm still typing" notice before timing out due to the above. I'm pretty sure this just needs to be less than the `STARTED_EXPIRY` period by a healthy network round-trip delay, . The events system is a reliable delivery system that won't drop events, so there's no reason to make this like 2x less than `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS` -- but probably a bit more buffer is fine.
* `TYPING_STOPPED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 30000`. This is basically how long we will wait with someone who has typed something in the compose box but hasn't actually hit a key before we stop showing them as typing. Any value above `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS` is pointless. But probably 30s of idleness is a fine period to wait with you thinking (but not doing anything) with text in your compose box before we decide you might have left?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-18 19:31 UTC

A complication, noted in #**api design>typing notifications constants**, is that the mobile clients hardcode that first parameter to 15000, so we might find we can't in practice increase those last two constants above 15 seconds immediately.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-10-18 20:44 UTC

Can we make some improvement around "sending typing notifications events" to "all the subscribers"?

Does the extra subscribers for whom we don't have active clients contribute to the tornado load?

Yeah, there's a related server change we can discuss in a new thread in #**backend**, which is whether we can avoid sending to Tornado the IDs of `long_term_idle` users for this event type. It would save a small bit of resources sending the list of 20K user IDs who are in that state, and dictionary lookups for them, etc. But such a change would not be visible in the analysis above -- since we only deliver events to connected clients anyway.

(Feel free to start such a thread, I'm going AFK shortly and might forget)

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-11-06 19:36 UTC

Because of #**api design>typing notifications constants**, does it make any sense to crank `TYPING_STARTED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS`  /  `TYPING_STOPPED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS` up slightly, to as close as we're comfortable below the currently-fixed 15s `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS`?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-06 19:39 UTC

Yeah I think a thing we could merge into `main` now would be `TYPING_STARTED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 12000`, `TYPING_STOPPED_WAIT_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 12000`, `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS = 45000`. We can't sensible raise those first two parameters above `15000 - likely RTT` without creating user-facing on-off flickering of typing notifications... at least until we get the mobile apps to either respect these parameters or hardcode a high value like `45000` for `TYPING_STARTED_EXPIRY_PERIOD_MILLISECONDS`, which would be a very low-effort solution with minimal downsides.
