## typeahead: buggy $.inArray ?

*2024-03-06 to 2024-03-07 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/typeahead.3A.20buggy.20.24.2EinArray.20.3F/with/1753178)*

**Evy** · 2024-03-06 21:00 UTC

I was looking at this code in the bootstrap typeahead file while trying to fix an issue where left-arrow with search pills (which I'm currently working on) wasn't  [highlighting pills](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/79/Q0ooom3QPC_CkxA_PsIVsZk4/image.png), specifically only when a [blank typeahead was open](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8f/Zuq7AZ4Ro-Jpb4T04OGJCI6i/image.png) (which is often the case)


The issue was that this was stopping the event propagation.

```js
 maybeStopAdvance(e) {
     const pseudo_keycode = get_pseudo_keycode(e);
     if ((this.options.stopAdvance || (pseudo_keycode != 9 && pseudo_keycode != 13))
        && $.inArray(e.keyCode, this.options.advanceKeyCodes)) {
         e.stopPropagation();
     }
```

I refactored this into its own function a little while back, but double checked just now that it was written like this when we moved the code into this file.

Using `$.inArray` like this is strange to me -- it [returns -1 when the list doesn't include the item](https://api.jquery.com/jQuery.inArray/), so this is only falsey when `e.keyCode` is the first element of `advanceKeyCodes`.

I'm pretty sure the code should look like this instead

```js
  , maybeStopAdvance(e) {
    const pseudo_keycode = get_pseudo_keycode(e);
    if ((this.options.stopAdvance || (pseudo_keycode !== 9 && pseudo_keycode !== 13))
        && this.options.advanceKeyCodes.includes(pseudo_keycode)) {
        e.stopPropagation();
    }
```

...but if we do that, then we'll propagate a bunch of keyboard events that we didn't previously. And we'll need to set `advanceKeyCodes` properly (which barely any users of `stopAdvance` do). Does this seem like the right way forward? Sort of an annoying bug to encounter and fix.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-06 21:07 UTC

This was introduced in #10092.

**Evy** · 2024-03-06 23:34 UTC

Ah, thanks!

**Evy** · 2024-03-06 23:48 UTC

Sounds like we actually want this then?

```
(this.options.stopAdvance && !this.options.advanceKeyCodes.includes(pseudo_keycode))
|| 
(!this.options.stopAdvance && pseudo_keycode !== 9 && pseudo_keycode !== 13)
```

Previously `$.inArray(e.keyCode, this.options.advanceKeyCodes)` was true for everywhere except search with backspace, so I think that should stay equivalent.

**Evy** · 2024-03-06 23:50 UTC

It's kinda messy though

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-06 23:56 UTC

It would be equivalent to simply replace `$.inArray(e.keyCode, this.options.advanceKeyCodes)` with `!this.options.advanceKeyCodes.includes(e.keyCode)`, given that `advanceKeyCodes` has at most one element at present.

Are you proposing an extra behavior change on top of that?

Continuing the discussion  @Rohan Gudimetla started in [TypeScript migration thread](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/TypeScript.20migration/near/1752899)

So I think `do_settings_change` function of `setting_ui.ts` in not typed completely. `request_method` params (presently of type `AjaxRequestHandler`) takes all types of method ie. `channel.patch`, `channel.post`, `channel.del` etc.

`AjaxRequestHandler`  works for all(`channel.post`, `channel.del`...)  but  `channel.patch` request_method since 
`type AjaxRequestHandler=(args: AjaxRequestHandlerOptions) => JQuery.jqXHR<unknown> | undefined;` and `channel.patch` is of type `( options: Omit<AjaxRequestHandlerOptions, "data"> & PatchRequestData,) ⇒ JQuery.jqXHR<unknown> | undefined`.

These two types don't overlap nicely....may be **we need to expand the request_method 's type** to account for `channel.patch`.Something like .....

```
export function do_settings_change(
    request_method: AjaxRequestHandler | AjaxPatchRequestHandler,
    ....,
    data: Omit<Parameters<AjaxRequestHandler>[0]["data"],"undefined"> |  PatchRequestData,
   ....
```

where type `AjaxPatchRequestHandler`=`( options: Omit<AjaxRequestHandlerOptions, "data"> & PatchRequestData,) ⇒ JQuery.jqXHR<unknown> | undefined` or  you can say `typeof patch`(from `channel.ts`). 
 `data` is never `undefined` for the function if I have checked correctly. 

Looking for other's opinion on this!!!

```
type AjaxRequestHandler = typeof call | typeof patch ;
```

## Hide right sidebar

*2024-03-12 to 2024-04-17 · 34 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Hide.20right.20sidebar/with/1756755)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-03-12 19:06 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg made a comment on my old PR for [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/19927#discussion_r1142773176), to use `@extend` instead of mixins, but I tested it and it was not working if you have selector inside instead of just properties.

So, this doesn't work:

```css

.hide-right-sidebar-styles {
    .app-main {
        display: none;
    }
}

@media (width < $xl_min) {
    @extend .hide-right-sidebar-styles;
}

```

but this does:

```css

.hide-right-sidebar-styles {
    display: none;
}

@media (width < $xl_min) {
    .app-main {
        @extend .hide-right-sidebar-styles;
    }
}

```

So, I am planning to use mixins.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-12 19:19 UTC

This works:

```css
.hide-right-sidebar-styles {
    .app-main {
        display: none;
    }
}

@media (width < $xl_min) {
    :root {
        @extend .hide-right-sidebar-styles;
    }
}
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-12 19:24 UTC

It makes sense that you can’t directly `@extend` in a `@media` query, because what would this mean?

```css
%foo {
    background: red;
}

@media (width < 30em) {
    @extend %foo;  /* we never selected an element, so which one becomes red? */
}
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-03-13 00:58 UTC

Thanks for the working example.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-03-13 13:46 UTC

To emulate hiding right / left sidebar on all screen widths, we need track all the CSS related to them in one place so that it is easy to make changes and override them if need be.

Just the above change of increasing specificity by wrapping the styles inside `:root` create issues. So, it is worth thinking about a long term goal here.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-03-13 13:48 UTC

How do you folks feel abuout adding a new css file which sits at the end in `app.ts` and only contains media queries that are relavant to hiding left / right sidebar. We will also need to add a custom check to ensure any other CSS files don't add a media query at `xl` and `md` max-widths.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-13 14:12 UTC

Instead of `:root`, would it be possible to attach a state class somewhere high in the DOM, and extend the properties from that?

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-13 14:13 UTC

A late-loading CSS file to me seems like an option of last resort…but maybe I’m more anxious about having order factor into the CSS stack like that than I need to be

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-03-13 15:51 UTC

Yeah, that's probably a better direction to think about which needs to be done for sure since it is easy to add styles which can even override the css in these media queries. But, I wanted to set an intent that this is the css we want to override everything else with at this width. That's why I feel more at ease with moving these media queries to a separate file. I feel like we will have to do this for all the media quries though.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-14 00:04 UTC

I would prefer to just have these by at the bottom of `left_sidebar.css` and `right_sidebar.css`... and maybe make more use of CSS variables or other techniques to avoid really thorny dependencies. But I'm not sure I have a good grasp on the complexities here.

## #29136 Paste stream and topic links with nice formatting

*2024-03-13 to 2024-03-26 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.2329136.20Paste.20stream.20and.20topic.20links.20with.20nice.20formatting/with/1757417)*

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2024-03-13 17:01 UTC

I've taken up #29136 and here's my plan to approach it:

- First, we have to extract the stream and topic hashes from a URL.

- Then we need to obtain the stream and topic names from the hashes. The codebase has a function `decodeHashComponent` in `internal_url.ts` which suits this purpose. 

- Once extracted, the pasted URL has to be replaced with the `#**stream>topic**` syntax.

I've made a preliminary implementation :

The following appears when pasting `http://localhost:9991/#narrow/stream/3-Denmark/topic/old.20API.20was.20de-duping.20quickly`

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/81/QqIJf4gqI_UZWlMelqCyWVXD/image.png)

On sending the message:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/15/SsqzFKW-BqIN5KwR-2w9meW3/image.png)

The link works as expected.
As per my understanding, this was the requirement of the issue.

Even though the implementation works, there are **LOTS** of edge cases possible, and I'm working on them one by one. I'll commit the change once some frequent corner cases are handled, and then the code can be reviewed.

Meanwhile, please suggest changes (if any) in how the feature is supposed to work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-14 00:02 UTC

I think roughly that plan is correct; the main things to be careful with will be:
- Checking the hostname is the same to avoid processing links to other Zulip servers
- Ensuring the URL-encoding/decoding logic is done properly.
- Having tests for the interesting part of the logic covering those corner cases.

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2024-03-14 05:13 UTC

Indeed

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2024-03-14 16:26 UTC

Here's the progress:
- Pasting a link to the **same** zulip server transforms it to the `#**stream>topic**` syntax.
- The link may or may not contain topic, but must contain a stream (else it is unaffected).
- `Ctrl+Z` removes the transformed link. 
- The feature works even when only the stream id is present in the pasted url, and not the name.
- Invalid urls are not transformed.

Many of the edge cases are covered.

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2024-03-15 13:45 UTC

Following the last review, I have:

- incorporated the syntax transforming logic into the existing code in `copy_and_paste.js`
- replaced my implementation of the parser with `parse_narrow` in `hash_util.ts`. (Created a wrapper around it)

I wanted to ask couple things:
- Do we actually need to handle relative links (`/#narrow...`)? The problem would be that we won't be able to know whether the link belongs to the same zulip server.
- If there are multiple valid links copied at once, do we wish to transform all of them to the syntax on pasting?
- When undoing, do we wish to replace the syntax with the original pasted url?

Additionally, I found a minor typescript bug in `hash_util.ts`

```
export function parse_narrow(hash: string): Term[] | undefined {
    // This will throw an exception when passed an invalid hash
    // at the decodeHashComponent call, handle appropriately.
    let i;
    const terms = [];
    for (i = 1; i < hash.length; i += 2) {
        // We don't construct URLs with an odd number of components,
        // but the user might write one.
        let operator = internal_url.decodeHashComponent(hash[i]);
        // Do not parse further if empty operator encountered.
        if (operator === "") {
            break;
        }
...
```

The argument `hash` is annotated with the `string` type, when in reality it is supposed to be `string[]`. The only place where this function is being used (`hashchange.js`) also passes it a string array.

I've corrected it in my latest commit.

> I think it would be nice if `Ctrl+Shift+V` pasted the url without any transformation. I'd appreciate others' opinions on it.

**Alya Abbott** · 2024-03-18 22:52 UTC

> * If there are multiple valid links copied at once, do we wish to transform all of them to the syntax on pasting?

That sounds right. It seems like it's not very likely to come up, though, so it wouldn't be worth it if that would make the implementation a lot more complicated or error-prone.

**Alya Abbott** · 2024-03-18 22:54 UTC

> * Do we actually need to handle relative links (`/#narrow...`)? The problem would be that we won't be able to know whether the link belongs to the same zulip server.

It might be OK to assume it's from the current server, but maybe someone else can comment on this question. It might not really come up in practice?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-18 23:23 UTC

Whenever we’re trying to do something magical with Markdown syntax like this, there’s a [use–mention distinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Use%E2%80%93mention_distinction) to be careful of.

- **Use:** someone pastes a URL to refer to a conversation—“here’s the last time we discussed this topic”.
- **Mention:** someone pastes a URL in order to talk about the URL itself—“here’s where Zulip embeds the stream ID in the URL”.

Associating a magical **use** with some syntax in a way that makes it difficult to **mention** that same syntax is always dangerous, because one often needs to **mention** it in order to explain how to **use** it (or develop it).

In this case, there’s no reason someone would try to **use** a relative URL if they were expecting it to function as a link. But there are plenty of good reasons to **mention** relative URLs. So we should be careful to avoid transforming them.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-18 23:58 UTC

There is at least the `Ctrl+Shift+V` paste workaround, but yeah I think that's a good argument for not having this feature try to transform relative links; the probability of it being valuable is not super high given that we tend to not generate those.

## Use [tabindex='0'] selector to query elements for navigation

*2024-03-19 to 2024-03-19 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Use.20.5Btabindex.3D.270.27.5D.20selector.20to.20query.20elements.20for.20navigation/with/1761130)*

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-03-19 17:41 UTC

Currently to query for the list of items that we want to support Up/Down arrow navigation in the popover menus, we use the `a:visible` selector. With the addition of theme-switcher in #29249, which adds elements other than the `a` tag that we want to navigate across, would it be a good idea to instead use `[tabindex='0']` as the selector?

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-19 17:55 UTC

As an abstract idea, that sounds good to me. I only see one place in the codebase where we use a positive integer other than 0 on `tabindex` (and that's for the Zulip logo), so for as long as we are sticking with only going with `0`, that selector probably works.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-19 17:56 UTC

The one question is whether that means we're going to have to start putting `tabindex` on things that don't need it, i.e., elements reachable by keyboard natively, in their order as presented in the HTML

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-03-19 19:16 UTC

To support elements reachable by keyboard natively, maybe we could use the `:tabbable` implementation of `jquery.ui`:

```js

//>>label: :tabbable Selector
//>>group: Core
//>>description: Selects elements which can be tabbed to.
//>>docs: http://api.jqueryui.com/tabbable-selector/

var tabbable = $.extend( $.expr.pseudos, {
	tabbable: function( element ) {
		var tabIndex = $.attr( element, "tabindex" ),
			hasTabindex = tabIndex != null;
		return ( !hasTabindex || tabIndex >= 0 ) && $.ui.focusable( element, hasTabindex );
	}
} );
```

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-03-19 19:20 UTC

Since the above code checks for the attribute `tabindex`, tags such as `a` will be taken into account without explicitly needing a `tabindex` to be defined.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-19 19:34 UTC

I don't want to pull in the separate `jqueryui` plugin for this sort of thing; we're going to eventually move off JQuery entirely and don't want further dependencies that are entangled with it.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-03-19 19:36 UTC

Sorry if it wasn't clear. I meant we could use this logic as a reference to define a custom method of our own.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-19 19:46 UTC

I mostly just don't want to make a change that requires complicated verification/testing here; possibly a union of the existing `a:visible` logic and `tabindex='0'` would just be fine?

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-03-19 20:11 UTC

Pushed changes to [2b5013f](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/29249/commits/2b5013f9cf74206a25e0d8b6b3a96a236bb1ce45). I went ahead with the following filter: `.find("a, [tabindex='0']").filter(":visible");`.

## Caching message lists #29259

*2024-04-03 to 2024-09-06 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Caching.20message.20lists.20.2329259/with/1773875)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-04-03 12:14 UTC

What are the cases for which we want to store and maintain the message list as rendered? I recall @Tim Abbott talked about keeping All messages rendered when it is your default view. Do we want to store previous narrow visited by user too?

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-05 13:33 UTC

Can you share a little bit of the context behind your question, Aman?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-04-05 13:53 UTC

Like right now, we have `All messages` always rendered and its rendered state maintained regardless of if it is ever visited by the user. So, this has a bit of cost associated with it, like fetching the list of messages for it and updating it for any event. 

So, we are moving it to the model of only keeping it rendered if "All messages" is your default view. The question is are there any other cases where we would like to keep a view rendered in the background even if it is not displayed?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-04-05 17:05 UTC

Yeah so to provide some background, Zulip today actually keeps the "Global feed" view in the DOM at all times, even if you never visit it. This design detail dates to the 2013-era original design of Zulip, which didn't have Inbox or Recent views, and it's an optimization to making switching to/from that view ultra fast.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-04-05 17:07 UTC

We likely don't need that optimization for users for whom "Global feed" is not their default view. But given that we have working infrastructure for that optimization, it might be a good idea to keep the support infrastructure for it, which involves some live-update code doing `for (const list of message_lists.all_rendered_message_lists())`, rather than doing that operation with just `message_lists.current`, just because it's already well-tested logic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-04-05 17:12 UTC

There's a few forms of message list caching worth talking about:
- We definitely want to support caching `message_list_data` objects for recently viewed narrows; this would be a very cheap-in-memory/CPU cost optimization that would make the "Back" button considerably faster in cases where the previous view required asking the server for data. This is tracked as #15131.
- I am uncertain to what extent we want to make use of keeping recently visited message list objects cached in the DOM to make it extra cheap to switch to them. We've squashed most of the bugs related to that architecture, but I am unsure to what extent it actually makes switching faster; ultimately that's a question about how much of the time of rendering from the raw message data to the fully displayed view is our own logic vs. the browser needing to do painting. I am certainly OK with temporarily disabling this optimization for the global as part of pursuing other goals, with a view towards doing some profiling to see whether it's net helpful.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-05 18:02 UTC

Yes. Profiling sounds good...I don't know what if any user-behavior data we have access to that would help make some of these calls, either. Or even if there were such data, that it would help come to some kind of decision here.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-04-11 00:57 UTC

Thanks! Will modify the PR accordingly.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-20 21:35 UTC

#31326 is test-deployed here. It definitely makes re-visiting a few snappier; what we're looking to find is any bugs it introduces.

- ul -> `role="menu"`

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-05-14 12:08 UTC

And the separators don't use an `aria-hidden` on them, since NVDA has the `s` key mapped to "next separator" in its browse mode. For context, NVDA has two modes: **Browse mode** and **Focus Mode**. 
* When reading a page, browse mode is used.
* When interacting with an element, focus mode is used.

And a user can switch between them as per his requirement.

## Allow multiple filters in ListWidget

*2024-04-05 to 2024-04-10 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Allow.20multiple.20filters.20in.20ListWidget/with/1775643)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-04-05 10:36 UTC

Following the comments on #29597. We need to modify ListWidget to accommodate  multiple filters. Here is my proposal to do that. 

Changes to the contract:

- We will introduce a field call `multi_filter` to `ListWidgetOpts`. 
- This is what the options for `multi_filter` will look like:
```javascript
type ListWidgetMultiFilterOpts<Item> = {
    filter_list: Array<{
        key: string;
        default: string;
    }>
    filterer: (list: Item[]) => Item[];
    onupdate?: () => void;
};
```
- We will introduce a method: `set_multi_filter_value: (key: string, value: string) => void;` to ListWidget to set the value for a particular key.  This function would also do things like `widget.hard_redraw();` which are usually done on the `on input` event in ListWidget.
- We will introduce a method: `get_multi_filter_value: (key: string) => string` to get the value for a particular key. This method will throw an error if the key does not exist. This will primarily be used by the filterer method.
 

How it will work + decisions made:


- We will eliminate the use of `$element` in multi_filter. Right now, the current filter options sets up an `on("input")` event for the `$element`. This requires the value to be stored in an input field. For components like dropdown widget, we are not storing the value in an input field, but instead in the `data-unique-id` attribute. The component using ListWidget should setup their own events instead and use set_multi_filter_value to set the value. If we want to use the current `$element` implementation, it would be possible , but then every component which does not have their value stored in an input field will need to setup a hidden input field of their own.
- Only string values would be supported for now for each key. Filterer is free to process the value however it likes.
- There will only be one filterer and onupdate for all the filters combined. I chose that instead of having a filterer for every key value to help avoid chaining of filters and to give us more flexibility on how we filter the list. Combining or ignoring filters based on the value of another filter would be much more straightforward in a central `filterer` function. 
- We will not be supporting predicate for now, I'm assuming if someone's setting up multi_filter, its starting to get a bit complex already and they can achieve the same functionality with filterer. 
-  The current filter option shall remain as is, we can deprecate it later if we want to. But I think we can keep it around since it will be much easier to setup for simple text filters. On the topic of whether to allow both filter and multi_filter together or not, I'm not sure yet, I think I might have more info on this at the type of implementation on how straightforward either of the option is. 
-  Instead of `get_multi_filter_value`, we can also a pass the filter key value object to filterer directly, but I though having an explicit function might help us with consistent error handling if the key is not found. 

Known pitfalls of this approach:
- More plumbing would be required for multi_filter on the component using ListWidget, setting up events, setting the key_value etc. But it will also give us way more flexibility. LMK if this feels like too much plumbing and I'll try to come up with some middle ground. 


cc. @Aman (amanagr) @Sahil Batra would love to hear your feedback on this :) . LMK If I shouldn't tag yall directly next time

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-04-05 10:45 UTC

Also, we will add our own event handlers for the change in input which will just redraw the list widget.

## KaTeX display area

*2024-04-11 to 2024-04-11 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/KaTeX.20display.20area/with/1778380)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-11 16:34 UTC

I've been working on refactoring the space between elements in the rendered Markdown area so that only bottom margins are ever used. As I've been doing that, though, I've been wondering about this portion of the `web/styles/rendered_markdown.css` file that @Anders Kaseorg introduced some time ago in #17829 for improving the scrollability of KaTeX's display area, in response to issue #14422:

```css
    /* LaTeX styling */
    .katex-display {
        /* KaTeX sometimes overdraws its bounding box by a little, so we
           enlarge its scrolling area by stealing 3px from the margin
           of the enclosing <p>. */
        margin: -3px 0;
        padding: 3px 0;
        overflow: auto hidden;
    }
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-11 16:34 UTC

As best I can tell, the `margin: -3px 0;` does not actually increase the size of the `.katex-display` box. Instead, it effectively removes the `3px` of margin currently around paragraph elements. This can be seen by measuring the size of the KaTeX box both with `margin: -3px 0` and `margin: 0`:

[katex-display-neg-3-margin.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8a/ebpba7iZnZrrsVrxLXksIVdi/katex-display-neg-3-margin.png)
[katex-display-0-margin.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/2c/N8Pu2T6h-Uqb6hVnxNQ2mlzR/katex-display-0-margin.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-11 16:35 UTC

And at least on Firefox/MacOS, there's no apparent change in the position of the scrollbar, either when comparing the current versus zeroed margins (that seems reasonable, as the scrollbar appears within the content box, and at least the example above indicates that the negative margins has no impact on the size of the content box):

[katex-scroll-neg-3-margin.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/e7/mXTXzN7c3UBCI7jJ1zSHvprK/katex-scroll-neg-3-margin.png)
[katex-scroll-0-margin.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f1/EP05zqtC4dcH_1-Gb0qJyvgL/katex-scroll-0-margin.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-11 16:35 UTC

I'm sensitive to blindspots I might have here, though. And I wonder if there might not be some good edge-case examples to test against? I've tried recreating some of the problems mentioned in #14422, but unfortunately all that was posted there were screenshots.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-04-11 16:58 UTC

The main point of that commit is `overflow: auto hidden`, to enable a horizontal scrollbar but not a vertical one:

```math
\int_0^{x^{446}} \frac{1 + 2x + 3x^2 + 4x^3 + 5x^4 + 6x^5 + 7x^6 + 8x^7 + 9x^8 + 10x^9 + 11x^{10} + 12x^{11} + 13x^{12} + 14x^{13} + 15x^{14} + 16x^{15}}{x}\,dx
```

Then the point of `padding: 3px 0` is to prevent the top of the `446` getting slightly cut off, and `margin: -3px 0` is there to visually cancel the extra padding.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-04-11 17:43 UTC

Cool. Thanks, Anders. That's helpful context.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-05-13 19:22 UTC

TypeScript only supports narrowing the types of variables, not type parameters. For example, here’s something you might hope to work (and would work, in a properly designed type system like Haskell’s), but doesn’t work in TypeScript:

```ts
function f<T>(x: T, is_string: T extends string ? boolean : false) {
    if (is_string) {
        const s: string = x; // error TS2322: Type 'T' is not assignable to type 'string'.
    }
}
```

So given an unconstrained `InputPillContainer<T>`, there’s no evidence you can provide to convince TypeScript that you can pass it a `InputPillItem<StreamPill>`.

The proper solution would be to rearrange things so that any code that assumes `StreamPill extends T` is moved outside the class itself where `T` is generic, into caller-provided callbacks where `T` is known.

**Lalit** · 2024-05-13 19:25 UTC

Yeah that makes sense, Thanks @Anders Kaseorg.

## using minimalistic assert vs assertion operator `!`

*2024-05-07 to 2024-05-07 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/using.20minimalistic.20assert.20vs.20assertion.20operator.20.60.21.60/with/1794995)*

**Afeefuddin** · 2024-05-07 19:01 UTC

I was working with a file migration and I faced this issue. It might seem trivial, but I felt like asking.

```typescript
function foo(a:number){
  if(a%2===0){
    return a;
  }
  return undefined
}

function bar(){
  let a = 8
  let b = foo(a*2)
  assert(b !== undefined)
  console.log(b/2)
  function cat(){
    console.log(b/2)
  }
  cat()
}
```

This code above gives an error ('b' is possibly 'undefined') when we use `b/2` within `cat` function, whereas it works completely fine outside of this code block, that is when we use `console.log(b/2)` outside the `cat` function and within the `bar` function.

However, when I use the assertion operator for the same code, it works completely fine in both cases.

```typescript
function foo(a:number){
  if(a%2===0){
    return a;
  }
  return undefined
}

function bar(){
  let a = 8
  let b = foo(a*2)!
  console.log(b/2)
  function cat(){
    console.log(b/2)
  }
  cat()
}
```
What could be the possible reason for this behavior, and when should we generally use `!` and when should we use `minimalistic-assert`?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-05-07 19:05 UTC

`!` doesn’t check anything at runtime. Ideally, you should only use it in performance-critical code where you can prove **locally** that the value is not nullish.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-05-07 19:09 UTC

Or I’m mostly okay with uses where a nullish value is already guaranteed to cause an **immediate** error, such as `obj!.key` and `obj![key]` and `func!()`.

*2024-05-13 to 2024-05-14 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Improving.20settings_components.20types/with/1798644)*

```
export function get_property_value(                                                                     
    property_name:                                                                                      
        | RealmSettingProperties                                                                        
        | StreamSettingProperties                                                                       
        | keyof UserGroup                                                                               
        | keyof CustomProfileField                                                                      
        | RealmUserSettingDefaultProperties,                                                            
    for_realm_default_settings?: boolean,                                                               
    sub?: StreamSubscription,                                                                           
    group?: UserGroup,                                                                                  
    custom_profile_field?: CustomProfileField,
```

If you look at how it's used, we would really be better off just having it be 5 functions, like `get_group_property_value`; almost all of the code is special cases that would only be in one of those functions.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-13 20:00 UTC

So we should probably invest in that before trying to do much more stream/group/settings UI modules.

*2024-05-16 to 2024-05-29 · 14 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/query_matches_person.20delivery.20email/with/1801858)*

**Evy** · 2024-05-16 23:05 UTC

Currently in `query_matches_person` we only check email if `person.delivery_email` is set. Previously, that was the only thing we checked before trying a match by email.

Since moving `composebox_typeahead` to typescript, I added `person.type === "user" || person.is_broadcast === undefined` to the check as well to confirm that `person` isn't a mention.

My suspicion is that `Boolean(person.delivery_email)` was there as a check for if `person` is a mention or a user object, but removing that check might change behavior because `delivery_email` isn't always set (it's of type  `string | null`). So I'm starting this thread to see how people feel about removing this check.

When we do check the email for matches, it's with `get_visible_email` which checks delivery email but *falls back to just `user.email`*, so the difference would be that we'd fall back when we weren't before.

Does anyone have thoughts or perspective on this to share that would help us decide if we can remove that check?

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-17 16:46 UTC

We'll want to avoid matching on the generated fake emails, like `userNNNN@chat.zulip.org`. It sounds (having not looked at the code) like `get_visible_email` will return those when the current user can't see the real email.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-17 16:48 UTC

I'm not sure just checking `person.delivery_email` is the right logic either, though. In at least the API (don't know if the web client normalizes this away in its data structures), there's a quirk where sometimes there's no `delivery_email` but the real email is in `email`, depending on email visibility settings.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-20 23:42 UTC

I believe in the current API, checking only `delivery_email` is correct. See https://zulip.com/api/get-user#response for details, but I think this changed in API feature level 163:
> * [`GET /users`](/api/get-users), [`GET /users/{user_id}`](/api/get-user), [`GET /users/{email}`](/api/get-user-by-email), [`GET /users/me`](/api/get-own-user), [`GET /events`](/api/get-events): The `delivery_email` field is always present in user objects, including the case when a user's `email_add …

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-20 23:44 UTC

So @Evy I think the code that falls back to checking `user.email` is just legacy code that predates that change. @Sahil Batra may be able to confirm as the author of that changeset, but I think you should proceed under the assumption that the documentation is correct.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-20 23:54 UTC

Ah great, I guess I'd forgotten about that change.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-05-21 04:04 UTC

Yes, we always include `delivery_email` field in user objects now with the value being `None` if user cannot access it.

**Evy** · 2024-05-28 22:44 UTC

@Sahil Batra when the user can't access it, what does `get_visible_email` return? Are we okay with showing the `user.email` in that case? Should we be falling back to empty string or something?

**Evy** · 2024-05-28 22:46 UTC

If there's a valid non-empty-string `user.email`, then I imagine we'd want `query_matches_person` use it for sorting. If not, then we should update `get_visible_email` to not consider `user.email`.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-29 00:00 UTC

AIUI from the above, if `delivery_email` is null, then `email` will be the unhelpful fake email string like `userNNNN@chat.zulip.org`.

That means that for an email to show in the UI, or to match on for a search query, we never want `email` — if we have a useful email at all for those purposes, it's in `delivery_email`.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-29 00:00 UTC

(The remaining use of `email` is then for any straggler parts of the API that still rely on "emails" to identify users, and/or old clients that do so.)

## ✔ Default channels Add channel modal error

*2024-05-27 to 2024-05-30 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Default.20channels.20Add.20channel.20modal.20error/with/1807636)*

**Varun** · 2024-05-27 18:30 UTC

The Add default channels feature seems to be broken (testing in my local dev enviorment)

[default-channel.mp4](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/33/vzMRaxXJ--zpXfFmwB5LqXcC/default-channel.mp4)

Possible Reason: In following code snippet inside `settings_streams.js` 

```javascript
function get_chosen_default_streams() {
    // Return the set of stream id's of streams chosen in the default stream modal.
    return new Set(
        $("#default-stream-choices .choice-row .dropdown_widget_value")
            .map((_i, elem) => Number($(elem).attr("data-stream-id")).toString())
            .get(),
    );
}

```
we are trying to the get the value of attribute `data-stream-id` -- but not every element with `#default-stream-choices .choice-row .dropdown_widget_value` has that attribute. (to be specific the dropdown element "Select channel" does not contain `data-stream-id` attr ). 
This causes something like `Number(undefined)` which returns`NaN`, which when passed in `channel.post` data field causes error.

A quick fix would be something like:
```javascript
.map((_i, elem) => {
                if($(elem).attr("data-stream-id"))
                    return Number($(elem).attr("data-stream-id"))
                else return undefined;
            })
.get()

```
but it might need some proper fix and hence reporting it here.

I guess it will always be the last element that will be the "Select channel" dropdown, so one solution could be to modify the jquery selector to exclude the last element.

```javascript
$("#default-stream-choices .choice-row .dropdown_widget_value:not(:last)")

```

```js
// Type defined earlier in code
$scroll_listening_element: JQuery | JQuery<Window>;
...
...
...
meta.$scroll_listening_element.off("scroll.list_widget_container");
```

Error on lint:
> web/src/list_widget.ts(471,48): error TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'TypeEventHandlers<HTMLElement, any, any, any>'.

Note that attaching the `scroll` event handler works without any typeahead errors.

```js
meta.$scroll_listening_element.on(
    "scroll.list_widget_container",
    function (this: HTMLElement) {...}
);
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-06-07 08:23 UTC

So, I don't know why `Typescript` expects `off`'s first parameter to always be an `HTMLElement`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-06-07 16:48 UTC

`scroll.list_widget_container` is a jQuery namespaced event, which is [not supported](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/discussions/69610) by the type declarations.

You can accomplish the same goal more reliably by passing a reference to the same handler function to `.off` as you did to `.on`.

(Documentation for [`.on`](https://api.jquery.com/on/) and [`.off`](https://api.jquery.com/off/).)

## rem units in the codebase

*2024-06-26 to 2024-06-27 · 18 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/rem.20units.20in.20the.20codebase/with/1839289)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:32 UTC

As I've been working on info density, I've been thinking more about the 86 or so instances of `rem` units in the code base. There's nothing immediately actionable here, but I want to toss out what I'm thinking so we can return to it after 9.0.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:34 UTC

All of those `rem` units are based on a 16px `rem`. The `rem` expands from the [root em unit](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-3/#font-relative-lengths), which is the font-size set on the root element, `<html>`

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:36 UTC

However, for historical reasons I don't understand, Zulip has set its font-size on the `<body>` element. That's why even though in the legacy sizing, `1rem` === `16px`, the browser default.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:42 UTC

So probably some combination of these things will need to happen:

* We'll need to discuss and see the side-effects of moving the `font-size` and probably `line-height` declaration up to the `html` selector
* But first, we'll likely need to decide which `rem` values actually should *not* adjust with the `font-size`, as the `rem` has basically been a constant value so far (16px), which means there could be unintended side-effects to moving a user-adjustable `font-size` declaration up to `html`
* If we do opt to set the `font-size` on `html`, there may be things (especially horizontal dimensions) currently expressed as `rem` that should be expressed as pixels or another fixed unit
* Additionally, again if we do opt to set the `font-size` on `html`, we might find that certain things expressed so far in the info density project as `em` units would be easier to reason about as `rem` units. For example, I had to add [this ugly little style declaration](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/30591/files#diff-e5c601c5a72f45689502f875b361fd804be923263b0c56af6ff5c6ed5571fe19R425) in the user-circle PR so as to not have the user circle on the user-profile modal turn enormous. Saying that user circles are a certain `rem` would obviate the need to redeclare font-size values like that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:50 UTC

How do you get the 86 instances number?

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:51 UTC

Sloppily. It's fewer than that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:51 UTC

I guess this is one metric:
```
$ git grep 'rem;' web/styles/ | grep -v portico | wc -l
46
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:52 UTC

`git grep "[0-9]rem" web/styles/*.css | wc` yields 50

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:52 UTC

I would guess that most of these are not intentional and should just be converted the the number of `em` that is mathematically equivalent.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:53 UTC

There's a couple used in `calc()` statements that aren't terminated with a semicolon.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:53 UTC

Certainly the ones in `settings.css` smell that way to me on quick read.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:54 UTC

Yes. At 16/140, there would be no change. But things would get smaller at legacy sizes.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:55 UTC

Or are you saying we take, say, `1rem` and convert it to `1.1429em` (16px at 14px/1em)?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:55 UTC

Well what I meant is if we currently have `1rem`, which ends up being 16px, turn that into `16/14em`, such that the thing looks identical in the legacy size, yeah.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:55 UTC

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-06-26 20:56 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 21:45 UTC

Sure. What I'm thinking is if we first purge items that would break if we changed the `font-size` on `<html>`, then we're free to just move the `font-size` declaration up to `<html>`.

There is an open PR (#28470) which removes the old `private_message_policy` setting and adds 2 new settings for DM permissions - `direct_message_permission_group` and `direct_message_initiator_group`.
- `direct_message_initiator_group` - Who can initiate DM thread
- `direct_message_permission_group` - Who must be in every DM conversation
***
Checking `direct_message_initator_group` permission requires checking for previous messages in the DM thread on the client side. Currently, this is done using `all_messages_data` but @Sahil Batra raised a problem with this solution:
Not all messages are loaded on the client initially and the ones which are left are loaded after narrowing to the view. So if I am trying to send a message to a group but the messages are not fetched yet because I have not narrowed to the thread, I will not be allowed to send the message even though there are previous messages in the group.
Here is the discussion on GitHub: [comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/28470#discussion_r1652838076)
**What could be the possible solutions for this issue?**
***
Quoting @Sahil Batra :
> That will be a problem. It will be fine to show UI/button when user is not allowed to send messages because server will return an error, but not the other way around.
> 
> Solution other than just showing the UI to send messages is check by sending a request to server.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-27 19:54 UTC

I think for v1, I'd be fine with `direct_message_intiator_group` not being enforced client-side when we don't have the data to be certain. 

We will have the data to know in a very common case, namely that you're looking at the DM view in question. We can check that by looking at `message_lists.current`, checking if its filter matches the DM view we're composing to, and then checking if both `fetch_status.has_found_oldest` shows that it's empty ... But there might be a better way that involves looking at whether we're currently displaying the empty-view notice.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-27 19:55 UTC

And we can avoid paying the cost of doing that whole check if we already have cached a message for that view.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-27 20:00 UTC

So I think that suggests the following client-side enforcement algorithm

- We extend the `RecentDirectMessages` class in `pm_conversations.ts` to support being queried with a `pm_conversations.has_conversation(user_ids_string)` method; this can be a prep PR.

Then to check `direct_message_initiator_group` client-side:
- First, we check if we're in the authorized group. If so, approve.
- We call `pm_conversations.has_conversation(user_ids_string)` to see if we know there's already a message there. If so, approve.
- We check if we're currently looking at an empty DM conversation view for the recipient. If so, reject.
- Otherwise, approve, ideally passing back some flag that disables local echo for this message for nicer error-handling if the server rejects the message.

## maxWidth on Tippy tooltips

*2024-07-03 to 2024-07-03 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/maxWidth.20on.20Tippy.20tooltips/with/1845656)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:15 UTC

We currently have `maxWidth: 300` as part of initializing Tippy in `tippyjs.ts`:

```js
tippy.default.setDefaultProps({
    // Tooltips shouldn't take more space than mobile widths.
    maxWidth: 300,
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:17 UTC

However, Tippy's own CSS includes `max-width: calc(100vw - 10px)`, which arguably better ensures that Tippies will never be larger than any viewport. [Tippy's documentation confirms](https://atomiks.github.io/tippyjs/v6/all-props/#maxwidth) that that's the purpose of their CSS.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:18 UTC

That said, `max-width: 300px` might apply to how we're using Tippy beyond the mobile concerns noted in the comment in `tippyjs.ts`, so I thought I'd ask after it here before removing the `maxWidth` line from the initalizer.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-07-03 15:31 UTC

It is fair to be a bit concerned since we have fixed a lot of bugs with tippy in the past. My main concerns when changing `maxWidth` would be to ensure tooltips don't take too much width, like we don't want them to take `calc(100vw - 10px)` on wide screen sizes. Also, we will need to ensure any tooltips using `appendTo: "parent"` have not overflow their parent width.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:33 UTC

Yes. There's for example in the message area a `width: max-content` declaration that would seem to serve that purpose, although even that will be beholden to any `max-width` value.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:36 UTC

What we might want to do is pull the 300 out of the initializer and write something like this in our CSS instead:

```css
[data-tippy-root] {
     max-width: min(300px, calc(100vw - 10px));
}
```

For viewports narrower than 300px, Tippy's preferred method takes over, but we hold everything else to 300px (but expressed in em units at 14px/1em). That should maintain the status quo, but also allow things to scale up with the font size.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-07-03 15:40 UTC

Sounds like the right thing to do.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 15:41 UTC

I'll be asking for your most mercilessly scrutinizing review once I get this put up :) Thanks, Aman!

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-07-03 16:36 UTC

Eh, walking this idea back. Tippy defaults to `350` for `maxWidth`, so for now I'm just going to change the initializers to `em` units (which Tippy accepts).

## CSS selector performance

*2024-07-03 to 2025-04-17 · 123 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/CSS.20selector.20performance/with/1845719)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-03 16:33 UTC

So I did a bit of testing with chrome's [CSS selector profiling](https://css-tricks.com/the-truth-about-css-selector-performance/) feature, and took a screenshot of where it flagged time as going:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ae/7FsOD9fjJ39Xd5jRw8NBcaAS/image.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-03 16:35 UTC

While some of the rows are from my ad blocker and thus beyond our control, a bunch of others look to be overly broad selectors, for example this `*` in `.color_animated_buttom`:

```
.color_animated_button {                                                                                
    display: flex;                                                                                      
    justify-content: center;                                                                            
    background-color: hsl(0deg 0% 90%);                                                                 
    color: hsl(0deg 0% 0%);                                                                             
    border-radius: 4px;                                                                                 
                                                                                                        
    & span {                                                                                            
        color: hsl(0deg 0% 0%);                                                                         
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    &:hover {                                                                                           
        cursor: pointer;                                                                                
        background-color: hsl(240deg 96% 68%);                                                          
        color: hsl(0deg 0% 100%);                                                                       
                                                                                                        
        & span {                                                                                        
            color: hsl(0deg 0% 100%);                                                                   
            transition: all 0.2s ease;                                                                  
        }                                                                                               
                                                                                                        
        transition: all 0.2s ease;                                                                      
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    * {                                                                                                 
        padding: 6px 3px;                                                                               
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    .fa {                                                                                               
        position: relative;                                                                             
        top: 3px;                                                                                       
    }                                                                                                   
}                                                                                                       
```

Using a `*` inner selector is, as I understand it, quite inefficient, because the browser's bottom-up matching process will end up processing that selector for every element it's trying to render, before checking that the parent selector situation doesn't match.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-24 17:16 UTC

When we’re fixing these, remember that the goal is to make each class name unique across the entire app, *by itself*. We cannot rely on descendant selectors or nesting to correctly establish a scope, as I [explained before](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/CSS.20nesting/near/1283355).

```scss
.foo {
    div { /* very bad */
    }
}

.foo div { /* very bad */
}

.foo {
    .title { /* bad */
    }
}

.foo .title { /* bad */
}

.foo-title { /* good */
}
```

This is also important for maintainability; it lets us grep for `foo-title` to find all of the associated code and styles and nothing irrelevant.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-24 17:18 UTC

This is one of those cases where the things that are bad for performance are also bad for maintainability; `.foo .title` will be much slower than `.foo-title` if we have thousands of elements with `.title` classes that mean different things in different places in the app.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-20 00:07 UTC

Adapting here a comment I just made on #31006 because it will apply to this work more generally:

A principle I recommend for these "example data" functions is that the data they produce should be maximally boring by default — anything interesting should be present in the data only when the individual test specifically mentioned that in its own source code.

So for example that means a message should by default have no reactions, no topic links, and definitely no submessages.

A function generating a reaction, a topic link, or a submessage can potentially still be useful to have as a shared helper in web/tests/lib/. The way to provide them is for that code to just export them, and then tests can call them and pass the results to e.g. a function that will make the whole message.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-20 00:28 UTC

More broadly, the data in tests should be
* realistic. So it satisfies the types that we'd put on real data, but also invariants that aren't in the type system: IDs are positive, if there's a channel/stream message with a given ID then there's never a DM with the same message ID, and numerous others.

  This is good because unrealistic data can make tests fail for silly reasons that don't happen in the real app. Unrealistic data can also get in the way of debugging a test failure — it can make it harder to tell whether a failure is because of a real bug in the app, or because the test's data doesn't make sense.

* boring, except in the aspects that are the point of the test. An object of type T is interesting when it uses some optional feature that some T's have but many don't; or when it exercises some tricky edge case that rarely happens. In any given test, each object should only be interesting in the ways that the test is intended to test.

  This is good because each of the ways the object is interesting is something that a reader of the test is likely to notice and may have to think about in order to understand what it's doing. When test data is interesting in irrelevant ways, that creates unnecessary work for the reader. When it's interesting only in relevant ways, that helps the reader focus immediately on those aspects.

  It's good also because when optional features and tricky edge cases are tested in their own test cases that are focused specifically on them, that often helps with writing more thorough tests for those areas too.

Then my comment above about "example data" functions can be summarized by saying they should be as helpful as possible toward tests producing data that's as boring as possible while being realistic.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-20 00:38 UTC

The current project of using real user/channel/etc. objects is basically all about making the data in the tests more realistic. Part of the motivation for that is so that we can eventually have the type-checker run on them (after we also deal with the other class of obstacle [discussed above](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/typescript.20node.20tests/near/1886812)), but it's also good for our test suite for the other reasons I described just now.

The data generated in PRs #30831 and #31006 is already nicely realistic and boring in a lot of ways; and I think the majority of the review comments on them so far are basically about further ways to make them realistic and boring:
* different stream IDs for different streams (realistic)
* different names for different streams (realistic)
* `rendered_description` is HTML (realistic; or merely boring, if you might also want to handle a case where the server sends invalid HTML)
* messages have no reactions, topic links, or submessages (boring)

On #30831, @Tim Abbott [asked](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/30831#issuecomment-2257235042):
> I think there remains an open question of whether this should automatically add the stream to `stream_data`; my guess is yes would be preferred, but it's worth some discussion in #frontend.

I agree that's likely to be convenient. (And if there are some tests that don't want that, the function could grow a boolean flag to opt out.)

We don't do that in zulip-mobile or zulip-flutter, because there isn't a sensible way it could work, because there isn't a global analogous to `stream_data`. Data like the list of streams lives on a state object which isn't a singleton.

But then our tests constantly have to be sure to add to the state the stream objects (and user objects, etc.) that they generate. We have helpers that make that all reasonably convenient, and it's not a problem for us — but as long as you do have all the state global, you probably might as well have these test-data-constructing helpers add their results to that global state by default.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-10-09 23:19 UTC

Another thought I had is that we can use [`Proxy`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Proxy) to create a partial object that throws when accessing missing properties, rather than giving `undefined`. It would then be typesafe to annotate that partial object with the full object type, since execution cannot continue with a mistyped value. This is probably not what we want for common objects like users and streams where we can easily delegate the creation of real objects to a common helper, but might be useful in the long tail of one-off object mocks.

**Greg Price** · 2024-10-09 23:30 UTC

Yeah, that sounds useful.

We do a version of that in the zulip-flutter tests — in our case, to make fakes for complicated objects that represent interfaces to the outside world, like an HTTP client or a client for receiving FCM notifications. We implement whatever methods are relevant, and if a method we didn't implement gets called then it throws.

In Dart, one does this with [the `Fake` class](https://pub.dev/documentation/test_api/0.7.3/fake/Fake-class.html) from the stdlib's test framework, like so:
```dart
class FakeImageHttpClient extends Fake implements HttpClient {
```

That class's implementation is about four lines of code, built atop a Dart feature akin to JS's `Proxy`. Just like with your suggestion, it makes it type-safe to say that a `FakeImageHttpClient` instance is a value of type `HttpClient`.

## hashchange while using `with` narrow operator #30114

*2024-07-13 to 2024-07-15 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/hashchange.20while.20using.20.60with.60.20narrow.20operator.20.2330114/with/1888080)*

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-07-13 13:33 UTC

I am starting this topic to discuss how to handle the hash changes while using the `with` operator.

So, in the current version of the PR #30114, in case the filter terms are adjusted after contacting the server and the  filter has `with` operator, then update the old hash (which reflects the old filter before adjustments made) to a new hash, which matches the current filter.

Now I guess I can't be using `browser_history.set_hash` here because it would add the `new_hash` on the top of `old_hash` in the history. Since the `old_hash` basically redirects to the `new_hash`, it makes the back option to not function.

I also can't use `window.location.replace` like how `near` operator does because unlike `near` operator, the anchor here is "last message id", rather than some fixed message id.  I feel this would cause an issue if user has "Automatic mark as read" because after redirecting, it is possible that the messages below last unread may be marked as read, and then when we call to `replace` the hash, then the new hash is loaded again, thus causing the anchor to shift to the `last_msg_id` since all the messages in that narrow would be marked read before calling `window.location.replace`.

Hence, I feel using `window.location.replaceState` would be most appropriate here (just replacing the hash and not loading in the updated hash). Thoughts on this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-15 05:49 UTC

If we just need to prevent triggering a view change, I thought we already had a mechanism for that, maybe `browser_history.changing_hash`? I'm not sure, maybe I'm misremembering.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-07-15 11:37 UTC

The closest I could find  was [`update_current_history_state_data`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/9a57505f63a80ed2362f8d2daa07456bd8d0235d/web/src/browser_history.ts#L164).  However, that too just updates the state and keeps the hash as `window.location.href`, so maybe I need to refactor it if I want to just update the hash without triggering hashchange or changing view.

## presence of `with` operator after processing the permalink

*2024-07-17 to 2024-11-11 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/presence.20of.20.60with.60.20operator.20after.20processing.20the.20permalink/with/1893035)*

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-07-17 20:27 UTC

In the [review comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/30924#discussion_r1680179129) @Tim Abbott discussed about the possibility of removing the `with` operator once we correct the narrow terms and go to the correct/expected narrow. This would mean a link of type `#narrow/stream/../topic/../with/12` would take you to the right topic, and then update the url to `#narrow/stream/../topic/..`.

This may keep the topic links consistent with the current ones. I don't think it would be any different in handling `is_conversation_view` because with #30924 a narrow containing`["channel", "topic", "with"]`is of conversation view. (mainly because it is more or less like ``["channel", "topic"]` itself -- returns the last unread of the conversation).

The trade off for removing the `with` operator after processing them is when a user tries to copy the url and post it somewhere else (which usually is much easier than copying link from left sidebar), it won't be a permalink.

From the implementation point of view, I guess it can't be added to [`this.fix_terms`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/c622622135d88753f3777e00d314f504a819546c/web/src/filter.ts#L873) like we do for  `dm` now (since it would wipe out `with` when filter is initially set up). This would mean we may require hash change calls to remove the `with` operator irrespective of whether the narrow has updated or not (currently if narrow is not updated, we don't make a hash change call).

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-17 21:05 UTC

The concern I have with the current model is that I suspect there's probably various random other code paths, whether existent or to be written in the future, that might sloppily directly inspect `sorted_term_types` and look for just channel/topic being present to see if it's a normal conversation view.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-17 21:07 UTC

So one strategy would be to try to avoid that outcome by being careful, but I'm just wondering if there's any sense in which a `with` view should look different to the codebase once it's resolved to being a redirect or not? 

At least it seems like it might be nice for the URL in the hash to just be that of the destination, but maybe we want the `with` in there so that if you send it to someone it'll work? I'm not sure.

But if it's not intended to be visible, it seems like it'd be nice if the `Filter` data structure looks identical once the redirect has been fully processed.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-24 20:05 UTC

Having the `with` in the URL bar seems useful for the sake of people copying the link and sharing it.

I think the trend I generally see in other apps would actually point to us going further in that direction: that when you visit a conversation and you have only stream/channel and topic in the link, we'd update the location URL so that you have a `with` operator too, making it automatically a permalink.

I don't know that we necessarily need to do that; in some apps that behavior can feel a bit annoying. But often it's annoying because it makes the URLs giant or adds a lot of noise that makes it hard to see the more human-readable parts, and I feel like we've successfully designed these permalinks in a way that avoids that. And it sure is nice for links to automatically just keep working.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-24 20:08 UTC

Yeah I have been thinking that's a direction we want to go in as well. Probably worth prototyping; @Rohan Gudimetla FYI.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-07-25 10:23 UTC

Yeah, this definitely makes a lot sense, I'll open a PR

## narrowing performance

*2024-07-27 to 2024-10-04 · 27 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/narrowing.20performance/with/1904245)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 00:40 UTC

So I did a little profiling of the end-to-end performance of navigating to #**frontend>typescript migration** just now, to collect some statistics that might be helpful for prioritizing web app performance work.

Here's a screenshot of the main work profile. There's actually a bunch more stuff that happens after the main 187ms `message_view.show` call, but a lot of that is after we've already shown the content, and feels less important to me.

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c5/Zai4optmKQEMg2vJ1H-SNMZn/image.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 01:02 UTC

- 11ms are spent in `load_local_messages`: This is constructing a `MessageListData` object of the messages cached by the web application's `all_messages_data` structure, and determining which messages actually match the view. Could be worth doing some localized profiling of that, which is largely `filter.predicted`, just because we've never done that before and there might be some silly things we do there. The function `_build_predicate` does have the comment `FIXME: This is probably pretty slow.` in it :).
- Basically the rest of the work, 169ms, is in `handle_post_message_list_change`. This breaks into several chunks, detailed next.
- 9ms is `build_message_groups`. Most of that time is timestamp manipulation, #**frontend>format_small_avatar_url**, and the `same_day` function, so there may be some opportunity for optimization or caching here. But obviously not a huge amount of opportunity here.
- 34ms is handlebars rendering. I wouldn't be surprised if this can be optimized, but it seems Fine and we might be best off working on replacing the templating engine with something faster over fiddling with this.
- 5ms is `post_process` -- our HTML manipulation in `rendered_markdown.ts`. We discussed in #**issues>thumbnailing** that we could probably make this stage faster by using the approach taken in edf34ada6380c83be48d52fedc5ad96f06272e6f for all of it.
- 20ms is recalculating style (the first purple section in each pair); #**frontend>CSS selector performance** could reduce this considerably. The main block is 13.5ms for the message feed itself, but there's another 7ms of other style recalculations from the sidebar updates 
- 31ms is opaque browser "Layout" (the second purple section in each pair), 19ms or so in the message feed itself. I suspect this can be optimized with HTML/CSS that is cheaper for the browser, but I don't know tools to use to do so. 
- 32ms is `unread.process_visible`; I think this is basically the work of marking a message as read and notifying the server. Almost all of this is `unread_ops.update_unread_counts`, and half is just `unread.get_counts`; these are more expensive than I'd expect and might be an opportunity for optimization. 
- ~35ms is updating the left and right sidebars, not counting the 15ms of "Recalculate Style/Layout", which I did bundle into numbers for those categories above.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 01:16 UTC

So I think there's basically a handful of things that seem like good opportunities from that profile:
- #**frontend>CSS selector performance** might save ~10ms, or ~5% in this sample. This might be a higher portion if there were more complex messages to render, though, and the work seems like it's pretty low-hanging fruit that improves code quality too, so we should just do it. 
- #**frontend>format_small_avatar_url** would be a very small win but is easy, we should just do it.
- We should probably look into whether the `_build_predicate` function can be optimized, given the comment. One thing I notice is that we're looking up the channel by name in every loop iteration, rather than using `._sub` or some other less silly approach. Probably only a few milliseconds of opportunity in this profile, but might be impactful when processing more messages.
- Not listed in this profile is the whole dance of fetching message history from the server. That probably deserves its own topic, since there's a lot of opportunity there that refactoring in 9.0 makes pretty accessible.
- We should probably look at optimizing the data flow around `unread.get_counts`, but that might deserve its own profiling thread.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-27 01:18 UTC

I’m somewhat alarmed by the *number* of purple style/layout recalculations, as it suggests there may be layout thrashing involved.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 01:23 UTC

I think it's not so bad -- the later ones are for the navbar/right sidebar/left sidebars having their content changed, respectively.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-27 01:25 UTC

I see at least 12 of them. Ideally we would write all our stuff to the DOM and the browser would efficiently recalculate everything that changed once right before painting it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 03:58 UTC

Profiling with a 600ms render of a "channel feed" with tons of message history in a development environment, it breaks down as roughly:
- 10% `build_message_groups`, of which 1/3 is `start_of_day` for `same_day`
- 14% "Recalculate Style"
- 22% "Layout", with a bunch more "Parse HTML" -- these likely scale with how much HTML we have.
- 30% Handlebars, half of which is `formatMessage` (translations), so that might be worth looking at.  
- A lot of the smaller things above don't show up very highly on the overall profile.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 04:00 UTC

I'm a bit puzzled how expensive `intl.formatMessage` is given that it has a cache. I wonder if there's a way to get that profile broken down by which strings are involved.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 04:09 UTC

- The `message_failed` DOM elements for messages that failed to send seem to be present unconditionally. I think they should be inside a `{{#unless msg/locally_echoed}}` block at the very least, since I believe only locally-echoed messages can ever have those elements. Opened #31332 to track this.
- The `message_length_controller` block with its "show more/less" buttons is present in every message even if the message hasn't been collapsed to show those. Opened #31333 to track this.
- `.message_edit` may or may not be needed there to hold that position in the DOM, but the `message_edit_form` div inside it seems like it could definitely only be there if the message was edited. Opened #31334 to track this.
