## narrowing performance: is_same_day

*2024-07-27 to 2024-07-29 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/narrowing.20performance.3A.20is_same_day/with/1904318)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 04:59 UTC

Following up on @Tim Abbott [this observatio](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/narrowing.20performance/near/1904285) from profiling switching message views in Zulip:
> * 10% `build_message_groups`, of which 1/3 is `start_of_day` for `same_day`

This is the code in question that we're spending ~3% of our time rendering a message feed calling:
```
/** Get the start of the day for the given date in the given time zone. */                              
export function start_of_day(date: number | Date, time_zone: string): Date {                            
    const offset = get_offset(date, time_zone);                                                         
    let t = Number(date) + offset;                                                                      
    t -= t % 86400000;                                                                                  
    return new Date(t - get_offset(new Date(t - offset), time_zone));                                   
}                                                                                                       

/** Are the given dates in the same day in the given time zone? */                                      
export function is_same_day(left: number | Date, right: number | Date, time_zone: string): boolean {    
    return start_of_day(left, time_zone).getTime() === start_of_day(right, time_zone).getTime();        
}                                                                                                       
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 05:00 UTC

What's a little unfortunate about it is that we call it mainly in loops where we iterate through a bunch of messages and so end up calling `start_of_date` for the same value twice in a row -- once when it was the current message, and the immediately after when it's the previous message for comparing with the next one.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 05:01 UTC

There's probably a few ways we could fix that, but I think this might be what LRU caches are for?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 05:15 UTC

https://www.npmjs.com/package/lru-cache seems to be already in the project, so we could look at if that helps. We'd need to be careful to use both the `date` (an integer in this case) and timezone string in our cache keys.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-27 06:17 UTC

I guess I'll defer opening an issue for discussion on whether a cache is the right strategy on this one. It looks like most of the time is in `get_offset`, so that might be the right function to cache? Not sure.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 00:48 UTC

Having not looked at the code of the loop, the first thing I'd try for a caching strategy is to move the equality check from `is_same_day` out into the loop body. Then the loop can just remember the last value in a local variable.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 00:51 UTC

It's also a bit puzzling that that `start_of_day` function calls `new Date` twice and `get_offset` twice.

I'm skeptical that that logic is even quite right. Even if it is I suspect it can be simplified.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 00:55 UTC

Plus, why is it taking an arbitrary time zone as an argument? We're always using the browser's local time zone for this calculation, right? (That's the behavior I see when I try changing my time zone in Zulip settings — it has no effect on the timestamps I see in the message feed.)

IIRC the API the browser gives us will happily do whatever date calculations we want in its own local time zone, but doing a calculation in some arbitrary other time zone involves pulling in a library that bundles the time-zone database, and the library may or may not be as well written for efficiency as one would like. So we could use the `Date` API straight from the browser instead, and it'd be simpler to think about and also quite likely faster.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 01:00 UTC

For comparison here's what we have [in zulip-flutter](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/blob/84b64fcef74a3c7ec67ecae944e23062caab7f3c/lib/model/message_list.dart#L292-L315):
```dart
bool messagesSameDay(Message prevMessage, Message message) {
  // TODO memoize [DateTime]s... also use memoized for showing date/time in msglist
  final prevTime = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(prevMessage.timestamp * 1000);
  final time = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(message.timestamp * 1000);
  if (!_sameDay(prevTime, time)) return false;
  return true;
}

bool _sameDay(DateTime date1, DateTime date2) {
  if (date1.year != date2.year) return false;
  if (date1.month != date2.month) return false;
  if (date1.day != date2.day) return false;
  return true;
}
```

As you can see we don't have any caching (there's a TODO for it), but the computation on each side is basically just one `DateTime` constructor call, which computes the year/month/day/etc. in the local time zone.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 01:03 UTC

(Rereading, two lines there would be clearer as just `return _sameDay(prevTime, time);`, or perhaps by then inlining `_sameDay`. That's a relic of [a refactor](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/commit/69767fb1e21a40ddfa4fa3c0b4b289054774c4c6) that could have gone farther.)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-29 01:12 UTC

We remember the browser’s time zone on page load and use the remembered version in calculations, because otherwise the user might change it out from under us and confuse our logic.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-29 01:13 UTC

The reason `start_of_day` is more complicated than you might expect is daylight saving time, because of course it is.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-29 01:15 UTC

I can’t wait to replace all this nonsense with [`Temporal`](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-temporal).

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 04:55 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> We remember the browser’s time zone on page load and use the remembered version in calculations, because otherwise the user might change it out from under us and confuse our logic.

Hmm, I see.

… How does one exercise that situation? I can't find a time-zone option in the settings of either Chrome or Firefox.

**Greg Price** · 2024-07-29 05:10 UTC

And right, I figured the reason `start_of_day` was complicated was to attempt to handle days where the time zone's offset changed. It's just that it has the look, to my eye, of code that applies repeated attempts at correcting the values it's getting. Usually code that applies N corrections to something still has a bug and is doomed to adding another correction, then another, until someone rewrites it to get the right answer in the first place by doing something more principled.

Looking in the Git history, I see you wrote it (33e335dbd1a0ac463e5d9973be180833965ec789). So I'll believe that it's probably correct after all, or at least that there's a good reason it can't just be rewritten to something simpler and more correct. It could definitely benefit from being made clearer about what its reasoning is, though: either comments, or pull out some subexpressions of that `return` line as locals in order to give them meaningful names.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-07-29 16:01 UTC

Changing the OS time zone exercises that situation.

So looking into this a bit more, we don't actually have a ton of translateable strings in message bodies. Of those:

So while there might be things we can do to improve `formatMessage` performance, for this goal, it looks like the most impactful thing to do here is to get inactive HTML out of these templates.

export function slug_to_name(slug: string): string {

*2024-08-02 to 2024-08-07 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Key.20for.20message.20list.20data.20cache/with/1910581)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2024-08-02 10:02 UTC

This is revival of an old question [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/16746/files#r638352148). I am working on - Cache multiple MessageListData objects in the webapp frontend for instant view changes #15131

Does this sound like a good key to store message list data objects?

* Get the filter of the message list data
* Sort the terms using `sorted_terms`:

```js
    sorted_terms(excluded_operators?: string[]): NarrowTerm[] {
        let filter_terms = this._terms;
        if (excluded_operators) {
            filter_terms = this._terms.filter(
                (term) => !excluded_operators.includes(term.operator),
            );
        }

        return filter_terms.sort((a, b) => {
            const a_joined = `${a.negated ? "0" : "1"}-${a.operator}-${a.operand}`;
            const b_joined = `${b.negated ? "0" : "1"}-${b.operator}-${b.operand}`;
            return util.strcmp(a_joined, b_joined);
        });
    }
```

* JSON.stringify the sorted terms
* Create a `sha256` hash of the key (not sure this is really necessary but might be desireable since we can have very large keys otherwise)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-06 04:23 UTC

- The filter for the list must be a superset of the target view's
- The target ID for the current view must be within the range that the target list possesses.
- Exact match of the set of filters preferred.

## stream_info.get bug?

*2024-08-04 to 2024-08-12 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/stream_info.2Eget.20bug.3F/with/1912486)*

**Evy** · 2024-08-04 18:29 UTC

```js
export function get_sub_by_id(stream_id: number): StreamSubscription | undefined {
    return stream_info.get(stream_id);
}
```

I was surprised today to find out that `stream_info.get(stream_id)` actually can't return `undefined`.

```js
    get(k: number): T {
        const res = this.trues.get(k);

        if (res !== undefined) {
            return res;
        }

        return this.falses.get(k)!;
    }
```

This seems wrong, since we can definitely be looking up stream ids that don't map to anything. I think we should change it to:


```js
    get(k: number): T | undefined {
        const res = this.trues.get(k);

        if (res !== undefined) {
            return res;
        }

        return this.falses.get(k);
    }
```

Does that seem right?

**Evy** · 2024-08-04 18:30 UTC

It seems like we've already been calling it everywhere assuming it can be undefined.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-08-06 21:46 UTC

Yes.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-12 18:52 UTC

While we're thinking about this, I wonder if we want to have variants for the "assert this exists" vs. "may not exist" cases, like we have with users. It's kinda handy to be able to have code call a function for "read the stream ID from somewhere that we just put a known-valid stream ID" that never returns `undefined`, and throws exceptions instead of the value is invalid, because we think that reflects a bug elsewhere, not a normal unusual state that the code should handle. 

But that only makes sense if we can be confident that streams are never deleted from `stream_info` during a session if the stream is deactivated or something.

## Support Streams

*2024-08-11 to 2024-09-24 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Support.20Streams/with/1917160)*

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-08-11 19:12 UTC

How should we handle creation of `UserMessage` rows for support stream when a soft-deactivated user becomes online?

One thing that came to my mind was doing something like this:
```python
subscription_logs = list(
        RealmAuditLog.objects.filter(
            modified_user=user_profile, 
            modified_stream_id__in=stream_ids, 
            modified_stream__can_access_stream_topics_group_id=everyone_group_id,
            event_type__in=events
        )
        .order_by("event_last_message_id", "id")
        .only("id", "event_type", "modified_stream_id", "event_last_message_id")
    )
```

But this is wrong because this won't create `UserMessage` rows for a soft deactivated user who is in `can_access_stream_topics_group` in a support stream.

Also this doesn't account for the scenario where a user who is not a member of `can_access_stream_topics_group` receives messages in a topic they created while they are soft-deactivated.

And we would need to handle the cases where the `can_access_stream_topics_group` setting is changed.

One simple solution is to just skip creating `UserMessage` row for support streams.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-12 21:42 UTC

Hmm. The simplest answer here is likely to have support channels have the property that `UserMessage` rows are always created eagerly in them, just like mentions are, and soft-reactivation skips such channels. I doubt soft-reactivation is a useful optimization for support streams.

This is annoying if we allow changing an existing channel into a support channel, vs. having it be an immutable property. I think a good answer is to have it be immutable (only editable during channel creation) for now, and leave a comment mentioning this concern in the part of the implementation where we don't offer changing it in the API.

(It should be possible to do some calculation to correct around that, but seems complex and not worth it for the benefit for a first version).

**Notification Bot** · 2024-08-19 22:28 UTC

2 messages were moved here from #**design>Support Streams** by @Alya Abbott.

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-09-18 14:28 UTC

One significant issue I am facing relates to the situation described by @Sahil Batra in [this](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/29520#issuecomment-2269226061) comment.
> What happens, if a user was initially part of the `can_access_stream_topics_group` group and send a message to a topic, but not started the topic, and then that user is not part of `can_access_stream_topics_group`. Can the user see the topic, i.e. atleast the message that they sent themselves? Or al …

This was further clarified by @Alya Abbott [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/29520#issuecomment-2271881620).
> I think the user should have access to messages based on their current permissions, regardless of their prior permissions. This is the same as for a user who is no longer subscribed to a private stream, and loses access to the messages they sent and received there.

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-09-18 14:31 UTC

To address this issue, I initially iterated through all message IDs in the backend and filtered out those messages the user should not have access to based on the current members of `can_access_stream_topics_group`, as well as whether the user started the topic. Something like this:

```python
for message_id in message_ids:
    msg_dict = message_dicts[message_id]
    if user_profile and msg_dict["recipient_type"] == Recipient.STREAM:
        stream_id = msg_dict["recipient_type_id"]
        stream = get_stream_by_id_in_realm(stream_id, realm)
        if (
            stream.is_support_stream()
            and not check_access_based_on_can_access_stream_topics_group(user_profile, stream)
        ):
            topic_creator_user_id = get_topic_creator_user_id(
                msg_dict["sender_realm_id"], msg_dict["recipient_id"], msg_dict["subject"]
            )
            if topic_creator_user_id and user_profile.id != topic_creator_user_id:
                continue
    message_list.append(msg_dict)

```

However, this approach has two significant drawbacks:

1. It requires 2-3 database queries for each message, which is costly (also [mentioned](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/29520/files#r1741697134) by @Sahil Batra ).
2. It filters out all messages before sending them to the client, meaning any messages sent or received by the user while they were part of `can_access_stream_topics_group` will not appear in search results.

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-09-18 14:34 UTC

**Second Approach:**

Instead of filtering messages after fetching them, I considered filtering directly in the database query when fetching message IDs for support streams. By adding conditions to narrow down the results, we can retrieve only the message IDs the user currently has access to. Something like this:

```python
def add_support_stream_conditions(
    user_profile: UserProfile | None,
    inner_msg_id_col: ColumnElement[Integer],
    query: Select,
    is_web_public_query: bool,
    realm: Realm,
    stream_name: str,
    topic_name: str | None,
    recipient_id: int,
) -> Select:
    assert user_profile is not None

    topic_column = topic_column_sa()

    if topic_name:
        topic_creator_id = get_topic_creator_user_id(realm.id, recipient_id, topic_name)

        # Restrict messages to only those in topics created by the user
        if topic_creator_id != user_profile.id:
            # Restrict access to topics created by the user
            query = query.where(
                not_(
                    topic_column == literal(topic_name),
                )
            )
    else:
        # Get all topics created by the user in the support stream
        user_topics = get_topic_history_for_support_stream(user_profile, recipient_id)
        user_topic_names = [topic["topic"] for topic in user_topics]

        # Add condition to restrict messages to topics created by the user
        if user_topic_names:
            query = query.where(topic_column.in_(user_topic_names))

        else:
            query = query.where(false())

    return query
```

 While this approach is more efficient, it introduces its own challenges:

1. When `narrow` is null, the backend sends all messages based on the existence of `UserMessage` rows. However, this is unreliable for support stream messages since members of `can_access_stream_topics_group` can be removed, leaving them with `UserMessage` rows for messages they received while they were members. This could grant access to messages that the user should not see. To avoid this, we could avoid using cached messages for support streams and instead force the backend to filter messages based on the current access conditions.
  
2. This solution does not work for scenarios like the combined feed and recent conversations, where `narrow` does not exist (or is not related to fetching messages from stream or topic), resulting in all messages being sent back to the client.

**Notification Bot** · 2024-09-18 15:25 UTC

3 messages were moved here from #**design>Support Streams** by @Alya Abbott.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-23 22:56 UTC

The techniques in #29380 might be helpful for doing a post-processing access check.

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-09-24 15:12 UTC

## wrangling inline elements

*2024-08-15 to 2024-08-21 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/wrangling.20inline.20elements/with/1922014)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 19:58 UTC

Picking up more explicitly from the discussion in #**issues>global time wrapping**, I want to talk about migrating from `inline-block` and `inline-flex` elements for global times and mention blocks to simple `inline` elements. I've started with mention blocks, because they are simpler--being only text, and not containing an icon the way global times do.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 19:59 UTC

For those new to the issue, this is the problem: both `inline-block` and `inline-flex` (as well as `inline-grid`) do not behave as ordinary inline content. This can be seen in how punctuation, such as a comma, immediately trailing an @-mention will spill onto the line that follows:

[inline-block-broken-comma.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/5d/IaXJX3gnxJmkamMUfMyS314P/inline-block-broken-comma.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:01 UTC

Simply by removing `display: inline-block` so that mentions (`<span>` elements) return to their browser-default `display: inline` value, we immediately resolve the comma issue:

[inline-no-broken-comma-16-140.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/da/OwCVeE45m5QZ00CRRmawPF-j/inline-no-broken-comma-16-140.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:02 UTC

But--and there's always a *but*--a new issue arises in this case that is much more visible in compact mode:

[inline-no-broken-comma-compact.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/43/2pQOfJjwqNzMWwUuHdiNCsFu/inline-no-broken-comma-compact.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:02 UTC

As you can see, the tighter the line-height is, the more the colors on the mention blocks overlap.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:06 UTC

That overlap is due, however, to the content box of the typeface in use, rather than the line height (though once the line height exceeds the height of the typeface's content box, there is no more overlap; we faced [a similar issue in vertically aligning inline emoji](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/101-design/topic/info.20density.3A.20inline.20emoji.20presentation/near/1804483)).

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:08 UTC

I have yet to find any way to reduce the height of `inline` blocks smaller than their content box. You can set `line-height: 0` on `.user-mention`, and the colored background will not budge. You can also set something like `margin: -5px 0` and again, the height of the mention pills remains unaltered.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:09 UTC

Only when you go larger than the content box, as in this case with `line-height: 2` set on `.user-mention`, is there any visible effect:

[inline-mentions-line-height-2.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/e5/J2bjKxVsYQR7rTfH78M0Tiax/inline-mentions-line-height-2.png)

The problem there is that now you're also affecting the line height of all lines that contain a mention pill, which on longer multi-line messages will be distracting at least to some degree.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:10 UTC

"But wait," you might say. "We display `<code>` spans as inline, and there is no overlap in their lines." And that's true:

[mentions-vs-code-spans-16-140.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8a/qE0CcSpXevr1KOwQswzWP0xA/mentions-vs-code-spans-16-140.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:11 UTC

But the reason code spans do not have their backgrounds overlap is that code spans have their `font-size` set to `0.825em`, or 82.5% of the font-size in the message area. A smaller font size means a smaller content box, which means a cleaner fit within all but unreasonably tight surrounding line heights.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:13 UTC

And although this dovetails somewhat with a discussion more properly had in #design, I did want to plumb for any ideas, including from @Anders Kaseorg, for how we might handle the background-overlap problem. Based on what I've been able to glean from this, there are three options here (some possibly more designy, I realize, than frontendy):

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:14 UTC

1. We decide that breaking a comma or period onto a newline in a message area is unacceptable--more unacceptable than those likely rare cases where nearby @-mentions stack up across multiple subsequent lines.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:16 UTC

2. We experiment with using a repeating image for the background of @-mentions (though global times features a surrounding border, presenting an additional complication). Using the `background-size` attribute, we simply shrink the area of the background to be closer to the line-height in the area, rather than the content box defined on the typeface.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 20:18 UTC

3. We do nothing, and just accept the case of punctuation trailing onto a new line as the cost of better management of the height of things like mention pills and global times (I don't think this is responsible or workable, but it is an option).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-08-15 20:49 UTC

It seems that an inline box’s height depends on its own font-size, but not the font-size of its children. So it can be shrunk by nesting: `<span style="font-size: .8em; background: purple"><span style="font-size: 1.25em">@Hello</span></span>`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-08-15 20:53 UTC

This effect can be seen in [figure 1 here](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-inline-3/#line-boxes).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-08-15 20:55 UTC

And I think the relevant [specification text](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-inline-3/#inline-height) is

> To find the [layout bounds](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-inline-3/#layout-bounds) of an [inline box](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-display-3/#inline-box), the UA must first align all the glyphs *directly* contained in the inline box to each other by their [dominant baselines](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-inline-3/#dominant-baseline). (See [§ 3.3 Baselines of Glyphs and Boxes](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-inline-3/#baseline-tables).) If the inline box contains no glyphs at all, or if it contains only glyphs from fallback fonts, it is considered to contain a “strut” (an invisible glyph of zero width) with the metrics of the box’s [first available font](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-fonts-4/#first-available-font).

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-15 21:04 UTC

Great, thank you, Anders. I'll try implementing that markup based approach.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-19 20:14 UTC

I've been working on this today, and the results look good and promising. But as I've been working on the backend Markdown processor, I'm curious about what happens to previous mention pills, etc. sent before these markup changes are put into effect. Put in frontend terms, is there a need to maintain CSS for the previous single-`<span>` mentions, even once the double-`<span>` mentions come into use?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-19 23:38 UTC

What you want to do is change `rendered_markdown.ts` which already does rewriting of the HTML to fit the frontend's needs, including various fiddling with mentions, to fiddle slightly differently.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-19 23:38 UTC

One should be thinking about the output of the backend Markdown processor as a syntax tree that's shared with all clients and not to be changed as part of styling work for a given client.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-08-21 20:05 UTC

All right. #31416 is up with fixes for both mentions and global times, which appear virtually identical as before, but now are proper inline elements that will not be separated from trailing punctuation.

## :not(#does-not-exist) selectors

*2024-09-06 to 2024-09-06 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.3Anot.28.23does-not-exist.29.20selectors/with/1937582)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-06 17:07 UTC

I've noticed lately the appearance of selectors like `.showing-cloud:not(#does-not-exist) .comparison-tab-cloud` when inspecting elements in Firefox's (and Chrome's) browser tools. 

I'm unclear if the `:not(#does-not-exist)` is part of our build process or what, but one significant issue with it is that a selector will take on the same specificity as the same simple selector inside [a negation pseudo-class, as defined in the spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/selectors-3/#negation). So `.foo:not(#some-id)` actually is treated by the browser as more specific than `#some-id`. And since `#does-not-exist` actually *does not exist*, that `:not()` rule will always be true.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-06 17:47 UTC

I've not seen those before.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-06 17:48 UTC

We can probably check by manually inspecting files if that's present in our actual CSS files, or if it could be something being generated by either the browser or an extension.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-06 18:17 UTC

I've checked, and they're not present in the source. But they're easily found in the generated CSS, e.g., http://localhost:9991/webpack/app.css

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-06 18:42 UTC

It seems like certain PostCSS plugins add `.does-not-exist` or `#does-not-exist`, but looking through the generated CSS, that's happening in places where we're not even doing anything all that exotic

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 18:55 UTC

It’s from [css-has-pseudo](https://www.npmjs.com/package/css-has-pseudo), which I did not expect postcss-preset-env to enable by default.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 18:56 UTC

The increased specificity is the point.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-06 19:00 UTC

The default enabling is an unpleasant surprise, but thank you for tracking that down.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 20:22 UTC

Ah, that’s in fact not enabled. It’s actually from [@csstools/postcss-is-pseudo-class](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@csstools/postcss-is-pseudo-class).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 20:24 UTC

Although we don’t directly use `:is()`, [postcss-nesting](https://www.npmjs.com/package/postcss-nesting) generates `:is()` to correctly model the [specificity of nesting](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_nesting/Nesting_and_specificity).

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-06 23:07 UTC

Is there a standard remediation for these?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 23:11 UTC

We want to animate compositor properties like `transform` and `opacity`, which can be entirely animated on the GPU, rather than layout properties like `width` and `padding` or paint properties like `background-color`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-06 23:18 UTC

And we want to list specific properties rather than `transition: all`, so the rule can see what we’re transitioning (and, like, we can see too).

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-06 23:20 UTC

Yeah, I'm sure `transition: all` is just sloppy coding, but I guess transitions on `border` might be a case where we actually need to make a design change to fix it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-06 23:21 UTC

Probably we should focus on app stuff here; this likely mostly doesn't matter for the portico pages because they're so simple.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-10-23 19:47 UTC

Opened #32109 to start catching and hopefully discouraging these.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-23 20:05 UTC

How did you determine which properties are being transitioned for the third commit?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-10-23 20:10 UTC

By manual inspection. Regressions are possible.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-23 20:10 UTC

I guess that leaves me with the puzzle of how to audit for that risk.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-10-23 20:15 UTC

Some behavior changes are known; I’ve removed transitions of properties like `width` and `height` that were transitioned implicitly on page resize due to media queries, since that seemed unintentional and/or gratuitous.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-23 20:21 UTC

Yeah agreed those were likely not designed. Noticed one oddity reading it, but otherwise I'm guessing I won't find anything else without hand-testing all these things which is probably not worth the time; if a transition regression is important, we'll likely notice eventually in regular use.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-23 20:21 UTC

## layout bugs in the help modal

*2024-09-11 to 2024-09-13 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/layout.20bugs.20in.20the.20help.20modal/with/1939999)*

**Saubhagya Patel** · 2024-09-11 06:42 UTC

@Tim Abbott  said:
>  Probably for an actual PR, we'll want a cleaner selector using CSS classes though to avoid introducing more instances of [#frontend > CSS selector performance](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/6-frontend/topic/CSS.20selector.20performance), among other things.

Based on the above feedback, I came up with the following selector:
```
#message-formatting .rendered_markdown{
    & p, ol, ul, blockquote, .spoiler-block, pre{
        margin-bottom: unset;
    }
}
```
I’ve used `#message-formatting` to ensure the changes are isolated to only the Message Formatting window. Please let me know if this approach is effective or any improvements could be made.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-11 13:09 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-11 15:48 UTC

We could just have some JS code add that class to the relevant elements dynamically in `info_overlay.ts` rendering.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-11 16:35 UTC

Oh, that’s a much smarter approach. And makes it so we wouldn’t have to do the brittle job of keeping things in step with the Markdown processor—especially if and when that changes.

**Greg Price** · 2024-09-11 18:12 UTC

(replying to Saubhagya Patel)
> Based on the above feedback, I came up with the following selector: ``` #message-formatting .rendered_markdown{ & p, ol, ul, blockquote, .spoiler-block, pre{ margin-bottom: unset; } } ``` I’ve used `#message-formatting` to ensure the changes are isolated to only the Message Formatting window. Please …

To be explicit: this is an example of the kind of CSS pattern that looks perfectly reasonable, and does have the right behavior semantically, but that we've recently come to understand is expensive.

Specifically I believe this will cause the browser to do some work for every `p` element in the whole app, even when the Message Formatting modal isn't around. (Also every `ul` element, etc.)

That's the "bottom-up matching" mentioned in that other thread.

**Saubhagya Patel** · 2024-09-11 20:50 UTC

Based on the insightful review received, I came up with a function to dynamically add a class named `unset_margin_bottom`. Here, are some key points:
* The function receives the processed HTML string and returns it after performing the required operations.
* For the rows that output `<p>`, `<ul>`, `<ol>` as the outermost element, we can directly apply the class to them.
* Special Cases:
  * For `<blockquote>`, the class is applied to both the `<blockquote>` element and any `<p>` tags inside it.
  * For the code fragments with the class `codehilite`, the class is applied to the`<pre>` tag.
  * For the spoiler element with the class `spoiler-block`, the class is applied to the element itself.
  * For the */poll* and */todo* sections (the two sections appearing as the second and third to last), I opted to apply the class directly within the `output_html` field of their respective rows.

In the `info_overlay.ts` file:
There would be a slight modification in the `set_up_toggler` function to use the function being implemented:
```
export function set_up_toggler(): void {
    for (const row of markdown_help_rows) {
        if (row.markdown) {
            if(!row.output_html) {
                const message = {
                    raw_content: row.markdown,
                    ...markdown.render(row.markdown),
                };
                row.output_html = postprocess_content(message.content);
            }
            row.output_html = add_margin_unset_class(row.output_html);
        }
    }
    // rest of the function is same.
```
The function is as follows:
```
function add_margin_unset_class(html_string: string): string {
    const $html = $(html_string);
    const element = $html[0]?.tagName.toLowerCase();
    const elements_to_unset_margin = ['p', 'ul', 'ol'];

    // If the outermost element is one of the margin unset tags
    if (element && elements_to_unset_margin.includes(element)) {
        $html.addClass("unset_margin_bottom");
        return $html.prop("outerHTML");
    }

    // Special handling for <blockquote>, ".codehilite", ".spoiler-block"
    switch (element) {
        case "blockquote":
            $html.addClass("unset_margin_bottom");
            $html.find('p').addClass("unset_margin_bottom");
            break;

        default:
            if ($html.hasClass("codehilite")) {
                $html.find('pre').addClass("unset_margin_bottom");
            } else if ($html.hasClass("spoiler-block")) {
                $html.addClass("unset_margin_bottom");
            }
            break;
    }
    return $html.prop("outerHTML");
}
```
I would like to know everyone's thoughts on the above implementation. Thank you.

```js
export function DISCUSSING_NAME_FOR_THIS(stream_id_string: string): StreamSubscription {
    const stream = get_sub_by_id_string(stream_id_string);
    assert(stream !== undefined);
    return stream;
}
```

During code review, Tim [said](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/31299#discussion_r1757884004)

> I think the naming scheme of having the one that can fail with `assert_valid` in its name would be a lot more consistent with other function names.

```
export function get_user_by_id_assert_valid(                                                            
    user_id: number,                                                                                    
    allow_missing_user = !settings_data.user_can_access_all_other_users(),                              
): User {

        return get_by_user_id(user_id);                                                                 
    }                                                                                                   
                                                                                                        
    let person = maybe_get_user_by_id(user_id, true);

    }

}                                                                                                       
```

That's cheap to do because the function is very simple; just adds a line or two at each call site.

**Greg Price** · 2024-09-19 18:25 UTC

I think some of these call sites only look at the name, not anything subscription-related. So if they don't actually need the user to be subscribed (and they probably don't), it'd be good to clarify that by having them call a function that only promises to return a stream object, not a subscription.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-20 20:17 UTC

We [create](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/86d5ee5bdf492aaba8286482f1ba059fbef4b6f7/web/src/stream_data.ts#L837) `StreamSubscription` objects even for `never_subscribed` non-subscriptions.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-20 20:19 UTC

They have `subscribed: false` and `previously_subscribed: false` properties. I’d say they aren’t so much “fake” as poorly named.

**Greg Price** · 2024-09-20 21:03 UTC

Cool, yeah — the type is poorly named, then.

**Greg Price** · 2024-09-20 21:07 UTC

Skimming through `git grep -wC8 StreamSubscription`, there are a lot of things with that type and with names like "sub" that look like they really only mean a stream, not a subscription:
* they only look at the stream's ID and/or its name,
* and they're in a context where it doesn't seem like we'd want to assume the user has a subscription.

So probably it'd be good to clarify those to refer to a "stream" (or "channel"?), rather than "sub" or "subscription".

**Greg Price** · 2024-09-20 21:08 UTC

And then I think 3 of the 4 call sites of `stream_data.get_valid_sub_by_id_string` are examples of that. So those should probably just switch to using a function that says "stream".

The one exception is in `message_view_header.ts` where it looks at the `color` property:
```js
export function colorize_message_view_header(): void {
    const filter = narrow_state.filter();
    let current_sub;
    if (filter?.has_operator("channel")) {
        current_sub = stream_data.get_valid_sub_by_id_string(filter.operands("channel")[0]!);
    }
    if (!current_sub) {
        return;
    }
    // selecting i instead of .fa because web public streams have custom icon.
    $("#message_view_header a.stream i").css("color", current_sub.color);
}
```

That `if (!current_sub)` logic is a bit tangly. The function would probably be clearer if `get_valid_sub_by_id_string` were inlined there.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-20 21:13 UTC

We already have a `Stream` type that’s used in a few places. (The “channel” name is awkward to use in the frontend while we still have a `channel.ts` module with an unrelated meaning.)


## image dimensions and display: inline-block

*2024-09-19 to 2024-09-19 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/image.20dimensions.20and.20display.3A.20inline-block/with/1944938)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 16:56 UTC

So I discovered yet another weird and unpleasant thing about `display: inline-block` and replaced content (e.g., `<img>` tags) this morning while working on #**design>grey background around image thumbnails**.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 16:58 UTC

Compare these two screenshots of [this Codepen](https://codepen.io/karlstolley/pen/WNqVyvq):

[display-block.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/12/sYB8zZWnNP5q0ALSNW1ftHEU/display-block.png)
[display-inline-block.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/d0/hyp58849_3fUAgBvu9Zj998q/display-inline-block.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 16:59 UTC

By referencing a non-existant image `foo.jpg`, I'm trying to replicate the state of an `<img>` tag before its source has loaded. In the first screenshot, `.container` is displaying as a block, as is the default for all `<div>` elements of course. And it is correctly applying a `max-width` value against the `height` and `width` attributes of the image tag, preserving the aspect ratio of the image.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 17:01 UTC

But when `display: inline-block` wraps the image, the aspect ratio is preserved but the critical `max-width` value on the image is ignored.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 17:01 UTC

On CZO, this is what would cause a layout shift, no matter what due diligence we might have around `height` and `width` attributes on thumbnail images.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 17:05 UTC

I'm not done fiddling with this, but one possibility we might think about is some post-processing code that places inline media into a separate container that behaves as a flexbox. I don't know that that would necessarily solve the dimensions problem, but setting `display: flex` on that Codepen is encouraging:

[Screenshot 2024-09-19 at 1.04.29PM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/aa/c1MqSySAMraqig2M3cHAUGyH/Screenshot-2024-09-19-at-1.04.29PM.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 17:06 UTC

A flexbox solution would also get us out of some brittle use of margin for spacing in the area as well, including at the bottom of the message area.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-19 17:23 UTC

I guess the thing we need to be careful with in complicating the HTML for inline image elements is what that will mean for eventual work on #**api design>HTML pattern for truly inline images**; but given we'd need different HTML for images in an inline context anyway, I guess the answer is "that's not relevant at all".

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-19 17:27 UTC

Possibly. But it's also the case that inline elements happily become flex items inside a flex container, where they take on very different behavior. 

It would probably present a small nightmare of context-checking code, figuring out what gets, um, gallery-ized and what gets left to display inline. But those two could potentially co-exist more happily than the standalone `display: inline-block` things we have right now.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-19 17:31 UTC

Well, we currently only have images that are gallery-style, and I imagine it'll be obvious from CSS classes on image elements whether they're in the gallery mode or inline mode.

## structuring components via classnames

*2024-09-20 to 2024-09-26 · 21 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/structuring.20components.20via.20classnames/with/1945772)*

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-20 16:43 UTC

For those not not in sync, the banner redesign is currently underway, and the prototyping phase is particularly interesting. We are developing the components based on @Vlad Korobov's design, hosted on GitHub Pages, independent of the web app. This approach allows for more focused design discussions, free from the technical complexities of integrating it with the web app.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-20 16:43 UTC

Now, coming to main discussion: In the current implementation of the banners redesign, which can be currently tested at https://sayamsamal.github.io/zulip-banners-redesign/, I have used the following classes to make the current banner possible.
```css
:root {
	/* Equivalent dark mode colors specified at %dark-theme */
	--color-banner-brand-bg: #ECE9F6;
	--color-banner-brand-text: #4704AA;
	--color-banner-brand-close-btn: var(--purple-600);
	--color-banner-brand-border: color-mix(in oklch, #5633CC 40%, transparent);
}

.banner {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    align-items: center;
    font-size: 0.9375rem;
	/* contains styling common across all banners */
    color: var(--banner-text-color);
    background-color: var(--banner-bg-color);
}

.banner--top {
	/* The top banner variant */
	border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-banner-border);
}

.banner--brand {
	--banner-bg-color: var(--color-banner-brand-bg);
	--banner-text-color: var(--color-banner-brand-text);
	--color-banner-border: var(--color-banner-brand-border);
}
```

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-20 16:43 UTC

The idea over here is that you would require the base class `.banner` and would add/remove the other component-sepcific utility classes to specify the type of banner you want.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-20 16:45 UTC

Now, @Karl Stolley, on our last call discussing the banners, suggested another  wayof seeing this—use specific classes for a particular banner, which would contain all the CSS needed for that particular banner. So, from what I understand, it would be like having a `.compose-error-banner` class which would contain all the necessary banner properties along with the colors defined. This way, a contributor would only need to see a single class to understand the whole banner, and would should make maintaining them easier in that future changes, if any, would be specific in nature. I guess we would still have a common class in such a case so that we wouldn't have to define the structure of the banner (grid/flex properties) again and again. (@Karl Stolley please jump in, if this required more clarity than what I have managed)

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-20 16:46 UTC

TL;DR
- The banner redesign will be chance to discuss how we want to define our components, since it results in the redesign of two important components, the banners and buttons.
- Should we use atomic classnames, which define a certain part of the component, and can be added and removed as per the requirement. (OR) should we use specialized classnames to target specific banners and aim redesigned those particular set of instances at a time. (OR) some other way to look at this problem.

**Vlad Korobov** · 2024-09-20 18:45 UTC

Design of banners since then changed. Figma is an actual truth visually and we might need to experiment with color there

**Vlad Korobov** · 2024-09-20 18:47 UTC

It is up to you how to atructure component. From my perspective extra classes just add colorization by redifining some variables while layout of the banner is a base class

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-09-20 19:47 UTC

Shared classes are something I think we should be moving away from. If there are values we want shared--a color, a certain amount of padding, etc.--then it's better to express those as CSS variables. Otherwise, we end up with "Oh, it should be like a `.foo`, but with slightly less `border-radius`, or whatever. And that's how we end up in ugly specificity wars, using `.foo.bar`, `!important` and whatnot.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-09-20 19:49 UTC

Yeah, agreed.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-20 19:51 UTC

The proposed classes here aren’t shared; they’re only applied to the component with the base class `.banner`. They’re modifiers in the sense of [BEM](https://getbem.com/introduction/).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-09-20 19:55 UTC

Er, that is, if we logically only have one `.banner` component, with one template that conditionally applies the modifier classes. If we have multiple templates generating variants of `.banner`, yeah, that would be bad.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-24 11:58 UTC

This would help with not having to redefine the same color logic, for let's say, every other error banner.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-24 12:00 UTC

But I think having all the banners be a part of the same template might be difficult, since the content of the banner can vary between having a close button vs not having one, having 2 buttons instead of 3, etc.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-24 12:03 UTC

And very specific properties, we would use a specific unique class.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-24 12:04 UTC

In the current code, .copy-btn and .copy-btn-square, .tab-picker and .tab-picker-vertical would be the examples.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-09-24 13:49 UTC

## understanding visible: false in waitForSelector

*2024-10-03 to 2024-10-03 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/understanding.20visible.3A.20false.20in.20waitForSelector/with/1954563)*

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-10-03 21:03 UTC

I was trying to debug puppeteer tests in one of my PRs -- #31152. The puppeteer test there fails there because it wasn't able to find the dm recipient in the compose typeahead -- More precisely --
[failure-0.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/b6/x4vXwp485yq_Pvo-El1l_NGy/failure-0.png)

I talked to @Prakhar Pratyush about this few weeks back, where he actually pointed out :
```ts
// PM typeaheads always have an image. This ensures we are waiting for the right typeahead to appear.
        const entry = await page.waitForSelector(".typeahead .active a .typeahead-image", {
            visible: false,
        });
```
in [`common.ts`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/1b47134d0d564f8ba4961d25743f3ad0f09e6dfb/web/e2e-tests/lib/common.ts#L39). However, according to the Zulip docs:

> When using waitForSelector, you always want to use the {visible: true} option; otherwise the test will stop waiting as soon as the target selector is present in the DOM even if it’s hidden.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-10-03 21:04 UTC

Getting `visible: true` however, somehow gets the puppeteer tests to pass -- so i was wondering what might be the significance of `visible:false` here.

This change was introduced in 7e99c90190532dc4d23a0651b1118353b7250f6a

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-03 21:48 UTC

We can ask @Sohaib Ahmed in case he remembers, but I don't see the benefit to doing `visible: false`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-03 21:49 UTC

Probably you've identified the bug; using `visible: true` is usually what one wants; without it, it's easy for code to stop waiting too early and try the next step before it'll actually work.

## unknown channel ID in URL

*2024-10-07 to 2024-10-09 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/unknown.20channel.20ID.20in.20URL/with/1956769)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

I was testing my changes for general URLs with the "channel" operator and I noticed an odd side effect of our changing to using channel IDs for narrows.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

When we decode the operand (in `hash_util.decode_operand`) for a valid link in a channel that we don't have access to (it's a private channel, we're not signed in and it's not a web-public channel, I'm a guest user and haven't been subscribed to the channel, etc.), then the filter for the message list is being set with `{"operator": "channel", "operand": "", "negated": false}`. 

[guest user example of an unknown channel](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/df/jpVC-FY_iCaX51ghPwm21Cvh/Screenshot-from-2024-10-07-20-25-17.png)

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

And we're sending that to the server to fetch messages, which of course returns a `BAD_NARROW` error with a message of "Invalid narrow operator: unknown channel " since the operand is an empty string.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

I imagine that when we were using channel names in `web/src/filter.ts`, the message fetch request was being sent with the slug from the URL, e.g. `{"operator": "channel", "operand": "1-Zulip", "negated": false}` from the screenshot example, which would have also returned a `BAD_NARROW` error with "Invalid narrow operator: unknown channel 1-Zulip".

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

And then checks for empty narrow banners with the channel operand being set to an empty string are kind of confusing since we're trying to parse it as an ID.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-07 19:49 UTC

I'm not sure what the best fix is here, so posting here to get other folks thoughts.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-07 20:04 UTC

This sounds like a regression from refactoring work that @Evy was doing in recent weeks to use channel IDs for valid narrows consistently.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-07 20:06 UTC

It seems possible we want to rethink the abstractions the web app uses; the current model ends up working by creating a `Filter` object that's kinda malformed, and serving an error page while still having that stored... but maybe we should be failing earlier.

**Notification Bot** · 2024-10-08 11:01 UTC

18 messages were moved from this topic to #**frontend>unknown channel ID - empty feed banner** by @Lauryn Menard.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-08 11:03 UTC

I moved the discussion about what the empty feed banner/text should be for an unknown channel.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-08 11:05 UTC

Because we still need to address the message list being set with a `Filter` object that has the "channel" operator set with an operand of an empty string:

`{operator: "channel", operand: "", negated: false}`

**Evy** · 2024-10-08 19:17 UTC

I agree it's not ideal, but I'm also curious if there are undesired effects of this

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-09 15:42 UTC

I put up #31934 and pinged you for a review. It refactors the `message_fetch` code to be a bit clearer in what we're doing to construct the narrow parameter for that /api/get-messages call.

Fixing the handling of the narrow to use the channel integer ID for the "channel" term in the filter was what caused me to notice when we're passing the empty string for unknown channels.

I think my main question is if we want to be doing that message fetch with the empty string for the operand as it will always return an error. And if we don't where/how would we want to catch that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-09 17:20 UTC

Yeah, that message fetch query is pointless, so it does seem like we shouldn't be doing it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-09 17:25 UTC

I suspect the actual bug here is that this block at the very top of `message_view.ts` should be checking if there are any invalid operators just after parsing with the `new Filter` logic, and if so, render an empty-feed thing.

```
    // No operators is an alias for the Combined Feed view.                                             
    if (raw_terms.length === 0) {                                                                       
        raw_terms = [{operator: "in", operand: "home"}];                                                
    }                                                                                                   
    const filter = new Filter(raw_terms);                                                               
    filter.try_adjusting_for_moved_with_target();                                                       
                                                                                                        
    if (!show_opts.force_rerender && try_rendering_locally_for_same_narrow(filter, show_opts)) {        
        return;                                                                                         
    }                                                                                                   
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-09 17:25 UTC

Structurally, I think we're failing to sufficiently distinguish "this is an impossible operator or operator combination" from "this is a view that happens to not have any messages in it yet"

## throttle loader

**Aman Vishwakarma (AMANVISHWAKARMA27)** · 2024-10-11 11:38 UTC

Can somebody tell me how can I throttle the loading of a loader to the processing behaviour? 
for example: the loading when click on save button after editing a text.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-11 19:02 UTC

Can you explain your question with more context on what you're trying to do? I'm very confused.

**Aman Vishwakarma (AMANVISHWAKARMA27)** · 2024-10-11 19:31 UTC

So I want to solve the [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/29028), here I want to know the behaviour of the whole process like how the message and saved and loader is shown and hide. But, normally the process is very fast I am not able to see the behaviour. So,  I want to implement throttling on loader so that its loading  time can be delayed. 
I hope you got me.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-11 22:09 UTC

A better answer is to add a `time.sleep` in `do_send_messages` in the server, and an even better one is to use  your browser's developer tools to set a delay for network requests. See, e.g., https://www.browserstack.com/guide/how-to-perform-network-throttling-in-chrome.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-15 13:59 UTC

```typescript
    const operators_supporting_ids = new Set(["dm"]);
...
        if (operators_supporting_ids.has(canonical_operator)) {
            const user_ids_array = people.emails_strings_to_user_ids_array(raw_term.operand);
            assert(user_ids_array !== undefined);

        }

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-15 13:59 UTC

And fixing that reveals that another assertion in `message_util.get_direct_message_permission_hints` would be triggered  as part of the compose box logic ...

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-10-15 13:59 UTC

```typescript
export function get_direct_message_permission_hints(
    recipient_ids_string: string,
): DirectMessagePermissionHints {
...
    const dm_conversation = message_lists.current?.data?.filter.operands("dm")[0];
    if (dm_conversation) {
        const current_user_ids_string = people.emails_strings_to_user_ids_string(dm_conversation);
        assert(current_user_ids_string !== undefined);
        // If it matches and the messages for the current filter are fetched,
        // then there are certainly no messages in the conversation.
        if (
            people.pm_lookup_key(recipient_ids_string) ===
                people.pm_lookup_key(current_user_ids_string) &&
            message_lists.current?.data?.fetch_status.has_found_newest()
        ) {
            return {is_known_empty_conversation: true, is_local_echo_safe: true};
        }
    }
```

## imports now require extensions

*2024-11-13 to 2024-11-15 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/imports.20now.20require.20extensions/with/1980477)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-13 17:43 UTC

I’ve made some important changes in #32327, which will unfortunately result in a lot of merge conflicts:

- `.js` and `.ts` files are now parsed as native ES modules in Node.
- All first-party `import` statements must include extensions.
- The Node tests and a handful of other modules were renamed from `.js` to `.cjs`.

This will help unblock various further changes, such as the `giphy.js` TypeScript migration (#32339), and modernizing our toolchain with [Rspack](https://rspack.dev/) and [swc](https://swc.rs/) for massive build performance improvements.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-15 19:11 UTC

I can't emphasize how excited I am about replacing `webpack`; it's one of the few things we can do that would make both development and production substantially nicer.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-11-14 19:19 UTC

I don't think much is gained from truncating `button` to `btn`. What I would like is to be able to visualize or at least evaluate the appropriateness of a button just by looking at the template where the class appears. **Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-14 19:58 UTC

Yeah, agreed, and we of course will always have different types of buttons across the app. E.g. we have classes like `modal_select` for dropdowns inside modals, and I've been pretty happy with that even though it's almost identical to `settings_select`. **Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-14 20:01 UTC

I proposed the change to get rid of `btn`, for two reasons:
- `btn` is a bootstrap class name, and most everything associated with it was from Bootstrap or someone trying to be consistent with it.
- It's better to have fewer choices for people to make when naming things. Our codebase was already 93% `button` vs `btn`, going to 100% makes it easier to name new things since it's not an extra decision to make.

## Make "Copy link" result pastable

*2024-11-15 to 2024-11-16 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Make.20.22Copy.20link.22.20result.20pastable/with/1981728)*

**Pulkit** · 2024-11-15 05:06 UTC

Hi everyone, Pulkit here! I'm currently working on making the "Copy link" function in Zulip allow links to be directly formatted and pasted, following up on issue [#31813](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/31813).

I've written the following code to make URLs pastable and automatically formatted as markdown links:

```javascript
if (isUrl(trimmed_paste_text)) {
    if (is_safe_url_paste_target($textarea)) {
        event.preventDefault();
        event.stopPropagation();
        const url = trimmed_paste_text;
        const formatted_url = formatUrlAsMarkdown(url);
        compose_ui.insert_and_scroll_into_view(formatted_url, $textarea);
        return;
    }

    if (!compose_ui.cursor_inside_code_block($textarea) &&
        !cursor_at_markdown_link_marker($textarea) &&
        !compose_ui.shift_pressed
    ) {
        const syntax_text = try_stream_topic_syntax_text(trimmed_paste_text);
        if (syntax_text) {
            event.preventDefault();
            event.stopPropagation();
            add_text_and_select(trimmed_paste_text, $textarea);
            compose_ui.insert_and_scroll_into_view(syntax_text + " ", $textarea);
            return;
        }

        event.preventDefault();
        event.stopPropagation();
        const formatted_url = formatUrlAsMarkdown(trimmed_paste_text);
        add_text_and_select(trimmed_paste_text, $textarea);
        compose_ui.insert_and_scroll_into_view(formatted_url, $textarea);
        return;
    }
}
```

My question is about the `is_safe_url_paste_target` function ([reference link](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/e0bd3713cc9c3e1c85d438eeb40f632f4b9a21ad/web/src/copy_and_paste.ts#L606)). I’ve noticed that removing the `is_safe_url_paste_target` check in the paste handler makes the code work as expected. However, when the check is included, it consistently returns `false` for any URL, which prevents formatting.

Could anyone help clarify how `is_safe_url_paste_target` functions and why it might return `false` in this context?

Thanks in advance!

hi man

**Pulkit** · 2024-11-16 03:28 UTC

I think likely what you want to do is have the `is_safe_url_paste_target` block check whether the `text/html` matches what we expect Zulip's copy handler to generate. Adding a specially named CSS class to the `text/html` format might help in writing such a check robustly.

## Convert Handlebars templates to JavaScript

*2024-11-21 to 2024-11-22 · 23 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Convert.20Handlebars.20templates.20to.20JavaScript/with/1986033)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-21 23:51 UTC

Handlebars is archaic, confusing, untyped, and poorly integrated with modern tooling like formatters, editor autocompletion, and internationalization. So I wanted to figure out what it would take to automatically migrate our Handlebars templates to something else. Prototype: #32426.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-21 23:56 UTC

Interesting! The ~3 extra tabs of indentation is a bit painful, but I assume that can be tweaked.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:02 UTC

Yeah. One layer comes from the extra `to_html(…)` wrappers on the outside which cancel the `{__html: …}` wrappers on the inside. We’ll want to get rid of both of them so that templates return `Html` objects rather than `string`, which will make everything safer, but I wanted to avoid making an incompatible API change for this prototype.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:03 UTC

Another factor is our early decision to override Prettier’s default 2-space indents with 4-space indents, for compatibility with our historical code. I think we want to revisit that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:04 UTC

There's perhaps some hack we can do to try to avoid extra indentation churn even if we don't bundle that incompatible API change into the PR, but we can think about that after making more high-level decisions.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:05 UTC

Currently I'm just skimming a sampling of files to think about what things feel potentially notably worse so we can discuss those.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:05 UTC

If we eventually target JSX rather than tagged template literals, that will remove another indentation layer.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:06 UTC

Do you think it'd be viable to directly convert to JSX without the intermediate stage?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:08 UTC

An obstacle there is that JSX and Handlebars treat booleans incompatibly. In Handlebars, `{{some_bool}}` outputs `true` or `false`; in JSX, it outputs the empty string (to enable constructions like `{some_bool && <span>Show this only if some_bool is set</span>}`).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:08 UTC

So we’ll likely want an intermediate stage where booleans throw errors in order to help us find them all.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:10 UTC

We could alternatively wrap every interpolation in a compatibility function, but that’s a lot of interpolations.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:10 UTC

I think the excessive indentation is probably less material than just all the lines that consist of `}}` / `)}`, optionally with a backtick at the end, in terms of how it feels to read the templates.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:12 UTC

I guess `message_reaction.ts` is a good example of where things feel worse. 

Before:
``` handlebars
<div class="message_reaction_container {{#if is_archived}}disabled{{/if}}">
    <div class="{{this.class}} {{#if is_archived}}disabled{{/if}}" aria-label="{{this.label}}" data-reaction-id="{{this.local_id}}">
        {{#if this.emoji_alt_code}}
            <div class="emoji_alt_code">&nbsp;:{{this.emoji_name}}:</div>
        {{else if this.is_realm_emoji}}
            <img src="{{this.url}}" class="emoji" />
        {{else}}
            <div class="emoji emoji-{{this.emoji_code}}"></div>
        {{/if}}
        <div class="message_reaction_count">{{this.vote_text}}</div>
    </div>
</div>
```

After:
``` js
import {html, to_html} from "../shared/src/html.ts";
import {to_bool} from "../src/hbs_compat.ts";

export default function render_message_reaction(context) {
    return to_html(
        html`<div
            class="message_reaction_container ${to_bool(context.is_archived) ? "disabled" : ""}"
        >
            <div
                class="${context.class} ${to_bool(context.is_archived) ? "disabled" : ""}"
                aria-label="${context.label}"
                data-reaction-id="${context.local_id}"
            >
                ${to_bool(context.emoji_alt_code)
                    ? html` <div class="emoji_alt_code">&nbsp;:${context.emoji_name}:</div> `
                    : to_bool(context.is_realm_emoji)
                      ? html` <img src="${context.url}" class="emoji" /> `
                      : html` <div class="emoji emoji-${context.emoji_code}"></div> `}
                <div class="message_reaction_count">${context.vote_text}</div>
            </div>
        </div> `,
    );
}
```
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 00:13 UTC

Gotta go AFK to pick up kids from school, but the main thing that feels worse readability-wise in there is just that the original construction felt a lot more obvious that there's 3 possible things just before `message_reaction_count` and what their conditions are.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:17 UTC

The `to_bool` wrapper deals with another boolean incompatibility between Handlebars and JavaScript: in Handlebars, `0` and `""` are true while `[]` is false. We’ll delete it in the vast majority of cases where we know we’re dealing with actual booleans.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:24 UTC

Ideally someone should not need to look at the template code just to see that there are 3 cases, because it will have a type signature that reflects that. I’m willing to tolerate a lot of suboptimal syntax just to have the ability to make this all type-safe, and that’s a significant force on the available options.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:28 UTC

But a human still has the ability to do things like extract variables and convert ternary expressions to `if` statements to improve readability. (In the future, Solid will give us different constraints but also different [options](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/conditional-rendering) there.)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:47 UTC

I removed one indentation level by extracting the `to_html` argument to a variable, since that’s easy.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 00:58 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> So we’ll likely want an intermediate stage where booleans throw errors in order to help us find them all.

I guess that could take the form of temporarily patching Handlebars, if we want to target a more direct jump to JSX.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 03:01 UTC

Yeah I would be quite happy with a temporary Handlebars patch for that. Seems valuable regardless.

BTW I think several of the prep commits for this PR we could just merge; they seem like generally positive cleanups.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 19:47 UTC

I'll let Anders do a separate PR for prep commits that we can integrate early.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-22 19:49 UTC

The other thing we'll of course need to manage is merge conflicts. I'm not aware of major open PRs with big handlebars 
changes right now, so it might not be a big deal. We have been doing a lot more JS/CSS refactoring than HTML refactoring.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-22 19:54 UTC

Yeah conflicts gonna conflict, but we’ll be able to automate resolution with another `git filter-branch` based tool as long as we keep manual changes to a minimum.

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-12-09 17:42 UTC

[`enable_or_disable_save_button`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/4b82c3258fbaa27ea79ad9f3b5b13171bda4dd0f/web/src/settings_components.ts#L1414) is a function used to enable or disable the save changes in the save changes/discard widget. This function acts as a central place to decide whether or not the button should be disabled for all places where the component is used. The function is called after certain status changes in [`change_save_button_state`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/4b82c3258fbaa27ea79ad9f3b5b13171bda4dd0f/web/src/settings_components.ts#L530).

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-12-09 17:42 UTC

I'm not really sure if we want to continue having this design pattern. It feels odd to me that a function of a generic component also has business logic of the different components calling it. I'm thinking of letting `enable_or_disable_save_button` just handle the enabling/disabling part + any tooltip we want to add. Components can then call that function explicitly when they want to enable of disable that button.

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-12-09 17:43 UTC

*2024-12-21 to 2025-01-23 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/popover.20radio.20button.20info.20density/with/2011693)*

**Evy** · 2024-12-21 05:19 UTC

Following up on the radio button part of [this PR comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32689#issuecomment-2542482702),  switching from px to em for the top margin of the radio button does most of the fixing:

```diff
--- a/web/styles/compose.css
+++ b/web/styles/compose.css
         & .enter_sends_choice_radio {
             width: auto;
             cursor: pointer;
-            margin: 4px 0 0;
+            /* 4px at 14px/1em */
+            margin: 0.2857em 0 0;
             accent-color: hsl(217deg 100% 60%);
```

[After moving to em it looks mostly fine](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/a2/q632ujhhsnYA_vRxIvhB2BFv/image.png), but you can see it's still a little bit too high. I think this is because the radio button itself is always [14x14](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/bf/gUQ5c3qneAVlbZW7CvAVUDgw/image.png), i.e. it doesn't grow with the font size

Thoughts on best ways to handle this?

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-01-03 16:58 UTC

I'd start by rewriting the outer container (`.enter_sends_choice`) using CSS grid, so as to be able to control the height and alignment on the first row (where the button and label sit).

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-01-03 17:00 UTC

As to the ratio of the selected button element dot and its outline, I'd probably err on the side of letting the browser do its thing. Yes, [you can fiddle with radio buttons](https://bryntum.com/blog/3-ways-to-style-radio-buttons-with-modern-css/), but I think it's reasonable to assume that users preferring larger text sizes are probably used to or welcoming of larger, unambiguous controls.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-01-06 16:09 UTC

Yes. That would be the more accessible, expected behavior, I'd think. The critical part is of course making sure the radio-label layout can accommodate those changes in size

## dropdown heights

*2024-12-24 to 2025-01-03 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/dropdown.20heights/with/2014022)*

**Evy** · 2024-12-24 04:31 UTC

Following up on [this code review comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32691#issuecomment-2542498706).

Dropdowns in the app are often different components with somewhat different heights. When making info density changes on one of these dropdowns, this effect became more extreme:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/af/-f3A8hmLTJN98pCPHye3AKT6/image.png)

My question here is when I go to try to make dropdowns more the same height, do we want me to bias towards making them taller? Or keeping them shorter? Or have them meet somewhere in the middle?

**Steve Howell** · 2024-12-25 21:28 UTC

I would push back on changing heights at all. Different components have different heights for a reason.  If I could only choose between equally tall and equally short, I would vote tall.

**Steve Howell** · 2024-12-25 21:31 UTC

(The image shown above seems completely vanilla to me in a good way. Nothing seems out of proportion or over-designed.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 19:40 UTC

I'll let @Karl Stolley comment on strategy here; I'm not sure what's best.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-01-03 16:46 UTC

I'd think some careful use of modern layout techniques (flexbox or grid), coupled with CSS variables for padding, line height, etc. Modals have a line height of `1.5` set, and that gets inherited of course on elements that aren't assigned a more precise line height. I haven't investigated thoroughly, but I'd bet that inheritance chains on properties like that are often to blame for the ramshackle sets of heights on different elements.

**Alya Abbott** · 2025-01-03 20:01 UTC

In case it's relevant, we expect to do a design pass on modals in the next release (@Vlad Korobov has WIP designs).

**Steve Howell** · 2024-12-28 12:49 UTC

I am not sure anything is actionable here, but I figured I'd share some results that I found while analyzing the HTML of about a half million real-world Zulip messages.

Generally, the HTML that we produce is pretty clean and easy to characterize as a subset of all potential HTML payloads that you could construct, but the one exception is that our `<span>` tags have a zillion different possible values for the `class` attribute.  Here is the incomplete list of possible span classes (for example, I exclude emojis, since every different type of emoji generates a unique span class):

**Steve Howell** · 2024-12-28 12:58 UTC

I think much of the span class spam is unavoidable due to our use of pygments and katex, but obviously some things are also directly from Zulip.  None of this is necessarily harmful, but it does clutter the namespace for CSS, and we need to be careful about creating classes outside of the message context that might collide with some of these classes.

One encouraging thing is that all the classes use the `class-name-with-hyphen` convention as opposed to underscore (when bothering with a descriptive name).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 19:36 UTC

I think that's basically all KaTeX, and outside our control? You can try adjusting your tool to skip anything inside a `katex` element.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-02 19:37 UTC

BTW #**frontend>CSS selector performance** and #**frontend>narrowing performance** are some recent conversations involved in removing a bunch of unnecessary complexity from the message rows HTML, with significant performance wins as a result.

Ooo, so a solution in this particular case is to move the font-size to the element that actually uses it:

```diff
--- a/web/styles/message_header.css
+++ b/web/styles/message_header.css
.message_header {
     vertical-align: middle;
     text-align: left;
     /* We can overflow-y if the font size gets big */
     overflow: hidden;
     text-overflow: ellipsis;
     white-space: nowrap;
     font-weight: 600;
-    font-size: calc(15em / 14);
     line-height: 120%;
     position: relative;
     z-index: 0;
     background-color: var(--color-background);
 
     .message-header-contents {
+        font-size: calc(15em / 14);
         display: flex;
         align-items: center;
         justify-content: space-between;
```

test('spy function', () => {

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-11 00:25 UTC

Here is the rough Zulip equivalent:

~~~ js
run_test("spy function", ({override}) => {
    const side_effect = new SideEffect("call market.buy");
    
    override(market, "buy", (fruit, count) => {
        assert.equal(fruit, "apples");
        assert.equal(count, 10);
        side_effect.has_happened();
    }); 
    
    do_your_laundry();

    side_effect.should_happen_during(() => {
        go_shopping();
    }); 

    mow_the_lawn();
}); 
~~~

There are some subtle differences that matter in our current codebase.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-11 00:40 UTC

For more context:

~~~ js
function go_shopping() {

    drive_to_market();

~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-11 01:11 UTC

And to summarize the API, it's this:

~~~ js
run_test("test SideEffect", () => {
    const side_effect = new SideEffect("do something");
    assert.equal(side_effect.label, "do something");
    side_effect.should_happen_during(() => {
        side_effect.has_happened();
        side_effect.has_happened();
        side_effect.has_happened();
        side_effect.has_happened();
    });
    assert.equal(side_effect.num_times_met, 4);
    side_effect.reset();
    side_effect.should_not_happen_during(() => {
        // do nothing
    });
});
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-11 01:28 UTC

The `SideEffect` mechanism is completely decoupled from `override` and `override_rewire` and `set_global`, which means you can also use it for function injection into well-written real Zulip modules that allow you to pass in callback functions.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-01-11 02:57 UTC
