## reload.ts drafts handling

*2025-10-03 to 2025-10-07 · 21 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/reload.2Ets.20drafts.20handling/with/2270250)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 00:59 UTC

So, in `reload.ts`, we have some very robust but ancient code for doing the fancy thing that Zulip does to have your state be the same after a server-initiated reload as it was before. @Evy and I had to read it all as part of #36085, moving that module to TypeScript. I'd like to propose a simplification to that logic:

- Keep the `reload_token` API for passing metadata to the post-reload app.
- But try to remove all the other compose-related fields except for a `draft_id`.

Currently we have the following fields:
``` ts
const reload_vars_schema = z.intersection(
    z.object({
        oldhash: z.string(),
        narrow_pointer: z.optional(z.string()),
        narrow_offset: z.optional(z.string()),
        send_after_reload: z.enum(["0", "1"]),
    }),
    z.union([
        z.object({
            msg: z.optional(z.undefined()),
        }),
        z.object({
            msg: z.string(),
            recipient: z.string(),
            message_type: z.enum(["private", "stream"]),
            stream_id: z.optional(z.string()),
            topic: z.optional(z.string()),
            draft_id: z.optional(z.string()),
        }),
    ]),
);
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 01:03 UTC

Basically, in the event we have a draft saved in local storage, I think that entire second half of the data should be entailed in the `draft_id`. So I think we should be able to:
- Only look at the `draft_id`, if present.
- Stop producing the other fields.

We don't need to consider the possibility that local storage is not enabled and thus the drafts system is not available, since the reload tokens aren't used in that case anyway.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 01:11 UTC

I think while we're at it, I'd propose we also move to a new format where we just store an object as the value for those reload tokens, not a `url` to be parsed. It should be easy to preserve parsing logic for both the old format and a new format. That object should be able to just have the following fields, then:
- `hash`: What's called `oldhash` above.
- `compose_active_draft_id`: The draft ID for the current view.
- `message_view_pointer`: Former `narrow_pointer`.
- `message_view_scroll_offset`: Former `narrow_offest`.

I suspect we should not need a `send_after_reload` field at all; logically, that information should be stored on the draft object, and logic in `drafts.initialize` should be responsible for sending or not as appropriate. But maybe it's better to have a field for it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 01:13 UTC

@Evy thoughts on this plan? I think it may be worth doing in the same PR, because changing that logic at all is a sensitive deployment.

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:17 UTC

Do we need to be careful about backwards compatibility? The reload that changes this would still need to parse the previous shape, right?

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:18 UTC

Oh I missed you saying "It should be easy to preserve parsing logic for both the old format and a new format." :thumbs_up:

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:19 UTC

`send_after_reload` makes more sense to me in reload data than draft data, since it's only relevant during a reload and not relevant to most drafts. But I could see it either way and don't feel that strongly about it.

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:22 UTC

I think it's possible that there is no draft id if the message is too short. We should send `force_save: true` to `drafts.update_draft()` to ensure we always get a draft (and assert the `draft_id` is defined).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:23 UTC

Yeah, the `force_save` option should be all we need there.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:24 UTC

For `send_after_reload`, I think it kinda need some rethinking -- I kinda feel like you care whether it's been 30 seconds or 3 weeks.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:26 UTC

You're probably right we do want to keep track of whether this window is the one that was attempting the change.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:26 UTC

I think we can probably keep it conceptually but turn it into a boolean to avoid entangling this technical change with a product change.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:27 UTC

Maybe `send_draft_immediately: bool`?

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:28 UTC

It is a boolean encoded as a string number for some reason (currently `let url = "#reload:send_after_reload=" + Number(send_after_reload);`)

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-03 22:29 UTC

Yeah because of compatibility with ancient history. We'll still parse the old version for upgrading old clients, but we should just make the new version we generate going forward not have that madness, so that in 2 years we can delete the madness :).

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:29 UTC

Making it a regular boolean now seems good then :)

**Evy** · 2025-10-03 22:31 UTC

So the new shape would be:

```js 
 z.object({
    hash: z.string(),
    message_view_pointer: z.optional(z.number()),
    message_view_scroll_offset: z.optional(z.number
    // I can make a union where these are both set or both not, if that feels worth it
    compose_active_draft_id: z.optional(z.string()),
    send_draft_immediately: z.optional(z.boolean()),
}),
```

## How to write tests for async functions

*2025-10-04 to 2025-10-07 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/How.20to.20write.20tests.20for.20async.20functions/with/2271151)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-10-04 13:33 UTC

I have been scratching my head over writing tests for #35852 which involves multiple async function calls. 

The tests I wrote are not reliable as we are sometimes clearing global variables or the entire testing script terminates before `await async_function` finishes.

I tried searching online but folks just quote examples from other testing libraries or recommend libraries like Jest or Mocha.

[Link to commit with the test I am having problem with](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/35852/commits/97c3ac75c151f216e32bd88f095aa3f9b2681371).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-10-05 00:07 UTC

You need to fix the `test_people` wrapper to pass along the `Promise` returned by an async function.

```diff
 function test_people(label, f) {
     run_test(label, (helpers) => {
         initialize();
-        f(helpers);
+        return f(helpers);
     });
 }
```

(Or just get rid of this wrapper and have the individual tests call `initialize()`. Wrappers like this only add confusion.)

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-10-05 02:09 UTC

Thanks!! That worked.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-07 00:00 UTC

Yeah I recommend removing the wrapper :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-07 00:00 UTC

I think every test helper of this form that runs "automatically" to do this kind of data setup ends up being super confusing for someone, and you're just "saving" a single function call in each test.

## determining first day of the week

*2025-10-24 to 2026-01-11 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/determining.20first.20day.20of.20the.20week/with/2284504)*

**Aadithya** · 2025-10-24 17:51 UTC

I was working on [#36092](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/36092).
If the user sets the week start day setting to **“automatic”**, my current approach is:

1. Use `Intl.Locale(navigator.language).getWeekInfo().firstDay` (supported in Chrome ≥141, Safari ≥17, Edge ≥141).
  
2. Fallback to **weekstart** with `navigator.language` for browsers without `getWeekInfo()` (e.g., Firefox).
  
3. Default to Sunday if both fail.
  

Would it be fine to use **weekstart** dependency here?

Angular had a similar function `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek` but it is deprecated and they recommend this:

> Angular recommends relying on the `Intl` API for i18n. Intl's [`getWeekInfo`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/Locale/getWeekInfo) has partial support (Chromium M99 & Safari 17). You may want to rely on the following alternatives:
> 
> * Libraries like [`Luxon`](https://moment.github.io/luxon/#/) rely on `Intl` but fallback on the ISO 8601 definition (Monday) if `getWeekInfo` is not supported.
>   
> * Other libraries like [`date-fns`](https://date-fns.org/), [`day.js`](https://day.js.org/en/), or [`weekstart`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/weekstart) provide their own locale-based data for the first day of the week.
>   

[source](https://www.jsdocs.io/package/@angular/common#getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek)

Since zulip already uses **date-fns**, I considered it for detecting the first day of the week, but it requires mapping `navigator.language` to a date-fns locale (like `enUS`, `fr`, `de`). **weekstart** provides a simple solution that works directly with `navigator.language`.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-24 18:27 UTC

Others should chime in, but because this is really a nice-to-have feature, and because there are native if not widely available browser supported methods for handling this, I would just default to Sunday when browser-native APIs aren’t supported, rather than introducing a dependency to polyfill for older browsers. (I didn’t look super close, but `weekstart` looks not to have been published to NPM in something like three years.)

But I’d be curious to hear others, especially @Anders Kaseorg, share their thoughts about this.

## data structure for topic links

*2025-10-24 to 2025-11-20 · 39 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/data.20structure.20for.20topic.20links/with/2284560)*

**Evy** · 2025-10-24 18:30 UTC

I've been brainstorming a bunch how to set up a data structure for topic links, and would love some input. Here is the context and constraints:

The **main data** we're storing is links in messages in channel conversations that link to: other channels, topics in channels, or messages (in topics in channels)

```js
export type TopicLink = {
    // Where the link occurs
    from_message_id: number;
    from_stream_id: number;
    from_topic: string;
    from_link: string;
    // What's being linked to
    to_stream_id: number;
    to_topic: string | undefined;
    to_message_id: number | undefined;
    to_link: string;
};
```

We need to store these links in some way such that we can quickly (i.e. in O(1) time) **get**:

* all outgoing links for a channel/topic pair
* all incoming links to a channel/topic pair
* all links associated with a message that's having its content edited, being moved to another topic, or being deleted (so that they can be updated)

---

I considered two maps, one for outgoing links and one for incoming links, mapped by channel -> topic -> message_id, and storing each topic link in both maps.

Some further details
* If a link doesn't have a `to_topic`,  it would only be in the outgoing link map, since only we're displaying this data in topic narrows (links to a topic and links from a topic).
* If a link doesn't have a `to_message_id`, it's stored in `topic_links_by_to.get(to_stream_id).get(to_topic).get(NO_MESSAGE_ID)` where `NO_MESSAGE_ID` is just a constant (probably 0).

But I'm unsure about this data structure for a few reasons:

* It's ugly to write `topic_links_by_to.get(stream_id)?.get(topic)?.get(message_id)`, though maybe that's fine
* Most topic links are stored in two maps, and I don't super like duplicating the data, but again maybe that's fine?
* I can get outgoing topic links in `O(1)` time because all links have a `from_topic` and `from_message_id`, but I can't do that for the incoming link map. For example, if a message linking to `#Verona>kings` (no message id) is moved to another topic, I have to iterate over all links in the narrow `topic_links_by_to.get(verona.stream_id).get("kings")` to find the relevant objects and update the new topic and new message id that's linking to `#Verona>kings`. In this situation I *know* the `from` data that can get me the object in `O(1)` time in `topic_links_by_from`, but `topic_links_by_to` has keys with the `to` data and not the `from` data, so I can't efficiently find it. Which leads me to believe I should be using a different data structure? Or maybe it's fine to iterate over all links in a topic in this situation?

I'd love some thoughts on this and if there's something else I could do that would feel cleaner. Thanks!

**Greg Price** · 2025-10-27 04:14 UTC

To your last question, I think there are several directions in which it can be simplified.

As an example, taking this from `remove_message_topic_links`:
```ts
            if (topic_links_by_from.has_message({message_id})) {
                const links_for_message = topic_links_by_from.get_links_for_message({message_id});
                const filtered_links = filter_set(
                    links_for_message,
                    (topic_link) => topic_link.message_id !== deleted_message_id,
                );

                const message = get(message_id);

```

* That's looking up the relevant map (for the narrow, within "by from") three times: the `has_message`, the `get_links_for_message`, and the `get_link_map_for_narrow`.

  It could instead look it up just once, and operate on that. (Plus if the message isn't present there, then that's an error, right? Here `message_id` is something that the "by to" map told us should be there.)

* That's looking up the message object corresponding to `message_id` three times: within those first two calls, and then explicitly before the `get_link_map_for_narrow` call. That could similarly be once.

**Greg Price** · 2025-10-27 04:31 UTC

```ts
    has_message(opts: {stream_id?: number; topic?: string; message_id: number}): boolean {
        const {stream_id, topic, message_id} = opts;
        if (topic !== undefined && stream_id !== undefined) {
            return this.map.get(stream_id)?.get(topic)?.get(message_id) !== undefined;
        }
        assert(message_id !== NO_MESSAGE_ID);
        const message = get(message_id);
        if (message?.type !== "stream") {
            return false;
        }
        return this.map.get(message.stream_id)?.get(message.topic)?.get(message_id) !== undefined;
    }
```

This feels like it wants to be two different methods with different signatures: either a stream/channel ID and topic, or a message ID.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-10-28 07:21 UTC

```js
    // Create the tooltip inside the parent element. This has the
    // undesirable side effect of CSS properties of the parent elements
    // applying to tooltips, which causes ugly clipping if the parent
    // element has overflow rules. Even with that, we prefer to have
    // tooltips appended to the parent so that the tooltip gets removed
    // if the parent is hidden / removed from DOM; which is not the case
    // with appending it to `body` which has side effect of tooltips
    // sticking around due to browser not communicating to tippy that
    // the element has been removed without having a Mutation Observer.
    appendTo: "parent",
```

The clipping is due to above. You can use `body` to fix it but make sure to remove the element from DOM once it is hidden.

```diff

diff --git a/web/styles/popovers.css b/web/styles/popovers.css
index 245a7cac2d..5084fcfa9e 100644
--- a/web/styles/popovers.css
+++ b/web/styles/popovers.css
@@ -1598,9 +1598,13 @@ ul.popover-menu-list {
 
 #topic-links-menu-popover {
     color: var(--color-text-popover-menu) !important;
-    padding: 0.6666em;
+
+    .popover-topic-links-list {
+        padding: 0.6666em;
+    }
 
     .topic-links-menu-title {
+        padding: 0.6666em;
         font-weight: 600;
         margin: 0;
     }
```

## Flatpickr customizations

*2025-10-31 to 2026-02-25 · 50 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Flatpickr.20customizations/with/2289219)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:39 UTC

We've had a few discussions lately regarding Flatpickr and the presentation of the calendar on the compose box's Add global time button:

* #**issues>calendar hover weirdness** 
* #**design>Calendar UI Enhancement**

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:39 UTC

I wanted to open a discussion here in #**frontend**, though, to talk about some possible routes to take with this dependency. (Tim and I had mentioned some of these ideas in DMs).

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:43 UTC

* One option would be to hunt down a more modern and better maintained library (Flatpickr hasn't had new commits [in some 3 years](https://github.com/flatpickr/flatpickr).
* Another option would be to move towards the browser-native date pickers presented with `<input type="datetime-local">`
* And yet another option, perhaps as a stopgap measure while investigating the first two options, would be to figure out a way to add customizations on top of Flatpickr's own CSS.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:45 UTC

Currently, we're loading up two different CSS files from Flatpickr:

* We load up the light theme (`flatpickr/dist/flatpickr.css`) in `web/src/bundles/app.ts`
* We load up the dark theme (`flatpickr/dist/themes/dark.css`) as an `@import` statement in our dark theme CSS file, `web/styles/dark_theme.css`

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:47 UTC

On top of that, we have a handful of customizations in `zulip.css` (about 20 lines, all told) and a few lines in `settings.css`.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:49 UTC

However, the customizations we have are being applied **only** in light theme, as Flatpickr's `dark.css` file is a full duplicate of `flatpickr.css`, with different colors referenced throughout. Because of how we load up `dark.css` in `dark_theme.css`, all of the `dark.css` styles get our `.dark-theme:root` selector attached, making them more specific than the light theme and the customizations we're trying to specify in `zulip.css` and `settings.css`.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:53 UTC

So, were we to want to simplify this situation and confidently apply our own customizations, one approach would be to:

1. Remove the `@import` line from `dark_theme.css`
2. Duplicate `flatpickr.css` into our own `web/styles/` directory, and stop loading up the upstream version from `web/src/bundles/app.ts`
3. Write CSS variables with `light-dark()` syntax for the ~17 light/dark colors currently used in Flatpickr (see the table below), and reference those from `web/styles/flatpickr.css`
4. Revisit the customizations we've already got in `zulip.css` and `settings.css`, removing those that don't make any sense, and preserving the rest at the bottom of the new `web/styles/flatpickr.css`

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:54 UTC

For reference, these are the ~17 colors in use by Flatpickr in both light and dark themes:

| Light color | Dark color |
|---|---|
| `#fff` (sometimes `transparent`)                 | `#3f4458`                       |
| `#e6e6e6`                                        | `#20222c` (sometimes `#646c8c`) |
| `rgba(0,0,0,0.9)` (sometimes `rgba(0,0,0,0.54)`) | `#fff`                          |
| `#eee`                                           | `#6a7395`                       |
| `#959ea9`                                        | `#eee`                          |
| `#569ff7`                                        | `#80cbc4`                       |
| `rgba(57,57,57,0.15)`                            | `rgba(255,255,255,0.15)`        |
| `#393939`                                        | `rgba(255,255,255,0.95)`        |
| `rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`                                | `rgba(192,187,167,0.1)`         |
| `rgba(0,0,0,0.2)`                                | `rgba(192,187,167,0.2)`         |
| `rgba(0,0,0,0.05)`                               | `rgba(192,187,167,0.05)`        |
| `rgba(57,57,57,0.6)`                             | `rgba(255,255,255,0.6)`         |
| `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`                                | `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)`         |
| `rgba(57,57,57,0.3)`                             | `rgba(255,255,255,0.3)`         |
| `rgba(57,57,57,0.1)`                             | `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)`         |

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:56 UTC

There are certainly colors we'd like to change, e.g., the odd use of red as the hover color on left/right arrows.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-31 18:58 UTC

And more to the point, if we do want to carry forward such fixes and customizations while researching another option, it would be nice to do so using CSS variables, rather than trying to up the selector specificity to successfully override what's happening in dark theme with the Flatpickr `dark.css`.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-07 15:12 UTC

I think the most promising date-picker I've found is [Air Datepicker](https://air-datepicker.com/) ([GitHub repo](https://github.com/t1m0n/air-datepicker/tree/v3)):

* It's written in pure JavaScript with zero additional dependencies
* It has [solid documentation](https://air-datepicker.com/docs) and a decent [API](https://air-datepicker.com/methods), and already ships with what we'd need to specify or auto-detect the first day of the week for a given locale (see #**frontend>determining first day of the week**)
* All CSS properties are specified as CSS variables, which should make it very easy to customize with Zulip UI colors
* There are only a couple element selectors (`span` plus `svg` and `path`); everything else is handled with classes
* The latest release (v. 3.6.0) came out about six months ago (May 2025)

I'd be interested in hearing opinions on this, especially from @Aman (amanagr) and @Anders Kaseorg

Looking at the native HTML5 datetime picker approach, I think there's a key problem we'll need to solve that is shown in this screenshot:
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/e1/EeTnUFd9g_2eTh_jOlXapC38/image.png) 

The workflow we have for our current date picker is that we have an item in the popover called "Custom", and once you click it, you open the date picker, and a "Confirm" button in that widget submits the change (e.g., sends your scheduled message).

The way the native HTML5 `datetime-local` picker element works is that it's expecting to be a visible form input element that shows the selected time, and there's no "Confirm/submit" button to submit the selected time; instead, you kinda have to just click outside the date picker popover (in our case, probably on our own UI sitting behind it). 

It's probably not hard to redo how scheduled message UI works to fit that, but the "Select a global time" UI I think would feel fairly awkward there.

**Satyam Bansal** · 2025-11-11 13:01 UTC

Thanks for creating the thread. 

Right now the [union type PopoverName](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/14161ad7f08d84d7ecbd431734fca337e5c43b10/web/src/popover_menus.ts#L16-L38) already has 21 possible hardcoded strings.

```ts
type PopoverName =
    | "compose_control_buttons"
    | "starred_messages"
    | "drafts"
    | "left_sidebar_inbox_popover"
    | "left_sidebar_all_messages_popover"
    | "left_sidebar_recent_view_popover"
    | "top_left_sidebar"
    | "message_actions"
    | "stream_card_popover"
    | "stream_settings"

    | "send_later"
    | "change_visibility_policy"
    | "personal_menu"
    | "gear_menu"
    | "help_menu"
    | "buddy_list"
    | "stream_actions_popover"
    | "color_picker_popover"
    | "show_folders_sidebar"
    | "send_later_options";
```

**Satyam Bansal** · 2025-11-11 13:01 UTC

Since, for adding popover to navigation views require adding popover names for the all the built in views. So, instead of typing out the names for each of them we can infer them from where they are defined already (i.e. from the [`built_in_views_meta_data` object](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/14161ad7f08d84d7ecbd431734fca337e5c43b10/web/src/navigation_views.ts#L23)).

Yes, grepping would certainly be affected in this case.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-11 19:00 UTC

**Satyam Bansal** · 2025-11-13 19:11 UTC

```js
        case "dm-including": {
            const people_in_dms = first_operand
                .split(",")
                .map((email) => people.get_by_email(email));
            if (people_in_dms.length === 1 && !people_in_dms[0]) {
                return {
                    title: $t({defaultMessage: "This user does not exist!"}),
                };
            }
            const valid_people_in_dms: people.User[] = [];
            for (const user of people_in_dms.values()) {
                if (user === undefined) {
                    return {
                        // We intentionally give the same non-specific
                        // error message as the single user case,
                        // since we don't display API email addresses
                        // or user IDs typically in UI errors, and we
                        // don't have any other handle as to which
                        // user this was supposed to be.
                        title: $t({defaultMessage: "This user does not exist!"}),
                    };
                }

## circle outline not centered #36490

*2025-11-13 to 2025-11-20 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/circle.20outline.20not.20centered.20.2336490/with/2299188)*

**Evy** · 2025-11-13 18:24 UTC

This user status circle's outline in #36490 isn't sized properly (thicker on the right) and I'm confused what's going on.

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c0/3NhfTLNeOcocizvthWxYq-bA/image.png)

I added an early `return` at the start of `hide()` in `bootstrap_typeahead` so I could inspect it. One thing I noticed is the background circle (and outline) is separate from the dot (it's in a `:before`), so the issue is actually that the container of the `:before` is a different size than the circle. But I couldn't figure out why. Can anyone offer insight?

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-13 18:31 UTC

I can pull down the PR and take a look.

One trick I use for inspecting typeaheads and other elements that disappear when they lose focus is to drop this into the console: `setTimeout(() => { debugger; }, 5000)`. That gives you 5 seconds to open the element in question, and then the debugger pauses so you can inspect it.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-13 19:53 UTC

Huh. This is tricky and weird. I think the issue stems from the `font-size: 0.4em` declaration which is meant to produce a `6.56px` equivalent at 16px/1em--which is the roughly 31.25% of the avatar size that we're using in the right sidebar. 

But that value seems to be causing rounding-based havoc with `line-height: 1`, resulting in a user circle in the typeahead that is 6.39999px tall and 6.5px wide--and therefore not a circle, but actually a bit of an oval. That's what's throwing off the border and the centering.

The best solution I've found is to just round up to whole pixels on the user-circle font size, 7px, and do the fairly tidy 16px/1em conversion: 7 ÷ 16 = 0.4375em, which then yields a user circle that is precisely 7px × 7px (9px × 9px with its 1px border).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-13 19:57 UTC

That seems OK. Could also do something with `line-height` for that element, perhaps?

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-13 20:10 UTC

Well, and that's the weird bit: `line-height: 1` should set the line height to the same value as `font-size`, but in this case, rounding errors were causing that not to happen. I'd guess there might be something unusual about the font metrics with the icon fonts, but that's just a hunch.

**Evy** · 2025-11-13 20:35 UTC

Wow interesting find! Thanks so much for investigating

**Evy** · 2025-11-13 21:24 UTC

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/a7/4D9UsZCY9SyK_9_vJlYoRiNG/image.png)

**Evy** · 2025-11-13 21:26 UTC

At 12px font size, the red is at the top and bottom
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ef/4uEDMp2NoAP6SbIOU6e_iiU6/image.png)

**Evy** · 2025-11-13 21:27 UTC

I could see this being good enough maybe? But a fully clean solution would be nice.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-13 22:03 UTC

Is it possible to replace the border with some padding, and set the background color on `.user-circle` instead? That’s probably the only way those little subpixel things won’t reveal themselves…I guess the only concern is what happens with the idle circle—though I’d think it would look okay over those neutral backgrounds.

## Auditing usage of `getSelection().type`

*2025-11-21 to 2025-12-30 · 18 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Auditing.20usage.20of.20.60getSelection.28.29.2Etype.60/with/2308048)*

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-11-21 15:42 UTC

For #36719, we want to replace `getSelection().type` with the `mouse_drag.is_drag` [utility](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/src/mouse_drag.ts).

I'd like to know if we should keep using `getSelection().type` if there is no unnecessary triggering of actions for a click + drag event where no text selection is involved.

For example:
A click + drag action on the message row not involving text will trigger a reply, so it makes sense to do something like:
```diff
-        if (document.getSelection()?.type === "Range") {
+        if (mouse_drag.is_drag(e)) {
             // Drags on the message (to copy message text) shouldn't trigger a reply.
+            // This also prevents triggering a reply when you click and drag through
+            // an area that doesn't contain text.
             return;
         }
```

But there are some places like the recipient row, where I haven't been able to trigger unexpected behavior on a click + drag action.
So, does it still make sense to replace `getSelection().type` for click handlers associated with such components for consistency?

OK, so this [puppeteer test](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/aca7495fa52c9f4e24ca503ffbbddce7a9f47c67/web/e2e-tests/mention.test.ts#L25) fails because of the introduction of the `is_drag` check in `bootstrap_typeahead.ts`.

I did some print debugging and surprisingly the [`drag_distance`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/aca7495fa52c9f4e24ca503ffbbddce7a9f47c67/web/src/mouse_drag.ts#L18) is deterministically computed as 1532 for the half a dozen runs I did.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-11-22 09:46 UTC

After quite a bit of searching, I think the problem was because we issued an [untrusted event](https://pptr.dev/faq#q-whats-the-difference-between-a-trusted-and-untrusted-input-event:~:text=sniffing%20for%20accompanying,a%20fake%20event) in the `select_item_via_typeahead` helper [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/aca7495fa52c9f4e24ca503ffbbddce7a9f47c67/web/e2e-tests/lib/common.ts#L603).
It doesn't trigger the `mousedown` and `mouseup` events like a user interaction, which is probably what led to that absurd drag distance, as the start_x, start_y values were probably from some stale trusted click event that fired before selecting the typeahead item.

## ✔ Notification key grouping.

*2025-11-24 to 2025-11-25 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Notification.20key.20grouping.2E/with/2309667)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2025-11-24 09:24 UTC

I'm not sure if we **need** to address #26729. 

```
function get_notification_key(message: Message | TestNotificationMessage): string {
    let key;

    if (message.type === "private" || message.type === "test-notification") {
        key = message.display_reply_to;
    } else {
        const stream_name = stream_data.get_stream_name_from_id(message.stream_id);
        key = message.sender_full_name + " to " + stream_name + " > " + message.topic;
    }

    return key;
}
```

Names are not allowed to have `>` as per `NAME_INVALID_CHARS = ["*", "`", "\\", ">", '"', "@"]`. Not sure how else we would have a collision between the stream keys and DM keys in that case. We can probably add a comment explaining this.

`>` getting removed from NAME_INVALID_CHARS in the future seems completely unlikely at this point.

From https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26363#discussion_r1324875910: 

> Yeah, which is not a realistic case; but the point is that with a data structure where objects are meant to be unique conversations, we should design the way we construct keys such that collisions are impossible.

The collisions are impossible in this case, not sure if there would be any real benefits to changing the key structure.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-24 18:22 UTC

But `>` is currently allowed in stream names and topics, right? As is " to ". So I think the following would all have the same key:

- Key: `Name to test test to > topic > topic`

Location 1:
- User `Name to test`
- Stream `test`
- Topic `topic > topic`

Location 2:
- User `Name`
- Stream `test to test`
- Topic `topic > topic`

Location 3:
- User `Name`
- Stream `test to test > topic`
- Topic `topic`

We should just use a sound encoding here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-24 18:23 UTC

I don't think this is hard, just do `channel:{sender_id}:{channel_id}:{topic_name}` for channels, and `dm:user_ids_string` for DMs.

**Shubham Padia** · 2025-11-25 14:37 UTC

Opened #36784. I'm not sure which browser standards we were talking about at this [comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/31963#discussion_r1800262419). If we were talking about some kind of limits on the notifications API side, the key itself is not being passed on in the notification, it is being used in `process_notification`. If we were talking about the maximum length of a key in the browser, that is ~1GB (https://stackoverflow.com/a/47781288). 

We could have a very long key when using `dm:list_of_user_ids` since that can be really long theoratically. If we are concerned about that, we can add recipient_id to `message_store.ts`, which will be an identifier with a finite and short length.

## channel vs stream in the web app codebase

*2025-12-03 to 2025-12-03 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/channel.20vs.20stream.20in.20the.20web.20app.20codebase/with/2316919)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-03 20:23 UTC

I feel like we should talk a bit about our strategy for the use of "channel" vs "stream" in the web app codebase. Right now, without a specific effort to migrate from "stream" to "channel", we're at roughly:
- In `web/templates`, 373 "channel" vs 546 "stream".
- In `web/src`, 1962 "channel" vs 6980 "stream".
- In `web/styles`, 111 "channel" vs 284 "stream".

Our original plan had been to not put much effort into migrating, since it'd be a lot of work to finish, without visible user-facing benefits. But one thing I've been noticing is folks adding new functions/files/etc. with "stream" in their name even in the middle of a module that is mostly using the "channel" terminology, and I've been finding that distracting when doing code reviews.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-03 20:27 UTC

So I've been thinking whether we should consider investing in certain easy classes of migrations that might lock down particular parts of the codebase towards using "channel". For example:
- It would be a trivial sweep to rename all the TypeScript classes with "Stream" in their name to use "Channel". Those account for 420 of the "stream" references in `web/src`.
- While some care would be required to not mess up partials and adjust import statements, I expect it would not be hard to rename everything under `web/templates/stream_settings` to live in `web/templates/channel_settings` and no longer have "channel" in filenames there, which would I think discourage making new ones. 
- We could do a purge of the 26 references to "stream" in translated strings, like `z-stream-name`, and then lint-ban the word "stream" in translated strings.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-12-03 20:28 UTC

Yeah. I've certainly been guilty of this kind of terminology slippage myself. It's hard to stare at a lot of lines of the codebase with `_stream_` and do the cognitive shift to use *channel* in commit messages and so on. And as this change recedes into the past, it'll be less clear to newer contributors that *stream* and *channel* are synonymous.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-03 20:31 UTC

I think I do want to avoid about attempting renaming efforts that will be difficult/tangly to verify, like trying to bulk-rename anything that's not type-checked or easy to cleanly sweep via `git grep`. But maybe it's reasonable to do some easy sweeps, maybe in about a week once we've integrated most of the remaining large PRs that would merge conflict with this transition.


## MessageListData.all_messages

*2025-12-08 to 2025-12-08 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/MessageListData.2Eall_messages/with/2320312)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-08 19:04 UTC

Apparently, `MessageListData.all_messages()` returned just `_items`, not `_all_items`, and so was incorrectly excluding topic-muted messages in some code paths (like when switching views to display that topic, where the source/cached message list excluded muted topics, but not the destination view).

In #36955, we're renaming it to `all_messages_after_mute_filtering` so it won't be misused. I posted several comments there on latent bugs revealed by renaming that; @Aman (amanagr) can you take point on fixing those? A few notes of more general interest:
- I think we'll add an `all_messages_before_mute_filtering` for the thing this sounded like; I want all callers to be explicitly answering the question of whether mute filtering should occur.
- I'm planning to leave `MessageList.all_messages = this.data.all_messages_after_mute_filtering()` unchanged, since that's currently always used correctly for logic around "What messages are displayed right now?".

## awaiting pending promises  #37148

*2025-12-18 to 2025-12-30 · 31 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/awaiting.20pending.20promises.20.20.2337148/with/2331055)*

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 18:11 UTC

In refactoring some stuff in `peer_data` I'm realizing I misunderstood something about how promises work. 

I thought I could create a new promise and until it was `await`ed it could be guaranteed to not be resolved yet. So I set up a `pending_subscriber_requests` object to store the promises when creating them, so that if we tried to fetch subscribers at the same time as an existing request, we could await the existing promise. Then when the promise resolved, it would delete itself from `pending_subscriber_requests`.

Now that I'm doing some refactoring, it seems like actually promises start running when they're created (which would have been easy for me to confirm earlier). In practice, making a `channel.get` request will probably always take long enough for the code to work out, but it's still not good code if the promise can be deleted from `pending_subscriber_requests` (as the promise finishes) before it gets added to `pending_subscriber_requests` (after it gets initially created).

I'm trying to figure out a better way to set this up so that if we try to fetch subscribers at the same time as an existing request, we could await the existing fetch.

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 18:21 UTC

`activity_ui` has a similar pattern, but nothing awaits on the contents of `all_pending_fetches_for_search` (except tests).

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 18:24 UTC

`people.fetch_users_storage` looks promising, at least for inspiration for direction.

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 19:32 UTC

Oh, and now I need to figure out how to write tests for this to have the promises not resolve immediately, so that I can test that they fall back to existing requests.

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 20:31 UTC

I think I figured it out, but I started having dev environment problems so updates to come once I rebuild everything.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-12-18 20:52 UTC

Any `await` expression is guaranteed to delay until at least the next microtask (even if the promise is already resolved). It is not possible for `subscribers_promise` to remove itself before it gets added.

**Evy** · 2025-12-18 20:58 UTC

Ah that's helpful to know. I think because I transitioned to using a promises wrapper (because #**frontend>errors for channel.get@2328646** ) this stopped working. I was wondering if the await made the difference

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-12-18 21:10 UTC

It is also guaranteed that `XMLHTTPRequest` can’t resolve synchronously unless the default `async=true` flag was explicitly changed to `false`. (But obviously a wrongly implemented mock can violate that guarantee.)

## callback patterns for third-party network fetches

*2025-12-24 to 2025-12-30 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/callback.20patterns.20for.20third-party.20network.20fetches/with/2334692)*

**Steve Howell** · 2025-12-24 18:17 UTC

What is the latest and greatest pattern for structuring code that sends a network request off to a third party provider like giphy or tenor?  Here is the piece of code I have now on a branch:

~~~ ts
function ask_tenor_for_gifs(url: string, data: TenorPayload, next_page = false): void {
    if (next_page) {
        is_loading_more = true;
        data = {...data, pos: next_pos_identifier};
    }

    void channel.get({
        url: url,
        data,
        success(raw_tenor_result) {
            const parsed_data = tenor_result_schema.parse(raw_tenor_result);
            const urls = parsed_data.results.map((result) => ({
                preview_url: result.media_formats.tinygif.url,
                insert_url: result.media_formats.mediumgif.url,
            }));
            next_pos_identifier = parsed_data.next;
            render_gifs_to_grid(urls, next_page);
            is_loading_more = false;
        },
    });
}
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2026-01-01 22:21 UTC

I think this is actually a symptom of Zulip itself being a little under-architected when it comes to these kind of background functions.  If you have background functions that are async but are never intended to be awaited for, then it might be prudent to wrap them in some kind of small `BackgroundTask` object.  Once you enforced that discipline, those types of situations would be easier for humans to spot, and you could even conceivably have the node test runner be able to automatically forbid the construction of `BackgroundTask` instances.  The `node` code could still test the wrapped function directly, of course; it just couldn't do deep stack testing.  We would do deep stack testing in another test runner, whether it's puppeteer or jest or whatever.  The node test runner was never intended for testing background tasks from way up in the stack.

class RealCode {

    async b() {

        }, 0);
    }
}

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-01-03 00:44 UTC

I pointed this out [before](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/istanbul.20coverage.20with.20void.20async.20calls.20.20.2334677/near/2179461), along with [another non-test-related reason](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/istanbul.20coverage.20with.20void.20async.20calls.20.20.2334677/near/2179475) to avoid patterns like this.

Note that `class RealCode` has *two* of these bugs, only one of which is that `this.b()` dangles a promise; the other is that `setTimeout(…)` dangles a timer, i.e., even `await this.b()` would return before `console.log("b")` executes. So focusing only on dangled promises won’t lead to the right solution.

(The right way to `await` a timer is to convert into a promise first: `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))`.)

While it’s not possible to block on dangled promises and timers after they’ve already been dangled, the modern [Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html) is able to correctly attribute errors thrown within them. But this only addresses part of the debuggability problem and not the several other reasons to avoid these patterns.

````spoiler Demo
```js
import test from "node:test";

class RealCode {
    a() {
        console.log("a");
        this.b();
    }

    async b() {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log("b");
            throw new Error("b");
        }, 0);
    }
}

test("first", () => {
    const real_code = new RealCode();
    real_code.a();
});

test("second", () => {
    console.log("c");
});
```

```
a
c
✔ first (1.661646ms)
✔ second (0.132559ms)
b
ℹ Error: Test "first" at my.test.mjs:17:1 generated asynchronous activity after the test ended. This activity created the error "Error: b" and would have caused the test to fail, but instead triggered an uncaughtException event.
```
````

I think 90% of the anonymous functions in the Zulip codebase should be extracted to named functions.  Just to give them a name, if nothing else.  I'm not claiming that every anonymous function in Zulip is the end of the world.  But they're generally a pain and unnecessary.

I didn't choose "10 lines" as some completely arbitrary metric.  I think that's about the right number.  I would choose a smaller number, but I have never seen an 11-line anonymous function that wouldn't lead to more readability by just lifting it into a properly named function.

**Steve Howell** · 2026-01-03 22:12 UTC

So let's be allies, not enemies.  In my own words, templates are painful:

* The overall syntax is painful.
* They don't even guarantee that you properly escape HTML.
* They are just as prone to double-escaping bugs as the DOM API.
* They are not native to the browsers (obviously), whereas DOM APIs are natural.
* They require extra `webpack` support.
* They require importing the third party handlebars library and managing its dependencies.
* They require special home-grown tooling to lint them (ironically, mostly written by me!) and to pretty-print them (also ironically mostly written by me!).
* They don't provide any kind of type signature that TypeScript transpilers can enforce.
* They are hard to refactor.
* The "partial" system makes it very difficult to read templates that call out to each other.
* The commenting syntax is awkward.
* They are prone to including dead code.
* You can't step-debug them.
* They impose indirection on the reader.  Instead of just building a widget inside the surrounding JS code (which provides useful context), you have to find the template in the file system.
* They require extra machinery for translation and custom methods.
* Their programming-language constructs such as `if` and `unless` and `each` are primitive and oddly different from either TypeScript or any other "language" that Zulip programmers learn.
* They don't have higher-level concepts like classes or closures, because it's not a real programming language.

export class Block {
    elements: Element[] = [];

    constructor(elements: (Element | Block)[]) {
        for (const member of elements) {
            if (member instanceof Block) {
                this.elements.push(...member.elements);
            } else {
                this.elements.push(member);
            }
        }
    }

        const dom = document.createDocumentFragment();
        for (const element of this.elements) {
            if (element instanceof Comment) {

            dom.append(element.to_dom());
        }
        return dom;

}

Apoorva/Steve version:

~~~ ts
// This builds the UI that looks like "<triangle icon> OTHERS" in the buddy list.
// Users can collapse or un-collapse the users by clicking on the header.
// The **entire** section header is a click target.  Most of the smaller components
// only get drawn and styled.
export function buddy_list_section_header(info: {
    id: string;
    header_text: string;
    is_collapsed: boolean;
}): h.Block {
    // This only draws the icon.
    // All the click handlers act on the div tag
    // that gets wrapped around it.
    function section_rotation_icon(): h.Tag {
        // The rotation_class sets an eventual class for the icon as either
        // "rotate-icon-right" or "rotate-icon-down".
        // They lead to rotate: 0deg and rotate: 90deg in the Zulip CSS.
        function rotation_class(): h.TrustedIfElseString {
            return h.trusted_if_else_string({
                bool: h.bool_var({label: "is_collapsed", b: info.is_collapsed}),
                yes_val: h.trusted_simple_string("rotate-icon-right"),
                no_val: h.trusted_simple_string("rotate-icon-down"),
            });
        }

        return h.i_tag({
            classes: [
                h.trusted_simple_string("buddy-list-section-toggle"),
                h.trusted_simple_string("zulip-icon"),
                h.trusted_simple_string("zulip-icon-heading-triangle-right"),
                rotation_class(),
            ],
            attrs: [h.attr("aria-hidden", h.trusted_simple_string("true"))],
        });
    }

    // The heading_text_span creates a span with the text of either
    // "THIS CONVERSATION" or "OTHERS" as determined by the color.
    // It has no handlers attached directly to it.
    // The buddy-list-heading-text class controls overflow, alignment,
    // and wrapping. Most of the additional styling (fonts, color, etc.)
    // happens via styles on the surrounding element(s).
    function heading_text_span(): h.Tag {
        return h.span_tag({
            suppress_indent: true,
            classes: [h.trusted_simple_string("buddy-list-heading-text")],
            children: [
                h.text_var({
                    label: "header_text",
                    s: h.unescaped_text_string(info.header_text),
                }),
            ],
        });
    }

    // user_count_span builds an outer span around a text element that
    // says something like "(35K)" to indicate how many users are inside
    // our section of the buddy list.
    function user_count_span(): h.Tag {
        return h.span_tag({
            classes: [
                // The buddy-list-heading-user-count-with-parens class is used to
                // drive styling in the Zulip CSS. It only sets opacity as of
                // this writing.
                h.trusted_simple_string("buddy-list-heading-user-count-with-parens"),
                h.trusted_simple_string("hide"),
            ],
            children: [
                h.parenthesized_tag(
                    // inner span for count of people in the section
                    h.span_tag({
                        classes: [h.trusted_simple_string("buddy-list-heading-user-count")],
                    }),
                ),
            ],
        });
    }

    // The h5 tag encloses the heading text (e.g. "OTHERS") and the user count
    // (e.g. "(35K)") but not the rotation icon (for reasons not clear, but probably fine).
    function buddy_list_heading(): h.Tag {
        return h.h5_tag({
            force_attrs_before_class: true,
            classes: [
                // The buddy-list-heading drives a lot of CSS styling. It's also used by jQuery
                // to find the element to attach to for mouse handling.
                h.trusted_simple_string("buddy-list-heading"),
                // The no-style class turns off text decoration and sets the cursor
                // to a pointer, since this is gonna be part of the overall click
                // target to toggle whether you show uses in the section.
                h.trusted_simple_string("no-style"),
                // The hidden-for-spectators class hides the section from Zulip
                // spectators using the standard mechanisms.
                h.trusted_simple_string("hidden-for-spectators"),
            ],
            attrs: [
                h.attr(
                    "id",
                    h.trusted_attr_string_var({
                        label: "id",
                        s: h.unescaped_attr_string(info.id),
                    }),
                ),
            ],
            children: [
                heading_text_span(),
                h.comment("Hide the count until we have fetched data to display the correct count"),
                user_count_span(),
            ],
        });
    }

    return h.block([section_rotation_icon(), buddy_list_heading()]);
}
~~~

One important distinction between the Anders version and the other version is that the Anders version produces a string whereas the other version produces a `DocumentFragment` in its `to_dom` method. **Steve Howell** · 2026-01-04 01:20 UTC

~~~ ts
export class Block {
    elements: Element[] = [];

    constructor(elements: (Element | Block)[]) {
        for (const member of elements) {
            if (member instanceof Block) {
                this.elements.push(...member.elements);
            } else {
                this.elements.push(member);
            }
        }
    }

    to_source(indent: string): string {
        let source = "";
        for (const element of this.elements) {
            source += element.to_source(indent) + "\n";
        }
        return source;
    }

    to_dom(): DocumentFragment {
        const dom = document.createDocumentFragment();
        for (const element of this.elements) {
            if (element instanceof Comment) {
                continue;
            }
            dom.append(element.to_dom());
        }
        return dom;
    }

   // ...
}
~~~

            : ""}
    </button> `;
    return to_html(out);
}

~~~

## visually separate DMs from channels (left sidebar) #37298

*2026-01-07 to 2026-02-03 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/visually.20separate.20DMs.20from.20channels.20.28left.20sidebar.29.20.2337298/with/2346214)*

**Evy** · 2026-01-07 05:22 UTC

I'm working on #**design>visually separate DMs from channels (left sidebar) #37298** and have some implementation questions.

Because of how the left sidebar scrolls, a line between the DM section and the channels can be one of two things:

(1) When DMs *aren't* collapsed, it's a line between the DM container (`.direct-messages-container`) and the list of channels under that (`.streams_list`). Notably once you scroll high enough, this spot scrolls up and out of view. Making it position sticky doesn't seem to work because of how it interacts with other sticky elements (channel headers) as they scroll through.

(2) When DMs *are* collapsed, it's a line under the DM header (`.direct-messages-section-header`) and the scrolling container (`#left_sidebar_scroll_container`), so that it stays in place as the left sidebar scrolls further. This isn't possible when DMs are open because then it would be above the DM conversation rows.

It would be ideal if we didn't have to put the divider in two different places, but I can't think of a nice way to have just one divider that's always in the right place. Am I missing something?

#37298 has what I did do, which is have two dividers and display/hide them depending on if the DM section is collapsed, but this is still causing some problems when `toggle_pm_header_icon` adjusts the collapse status depending on scroll position, because displaying/hiding the divider changes the scroll position in a way that jumps.

A next step could be to fix the scrolling position, but what started out as a not-ideal-but-fine solution now feels much less ideal, and it would be great to find something less brittle.

Any advice?

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-01-07 19:38 UTC

I think the key to a better fix here is to fix a long-standing oddity with the structure in this area of the left sidebar. 

We have a `#direct-messages-section-header`div that sits *between* the `#left-sidebar-navigation-area` (a div that contains both the VIEWS header and the individual views), and the `#left_sidebar_scroll_container` that includes the actual DM rows plus all the channel things below it.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-01-07 19:39 UTC

The pain of trying to put this line in in a one-and-done fashion is that that heading is structurally distant from the DM rows, and so doing these kinds of gymnastics becomes necessary in different states.

My suspicion is that this structure was developed prior to good support for `position: sticky` and similar tools for preventing something from scrolling, but I don't see any immediate reason to carry that old approach forward.

## partial_subscribers on dev

*2026-01-08 to 2026-01-08 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/partial_subscribers.20on.20dev/with/2347026)*

**Evy** · 2026-01-08 00:37 UTC

Following up on [this comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/37311#discussion_r2666590026)

> I think the right path forward here is for you to post some notes in #frontend about what process you've used for testing the partial_subscribers feature and what's been helpful, and we can turn that into something to the developer documentation or configuration based on that?

What I do is:

```diff
diff --git a/web/src/buddy_data.ts b/web/src/buddy_data.ts
index 7a9ba7a0c1..01cecf710d 100644
--- a/web/src/buddy_data.ts
+++ b/web/src/buddy_data.ts
@@ -31,7 +31,7 @@ export function rewire_max_size_before_shrinking(value: typeof max_size_before_s
     max_size_before_shrinking = value;
 }
 
-export let max_channel_size_to_show_all_subscribers = 75;
+export let max_channel_size_to_show_all_subscribers = 3;
 
 export function rewire_max_channel_size_to_show_all_subscribers(
     value: typeof max_channel_size_to_show_all_subscribers,
diff --git a/zproject/default_settings.py b/zproject/default_settings.py
index 4f4231d1ad..0a9010e98a 100644
--- a/zproject/default_settings.py
+++ b/zproject/default_settings.py
@@ -761,7 +761,7 @@ SCIM_CONFIG: dict[str, SCIMConfigDict] = {}
 
 # Minimum number of subscribers in a channel for us to no longer
 # send full subscriber data to the client.
-MIN_PARTIAL_SUBSCRIBERS_CHANNEL_SIZE = 1000
+MIN_PARTIAL_SUBSCRIBERS_CHANNEL_SIZE = 5
 
 # Whether to prefer direct message group over personal recipient
 # for 1:1 or self messages.
```

And then it fetches complete data for 3 channels on pageload (for the default dev environment) and has to do followup fetches for the rest. It's important to keep `max_channel_size_to_show_all_subscribers` less than `MIN_PARTIAL_SUBSCRIBERS_CHANNEL_SIZE`.

It can also be helpful to add a delay at the top of `fetch_stream_subscribers_from_server` (`await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));`) if I want to test what happens if the fetch takes a while.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-01-08 17:08 UTC

That last thing about the delay is probably better managed instead using the browser developer tools Network tab to add a profile that adds 1s delay to all network requests.

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-10 04:28 UTC

I am using an uppy cropper similar in implementation to `build_direct_upload_widget` for cropping custom emojis in [#37231](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/37231)

The current flaw with my implementation is that it works fine for static images, but if the user uploads an animated webp/avif or a gif, then it gets converted into a static image after being cropped through uppy. What would be the correct approach here? 

Would it be plausible to limit the cropping to png/jpeg formats only, but allowing the upload of aforementioned animated formats without cropping? Even though ideally we would want to support the maximum number of formats.

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-10 10:00 UTC

@Sahil Batra I had some input from you earlier too on this feature. Any thoughts on this?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-01-11 06:41 UTC

I don't think Uppy allows to crop GIFs as it just uses the first frame of GIF as an image. So, yeah we would either need to skip cropping GIFs and other animated files or find another library that does that.

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-11 07:23 UTC

Yup, uppy uses only the first frame of the GIF. From a user perspective, we should ideally try to support as many formats as possible. So, I think using a different library is plausible. 

If I pivot my implementation towards using a separate library for the formats not supported by uppy then there are two scenarios:
1. replace uppy for cropping emojis (so the other library would have to handle both images and animated files)
2. add this library alongside uppy, so that uppy handles the images and this library would handle the animated files.

I'd have to go with (1) as it would look uniform to the user for both types of files. Does it sound alright? @Alya Abbott @Sahil Batra

**Alya Abbott** · 2026-01-12 18:46 UTC

Can we offer cropping for non-animated images but not for animated images?

**Alya Abbott** · 2026-01-12 18:47 UTC

It's not important to offer cropping for animated GIFs. It *is* important not to mess up the animation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-01-12 20:38 UTC

We're definitely not replacing `uppy` for this use case.

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-13 03:49 UTC

Yup, that sounds good. I presumed it was important to offer cropping for animated files as well.

One thing I've noticed with animated images is that they are *most often* GIFs. Animated avifs/webp are rare; they are mostly static.

So,  when a GIF comes up, we skip the `uppy` flow, but for all of the other formats we trigger uppy. That'd more meaningful.

**Alya Abbott** · 2026-01-13 16:33 UTC

Well, can we actually know whether a file is animated? Users uploading a non-animated GIF would be missing out on cropping in your proposal.

**Alya Abbott** · 2026-01-13 16:33 UTC

And also it would mess up animated webp images without any workaround, which isn't really OK.

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-14 09:06 UTC

Ah, you're right. I didn't think of those cases as that important, but they are - thanks for clarifying!

I found that we are doing this sort of validation when we are adding the user uploaded emoji on the server; using `libvips_check_image` which gets called inside `resize_emoji` in `thumbnail.py`

There's no validation endpoint which uses `pyvips` for only validating if the uploaded file is animated or is an image. Therefore, I find it reasonable to *add* an endpoint that calls a *new* function which uses `pyvips` to do this. And, according to the result of this endpoint we trigger or not trigger `uppy` on user-upload.

Does that sound plausible @Tim Abbott ?

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-01-14 18:32 UTC

Maybe. I've not investigated whether the browser can tell you if an image is animated without talking to the server. I think probably not.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-01-14 20:13 UTC

I don't love an endpoint which lets you feed an arbitrary image into libvips without us storing it at all.  It makes the attack surface for untraceable attacks bigger.

In general, I'm not much convinced that cropping on custom emoji makes sense.  Most custom emoji are passed around, and don't need to be changed other than resizing, which the server does.

Did we have any actual user requests for #36927, or are we just building the feature because it seemed like an extension of the cropping of logos and avatars?  As we're noting, they've actually got quite different uses.

Continuing the discussion from https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/35342#issuecomment-3716019529.

We discussed in #**issues>📂 generate channel email - admin can view private channels** that we want to show the email UI only to users who can send messages to the stream. ## calculating total muted messages for user

*2026-01-16 to 2026-01-20 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/calculating.20total.20muted.20messages.20for.20user/with/2355447)*

**Sayam Samal** · 2026-01-16 18:26 UTC

I'm working on #31607, to show a warning navbar banner in the combined feed when a user mutes more than a said percentage of messages (currently 90%). I was thinking of an alternative solution we could use to tackle the issue than what is described in the issue:

**Sayam Samal** · 2026-01-16 18:27 UTC

Approach 1: This basically follows exactly what the issue describes. We check for the condition when the initial backfill for all messages is done.
```ts
export function check_and_show_muted_banner(): void {
    if (all_messages_data.empty()) {
        // If all_messages_data is empty, even after waiting for
        // initial_backfill_for_all_messages_done then there are
        // no messages to check. And the ratio calculation below
        // would result in a division by zero.
        return;
    }

    // We use all_messages_after_mute_filtering() here because all_messages_data
    // is initialized with muting disabled (excludes_muted_topics: false,
    // excludes_muted_users: false). Therefore, this method returns all messages
    // effectively ignoring muting, and we have to manually calculate how many
    // messages would be hidden if muting were applied.
    const messages = all_messages_data.all_messages_after_mute_filtering();

    let muted_count = 0;
    for (const message of messages) {
        if (muted_users.is_user_muted(message.sender_id)) {
            muted_count += 1;
        } else if (
            message.type === "stream" &&
            !user_topics.is_topic_visible_in_home(message.stream_id, message.topic)
        ) {
            muted_count += 1;
        }
    }

    if (muted_count / messages.length > 0.9) {
        // If more than 90% of the loaded messages are muted,
        // show the warning banner.
        open_navbar_banner_and_resize(TOO_MANY_MUTED_MESSAGES_BANNER);
    }
}
```

**Sayam Samal** · 2026-01-16 18:27 UTC

**Alternative approach:** Call the banner when the narrow changes to Combined Feed, and the message_list for the combined feed would provide us with the data required to calculate the ratio. From my understanding, Combined Feed would be affected the most when too many messages are muted, and this way any additional muted topics/users after page load are taken in consideration.
```ts
export function check_and_show_muted_banner(): void {
    if (!initial_backfill_for_all_messages_done) {
        // We wait until the initial backfill is complete to ensure
        // that all_messages_data cache has been populated.
        setTimeout(check_and_show_muted_banner, 2000);
        return;
    }

    if (all_messages_data.empty()) {
        // If all_messages_data is empty, even after waiting for
        // initial_backfill_for_all_messages_done then there are
        // no messages to check. And the ratio calculation below
        // would result in a division by zero.
        return;
    }

    const msg_list = message_lists.current;
    if (!msg_list || !msg_list.is_combined_feed_view) {
        // If the msg_list undefined or the user has switched
        // to different view by the time the initial backfill
        // was complete, do not show the banner.
        return;
    }

    const total_count = all_messages_data.num_items();
    const muted_count = total_count - msg_list.data.num_items();

    if (muted_count / total_count > 0.9) {
        // If more than 90% of the loaded messages are muted,
        // show the warning banner.
        open_navbar_banner_and_resize(TOO_MANY_MUTED_MESSAGES_BANNER);
    }
}
```

**Sayam Samal** · 2026-01-16 18:33 UTC

I don't particularly think the alternative solution is higher quality, but I wanted to run it through here just in case we wanted this approach to showing the banner.

## ✔ Forward message template based on recipient #37145

*2026-01-22 to 2026-02-23 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Forward.20message.20template.20based.20on.20recipient.20.2337145/with/2361096)*

**Pieter K** · 2026-01-22 16:37 UTC

Issue: #37103
PR: #37145

CZO discussion: #**feedback>Include Topic Name in quoted message "said" line**

I wanted to discuss how we might implement the dynamic forward message template, i.e, if the message is being sent to another topic/channel/dm, use the template in #37103.

My current approach is to add a logic in `compose_recipient.item_click_callback` that check if `get_is_processing_forward_message` is true and call `compose_reply.quote_message` again. This requires refactoring `set_is_processing_forward_message` to also store the original parameter of `quote_message` for the message being forwarded.

My main concerns with this approach are the potential jankiness/complexity in handling these cases:
- When should we mark `set_is_processing_forward_message` as false? Do we also do that when the user deletes the whole compose area, when the user puts the message in draft (which brings its own complexity), etc.
- What happens if the user edits the initial forwarded message template?

So, I'm not confident with this approach, would love to hear if anyone has other ideas.

## ✔ _get_topic_link_content escaping

*2026-01-28 to 2026-02-09 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20_get_topic_link_content.20escaping/with/2365437)*

**Evy** · 2026-01-28 18:34 UTC

I'd like to propose we fully escape text in `_get_topic_link_content` instead of only escaping the stream and topic name:

```diff
diff --git a/web/src/topic_link_util.ts b/web/src/topic_link_util.ts
index 8d561ecbbc..8b26500cf9 100644
--- a/web/src/topic_link_util.ts
+++ b/web/src/topic_link_util.ts
@@ -91,17 +91,17 @@ function _get_topic_link_content(opts: {
         const topic_display_name = util.get_final_topic_display_name(topic_name);
         if (message_id !== undefined) {
             return {
-                text: `#${escape(stream_name)} > ${escape(topic_display_name)} @ 💬`,
+                text: escape(`#${stream_name} > ${topic_display_name} @ 💬`),
                 url: `${stream_topic_url}/near/${message_id}`,
             };
         }
         return {
-            text: `#${escape(stream_name)} > ${escape(topic_display_name)}`,
+            text: escape(`#${stream_name} > ${topic_display_name}`),
             url: stream_topic_url,
         };
     }
     return {
-        text: `#${escape(stream_name)}`,
+        text: escape(`#${stream_name}`),
         url: hash_util.channel_url_by_user_setting(stream_id),
     };
 }

```

This is used for `get_fallback_markdown_link` and html/markdown styntax for `copy_link_to_clipboard`. This means markdown links will show with `&gt;`, but that seems fine because it still seems to render correctly in markdown readers (I tried with Zulip and GitHub).

If we can indeed escape it completely this way, that will simplify the code for cross-topic links which needs to show that text in a handlebars template, since we could render it as already escaped html. (I was previously trying to refactor the function to have options to return the text partially escaped, as before, and also not escaped at all.)

Thoughts?

## Performance Issue - User Group Descriptions Rendered Repeate

*2026-02-08 to 2026-02-14 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/6-frontend/topic/Performance.20Issue.20-.20User.20Group.20Descriptions.20Rendered.20Repeate/with/2373357)*

**Om kapale** · 2026-02-08 04:03 UTC

Hey everyone! 👋

So I was working on a different issue and stumbled upon something that seemed off. I wanted to get your thoughts before moving forward.
**The Issue:**

I noticed that user group descriptions are being rendered from markdown **every single time** they're displayed. Unlike realm descriptions or stream descriptions (which cache the rendered HTML), user groups don't have any caching mechanism. This means we're doing unnecessary markdown rendering over and over.
**Here's what I found:**
**Before** (current behavior):
* User group has description in markdown: `"Nobody"`
* No `rendered_description_html` field exists
* Markdown gets rendered every time it's displayed
* Pretty inefficient, especially if you have lots of user groups

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/30/EJvipQRGBOL6sLWXlPVVmvef/image.png)

**After** (my fix):
* Added `rendered_description_html` field to cache the HTML
* Added `rendered_description_version` to track markdown engine version
* Now it renders once on create/update, then just serves the cached version
* Works exactly like how we handle realm descriptions

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/36/zIJuPySmAFcN8pbRHxSjt9mC/image.png)

**My approach:**

I basically followed the same pattern from #37314 (realm descriptions). The fix includes:
* New database fields for cached HTML and version tracking
* Rendering happens in `render_user_group_description()`
* Updated events to include the rendered fields
* All existing tests still pass ✓

**Testing:**
Tested markdown rendering with bold, italic, links, and emojis - everything renders correctly and gets cached properly.


I've got PR #37667 up if you want to see the full code changes. Happy to make any adjustments based on feedback!

**Om kapale** · 2026-02-08 04:04 UTC

Screenshots are from Django shell rather than the UI because the user groups settings page wasn't accessible in my dev environment. The cached field works correctly in the backend and will render properly wherever user group descriptions are displayed in the UI.

I've spent some time researching the ts migration on `spoilers.test.cjs` -> `spoilers.test.ts`. Identified the following issues:

1.
`test-js-with-node` is hardcoded to append the `.test.cjs` extension if it does not find one.
 
```
if not fn.endswith(".test.cjs"):
        fn += ".test.cjs"
```

2.
Renaming to `.ts` forces the file into ES module scope in Node v24. ESM does not support `require`. Temporarily, I'm using `createRequire`. However, for a complete ts migration, we would need to look into migrating `namespace.cjs` itself.

3.
Even after using `createRequire`, the run fails as `zrequire` looks for a relative path, probably based on the python runner (currently fails when run using `node --experimental-strip-types`)

```
return require(`../../src/${short_fn}`);
```

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-03 17:27 UTC

One of the rules you disabled is `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment`. What's the meaning of that rule?

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-03-03 17:48 UTC

`@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment` linter error is flagged whenever we try to assign a value of type `any` to a variable.
In `.cts` file, we must use `import type ... from ...` and `require()`.  And `require` tends to return the `any` type. The linter flags that as unsafe assignment even though we try to cast the result using `typeof`. 
In the `spoilers.test.cts` the following lines of code are flagged:

```
const assert: typeof assert_module = require("node:assert/strict");

const {noop, run_test}: typeof test_lib_types = require("./lib/test.cjs");
```

The rest of the file is strictly checked so that such errors do not pop up elsewhere.

[no-unsafe-assignment-errors.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/84/CkuLgPzZD7bfOs2p0cKApAg3/image.png)

**Greg Price** · 2026-03-03 18:13 UTC

> The type safety related rules are still fully active and all types are still validated by typescript.

> `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment` linter error is flagged whenever we try to assign a value of type `any` to a variable.

How do these fit together?

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-03-03 18:32 UTC

Youre right to point that out. `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment` is a key type-safety rule.
In my earlier comment I was referring to the fact that the test logic itself is type-safe.
However i've actually updated the file now to remove that eslint-disable altogether. By using both, type annotation and assertion in the same line, we satisfy both the linter and the ts compiler.

```
const assert: typeof assert_module = require("node:assert/strict") as typeof assert_module;

const {noop, run_test}: typeof test_lib_types = require("./lib/test.cjs") as typeof test_lib_types;
```

(earlier when using only type assertion, the `ts(2775)` compiler error popped up that required `assert` to have an explicit type annotation)

This ensures that `no-unsafe-assignment` is no longer disabled.

I researched about the cause behind the failing of the `Zulip CI / Ubuntu 22.04 (Python 3.10, backend + frontend) (pull_request)` Github workflow job in #38418, #38738, #38494.

Here are my findings:
- The main cause: The `istanbul/nyc` and `pirates` hooks take control over the code before `node` has the time to strip the types.
- This is proved by looking at the stack trace. I was able to reproduce the issue by running the following command:
  `./tools/test-js-with-node --coverage web/tests/user_pill.test.cjs`

  Stack trace:
  ![stack_trace_error.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/80/xST471TZ7oFKPCTg_gDCJo-0/image.png)
  Notice the control being passed to `node_modules/.pnpm/append-transform@2.0.0/node_modules/append-transform/index.js` for generating the coverage report. It then calls `module._compile` which bypasses the node's built-in type-stripping.

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-03-30 18:29 UTC

"nyc": {
  "exclude": [

}
```
